1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:03,946
Sweetheart, last December my granddaughter paid thirty-two

2
00:00:03,946 --> 00:00:06,668
dollars for one little tin of peppermint

3
00:00:06,668 --> 00:00:07,825
bark at the mall.

4
00:00:08,005 --> 00:00:09,526
Thirty-two dollars.

5
00:00:09,706 --> 00:00:11,595
She brought it to my house so

6
00:00:11,595 --> 00:00:13,093
proud, and I opened it,

7
00:00:13,093 --> 00:00:15,308
and the white layer slid right off

8
00:00:15,308 --> 00:00:17,589
the chocolate like a loose shingle.

9
00:00:17,769 --> 00:00:18,830
I said, honey,

10
00:00:18,830 --> 00:00:21,332
give me five dollars and an hour,

11
00:00:21,332 --> 00:00:23,606
and I'll make you a better one

12
00:00:23,606 --> 00:00:25,350
that never comes apart.

13
00:00:25,699 --> 00:00:28,293
So tonight I'm giving you my peppermint

14
00:00:28,293 --> 00:00:28,625
bark.

15
00:00:28,805 --> 00:00:30,515
A dark chocolate layer,

16
00:00:30,515 --> 00:00:32,300
a white chocolate layer,

17
00:00:32,300 --> 00:00:34,307
crushed candy canes on top,

18
00:00:34,307 --> 00:00:37,133
and the two layers stuck together like

19
00:00:37,133 --> 00:00:38,918
they were born that way.

20
00:00:39,098 --> 00:00:41,192
Every ingredient, every step,

21
00:00:41,192 --> 00:00:43,793
and the three mistakes that make the

22
00:00:43,793 --> 00:00:44,949
layers separate.

23
00:00:45,129 --> 00:00:47,970
It's the easiest Christmas candy you will

24
00:00:47,970 --> 00:00:50,326
ever make, and it's the one people

25
00:00:50,326 --> 00:00:51,642
ask for every year.

26
00:00:51,822 --> 00:00:53,127
And stay with me,

27
00:00:53,127 --> 00:00:56,044
because the step that keeps the layers

28
00:00:56,044 --> 00:00:58,731
together is one almost nobody does,

29
00:00:58,731 --> 00:01:01,265
and I'll show you exactly when to

30
00:01:01,265 --> 00:01:01,725
do it.

31
00:01:02,076 --> 00:01:04,290
When I was a girl in Mansfield,

32
00:01:04,290 --> 00:01:07,005
candy canes came in a little cardboard

33
00:01:07,005 --> 00:01:09,220
box of twelve from the five and

34
00:01:09,220 --> 00:01:11,649
dime, and they were all white with

35
00:01:11,649 --> 00:01:13,720
red stripes and nothing else.

36
00:01:13,900 --> 00:01:15,888
My mother hung them on the tree

37
00:01:15,888 --> 00:01:18,068
with the hook end over the branch.

38
00:01:18,248 --> 00:01:20,099
And every one that broke,

39
00:01:20,099 --> 00:01:21,728
and they always broke,

40
00:01:21,728 --> 00:01:23,949
went into a jar in the pantry.

41
00:01:24,129 --> 00:01:25,555
By Christmas Eve,

42
00:01:25,555 --> 00:01:27,903
that jar was full of red and

43
00:01:27,903 --> 00:01:28,993
white pieces.

44
00:01:29,343 --> 00:01:31,635
And on Christmas Eve afternoon,

45
00:01:31,635 --> 00:01:34,222
my mother melted a bar of chocolate

46
00:01:34,222 --> 00:01:35,922
in a bowl over the pot,

47
00:01:35,922 --> 00:01:38,361
poured it thin on a buttered pan,

48
00:01:38,361 --> 00:01:40,948
and threw the broken candy canes on

49
00:01:40,948 --> 00:01:41,244
top.

50
00:01:41,424 --> 00:01:43,432
She called it peppermint scrap.

51
00:01:43,612 --> 00:01:46,106
Danny and I broke it into pieces

52
00:01:46,106 --> 00:01:47,664
with a butter knife.

53
00:01:47,844 --> 00:01:49,702
It was nothing fancy.

54
00:01:49,882 --> 00:01:52,476
But that is the grandmother of every

55
00:01:52,476 --> 00:01:55,070
fancy tin of peppermint bark you see

56
00:01:55,070 --> 00:01:56,511
in the stores today.

57
00:01:56,860 --> 00:01:58,950
The white layer came later.

58
00:01:59,130 --> 00:02:00,939
In nineteen seventy-one,

59
00:02:00,939 --> 00:02:04,330
my sister-in-law brought a version with white

60
00:02:04,330 --> 00:02:05,610
chocolate on top,

61
00:02:05,610 --> 00:02:08,097
and my mother tasted it and said,

62
00:02:08,097 --> 00:02:10,659
well, now that's just showing off.

63
00:02:10,839 --> 00:02:13,369
Then she asked for the recipe before

64
00:02:13,369 --> 00:02:14,844
the evening was over.

65
00:02:15,024 --> 00:02:17,677
That's the version I've made every year

66
00:02:17,677 --> 00:02:20,330
since, and I've changed only one thing.

67
00:02:20,510 --> 00:02:23,192
The thing that keeps the layers together.

68
00:02:23,542 --> 00:02:25,249
Here's what you need,

69
00:02:25,249 --> 00:02:25,737
honey.

70
00:02:25,917 --> 00:02:29,042
Twelve ounces of good semi-sweet or dark

71
00:02:29,042 --> 00:02:30,526
chocolate, chopped.

72
00:02:30,706 --> 00:02:33,182
Twelve ounces of white chocolate,

73
00:02:33,182 --> 00:02:33,783
chopped.

74
00:02:33,963 --> 00:02:37,383
Two teaspoons of vegetable oil or coconut

75
00:02:37,383 --> 00:02:39,384
oil, one for each layer.

76
00:02:39,564 --> 00:02:42,351
Half a teaspoon of peppermint extract.

77
00:02:42,531 --> 00:02:45,284
And about eight regular candy canes,

78
00:02:45,284 --> 00:02:48,266
or a cup of crushed peppermint candies.

79
00:02:48,446 --> 00:02:50,025
That's the whole list.

80
00:02:50,205 --> 00:02:51,540
Five things.

81
00:02:51,890 --> 00:02:54,105
Now listen about the chocolate,

82
00:02:54,105 --> 00:02:55,606
because this matters.

83
00:02:55,786 --> 00:02:57,466
Buy real chocolate bars,

84
00:02:57,466 --> 00:02:59,776
the kind that say cocoa butter on

85
00:02:59,776 --> 00:03:00,476
the label.

86
00:03:00,656 --> 00:03:02,479
Not chocolate chips.

87
00:03:02,659 --> 00:03:05,282
Chips have something added so they hold

88
00:03:05,282 --> 00:03:06,828
their shape in cookies,

89
00:03:06,828 --> 00:03:09,316
and that means they don't melt smooth

90
00:03:09,316 --> 00:03:11,401
and they don't set with a snap.

91
00:03:11,581 --> 00:03:14,646
And not those colored candy melts either.

92
00:03:14,826 --> 00:03:17,032
They taste like sweet wax.

93
00:03:17,382 --> 00:03:20,016
And the white chocolate is the fussy

94
00:03:20,016 --> 00:03:20,308
one.

95
00:03:20,488 --> 00:03:23,460
Look for cocoa butter in the ingredients.

96
00:03:23,640 --> 00:03:26,148
If the label says white baking chips

97
00:03:26,148 --> 00:03:27,472
or vanilla coating,

98
00:03:27,472 --> 00:03:29,701
it isn't really white chocolate,

99
00:03:29,701 --> 00:03:31,791
and it won't stick to the dark

100
00:03:31,791 --> 00:03:33,114
layer the same way.

101
00:03:33,294 --> 00:03:35,526
This is where people save a dollar

102
00:03:35,526 --> 00:03:37,890
and then wonder why their bark falls

103
00:03:37,890 --> 00:03:39,006
apart in the tin.

104
00:03:39,186 --> 00:03:41,051
In a minute I'll show you the

105
00:03:41,051 --> 00:03:43,816
one moment that decides whether your layers

106
00:03:43,816 --> 00:03:44,202
stick.

107
00:03:44,551 --> 00:03:46,748
You need an eight by eight pan

108
00:03:46,748 --> 00:03:47,846
for thick bark,

109
00:03:47,846 --> 00:03:50,262
or a nine by thirteen for thinner

110
00:03:50,262 --> 00:03:50,774
pieces.

111
00:03:50,954 --> 00:03:53,697
Line it with parchment or wax paper,

112
00:03:53,697 --> 00:03:56,058
and let the paper hang over two

113
00:03:56,058 --> 00:03:58,496
sides, so you can lift the whole

114
00:03:58,496 --> 00:04:00,324
slab out when it's done.

115
00:04:00,504 --> 00:04:02,654
My mother used a buttered pan,

116
00:04:02,654 --> 00:04:04,517
and we had to pry the bark

117
00:04:04,517 --> 00:04:05,879
out with a spatula.

118
00:04:06,059 --> 00:04:08,225
Parchment is one of the few new

119
00:04:08,225 --> 00:04:10,181
things I'll admit is better.

120
00:04:10,530 --> 00:04:11,494
Step one.

121
00:04:11,674 --> 00:04:13,543
Crush the candy canes.

122
00:04:13,723 --> 00:04:15,453
Put them in a zip bag,

123
00:04:15,453 --> 00:04:17,732
wrap the bag in a dish towel,

124
00:04:17,732 --> 00:04:20,012
and tap it with a rolling pin

125
00:04:20,012 --> 00:04:22,291
or the bottom of a heavy pot.

126
00:04:22,471 --> 00:04:23,981
Not too fine.

127
00:04:24,161 --> 00:04:26,867
You want little pieces like gravel,

128
00:04:26,867 --> 00:04:27,562
not dust.

129
00:04:27,742 --> 00:04:30,015
Then shake them in a strainer to

130
00:04:30,015 --> 00:04:31,365
get the powder out.

131
00:04:31,545 --> 00:04:33,925
Save the powder for your cocoa.

132
00:04:34,105 --> 00:04:36,139
The powder makes the top of the

133
00:04:36,139 --> 00:04:36,926
bark sticky.

134
00:04:37,276 --> 00:04:38,321
Step two.

135
00:04:38,501 --> 00:04:41,635
Melt the dark chocolate with one teaspoon

136
00:04:41,635 --> 00:04:42,170
of oil.

137
00:04:42,350 --> 00:04:44,830
The easy way is in the microwave,

138
00:04:44,830 --> 00:04:46,032
in a glass bowl,

139
00:04:46,032 --> 00:04:47,911
thirty seconds at a time,

140
00:04:47,911 --> 00:04:49,790
stirring well every time,

141
00:04:49,790 --> 00:04:52,420
even when it doesn't look like it's

142
00:04:52,420 --> 00:04:53,322
melting yet.

143
00:04:53,502 --> 00:04:55,884
Stop when there are still a few

144
00:04:55,884 --> 00:04:58,805
little lumps, and just stir until they

145
00:04:58,805 --> 00:04:59,574
disappear.

146
00:04:59,754 --> 00:05:01,867
If you overheat chocolate,

147
00:05:01,867 --> 00:05:03,980
it turns thick and grainy,

148
00:05:03,980 --> 00:05:05,686
and you can't fix it.

149
00:05:05,866 --> 00:05:07,553
If this is helping you,

150
00:05:07,553 --> 00:05:10,046
honey, tap the like button for me.

151
00:05:10,226 --> 00:05:13,070
It helps Grandma more than you know.

152
00:05:13,420 --> 00:05:15,394
Or do it my mother's way.

153
00:05:15,574 --> 00:05:17,434
A bowl sitting on top of a

154
00:05:17,434 --> 00:05:19,724
small pot with an inch of barely

155
00:05:19,724 --> 00:05:20,868
simmering water.

156
00:05:21,048 --> 00:05:23,132
The bowl must not touch the water,

157
00:05:23,132 --> 00:05:24,910
and not one drop of water can

158
00:05:24,910 --> 00:05:26,319
get into the chocolate.

159
00:05:26,499 --> 00:05:29,233
One drop of water and the whole

160
00:05:29,233 --> 00:05:31,438
bowl seizes into a stiff,

161
00:05:31,438 --> 00:05:32,409
dull paste.

162
00:05:32,589 --> 00:05:34,862
My mother wiped the bottom of the

163
00:05:34,862 --> 00:05:37,066
bowl with a towel every time she

164
00:05:37,066 --> 00:05:37,755
lifted it.

165
00:05:38,105 --> 00:05:39,232
Step three.

166
00:05:39,412 --> 00:05:42,023
Stir a quarter teaspoon of the peppermint

167
00:05:42,023 --> 00:05:44,570
extract into the dark chocolate and pour

168
00:05:44,570 --> 00:05:45,971
it into the lined pan.

169
00:05:46,151 --> 00:05:48,407
Spread it even with the back of

170
00:05:48,407 --> 00:05:49,935
a spoon or a spatula,

171
00:05:49,935 --> 00:05:51,608
right into the corners.

172
00:05:51,788 --> 00:05:54,024
Then tap the pan on the counter

173
00:05:54,024 --> 00:05:56,116
a few times to settle it flat

174
00:05:56,116 --> 00:05:57,558
and pop the bubbles.

175
00:05:57,908 --> 00:06:00,821
Step four, and this is the secret,

176
00:06:00,821 --> 00:06:01,763
sweetheart.

177
00:06:01,943 --> 00:06:04,025
Put the pan in the icebox for

178
00:06:04,025 --> 00:06:06,250
only fifteen to twenty minutes.

179
00:06:06,430 --> 00:06:07,440
Not an hour.

180
00:06:07,620 --> 00:06:09,700
You want the dark layer set enough

181
00:06:09,700 --> 00:06:11,841
that it doesn't swirl when you pour

182
00:06:11,841 --> 00:06:12,941
on the next layer,

183
00:06:12,941 --> 00:06:14,960
but still a little soft and tacky

184
00:06:14,960 --> 00:06:16,061
when you touch it.

185
00:06:16,241 --> 00:06:17,344
Touch the corner.

186
00:06:17,524 --> 00:06:19,910
If it leaves a faint fingerprint,

187
00:06:19,910 --> 00:06:20,705
it's ready.

188
00:06:21,054 --> 00:06:23,176
This is why store bark and so

189
00:06:23,176 --> 00:06:25,443
much homemade bark comes apart.

190
00:06:25,623 --> 00:06:27,954
If the dark layer gets cold and

191
00:06:27,954 --> 00:06:30,660
hard, the warm white layer just sits

192
00:06:30,660 --> 00:06:32,690
on top of it like a blanket

193
00:06:32,690 --> 00:06:33,367
on a bed.

194
00:06:33,547 --> 00:06:34,928
They never join.

195
00:06:35,108 --> 00:06:37,108
But when the bottom is still a

196
00:06:37,108 --> 00:06:40,106
little soft, the two chocolates melt together

197
00:06:40,106 --> 00:06:41,572
right where they meet,

198
00:06:41,572 --> 00:06:43,305
and they set as one piece.

199
00:06:43,485 --> 00:06:44,562
Stay with me,

200
00:06:44,562 --> 00:06:47,460
because the next step has to happen

201
00:06:47,460 --> 00:06:47,874
fast.

202
00:06:48,223 --> 00:06:49,431
Step five.

203
00:06:49,611 --> 00:06:51,760
While the dark layer chills,

204
00:06:51,760 --> 00:06:54,753
melt the white chocolate with the other

205
00:06:54,753 --> 00:06:55,981
teaspoon of oil,

206
00:06:55,981 --> 00:06:56,979
the same way,

207
00:06:56,979 --> 00:06:57,900
but gentler.

208
00:06:58,080 --> 00:07:00,015
Twenty seconds at a time,

209
00:07:00,015 --> 00:07:03,653
because white chocolate burns faster than dark.

210
00:07:03,833 --> 00:07:06,394
Stir in the last quarter teaspoon of

211
00:07:06,394 --> 00:07:07,746
peppermint extract.

212
00:07:07,926 --> 00:07:10,726
It should be smooth and pourable,

213
00:07:10,726 --> 00:07:12,338
and only just warm.

214
00:07:12,518 --> 00:07:13,621
If it's hot,

215
00:07:13,621 --> 00:07:15,919
let it sit a few minutes.

216
00:07:16,269 --> 00:07:17,454
Step six.

217
00:07:17,634 --> 00:07:20,346
Pour the white chocolate over the tacky

218
00:07:20,346 --> 00:07:22,920
dark layer, and spread it quickly and

219
00:07:22,920 --> 00:07:25,145
gently all the way to the edges.

220
00:07:25,325 --> 00:07:26,533
Then right away,

221
00:07:26,533 --> 00:07:27,666
before it sets,

222
00:07:27,666 --> 00:07:30,686
scatter the crushed candy canes all over

223
00:07:30,686 --> 00:07:33,329
the top and press them down lightly

224
00:07:33,329 --> 00:07:34,462
with your palm,

225
00:07:34,462 --> 00:07:35,519
so they stick.

226
00:07:35,699 --> 00:07:37,820
If you wait even five minutes,

227
00:07:37,820 --> 00:07:40,224
they'll just roll off when you cut

228
00:07:40,224 --> 00:07:40,436
it.

229
00:07:40,785 --> 00:07:41,842
Step seven.

230
00:07:42,022 --> 00:07:44,434
Back in the icebox for about an

231
00:07:44,434 --> 00:07:47,003
hour, until it's completely firm.

232
00:07:47,183 --> 00:07:49,345
Then lift the whole slab out by

233
00:07:49,345 --> 00:07:51,298
the paper, and let it sit on

234
00:07:51,298 --> 00:07:53,600
the counter for ten minutes so it

235
00:07:53,600 --> 00:07:55,484
doesn't crack into slivers.

236
00:07:55,664 --> 00:07:58,382
Break it into rough pieces with your

237
00:07:58,382 --> 00:08:00,421
hands, or cut it with a big

238
00:08:00,421 --> 00:08:03,291
knife warmed under hot water and wiped

239
00:08:03,291 --> 00:08:03,593
dry.

240
00:08:03,773 --> 00:08:06,026
Warm knife, clean cuts.

241
00:08:06,375 --> 00:08:08,090
So the three mistakes,

242
00:08:08,090 --> 00:08:08,558
honey.

243
00:08:08,738 --> 00:08:11,607
Mistake one, the dark layer gets too

244
00:08:11,607 --> 00:08:13,997
cold before the white goes on.

245
00:08:14,177 --> 00:08:16,354
Fifteen to twenty minutes,

246
00:08:16,354 --> 00:08:17,359
not an hour,

247
00:08:17,359 --> 00:08:18,531
not overnight.

248
00:08:18,711 --> 00:08:22,239
Mistake two, chocolate chips or candy melts

249
00:08:22,239 --> 00:08:24,783
instead of real chocolate bars.

250
00:08:24,963 --> 00:08:26,374
And mistake three,

251
00:08:26,374 --> 00:08:28,411
overheating the chocolate.

252
00:08:28,591 --> 00:08:30,968
Short bursts, stir every time,

253
00:08:30,968 --> 00:08:33,424
and take it off before it's all

254
00:08:33,424 --> 00:08:33,978
melted.

255
00:08:34,158 --> 00:08:35,617
But there's one more,

256
00:08:35,617 --> 00:08:38,257
and you'll see why my husband laughed.

257
00:08:38,606 --> 00:08:40,415
And here's one more,

258
00:08:40,415 --> 00:08:41,590
a little one.

259
00:08:41,770 --> 00:08:44,926
Don't add the peppermint extract to chocolate

260
00:08:44,926 --> 00:08:45,978
that's too hot,

261
00:08:45,978 --> 00:08:48,643
and never use a water-based flavoring.

262
00:08:48,823 --> 00:08:52,558
Use oil-based or regular peppermint extract,

263
00:08:52,558 --> 00:08:53,746
just a little.

264
00:08:53,926 --> 00:08:56,343
One year I used a whole teaspoon

265
00:08:56,343 --> 00:08:57,400
in each layer,

266
00:08:57,400 --> 00:08:59,968
and my husband said it tasted like

267
00:08:59,968 --> 00:09:00,799
toothpaste.

268
00:09:00,979 --> 00:09:02,012
He was right.

269
00:09:02,192 --> 00:09:04,816
Half a teaspoon total is plenty.

270
00:09:05,166 --> 00:09:07,663
Now, why I love this one.

271
00:09:07,843 --> 00:09:10,641
A batch costs about five dollars and

272
00:09:10,641 --> 00:09:12,429
fills four little tins.

273
00:09:12,609 --> 00:09:15,381
Put the pieces in a cellophane bag

274
00:09:15,381 --> 00:09:17,094
tied with red ribbon,

275
00:09:17,094 --> 00:09:19,296
or in a jar with wax paper.

276
00:09:19,476 --> 00:09:20,653
For the mailman,

277
00:09:20,653 --> 00:09:22,640
the teachers, the neighbor,

278
00:09:22,640 --> 00:09:24,039
the lady at church.

279
00:09:24,219 --> 00:09:26,921
I give away twelve bags every year,

280
00:09:26,921 --> 00:09:29,932
and every December somebody stops me in

281
00:09:29,932 --> 00:09:32,325
the grocery store to ask if the

282
00:09:32,325 --> 00:09:33,483
bark is coming.

283
00:09:33,833 --> 00:09:35,456
Keep it in a tin in a

284
00:09:35,456 --> 00:09:37,775
cool spot, or in the icebox if

285
00:09:37,775 --> 00:09:39,244
your house is warm.

286
00:09:39,424 --> 00:09:42,048
It keeps two or three weeks.

287
00:09:42,228 --> 00:09:44,605
Put wax paper between the layers so

288
00:09:44,605 --> 00:09:46,779
the pieces don't stick together.

289
00:09:46,959 --> 00:09:49,501
And keep it away from the cookies.

290
00:09:49,681 --> 00:09:52,722
Peppermint makes everything in the tin taste

291
00:09:52,722 --> 00:09:55,901
like peppermint, and nobody wants a peppermint

292
00:09:55,901 --> 00:09:57,007
gingerbread man.

293
00:09:57,357 --> 00:09:58,756
And for the children,

294
00:09:58,756 --> 00:10:00,887
honey, let them do the crushing.

295
00:10:01,067 --> 00:10:03,124
Give them the bag wrapped in a

296
00:10:03,124 --> 00:10:04,839
towel and a wooden spoon,

297
00:10:04,839 --> 00:10:06,759
and let them whack it on the

298
00:10:06,759 --> 00:10:07,719
kitchen floor.

299
00:10:07,899 --> 00:10:10,327
They'll feel like they made the whole

300
00:10:10,327 --> 00:10:10,721
thing.

301
00:10:10,901 --> 00:10:13,763
My grandson did the crushing every year

302
00:10:13,763 --> 00:10:14,791
from age four,

303
00:10:14,791 --> 00:10:17,433
and now he's twenty-six and he still

304
00:10:17,433 --> 00:10:19,635
calls me in December to ask if

305
00:10:19,635 --> 00:10:21,837
I need my candy canes crushed.

306
00:10:22,187 --> 00:10:23,639
So one more time.

307
00:10:23,819 --> 00:10:25,692
Real chocolate bars,

308
00:10:25,692 --> 00:10:26,628
not chips.

309
00:10:26,808 --> 00:10:28,049
Melt it gently,

310
00:10:28,049 --> 00:10:30,117
thirty seconds at a time.

311
00:10:30,297 --> 00:10:33,119
Dark layer in the icebox only fifteen

312
00:10:33,119 --> 00:10:34,492
or twenty minutes,

313
00:10:34,492 --> 00:10:36,857
until it's set but still tacky.

314
00:10:37,037 --> 00:10:38,781
White chocolate on top,

315
00:10:38,781 --> 00:10:41,360
candy canes pressed in right away,

316
00:10:41,360 --> 00:10:42,877
then an hour to set.

317
00:10:43,057 --> 00:10:44,229
Warm knife.

318
00:10:44,409 --> 00:10:46,999
That's how you make peppermint bark that

319
00:10:46,999 --> 00:10:48,165
never comes apart,

320
00:10:48,165 --> 00:10:50,690
for five dollars instead of thirty-two.

321
00:10:51,040 --> 00:10:52,919
Tell me in the comments,

322
00:10:52,919 --> 00:10:53,780
sweetheart.

323
00:10:53,960 --> 00:10:56,788
Who in your family made the Christmas

324
00:10:56,788 --> 00:10:57,246
candy?

325
00:10:57,426 --> 00:11:00,830
Fudge, divinity, peanut brittle,

326
00:11:00,830 --> 00:11:01,362
bark?

327
00:11:01,542 --> 00:11:03,558
I bet I can guess what your

328
00:11:03,558 --> 00:11:04,827
grandmother made.

329
00:11:05,007 --> 00:11:07,699
Every day I'm bringing you another Christmas

330
00:11:07,699 --> 00:11:09,106
recipe from my kitchen.

331
00:11:09,286 --> 00:11:11,920
And if you want another one tonight,

332
00:11:11,920 --> 00:11:14,993
the whole playlist of Grandma's recipes is

333
00:11:14,993 --> 00:11:16,968
right there on your screen,

334
00:11:16,968 --> 00:11:19,017
and I'll see you in the next

335
00:11:19,017 --> 00:11:19,456
video.

336
00:11:19,636 --> 00:11:21,134
Good night, honey.

337
00:11:21,314 --> 00:11:22,742
Merry Christmas.
oUtH0r-1KCo:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:02,239
Sweetheart, I've been to a lot of

2
00:00:02,239 --> 00:00:04,818
Christmas dinners in eighty-two years.

3
00:00:04,998 --> 00:00:06,450
And I can tell you,

4
00:00:06,450 --> 00:00:09,585
the most beautiful Christmas table I ever

5
00:00:09,585 --> 00:00:12,184
sat at cost less than ten dollars.

6
00:00:12,364 --> 00:00:13,934
It was my mother's,

7
00:00:13,934 --> 00:00:15,751
in nineteen fifty-two,

8
00:00:15,751 --> 00:00:18,395
and it was made of pine branches

9
00:00:18,395 --> 00:00:19,552
from the yard,

10
00:00:19,552 --> 00:00:20,956
a white bedsheet,

11
00:00:20,956 --> 00:00:22,360
and four candles.

12
00:00:22,540 --> 00:00:24,802
People who came to our house that

13
00:00:24,802 --> 00:00:27,544
night talked about that table for years.

14
00:00:27,895 --> 00:00:29,591
And last year I went to a

15
00:00:29,591 --> 00:00:32,305
house where they had spent three hundred

16
00:00:32,305 --> 00:00:34,273
dollars on table decorations,

17
00:00:34,273 --> 00:00:36,445
and it looked like a store shelf

18
00:00:36,445 --> 00:00:37,531
fell over on it.

19
00:00:37,711 --> 00:00:40,357
So tonight I'm giving you nine Christmas

20
00:00:40,357 --> 00:00:42,804
table mistakes that make a table look

21
00:00:42,804 --> 00:00:44,921
cheap, no matter what you spent.

22
00:00:45,101 --> 00:00:46,744
And for every one,

23
00:00:46,744 --> 00:00:49,026
the old way to fix it for

24
00:00:49,026 --> 00:00:50,395
almost nothing.

25
00:00:50,575 --> 00:00:51,933
And stay with me,

26
00:00:51,933 --> 00:00:54,969
because the last mistake is one nobody

27
00:00:54,969 --> 00:00:58,084
thinks about, and it costs five dollars

28
00:00:58,084 --> 00:00:58,644
to fix.

29
00:00:58,994 --> 00:01:00,677
Mistake number one.

30
00:01:00,857 --> 00:01:03,820
A centerpiece so tall that nobody can

31
00:01:03,820 --> 00:01:05,501
see across the table.

32
00:01:05,681 --> 00:01:07,861
Big vases, tall branches,

33
00:01:07,861 --> 00:01:09,605
towers of ornaments.

34
00:01:09,785 --> 00:01:12,212
It looks grand when the table is

35
00:01:12,212 --> 00:01:15,093
empty, but the minute people sit down,

36
00:01:15,093 --> 00:01:17,443
Aunt Carol is talking to a wall

37
00:01:17,443 --> 00:01:18,353
of greenery.

38
00:01:18,533 --> 00:01:21,160
A Christmas table is for faces,

39
00:01:21,160 --> 00:01:21,668
honey.

40
00:01:21,848 --> 00:01:23,636
Not for decorations.

41
00:01:23,986 --> 00:01:24,856
The fix.

42
00:01:25,036 --> 00:01:27,501
Keep everything in the middle lower than

43
00:01:27,501 --> 00:01:29,657
your chin when you're sitting down.

44
00:01:29,837 --> 00:01:31,776
About twelve inches.

45
00:01:31,956 --> 00:01:33,396
My mother's rule was,

46
00:01:33,396 --> 00:01:35,521
put your elbow on the table and

47
00:01:35,521 --> 00:01:37,029
your hand straight up.

48
00:01:37,209 --> 00:01:39,590
Nothing taller than your fingertips.

49
00:01:39,770 --> 00:01:41,604
Go long instead of tall.

50
00:01:41,784 --> 00:01:44,050
A low line of greenery running down

51
00:01:44,050 --> 00:01:45,604
the middle of the table,

52
00:01:45,604 --> 00:01:47,287
from one end to the other.

53
00:01:47,637 --> 00:01:49,436
Mistake number two.

54
00:01:49,616 --> 00:01:51,381
Every color at once.

55
00:01:51,561 --> 00:01:54,021
Red plates, green napkins,

56
00:01:54,021 --> 00:01:56,859
gold chargers, blue ornaments,

57
00:01:56,859 --> 00:02:00,454
silver tinsel, and a plaid tablecloth.

58
00:02:00,634 --> 00:02:02,462
It looks busy and cheap,

59
00:02:02,462 --> 00:02:04,442
like a dollar store aisle.

60
00:02:04,622 --> 00:02:08,390
The tables that look expensive almost always

61
00:02:08,390 --> 00:02:10,102
use only two colors,

62
00:02:10,102 --> 00:02:13,013
maybe three, and lots of green and

63
00:02:13,013 --> 00:02:13,527
white.

64
00:02:13,877 --> 00:02:14,979
Pick two.

65
00:02:15,159 --> 00:02:16,576
Red and white.

66
00:02:16,756 --> 00:02:18,161
Or green and gold.

67
00:02:18,341 --> 00:02:20,245
Or white and silver.

68
00:02:20,425 --> 00:02:22,956
Use what you already have in those

69
00:02:22,956 --> 00:02:25,413
colors, and put the rest away for

70
00:02:25,413 --> 00:02:26,381
another year.

71
00:02:26,561 --> 00:02:29,517
My mother's table was white and green,

72
00:02:29,517 --> 00:02:32,007
with red only in the candles and

73
00:02:32,007 --> 00:02:33,329
a bowl of apples.

74
00:02:33,509 --> 00:02:34,647
That's it.

75
00:02:34,827 --> 00:02:37,411
Three things red on the whole table,

76
00:02:37,411 --> 00:02:39,564
and it looked like a magazine.

77
00:02:39,914 --> 00:02:42,721
And if you want a little sparkle,

78
00:02:42,721 --> 00:02:44,337
use only one metal.

79
00:02:44,517 --> 00:02:46,839
All gold, or all silver.

80
00:02:47,019 --> 00:02:48,401
Not both.

81
00:02:48,581 --> 00:02:51,469
My mother had six brass candlesticks from

82
00:02:51,469 --> 00:02:54,216
Grandma Pearl, and she polished them on

83
00:02:54,216 --> 00:02:57,315
the twenty-third of December every year with

84
00:02:57,315 --> 00:02:59,076
a rag and a jar of paste.

85
00:02:59,256 --> 00:03:02,389
Six gold candlesticks and white candles on

86
00:03:02,389 --> 00:03:04,179
a green and white table.

87
00:03:04,359 --> 00:03:06,448
People thought we were rich.

88
00:03:06,628 --> 00:03:07,993
We were not rich,

89
00:03:07,993 --> 00:03:08,474
honey.

90
00:03:08,825 --> 00:03:10,659
Mistake number three.

91
00:03:10,839 --> 00:03:14,319
The shiny plastic tablecloth with printed holly

92
00:03:14,319 --> 00:03:14,763
on it.

93
00:03:14,943 --> 00:03:17,720
Nothing makes a table look cheaper,

94
00:03:17,720 --> 00:03:18,275
faster.

95
00:03:18,455 --> 00:03:21,346
It wrinkles, it shines under the lights,

96
00:03:21,346 --> 00:03:23,442
and it squeaks when you put a

97
00:03:23,442 --> 00:03:24,237
plate down.

98
00:03:24,417 --> 00:03:25,554
In the fifties,

99
00:03:25,554 --> 00:03:28,586
a plastic tablecloth was for the kitchen

100
00:03:28,586 --> 00:03:29,723
and the picnic.

101
00:03:29,903 --> 00:03:31,865
Never for Christmas dinner.

102
00:03:32,045 --> 00:03:34,336
In a minute I'll show you what

103
00:03:34,336 --> 00:03:36,093
my mother used instead,

104
00:03:36,093 --> 00:03:37,850
and you already own it.

105
00:03:38,200 --> 00:03:40,382
The fix costs nothing.

106
00:03:40,562 --> 00:03:42,955
A plain white flat bedsheet,

107
00:03:42,955 --> 00:03:45,775
ironed, folded under at the ends.

108
00:03:45,955 --> 00:03:48,788
That's exactly what my mother used.

109
00:03:48,968 --> 00:03:51,432
Nobody can tell it's a sheet once

110
00:03:51,432 --> 00:03:52,776
the plates are on.

111
00:03:52,956 --> 00:03:55,211
Or a length of plain burlap or

112
00:03:55,211 --> 00:03:57,766
cotton from the fabric store for a

113
00:03:57,766 --> 00:03:58,668
few dollars.

114
00:03:58,848 --> 00:04:02,397
Plain fabric always looks richer than printed

115
00:04:02,397 --> 00:04:03,028
plastic.

116
00:04:03,208 --> 00:04:04,392
Always.

117
00:04:04,742 --> 00:04:06,471
Mistake number four.

118
00:04:06,651 --> 00:04:09,438
Plastic garland and fake berries.

119
00:04:09,618 --> 00:04:11,488
Real greenery is free,

120
00:04:11,488 --> 00:04:15,227
honey, and nothing smells like Christmas the

121
00:04:15,227 --> 00:04:16,247
way it does.

122
00:04:16,427 --> 00:04:17,718
Go out to the yard,

123
00:04:17,718 --> 00:04:19,688
or ask a neighbor with a pine

124
00:04:19,688 --> 00:04:21,997
tree, or ask at the Christmas tree

125
00:04:21,997 --> 00:04:24,510
lot for the trimmed branches they cut

126
00:04:24,510 --> 00:04:25,529
off the bottom.

127
00:04:25,709 --> 00:04:28,008
Most lots give them away.

128
00:04:28,188 --> 00:04:30,156
Some leave them in a pile by

129
00:04:30,156 --> 00:04:30,858
the fence.

130
00:04:31,209 --> 00:04:33,956
Lay the branches flat down the middle

131
00:04:33,956 --> 00:04:34,921
of the table,

132
00:04:34,921 --> 00:04:36,851
overlapping like shingles.

133
00:04:37,031 --> 00:04:39,283
Tuck in a few sprigs of holly,

134
00:04:39,283 --> 00:04:41,310
or rosemary from the store,

135
00:04:41,310 --> 00:04:43,788
and some pinecones from the yard.

136
00:04:43,968 --> 00:04:45,245
That's your runner.

137
00:04:45,425 --> 00:04:48,009
Mist it with water the night before

138
00:04:48,009 --> 00:04:49,338
so it stays fresh.

139
00:04:49,518 --> 00:04:51,949
And put a towel underneath at the

140
00:04:51,949 --> 00:04:54,454
ends, so the sap doesn't touch the

141
00:04:54,454 --> 00:04:55,265
tablecloth.

142
00:04:55,445 --> 00:04:57,328
If this is helping you,

143
00:04:57,328 --> 00:05:00,112
honey, tap the like button for me.

144
00:05:00,292 --> 00:05:03,055
It helps Grandma more than you know.

145
00:05:03,405 --> 00:05:05,285
Mistake number five.

146
00:05:05,465 --> 00:05:07,729
Eating under the big ceiling light.

147
00:05:07,909 --> 00:05:10,899
That bright white light from above makes

148
00:05:10,899 --> 00:05:12,320
the food look gray,

149
00:05:12,320 --> 00:05:13,815
the table look flat,

150
00:05:13,815 --> 00:05:16,431
and everybody look ten years older.

151
00:05:16,611 --> 00:05:18,608
Your table could be perfect,

152
00:05:18,608 --> 00:05:21,033
and the ceiling light will make it

153
00:05:21,033 --> 00:05:22,602
look like a cafeteria.

154
00:05:22,952 --> 00:05:25,605
Turn off the overhead light at dinner,

155
00:05:25,605 --> 00:05:27,909
and light the table with candles.

156
00:05:28,089 --> 00:05:29,128
Lots of them,

157
00:05:29,128 --> 00:05:31,607
low ones, at different heights.

158
00:05:31,787 --> 00:05:33,917
Plain white candles in jars,

159
00:05:33,917 --> 00:05:36,427
or in glasses from your cupboard,

160
00:05:36,427 --> 00:05:38,405
or in hollowed-out apples.

161
00:05:38,585 --> 00:05:40,962
Then turn on one small lamp in

162
00:05:40,962 --> 00:05:43,101
the corner so nobody trips.

163
00:05:43,281 --> 00:05:46,121
Candlelight makes every table look like it

164
00:05:46,121 --> 00:05:47,135
cost a fortune.

165
00:05:47,315 --> 00:05:49,103
And every face,

166
00:05:49,103 --> 00:05:49,579
too.

167
00:05:49,930 --> 00:05:52,808
But please, no scented candles on the

168
00:05:52,808 --> 00:05:53,819
dinner table.

169
00:05:53,999 --> 00:05:56,728
Cinnamon and vanilla candles fight with the

170
00:05:56,728 --> 00:05:58,887
smell of the turkey and the rolls.

171
00:05:59,067 --> 00:06:00,831
Your nose gets confused,

172
00:06:00,831 --> 00:06:03,111
and the food tastes like a gift

173
00:06:03,111 --> 00:06:03,479
shop.

174
00:06:03,659 --> 00:06:06,372
Save the scented candles for the bathroom

175
00:06:06,372 --> 00:06:07,629
and the front hall.

176
00:06:07,809 --> 00:06:11,199
Plain, unscented white candles on the table.

177
00:06:11,550 --> 00:06:13,924
And put a small vase of greenery

178
00:06:13,924 --> 00:06:16,225
or a jar candle in the bathroom

179
00:06:16,225 --> 00:06:17,413
too, sweetheart.

180
00:06:17,593 --> 00:06:20,478
That's the one room every guest visits

181
00:06:20,478 --> 00:06:22,225
alone, and they notice.

182
00:06:22,405 --> 00:06:24,881
A clean towel folded nice,

183
00:06:24,881 --> 00:06:27,453
a sprig of pine in a glass,

184
00:06:27,453 --> 00:06:28,500
one candle.

185
00:06:28,680 --> 00:06:30,989
My mother said you can tell everything

186
00:06:30,989 --> 00:06:33,115
about a house from the guest towel.

187
00:06:33,295 --> 00:06:35,037
She was a little dramatic.

188
00:06:35,217 --> 00:06:36,622
But she wasn't wrong.

189
00:06:36,972 --> 00:06:39,038
Mistake number six.

190
00:06:39,218 --> 00:06:41,900
Paper napkins with Santa on them.

191
00:06:42,080 --> 00:06:43,955
I understand, honey,

192
00:06:43,955 --> 00:06:45,923
nobody wants to iron.

193
00:06:46,103 --> 00:06:48,255
But a real cloth napkin,

194
00:06:48,255 --> 00:06:49,779
even a cheap one,

195
00:06:49,779 --> 00:06:51,931
changes the whole table.

196
00:06:52,111 --> 00:06:54,923
You can buy plain white cotton napkins

197
00:06:54,923 --> 00:06:56,920
in a pack for a few dollars

198
00:06:56,920 --> 00:06:59,806
and use them every Christmas for twenty

199
00:06:59,806 --> 00:07:00,250
years.

200
00:07:00,430 --> 00:07:02,578
I'll show you my mother's trick.

201
00:07:02,928 --> 00:07:05,414
And here's my mother's trick for making

202
00:07:05,414 --> 00:07:06,561
them look special.

203
00:07:06,741 --> 00:07:08,871
Tie each one with a piece of

204
00:07:08,871 --> 00:07:10,848
red yarn or kitchen twine,

205
00:07:10,848 --> 00:07:13,053
and tuck in a little sprig of

206
00:07:13,053 --> 00:07:14,346
pine or rosemary.

207
00:07:14,526 --> 00:07:16,616
Or a single candy cane.

208
00:07:16,796 --> 00:07:18,630
Lay it right on the plate.

209
00:07:18,810 --> 00:07:21,189
It takes ten minutes for the whole

210
00:07:21,189 --> 00:07:23,568
table, and it looks like you hired

211
00:07:23,568 --> 00:07:24,197
somebody.

212
00:07:24,548 --> 00:07:26,672
Mistake number seven.

213
00:07:26,852 --> 00:07:28,257
Too much stuff.

214
00:07:28,437 --> 00:07:31,096
Decorations, serving dishes,

215
00:07:31,096 --> 00:07:32,615
salt and pepper,

216
00:07:32,615 --> 00:07:36,033
butter, gravy, three kinds of rolls,

217
00:07:36,033 --> 00:07:39,072
and no room for anyone's elbows.

218
00:07:39,252 --> 00:07:41,808
A crowded table looks cluttered,

219
00:07:41,808 --> 00:07:43,884
and cluttered looks cheap.

220
00:07:44,064 --> 00:07:45,585
In my mother's house,

221
00:07:45,585 --> 00:07:48,700
the serving dishes stayed on the sideboard,

222
00:07:48,700 --> 00:07:51,017
and my father carved at the head

223
00:07:51,017 --> 00:07:51,959
of the table.

224
00:07:52,309 --> 00:07:54,660
So clear the decorations to one low

225
00:07:54,660 --> 00:07:56,070
line down the middle.

226
00:07:56,250 --> 00:07:58,475
Put the big serving dishes on the

227
00:07:58,475 --> 00:08:00,565
counter or a side table and let

228
00:08:00,565 --> 00:08:02,183
people serve themselves.

229
00:08:02,363 --> 00:08:03,958
Leave only the bread,

230
00:08:03,958 --> 00:08:06,389
the gravy, and the butter on the

231
00:08:06,389 --> 00:08:06,844
table.

232
00:08:07,024 --> 00:08:09,567
Give each person at least two feet

233
00:08:09,567 --> 00:08:10,240
of space.

234
00:08:10,420 --> 00:08:13,474
A table with breathing room looks generous.

235
00:08:13,824 --> 00:08:15,577
Mistake number eight.

236
00:08:15,757 --> 00:08:18,334
A table with nothing personal on it.

237
00:08:18,514 --> 00:08:21,123
You can buy a beautiful table setting

238
00:08:21,123 --> 00:08:22,040
in any store,

239
00:08:22,040 --> 00:08:24,296
and it will look like any store.

240
00:08:24,476 --> 00:08:26,608
What makes a table yours is one

241
00:08:26,608 --> 00:08:29,427
small thing that tells people they belong

242
00:08:29,427 --> 00:08:29,840
there.

243
00:08:30,020 --> 00:08:31,300
In our house,

244
00:08:31,300 --> 00:08:33,073
it was name cards.

245
00:08:33,253 --> 00:08:36,007
Wait until you see what my mother

246
00:08:36,007 --> 00:08:36,341
did.

247
00:08:36,692 --> 00:08:39,119
My mother wrote each person's name on

248
00:08:39,119 --> 00:08:41,678
a little card in her round handwriting,

249
00:08:41,678 --> 00:08:43,581
and propped it on a walnut or

250
00:08:43,581 --> 00:08:45,155
tucked it in a pinecone.

251
00:08:45,335 --> 00:08:47,279
Or write each name on a paper

252
00:08:47,279 --> 00:08:49,290
tag and tie it to an ornament,

253
00:08:49,290 --> 00:08:51,837
and let people take the ornament home.

254
00:08:52,017 --> 00:08:54,769
My grandchildren still have the little glass

255
00:08:54,769 --> 00:08:57,020
balls with their names in gold paint

256
00:08:57,020 --> 00:08:58,646
from when they were small.

257
00:08:58,996 --> 00:09:00,935
And mistake number nine,

258
00:09:00,935 --> 00:09:03,198
the one nobody thinks about.

259
00:09:03,378 --> 00:09:06,707
A Christmas table should smell like Christmas

260
00:09:06,707 --> 00:09:08,556
before anybody sits down.

261
00:09:08,736 --> 00:09:11,651
My mother's trick cost almost nothing.

262
00:09:11,831 --> 00:09:14,476
She pushed whole cloves into oranges,

263
00:09:14,476 --> 00:09:16,407
in rows or in little stars,

264
00:09:16,407 --> 00:09:18,195
and set them in a bowl in

265
00:09:18,195 --> 00:09:19,911
the middle of the table.

266
00:09:20,091 --> 00:09:21,953
They're called pomanders,

267
00:09:21,953 --> 00:09:24,784
and people have made them for hundreds

268
00:09:24,784 --> 00:09:25,455
of years.

269
00:09:25,805 --> 00:09:28,291
Make them with the children a few

270
00:09:28,291 --> 00:09:29,195
days before.

271
00:09:29,375 --> 00:09:31,855
An orange, a small jar of whole

272
00:09:31,855 --> 00:09:34,734
cloves, and a toothpick to start the

273
00:09:34,734 --> 00:09:35,214
holes.

274
00:09:35,394 --> 00:09:36,949
They smell wonderful,

275
00:09:36,949 --> 00:09:40,057
they look like little Christmas ornaments,

276
00:09:40,057 --> 00:09:42,500
and when the warm room heats them

277
00:09:42,500 --> 00:09:45,312
up, the whole table smells like orange

278
00:09:45,312 --> 00:09:46,052
and spice.

279
00:09:46,232 --> 00:09:48,493
A bag of oranges and a jar

280
00:09:48,493 --> 00:09:50,579
of cloves, five dollars,

281
00:09:50,579 --> 00:09:53,709
and the best centerpiece in America.

282
00:09:54,060 --> 00:09:56,552
And one more piece of advice,

283
00:09:56,552 --> 00:09:58,529
the most practical one.

284
00:09:58,709 --> 00:10:00,985
Set the table the night before.

285
00:10:01,165 --> 00:10:02,460
On Christmas Eve,

286
00:10:02,460 --> 00:10:04,745
after the children are in bed,

287
00:10:04,745 --> 00:10:05,812
lay the cloth,

288
00:10:05,812 --> 00:10:07,792
the branches, the candles,

289
00:10:07,792 --> 00:10:09,849
the plates and the napkins.

290
00:10:10,029 --> 00:10:11,717
Then on Christmas Day,

291
00:10:11,717 --> 00:10:14,096
when the kitchen is a storm and

292
00:10:14,096 --> 00:10:15,554
the turkey is late,

293
00:10:15,554 --> 00:10:18,470
the table is already done and waiting.

294
00:10:18,650 --> 00:10:20,870
My mother never once set a table

295
00:10:20,870 --> 00:10:21,633
in a hurry.

296
00:10:21,984 --> 00:10:25,437
So here is my ten-dollar Christmas table,

297
00:10:25,437 --> 00:10:25,943
honey.

298
00:10:26,123 --> 00:10:27,477
A white sheet,

299
00:10:27,477 --> 00:10:28,154
ironed.

300
00:10:28,334 --> 00:10:31,077
Pine branches from the yard down the

301
00:10:31,077 --> 00:10:31,991
middle, low.

302
00:10:32,171 --> 00:10:35,190
A few pinecones and clove oranges.

303
00:10:35,370 --> 00:10:38,865
Plain white candles in jars and glasses.

304
00:10:39,045 --> 00:10:42,089
Cloth napkins tied with red yarn and

305
00:10:42,089 --> 00:10:43,526
a sprig of green.

306
00:10:43,706 --> 00:10:45,320
A name on every plate.

307
00:10:45,500 --> 00:10:46,684
Two colors.

308
00:10:46,864 --> 00:10:48,861
Overhead light off.

309
00:10:49,041 --> 00:10:49,970
That's all.

310
00:10:50,150 --> 00:10:51,996
It will look like a magazine.

311
00:10:52,346 --> 00:10:54,208
Tell me in the comments,

312
00:10:54,208 --> 00:10:55,062
sweetheart.

313
00:10:55,242 --> 00:10:57,898
What did your family's Christmas table look

314
00:10:57,898 --> 00:10:59,503
like when you were little?

315
00:10:59,683 --> 00:11:01,774
Did you have the good china,

316
00:11:01,774 --> 00:11:02,969
or paper plates?

317
00:11:03,149 --> 00:11:04,972
I read every comment.

318
00:11:05,152 --> 00:11:07,588
And if you want another one tonight,

319
00:11:07,588 --> 00:11:10,701
the whole playlist of Grandma's Christmas tips

320
00:11:10,701 --> 00:11:12,731
is right there on your screen,

321
00:11:12,731 --> 00:11:14,626
and I'll see you in the next

322
00:11:14,626 --> 00:11:15,032
video.

323
00:11:15,212 --> 00:11:16,849
Good night, honey.

324
00:11:17,029 --> 00:11:18,480
Merry Christmas.

1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:02,951
Sweetheart, I'm going to tell you something

2
00:00:02,951 --> 00:00:05,421
my mother would never have believed.

3
00:00:05,601 --> 00:00:08,086
The best chili I make isn't red.

4
00:00:08,266 --> 00:00:09,392
It's white.

5
00:00:09,572 --> 00:00:11,222
Chicken, white beans,

6
00:00:11,222 --> 00:00:14,129
green chiles, and a creamy broth that

7
00:00:14,129 --> 00:00:16,487
tastes like it cooked all day,

8
00:00:16,487 --> 00:00:19,394
and it's ready in forty-five minutes.

9
00:00:19,574 --> 00:00:22,172
My grandson asks for it every single

10
00:00:22,172 --> 00:00:24,481
time he comes home from college,

11
00:00:24,481 --> 00:00:26,935
before he even takes his coat off.

12
00:00:27,284 --> 00:00:29,792
But almost everybody who makes it at

13
00:00:29,792 --> 00:00:31,812
home tells me the same thing.

14
00:00:31,992 --> 00:00:35,162
Grandma, mine tastes like nothing.

15
00:00:35,342 --> 00:00:37,162
It's watery and bland,

16
00:00:37,162 --> 00:00:40,224
like chicken soup that forgot what it

17
00:00:40,224 --> 00:00:40,555
was.

18
00:00:40,735 --> 00:00:43,354
So tonight I'm giving you my white

19
00:00:43,354 --> 00:00:45,819
chicken chili, every ingredient,

20
00:00:45,819 --> 00:00:48,747
every step, and the five mistakes that

21
00:00:48,747 --> 00:00:49,825
make it bland.

22
00:00:50,005 --> 00:00:52,684
One pot, and it feeds six people

23
00:00:52,684 --> 00:00:54,777
for about twelve dollars.

24
00:00:54,957 --> 00:00:56,135
And stay with me,

25
00:00:56,135 --> 00:00:58,559
because the very last thing you add

26
00:00:58,559 --> 00:01:00,707
is the one that wakes the whole

27
00:01:00,707 --> 00:01:01,192
pot up.

28
00:01:01,541 --> 00:01:04,363
Now, I didn't grow up with this.

29
00:01:04,543 --> 00:01:07,105
In Mansfield in the fifties,

30
00:01:07,105 --> 00:01:08,386
chili was red.

31
00:01:08,566 --> 00:01:10,625
Ground beef, kidney beans,

32
00:01:10,625 --> 00:01:12,051
a can of tomatoes,

33
00:01:12,051 --> 00:01:14,270
and a spoon of chili powder,

34
00:01:14,270 --> 00:01:17,993
served on Saturday night with saltine crackers.

35
00:01:18,173 --> 00:01:20,540
My father put a slice of cheese

36
00:01:20,540 --> 00:01:23,061
on top and called it Texas style.

37
00:01:23,241 --> 00:01:25,354
He had never been to Texas.

38
00:01:25,534 --> 00:01:26,927
None of us had.

39
00:01:27,277 --> 00:01:29,915
The white chili came into my kitchen

40
00:01:29,915 --> 00:01:31,748
in nineteen ninety-three,

41
00:01:31,748 --> 00:01:33,507
from my daughter-in-law,

42
00:01:33,507 --> 00:01:35,926
Linda, who grew up in New Mexico.

43
00:01:36,106 --> 00:01:38,447
She made it for a church supper,

44
00:01:38,447 --> 00:01:40,496
and I went back for seconds,

45
00:01:40,496 --> 00:01:41,960
and then for thirds,

46
00:01:41,960 --> 00:01:44,301
and then I went into the kitchen

47
00:01:44,301 --> 00:01:46,569
and stood next to her until she

48
00:01:46,569 --> 00:01:47,960
told me everything.

49
00:01:48,140 --> 00:01:50,206
White chili was all the rage at

50
00:01:50,206 --> 00:01:52,273
church suppers in the nineties.

51
00:01:52,453 --> 00:01:53,974
It still should be.

52
00:01:54,323 --> 00:01:56,718
And I changed a few things over

53
00:01:56,718 --> 00:01:59,652
thirty years, the way grandmothers do.

54
00:01:59,832 --> 00:02:02,191
Linda used chicken breasts,

55
00:02:02,191 --> 00:02:03,675
and I use thighs.

56
00:02:03,855 --> 00:02:06,665
She used water and I use broth.

57
00:02:06,845 --> 00:02:09,226
And I added the one thing that

58
00:02:09,226 --> 00:02:10,258
made her say,

59
00:02:10,258 --> 00:02:12,638
Ruth, that's better than mine.

60
00:02:12,818 --> 00:02:15,024
I'll tell you what it is.

61
00:02:15,204 --> 00:02:17,236
But first, the list.

62
00:02:17,585 --> 00:02:19,166
Here's what you need,

63
00:02:19,166 --> 00:02:19,617
honey.

64
00:02:19,797 --> 00:02:22,804
Two pounds of boneless chicken thighs.

65
00:02:22,984 --> 00:02:24,262
One big onion,

66
00:02:24,262 --> 00:02:24,993
chopped.

67
00:02:25,173 --> 00:02:26,961
Four cloves of garlic.

68
00:02:27,141 --> 00:02:29,932
Two cans of chopped green chiles,

69
00:02:29,932 --> 00:02:31,624
the four-ounce cans,

70
00:02:31,624 --> 00:02:32,639
mild or hot,

71
00:02:32,639 --> 00:02:33,654
your choice.

72
00:02:33,834 --> 00:02:35,980
Three cans of white beans,

73
00:02:35,980 --> 00:02:38,373
great northern or cannellini,

74
00:02:38,373 --> 00:02:39,941
drained and rinsed.

75
00:02:40,121 --> 00:02:42,443
And four cups of chicken broth.

76
00:02:42,792 --> 00:02:43,803
For the seasoning.

77
00:02:43,983 --> 00:02:46,618
Two teaspoons of ground cumin.

78
00:02:46,798 --> 00:02:49,689
One teaspoon of dried oregano.

79
00:02:49,869 --> 00:02:52,214
One teaspoon of chili powder.

80
00:02:52,394 --> 00:02:53,857
Salt and pepper.

81
00:02:54,037 --> 00:02:55,243
And at the end,

82
00:02:55,243 --> 00:02:57,496
four ounces of cream cheese,

83
00:02:57,496 --> 00:02:59,507
half a cup of sour cream,

84
00:02:59,507 --> 00:03:01,276
the juice of one lime,

85
00:03:01,276 --> 00:03:04,011
and a handful of chopped cilantro,

86
00:03:04,011 --> 00:03:05,217
if you like it.

87
00:03:05,397 --> 00:03:08,878
My husband said cilantro tasted like soap,

88
00:03:08,878 --> 00:03:11,365
so half the pot never got any.

89
00:03:11,714 --> 00:03:13,665
Why thighs, sweetheart?

90
00:03:13,845 --> 00:03:17,102
Because chicken breast cooks dry and stringy

91
00:03:17,102 --> 00:03:19,174
in a pot of simmering broth.

92
00:03:19,354 --> 00:03:21,282
Thighs have a little fat,

93
00:03:21,282 --> 00:03:23,673
and they stay tender and juicy,

94
00:03:23,673 --> 00:03:26,064
and they give the broth flavor.

95
00:03:26,244 --> 00:03:27,940
They're cheaper, too.

96
00:03:28,120 --> 00:03:29,791
If you only have breasts,

97
00:03:29,791 --> 00:03:31,865
fine, but take them out as soon

98
00:03:31,865 --> 00:03:34,607
as they're cooked through and shred them,

99
00:03:34,607 --> 00:03:36,212
and don't let them boil.

100
00:03:36,392 --> 00:03:38,485
In a minute I'll tell you my

101
00:03:38,485 --> 00:03:41,252
secret, the one Linda said was better

102
00:03:41,252 --> 00:03:41,999
than hers.

103
00:03:42,349 --> 00:03:44,658
And rinse the canned beans,

104
00:03:44,658 --> 00:03:45,171
honey.

105
00:03:45,351 --> 00:03:48,013
That thick, cloudy liquid in the can

106
00:03:48,013 --> 00:03:49,566
is salty and starchy,

107
00:03:49,566 --> 00:03:52,154
and it makes the chili taste tinny.

108
00:03:52,334 --> 00:03:54,925
Pour them into a colander and run

109
00:03:54,925 --> 00:03:57,752
cold water over them until the water

110
00:03:57,752 --> 00:03:58,615
runs clear.

111
00:03:58,795 --> 00:04:01,320
If you'd rather cook dried beans,

112
00:04:01,320 --> 00:04:04,227
a pound of dried great northern beans,

113
00:04:04,227 --> 00:04:07,133
soaked overnight, is about the same as

114
00:04:07,133 --> 00:04:09,581
three cans, and it costs half as

115
00:04:09,581 --> 00:04:09,964
much.

116
00:04:10,313 --> 00:04:11,231
Step one.

117
00:04:11,411 --> 00:04:14,000
Salt and pepper the chicken thighs.

118
00:04:14,180 --> 00:04:15,942
Heat a spoon of oil in a

119
00:04:15,942 --> 00:04:18,292
big heavy pot until it shimmers,

120
00:04:18,292 --> 00:04:19,908
and lay the thighs in,

121
00:04:19,908 --> 00:04:20,275
flat.

122
00:04:20,455 --> 00:04:22,959
Let them brown for four minutes on

123
00:04:22,959 --> 00:04:25,169
each side without moving them.

124
00:04:25,349 --> 00:04:27,404
They don't need to cook through.

125
00:04:27,584 --> 00:04:29,673
You just want a golden crust.

126
00:04:29,853 --> 00:04:32,975
That brown crust is mistake number one,

127
00:04:32,975 --> 00:04:35,136
the flavor everybody skips.

128
00:04:35,485 --> 00:04:36,600
Step two.

129
00:04:36,780 --> 00:04:38,742
Take the chicken out and put it

130
00:04:38,742 --> 00:04:39,439
on a plate.

131
00:04:39,619 --> 00:04:41,617
Put the onion in the same pot,

132
00:04:41,617 --> 00:04:43,216
in all that chicken fat,

133
00:04:43,216 --> 00:04:45,015
and cook it for five or six

134
00:04:45,015 --> 00:04:47,614
minutes until it's soft and starting to

135
00:04:47,614 --> 00:04:48,280
turn gold.

136
00:04:48,460 --> 00:04:50,700
Then the garlic for one minute.

137
00:04:50,880 --> 00:04:53,014
Scrape up the brown bits stuck to

138
00:04:53,014 --> 00:04:54,823
the bottom of the pot with a

139
00:04:54,823 --> 00:04:55,664
wooden spoon.

140
00:04:55,844 --> 00:04:58,119
Those bits are pure flavor.

141
00:04:58,299 --> 00:05:00,042
If this is helping you,

142
00:05:00,042 --> 00:05:02,618
honey, tap the like button for me.

143
00:05:02,798 --> 00:05:05,445
It helps Grandma more than you know.

144
00:05:05,796 --> 00:05:08,171
Step three, and this is the one

145
00:05:08,171 --> 00:05:10,010
that changes everything.

146
00:05:10,190 --> 00:05:11,308
Add the cumin,

147
00:05:11,308 --> 00:05:14,424
oregano and chili powder right into the

148
00:05:14,424 --> 00:05:15,942
onions and the fat,

149
00:05:15,942 --> 00:05:18,738
and stir them for one minute before

150
00:05:18,738 --> 00:05:20,256
any liquid goes in.

151
00:05:20,436 --> 00:05:22,723
The heat wakes up the spices.

152
00:05:22,903 --> 00:05:25,527
You'll smell it the second it happens.

153
00:05:25,707 --> 00:05:29,445
Spices dumped into broth just float there,

154
00:05:29,445 --> 00:05:30,780
dusty and flat.

155
00:05:30,960 --> 00:05:32,367
Toasted in fat,

156
00:05:32,367 --> 00:05:33,398
they bloom.

157
00:05:33,749 --> 00:05:34,793
Step four.

158
00:05:34,973 --> 00:05:37,013
Pour in the broth and the green

159
00:05:37,013 --> 00:05:38,921
chiles, with all their juice.

160
00:05:39,101 --> 00:05:41,005
Put the chicken back in.

161
00:05:41,185 --> 00:05:42,558
Bring it to a boil,

162
00:05:42,558 --> 00:05:44,872
turn it down to a gentle simmer,

163
00:05:44,872 --> 00:05:47,113
and cook it with the lid tilted

164
00:05:47,113 --> 00:05:48,847
for twenty-five minutes.

165
00:05:49,027 --> 00:05:51,065
Then take the chicken out,

166
00:05:51,065 --> 00:05:53,651
pull it apart with two forks into

167
00:05:53,651 --> 00:05:56,551
bite-sized shreds, and put it back in

168
00:05:56,551 --> 00:05:57,178
the pot.

169
00:05:57,528 --> 00:05:59,352
Step five, my secret,

170
00:05:59,352 --> 00:06:02,306
the one Linda said was better than

171
00:06:02,306 --> 00:06:02,740
hers.

172
00:06:02,920 --> 00:06:04,116
Add the beans.

173
00:06:04,296 --> 00:06:06,551
Then take one cup of the beans

174
00:06:06,551 --> 00:06:07,603
and broth out,

175
00:06:07,603 --> 00:06:09,406
mash it with a fork or a

176
00:06:09,406 --> 00:06:12,337
potato masher until it's a thick paste,

177
00:06:12,337 --> 00:06:13,840
and stir it back in.

178
00:06:14,020 --> 00:06:16,908
That mashed bean thickens the chili like

179
00:06:16,908 --> 00:06:19,869
nothing else, and makes it creamy without

180
00:06:19,869 --> 00:06:20,591
any flour.

181
00:06:20,771 --> 00:06:22,605
Simmer ten more minutes.

182
00:06:22,956 --> 00:06:24,128
Step six.

183
00:06:24,308 --> 00:06:25,806
Turn off the heat.

184
00:06:25,986 --> 00:06:28,705
Cut the cream cheese into cubes and

185
00:06:28,705 --> 00:06:30,725
stir it in until it melts,

186
00:06:30,725 --> 00:06:32,278
then the sour cream.

187
00:06:32,458 --> 00:06:35,178
Don't let it boil after the cream

188
00:06:35,178 --> 00:06:37,486
goes in, or it can separate.

189
00:06:37,666 --> 00:06:40,266
Then squeeze in the lime juice.

190
00:06:40,446 --> 00:06:41,479
Taste it.

191
00:06:41,659 --> 00:06:43,610
Add salt until it's right.

192
00:06:43,790 --> 00:06:46,147
Most people are afraid of salt,

193
00:06:46,147 --> 00:06:49,036
and it's the reason their chili tastes

194
00:06:49,036 --> 00:06:50,024
like nothing.

195
00:06:50,204 --> 00:06:53,455
But first, the shortcut for busy nights.

196
00:06:53,806 --> 00:06:55,564
If you're in a hurry on a

197
00:06:55,564 --> 00:06:58,589
weeknight, sweetheart, here's the shortcut.

198
00:06:58,769 --> 00:07:01,432
Use a store rotisserie chicken,

199
00:07:01,432 --> 00:07:03,065
pulled into shreds.

200
00:07:03,245 --> 00:07:05,691
Brown the onions in a spoon of

201
00:07:05,691 --> 00:07:07,729
butter, toast the spices,

202
00:07:07,729 --> 00:07:09,768
add the broth and chiles,

203
00:07:09,768 --> 00:07:11,643
simmer fifteen minutes,

204
00:07:11,643 --> 00:07:13,844
then the chicken and beans.

205
00:07:14,024 --> 00:07:15,973
You lose a little of the brown

206
00:07:15,973 --> 00:07:18,377
flavor, but you'll have supper on the

207
00:07:18,377 --> 00:07:19,936
table in thirty minutes,

208
00:07:19,936 --> 00:07:22,209
and it's still better than any can.

209
00:07:22,560 --> 00:07:24,393
So the five mistakes,

210
00:07:24,393 --> 00:07:24,916
honey.

211
00:07:25,096 --> 00:07:28,105
Mistake one, putting raw chicken straight in

212
00:07:28,105 --> 00:07:30,019
the broth, with no browning.

213
00:07:30,199 --> 00:07:33,104
Mistake two, dumping the spices into the

214
00:07:33,104 --> 00:07:35,864
liquid instead of toasting them in the

215
00:07:35,864 --> 00:07:36,155
fat.

216
00:07:36,335 --> 00:07:39,946
Mistake three, using water instead of broth.

217
00:07:40,126 --> 00:07:41,995
Water makes watery chili.

218
00:07:42,175 --> 00:07:44,009
It's right there in the name.

219
00:07:44,360 --> 00:07:47,192
Mistake four, forgetting the acid.

220
00:07:47,372 --> 00:07:49,649
A squeeze of lime at the very

221
00:07:49,649 --> 00:07:52,084
end is what makes all the other

222
00:07:52,084 --> 00:07:53,340
flavors wake up.

223
00:07:53,520 --> 00:07:56,599
Without it, white chili tastes heavy and

224
00:07:56,599 --> 00:07:57,061
muddy.

225
00:07:57,241 --> 00:07:59,203
If you don't have a lime,

226
00:07:59,203 --> 00:08:01,637
a spoon of vinegar or the juice

227
00:08:01,637 --> 00:08:04,149
from a jar of pickled jalapenos.

228
00:08:04,329 --> 00:08:05,902
And mistake five,

229
00:08:05,902 --> 00:08:07,382
too little salt.

230
00:08:07,562 --> 00:08:09,750
Taste, salt, stir,

231
00:08:09,750 --> 00:08:11,208
taste again.

232
00:08:11,558 --> 00:08:13,462
And if it's too thin,

233
00:08:13,462 --> 00:08:14,913
don't add flour.

234
00:08:15,093 --> 00:08:16,287
Mash more beans,

235
00:08:16,287 --> 00:08:18,453
or let it simmer with the lid

236
00:08:18,453 --> 00:08:19,946
off for ten minutes.

237
00:08:20,126 --> 00:08:21,838
If it's too thick,

238
00:08:21,838 --> 00:08:23,551
a splash of broth.

239
00:08:23,731 --> 00:08:26,204
And if it isn't spicy enough for

240
00:08:26,204 --> 00:08:29,295
your family, a chopped jalapeno with the

241
00:08:29,295 --> 00:08:31,614
onions, or a pinch of cayenne.

242
00:08:31,794 --> 00:08:35,221
My grandson puts hot sauce on everything,

243
00:08:35,221 --> 00:08:37,144
including my apple pie,

244
00:08:37,144 --> 00:08:38,899
so I gave up arguing.

245
00:08:39,079 --> 00:08:41,448
Now, the best part is coming up.

246
00:08:41,628 --> 00:08:42,835
The toppings.

247
00:08:43,185 --> 00:08:44,884
Serve it in deep bowls,

248
00:08:44,884 --> 00:08:47,248
with whatever toppings you have.

249
00:08:47,428 --> 00:08:49,866
Shredded Monterey Jack cheese,

250
00:08:49,866 --> 00:08:51,654
a spoon of sour cream,

251
00:08:51,654 --> 00:08:53,279
sliced green onions,

252
00:08:53,279 --> 00:08:56,693
avocado, crushed tortilla chips on top for

253
00:08:56,693 --> 00:08:57,262
crunch.

254
00:08:57,442 --> 00:08:59,657
Put the toppings in little bowls in

255
00:08:59,657 --> 00:09:01,618
the middle of the table and let

256
00:09:01,618 --> 00:09:03,200
everybody make their own.

257
00:09:03,380 --> 00:09:05,662
Children eat twice as much when they

258
00:09:05,662 --> 00:09:07,374
get to build it themselves.

259
00:09:07,724 --> 00:09:09,788
And make a pan of cornbread to

260
00:09:09,788 --> 00:09:10,545
go with it.

261
00:09:10,725 --> 00:09:12,828
Or do what my father would have

262
00:09:12,828 --> 00:09:15,678
done and crumble saltine crackers right on

263
00:09:15,678 --> 00:09:15,949
top.

264
00:09:16,129 --> 00:09:18,419
White chili freezes beautifully,

265
00:09:18,419 --> 00:09:20,422
so I make a double batch and

266
00:09:20,422 --> 00:09:22,712
freeze half in quart containers.

267
00:09:22,892 --> 00:09:25,616
Then on a cold Tuesday in January,

268
00:09:25,616 --> 00:09:27,780
it's dinner in ten minutes.

269
00:09:27,960 --> 00:09:30,363
Freeze it before you add the cream

270
00:09:30,363 --> 00:09:31,917
cheese and sour cream,

271
00:09:31,917 --> 00:09:34,037
and stir them in when you warm

272
00:09:34,037 --> 00:09:34,461
it up.

273
00:09:34,812 --> 00:09:37,193
It keeps four days in the icebox

274
00:09:37,193 --> 00:09:39,871
and tastes even better the next day,

275
00:09:39,871 --> 00:09:42,252
when the spices have had time to

276
00:09:42,252 --> 00:09:42,997
settle in.

277
00:09:43,177 --> 00:09:45,746
And it's the perfect thing to bring

278
00:09:45,746 --> 00:09:47,801
to a family with a new baby,

279
00:09:47,801 --> 00:09:49,783
or someone who's been sick.

280
00:09:49,963 --> 00:09:51,290
A pot of chili,

281
00:09:51,290 --> 00:09:52,972
a pan of cornbread,

282
00:09:52,972 --> 00:09:54,653
and a bag of chips.

283
00:09:54,833 --> 00:09:56,609
They'll eat for three days.

284
00:09:56,959 --> 00:09:59,516
Linda taught me one more thing about

285
00:09:59,516 --> 00:10:01,789
this chili, and I'll pass it on.

286
00:10:01,969 --> 00:10:04,690
Make it on Saturday afternoon while the

287
00:10:04,690 --> 00:10:05,736
football is on,

288
00:10:05,736 --> 00:10:07,759
and leave the pot on the back

289
00:10:07,759 --> 00:10:09,782
burner on low with a ladle in

290
00:10:09,782 --> 00:10:09,992
it.

291
00:10:10,172 --> 00:10:12,952
People wander in all afternoon and help

292
00:10:12,952 --> 00:10:13,736
themselves.

293
00:10:13,916 --> 00:10:16,306
Nobody has to sit down at a

294
00:10:16,306 --> 00:10:17,457
certain time.

295
00:10:17,637 --> 00:10:19,842
It's the most relaxed meal in my

296
00:10:19,842 --> 00:10:20,876
whole cookbook.

297
00:10:21,226 --> 00:10:22,728
So one more time,

298
00:10:22,728 --> 00:10:23,258
honey.

299
00:10:23,438 --> 00:10:26,201
Chicken thighs, browned hard.

300
00:10:26,381 --> 00:10:28,460
Onions in the chicken fat.

301
00:10:28,640 --> 00:10:31,542
Toast the spices before the broth.

302
00:10:31,722 --> 00:10:33,905
Green chiles with their juice.

303
00:10:34,085 --> 00:10:35,548
Simmer and shred.

304
00:10:35,728 --> 00:10:37,702
Mash a cup of beans to make

305
00:10:37,702 --> 00:10:38,433
it creamy.

306
00:10:38,613 --> 00:10:40,681
Cream cheese off the heat,

307
00:10:40,681 --> 00:10:43,305
then a squeeze of lime and plenty

308
00:10:43,305 --> 00:10:43,942
of salt.

309
00:10:44,122 --> 00:10:46,528
That's my white chicken chili,

310
00:10:46,528 --> 00:10:49,416
and nobody has ever called it bland.

311
00:10:49,765 --> 00:10:51,652
Tell me in the comments,

312
00:10:51,652 --> 00:10:52,517
sweetheart.

313
00:10:52,697 --> 00:10:55,077
Red chili or white chili?

314
00:10:55,257 --> 00:10:57,614
And beans or no beans?

315
00:10:57,794 --> 00:10:59,985
I know that one starts fights,

316
00:10:59,985 --> 00:11:01,811
so be nice to each other.

317
00:11:01,991 --> 00:11:04,814
Every day I'm bringing you another recipe

318
00:11:04,814 --> 00:11:05,915
from my kitchen.

319
00:11:06,095 --> 00:11:08,711
And if you want another one tonight,

320
00:11:08,711 --> 00:11:11,763
the whole playlist of Grandma's recipes is

321
00:11:11,763 --> 00:11:13,725
right there on your screen,

322
00:11:13,725 --> 00:11:15,760
and I'll see you in the next

323
00:11:15,760 --> 00:11:16,196
video.

324
00:11:16,376 --> 00:11:17,897
Good night, honey.
