1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:03,160
Sweetheart, every Christmas Eve in my house,

2
00:00:03,160 --> 00:00:05,890
there's a big blue enamel roasting pan

3
00:00:05,890 --> 00:00:07,542
on the kitchen counter,

4
00:00:07,542 --> 00:00:10,057
full to the top with homemade party

5
00:00:10,057 --> 00:00:10,344
mix.

6
00:00:10,524 --> 00:00:12,275
Crunchy cereal, nuts,

7
00:00:12,275 --> 00:00:16,444
pretzels, all toasted in butter and Worcestershire

8
00:00:16,444 --> 00:00:16,944
sauce.

9
00:00:17,124 --> 00:00:18,826
By midnight it's empty,

10
00:00:18,826 --> 00:00:21,934
and the grandchildren are licking the salt

11
00:00:21,934 --> 00:00:23,266
off their fingers.

12
00:00:23,446 --> 00:00:25,629
That pan has been on my counter

13
00:00:25,629 --> 00:00:28,798
every Christmas Eve since nineteen sixty-one.

14
00:00:29,148 --> 00:00:31,733
But today, most people make it in

15
00:00:31,733 --> 00:00:34,474
the microwave, or they buy the bags

16
00:00:34,474 --> 00:00:35,492
at the store,

17
00:00:35,492 --> 00:00:37,371
and it comes out greasy,

18
00:00:37,371 --> 00:00:39,720
or soggy, or so salty you need

19
00:00:39,720 --> 00:00:41,130
a gallon of water.

20
00:00:41,310 --> 00:00:43,727
So tonight I'm giving you the old

21
00:00:43,727 --> 00:00:44,387
oven way.

22
00:00:44,567 --> 00:00:46,950
Every ingredient, every step,

23
00:00:46,950 --> 00:00:49,991
and the four mistakes that make party

24
00:00:49,991 --> 00:00:50,813
mix soggy.

25
00:00:50,993 --> 00:00:53,880
It's the best Christmas snack there is,

26
00:00:53,880 --> 00:00:56,693
and the easiest gift you'll ever give.

27
00:00:56,873 --> 00:00:58,218
And stay with me,

28
00:00:58,218 --> 00:01:01,777
because the step almost everybody skips comes

29
00:01:01,777 --> 00:01:02,963
after the oven,

30
00:01:02,963 --> 00:01:05,732
and it's the one that matters most.

31
00:01:06,081 --> 00:01:08,880
This recipe came from the back of

32
00:01:08,880 --> 00:01:09,982
a cereal box.

33
00:01:10,162 --> 00:01:12,484
In the early nineteen fifties,

34
00:01:12,484 --> 00:01:15,658
the company that made Chex cereal started

35
00:01:15,658 --> 00:01:18,289
printing a party mix recipe on its

36
00:01:18,289 --> 00:01:21,231
boxes, and every mother in America cut

37
00:01:21,231 --> 00:01:21,772
it out.

38
00:01:21,952 --> 00:01:24,345
My mother taped hers to the inside

39
00:01:24,345 --> 00:01:25,823
of the cupboard door,

40
00:01:25,823 --> 00:01:27,723
next to the measuring cups.

41
00:01:27,903 --> 00:01:30,554
It stayed there until the tape turned

42
00:01:30,554 --> 00:01:32,919
brown and the paper fell apart in

43
00:01:32,919 --> 00:01:34,137
nineteen seventy.

44
00:01:34,487 --> 00:01:35,643
In the fifties,

45
00:01:35,643 --> 00:01:37,878
it was the snack for company.

46
00:01:38,058 --> 00:01:40,642
When the neighbors came over to watch

47
00:01:40,642 --> 00:01:43,506
Perry Como's Christmas show on our little

48
00:01:43,506 --> 00:01:45,391
black and white television,

49
00:01:45,391 --> 00:01:47,557
my mother brought out a bowl of

50
00:01:47,557 --> 00:01:50,001
party mix and a bottle of Coca-Cola

51
00:01:50,001 --> 00:01:51,188
for each of them.

52
00:01:51,368 --> 00:01:53,408
Danny and I sat on the floor

53
00:01:53,408 --> 00:01:55,230
with our own little bowl,

54
00:01:55,230 --> 00:01:57,415
and we picked out all the nuts

55
00:01:57,415 --> 00:01:59,310
first and left the cereal.

56
00:01:59,659 --> 00:02:01,492
I made my first batch as a

57
00:02:01,492 --> 00:02:03,888
young bride in nineteen sixty-one,

58
00:02:03,888 --> 00:02:06,707
for my husband's office Christmas party.

59
00:02:06,887 --> 00:02:08,420
I forgot to stir it,

60
00:02:08,420 --> 00:02:10,567
and the bottom burned black.

61
00:02:10,747 --> 00:02:13,059
I scraped the top half into a

62
00:02:13,059 --> 00:02:14,973
bowl and took it anyway.

63
00:02:15,153 --> 00:02:17,853
His boss ate three handfuls and asked

64
00:02:17,853 --> 00:02:18,729
who made it.

65
00:02:18,909 --> 00:02:20,299
From that day on,

66
00:02:20,299 --> 00:02:22,914
I never forgot to stir it again.

67
00:02:23,264 --> 00:02:25,095
Here's what you need,

68
00:02:25,095 --> 00:02:27,885
honey, for one big roasting pan.

69
00:02:28,065 --> 00:02:30,572
Three cups each of corn Chex,

70
00:02:30,572 --> 00:02:32,732
rice Chex and wheat Chex.

71
00:02:32,912 --> 00:02:35,165
That's nine cups of cereal.

72
00:02:35,345 --> 00:02:36,995
One cup of mixed nuts,

73
00:02:36,995 --> 00:02:40,221
or peanuts if you're watching your pennies.

74
00:02:40,401 --> 00:02:42,746
One cup of small pretzels.

75
00:02:42,926 --> 00:02:45,355
And one cup of bagel chips or

76
00:02:45,355 --> 00:02:49,207
plain crackers, broken into bite-sized pieces.

77
00:02:49,387 --> 00:02:53,112
Any store brand cereal squares work just

78
00:02:53,112 --> 00:02:53,857
as well.

79
00:02:54,206 --> 00:02:55,576
For the butter coating.

80
00:02:55,756 --> 00:02:57,986
Six tablespoons of butter.

81
00:02:58,166 --> 00:03:01,173
Two tablespoons of Worcestershire sauce.

82
00:03:01,353 --> 00:03:04,625
One and a half teaspoons of seasoned

83
00:03:04,625 --> 00:03:05,079
salt.

84
00:03:05,259 --> 00:03:08,053
Three quarters of a teaspoon of garlic

85
00:03:08,053 --> 00:03:08,568
powder.

86
00:03:08,748 --> 00:03:11,326
Half a teaspoon of onion powder.

87
00:03:11,506 --> 00:03:12,434
That's it.

88
00:03:12,614 --> 00:03:15,087
My mother added a pinch of cayenne

89
00:03:15,087 --> 00:03:16,105
for my father,

90
00:03:16,105 --> 00:03:17,850
and I still do it for my

91
00:03:17,850 --> 00:03:18,141
son.

92
00:03:18,321 --> 00:03:20,341
In a minute I'll show you the

93
00:03:20,341 --> 00:03:22,849
oven trick that keeps it crunchy for

94
00:03:22,849 --> 00:03:23,267
weeks.

95
00:03:23,617 --> 00:03:25,605
A word about the nuts,

96
00:03:25,605 --> 00:03:26,147
honey.

97
00:03:26,327 --> 00:03:27,835
Mixed nuts are best,

98
00:03:27,835 --> 00:03:30,775
but they're the most expensive thing in

99
00:03:30,775 --> 00:03:31,378
the pan.

100
00:03:31,558 --> 00:03:34,486
Plain dry-roasted peanuts are half the price

101
00:03:34,486 --> 00:03:37,015
and taste wonderful toasted in butter.

102
00:03:37,195 --> 00:03:39,646
My mother used peanuts every year,

103
00:03:39,646 --> 00:03:42,025
and only on Christmas Eve did she

104
00:03:42,025 --> 00:03:44,044
splurge on a can of cashews.

105
00:03:44,224 --> 00:03:46,635
She'd pick them out herself and put

106
00:03:46,635 --> 00:03:48,702
them in a little dish just for

107
00:03:48,702 --> 00:03:49,391
my father.

108
00:03:49,740 --> 00:03:50,681
Step one.

109
00:03:50,861 --> 00:03:53,455
Heat the oven to two hundred fifty

110
00:03:53,455 --> 00:03:54,065
degrees.

111
00:03:54,245 --> 00:03:56,012
That's low, sweetheart,

112
00:03:56,012 --> 00:03:57,856
and it's supposed to be.

113
00:03:58,036 --> 00:03:59,966
Party mix isn't baked,

114
00:03:59,966 --> 00:04:02,599
it's dried and toasted slowly.

115
00:04:02,779 --> 00:04:05,969
High heat burns the outside before the

116
00:04:05,969 --> 00:04:07,481
inside gets crisp.

117
00:04:07,661 --> 00:04:09,677
Low heat dries it all the way

118
00:04:09,677 --> 00:04:12,527
through, and that's what makes it crunchy

119
00:04:12,527 --> 00:04:13,222
for weeks.

120
00:04:13,572 --> 00:04:14,628
Step two.

121
00:04:14,808 --> 00:04:15,973
Put the cereal,

122
00:04:15,973 --> 00:04:18,848
nuts, pretzels and bagel chips in the

123
00:04:18,848 --> 00:04:21,101
biggest roasting pan you own.

124
00:04:21,281 --> 00:04:22,178
A big pan,

125
00:04:22,178 --> 00:04:23,882
so it's spread out,

126
00:04:23,882 --> 00:04:26,215
no deeper than two inches.

127
00:04:26,395 --> 00:04:28,173
If your pan is small,

128
00:04:28,173 --> 00:04:29,274
use two pans.

129
00:04:29,454 --> 00:04:31,869
A pile that's too deep steams in

130
00:04:31,869 --> 00:04:34,586
the middle, and steamed party mix is

131
00:04:34,586 --> 00:04:35,793
soggy party mix.

132
00:04:36,144 --> 00:04:37,386
Step three.

133
00:04:37,566 --> 00:04:39,830
Melt the butter in a small pot

134
00:04:39,830 --> 00:04:41,339
or in the microwave.

135
00:04:41,519 --> 00:04:43,632
Stir in the Worcestershire,

136
00:04:43,632 --> 00:04:47,231
seasoned salt, garlic powder and onion powder.

137
00:04:47,411 --> 00:04:49,923
Now pour it slowly over the mix,

138
00:04:49,923 --> 00:04:51,415
a little at a time,

139
00:04:51,415 --> 00:04:54,633
while you stir and turn everything gently

140
00:04:54,633 --> 00:04:55,968
with a big spoon.

141
00:04:56,148 --> 00:04:58,077
Pour, stir, pour,

142
00:04:58,077 --> 00:04:58,644
stir.

143
00:04:58,824 --> 00:05:01,552
Every piece should get a little shine.

144
00:05:01,732 --> 00:05:02,661
Not a soak.

145
00:05:02,841 --> 00:05:03,793
A shine.

146
00:05:03,973 --> 00:05:05,566
If this is helping you,

147
00:05:05,566 --> 00:05:07,920
honey, tap the like button for me.

148
00:05:08,100 --> 00:05:10,655
It helps Grandma more than you know.

149
00:05:11,005 --> 00:05:12,096
Step four.

150
00:05:12,276 --> 00:05:13,622
Bake for one hour,

151
00:05:13,622 --> 00:05:16,165
and stir it every fifteen minutes.

152
00:05:16,345 --> 00:05:17,388
Set a timer,

153
00:05:17,388 --> 00:05:20,084
honey, because you will forget.

154
00:05:20,264 --> 00:05:21,205
When you stir,

155
00:05:21,205 --> 00:05:23,624
bring the pieces from the bottom and

156
00:05:23,624 --> 00:05:25,372
the corners up to the top.

157
00:05:25,552 --> 00:05:27,688
The corners brown fastest.

158
00:05:27,868 --> 00:05:29,726
Four stirs in one hour.

159
00:05:29,906 --> 00:05:32,814
That's how you get every piece golden

160
00:05:32,814 --> 00:05:35,644
and crisp, and no burned bottom like

161
00:05:35,644 --> 00:05:37,766
mine in nineteen sixty-one.

162
00:05:38,116 --> 00:05:40,679
Step five, and this is the one

163
00:05:40,679 --> 00:05:42,643
almost everybody skips.

164
00:05:42,823 --> 00:05:45,175
When it comes out of the oven,

165
00:05:45,175 --> 00:05:47,683
spread it out on paper towels or

166
00:05:47,683 --> 00:05:49,643
brown paper grocery bags,

167
00:05:49,643 --> 00:05:51,916
cut open flat on the counter,

168
00:05:51,916 --> 00:05:54,033
and let it cool completely,

169
00:05:54,033 --> 00:05:55,130
about an hour.

170
00:05:55,310 --> 00:05:58,022
The paper soaks up any extra butter,

171
00:05:58,022 --> 00:06:00,809
and the mix finishes getting crisp as

172
00:06:00,809 --> 00:06:01,487
it cools.

173
00:06:01,667 --> 00:06:03,430
If you put it in a tin

174
00:06:03,430 --> 00:06:05,994
warm, the steam turns it soft by

175
00:06:05,994 --> 00:06:06,636
morning.

176
00:06:06,986 --> 00:06:08,495
How do you know it's done?

177
00:06:08,675 --> 00:06:10,902
Take out one piece of the corn

178
00:06:10,902 --> 00:06:13,277
cereal, let it cool for a minute

179
00:06:13,277 --> 00:06:14,390
on the counter,

180
00:06:14,390 --> 00:06:15,281
and bite it.

181
00:06:15,461 --> 00:06:18,876
It should snap clean and taste toasty,

182
00:06:18,876 --> 00:06:20,674
with no chew at all.

183
00:06:20,854 --> 00:06:22,997
If it bends or feels a little

184
00:06:22,997 --> 00:06:25,732
tough, give the whole pan another ten

185
00:06:25,732 --> 00:06:27,506
minutes and check again.

186
00:06:27,686 --> 00:06:29,672
Humid days take longer.

187
00:06:29,852 --> 00:06:32,128
My kitchen in July and my kitchen

188
00:06:32,128 --> 00:06:34,612
in December are two different ovens.

189
00:06:34,962 --> 00:06:36,523
So the four mistakes,

190
00:06:36,523 --> 00:06:37,342
sweetheart.

191
00:06:37,522 --> 00:06:40,180
Mistake one, the microwave.

192
00:06:40,360 --> 00:06:42,739
Yes, it's on the box now,

193
00:06:42,739 --> 00:06:44,737
and yes, it's faster.

194
00:06:44,917 --> 00:06:47,678
But the microwave cooks it unevenly,

195
00:06:47,678 --> 00:06:49,059
some pieces chewy,

196
00:06:49,059 --> 00:06:49,979
some burned.

197
00:06:50,159 --> 00:06:52,530
The oven at two-fifty is the only

198
00:06:52,530 --> 00:06:54,757
way to get every piece crunchy.

199
00:06:54,937 --> 00:06:57,561
Mistake two, too much butter.

200
00:06:57,741 --> 00:07:00,086
More butter doesn't make it better.

201
00:07:00,266 --> 00:07:01,909
It makes it greasy,

202
00:07:01,909 --> 00:07:03,726
and greasy goes soft.

203
00:07:03,906 --> 00:07:06,764
And wait until you hear mistake three,

204
00:07:06,764 --> 00:07:09,397
because I see it every single year.

205
00:07:09,747 --> 00:07:13,322
Mistake three, a pan that's too crowded.

206
00:07:13,502 --> 00:07:14,746
Spread it thin,

207
00:07:14,746 --> 00:07:17,067
use two pans if you have to.

208
00:07:17,247 --> 00:07:18,506
And mistake four,

209
00:07:18,506 --> 00:07:19,691
storing it warm,

210
00:07:19,691 --> 00:07:22,506
or in a container that isn't airtight.

211
00:07:22,686 --> 00:07:24,235
Cool it all the way,

212
00:07:24,235 --> 00:07:26,792
then into tins or jars with tight

213
00:07:26,792 --> 00:07:27,179
lids.

214
00:07:27,359 --> 00:07:30,265
Done right, it stays crunchy for two

215
00:07:30,265 --> 00:07:30,749
weeks.

216
00:07:30,929 --> 00:07:33,200
In my house it never lasts two

217
00:07:33,200 --> 00:07:34,714
weeks, but it could.

218
00:07:35,064 --> 00:07:37,308
And if a batch does go soft

219
00:07:37,308 --> 00:07:38,222
in the tin,

220
00:07:38,222 --> 00:07:39,885
don't throw it away,

221
00:07:39,885 --> 00:07:40,799
sweetheart.

222
00:07:40,979 --> 00:07:43,005
Spread it on a baking sheet and

223
00:07:43,005 --> 00:07:44,835
put it back in a two hundred

224
00:07:44,835 --> 00:07:47,318
fifty degree oven for fifteen minutes.

225
00:07:47,498 --> 00:07:50,110
Let it cool flat on paper again,

226
00:07:50,110 --> 00:07:52,966
and it comes right back to crunchy.

227
00:07:53,146 --> 00:07:55,792
I've rescued more than one batch the

228
00:07:55,792 --> 00:07:57,849
morning of a party that way,

229
00:07:57,849 --> 00:07:59,392
and nobody ever knew.

230
00:07:59,743 --> 00:08:01,381
Now, for Christmas,

231
00:08:01,381 --> 00:08:03,708
here's what I do to make it

232
00:08:03,708 --> 00:08:04,398
festive.

233
00:08:04,578 --> 00:08:06,633
After it's completely cool,

234
00:08:06,633 --> 00:08:08,308
I stir in a cup of red

235
00:08:08,308 --> 00:08:11,885
and green candy-coated chocolates and a handful

236
00:08:11,885 --> 00:08:13,483
of mini marshmallows.

237
00:08:13,663 --> 00:08:15,695
Sweet and salty together.

238
00:08:15,875 --> 00:08:18,841
Never add the chocolate while it's warm,

239
00:08:18,841 --> 00:08:21,436
or you'll have a melted brown mess.

240
00:08:21,616 --> 00:08:25,148
The grandchildren call this one Grandma's Christmas

241
00:08:25,148 --> 00:08:25,633
crunch.

242
00:08:25,983 --> 00:08:28,394
Or make a sweet version for people

243
00:08:28,394 --> 00:08:29,884
who don't like salty.

244
00:08:30,064 --> 00:08:32,829
Instead of the Worcestershire and garlic,

245
00:08:32,829 --> 00:08:35,122
melt the butter with a quarter cup

246
00:08:35,122 --> 00:08:37,281
of brown sugar and a teaspoon of

247
00:08:37,281 --> 00:08:39,642
cinnamon, and bake it the same way.

248
00:08:39,822 --> 00:08:41,397
Then when it's cool,

249
00:08:41,397 --> 00:08:44,705
drizzle melted white chocolate over it and

250
00:08:44,705 --> 00:08:46,753
toss in dried cranberries.

251
00:08:46,933 --> 00:08:49,255
It tastes like Christmas morning.

252
00:08:49,435 --> 00:08:51,942
Coming up, the reason I make three

253
00:08:51,942 --> 00:08:53,638
batches every December.

254
00:08:53,988 --> 00:08:56,638
And this is why I love party

255
00:08:56,638 --> 00:08:57,680
mix, honey.

256
00:08:57,860 --> 00:09:00,815
One batch costs about ten dollars and

257
00:09:00,815 --> 00:09:02,492
fills six quart jars.

258
00:09:02,672 --> 00:09:04,518
Put it in a clear jar with

259
00:09:04,518 --> 00:09:06,507
a red ribbon around the lid,

260
00:09:06,507 --> 00:09:08,566
or in a cellophane bag with a

261
00:09:08,566 --> 00:09:09,348
little tag.

262
00:09:09,528 --> 00:09:12,056
It doesn't break in the mail like

263
00:09:12,056 --> 00:09:14,815
cookies, it doesn't melt like candy,

264
00:09:14,815 --> 00:09:16,041
and men love it.

265
00:09:16,221 --> 00:09:18,530
Every man in my family gets a

266
00:09:18,530 --> 00:09:20,918
jar of party mix at Christmas,

267
00:09:20,918 --> 00:09:23,147
and not one of them has ever

268
00:09:23,147 --> 00:09:24,023
complained.

269
00:09:24,373 --> 00:09:26,569
I make mine the second week of

270
00:09:26,569 --> 00:09:29,863
December, three big batches in one afternoon,

271
00:09:29,863 --> 00:09:31,327
one after the other.

272
00:09:31,507 --> 00:09:34,401
The whole house smells like toasted butter

273
00:09:34,401 --> 00:09:35,710
and Worcestershire.

274
00:09:35,890 --> 00:09:37,985
Then I fill the jars on the

275
00:09:37,985 --> 00:09:40,314
kitchen table, write the tags,

276
00:09:40,314 --> 00:09:42,565
and give them to the mailman,

277
00:09:42,565 --> 00:09:43,651
the paper boy,

278
00:09:43,651 --> 00:09:45,126
my doctor's nurses,

279
00:09:45,126 --> 00:09:47,610
and every one of my neighbors on

280
00:09:47,610 --> 00:09:48,463
the street.

281
00:09:48,814 --> 00:09:50,211
And for the children,

282
00:09:50,211 --> 00:09:52,142
give them a bowl and let them

283
00:09:52,142 --> 00:09:54,471
each make their own mix from little

284
00:09:54,471 --> 00:09:55,803
bowls of everything.

285
00:09:55,983 --> 00:09:58,540
Cereal, pretzels, nuts,

286
00:09:58,540 --> 00:10:00,987
candies, marshmallows.

287
00:10:01,167 --> 00:10:03,219
They scoop what they like into a

288
00:10:03,219 --> 00:10:05,079
bag and tie it with a ribbon.

289
00:10:05,259 --> 00:10:07,430
Then they give it to their teacher.

290
00:10:07,610 --> 00:10:11,105
My great-granddaughter made eleven bags last year

291
00:10:11,105 --> 00:10:13,030
and gave one to the man who

292
00:10:13,030 --> 00:10:14,600
drives her school bus.

293
00:10:14,950 --> 00:10:16,505
So one more time.

294
00:10:16,685 --> 00:10:19,608
Nine cups of cereal and three cups

295
00:10:19,608 --> 00:10:22,014
of nuts, pretzels and chips.

296
00:10:22,194 --> 00:10:25,707
Six tablespoons of butter with Worcestershire,

297
00:10:25,707 --> 00:10:28,150
seasoned salt, garlic and onion.

298
00:10:28,330 --> 00:10:29,810
Pour it slowly,

299
00:10:29,810 --> 00:10:31,093
just a shine.

300
00:10:31,273 --> 00:10:34,132
Two hundred fifty degrees for one hour,

301
00:10:34,132 --> 00:10:36,405
stirring every fifteen minutes.

302
00:10:36,585 --> 00:10:38,391
Cool it flat on paper,

303
00:10:38,391 --> 00:10:40,114
then into tight jars.

304
00:10:40,294 --> 00:10:42,595
That's the party mix that's been on

305
00:10:42,595 --> 00:10:45,554
my counter every Christmas Eve for sixty-five

306
00:10:45,554 --> 00:10:45,948
years.

307
00:10:46,299 --> 00:10:48,337
Tell me in the comments,

308
00:10:48,337 --> 00:10:49,271
sweetheart.

309
00:10:49,451 --> 00:10:51,637
What do you pick out first,

310
00:10:51,637 --> 00:10:53,499
the nuts, the pretzels,

311
00:10:53,499 --> 00:10:55,441
or the little rye chips?

312
00:10:55,621 --> 00:10:57,806
Everybody has a favorite piece,

313
00:10:57,806 --> 00:11:00,906
and everybody leaves something at the bottom

314
00:11:00,906 --> 00:11:01,752
of the bowl.

315
00:11:01,932 --> 00:11:04,798
Every day I'm bringing you another Christmas

316
00:11:04,798 --> 00:11:06,297
recipe from my kitchen.

317
00:11:06,477 --> 00:11:08,931
And if you want another one tonight,

318
00:11:08,931 --> 00:11:11,793
the whole playlist of Grandma's recipes is

319
00:11:11,793 --> 00:11:13,633
right there on your screen,

320
00:11:13,633 --> 00:11:15,542
and I'll see you in the next

321
00:11:15,542 --> 00:11:15,951
video.

322
00:11:16,131 --> 00:11:17,791
Good night, honey.

323
00:11:17,971 --> 00:11:19,469
Merry Christmas.

1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:04,179
Sweetheart, I have decorated eighty-one Christmas trees

2
00:00:04,179 --> 00:00:05,015
in my life.

3
00:00:05,195 --> 00:00:06,391
I counted.

4
00:00:06,571 --> 00:00:08,370
The first one I remember,

5
00:00:08,370 --> 00:00:09,953
I was three years old,

6
00:00:09,953 --> 00:00:12,040
and my father lifted me up to

7
00:00:12,040 --> 00:00:13,479
put the star on top.

8
00:00:13,659 --> 00:00:15,233
And in all those years,

9
00:00:15,233 --> 00:00:17,834
I've learned that a beautiful tree has

10
00:00:17,834 --> 00:00:20,161
almost nothing to do with how much

11
00:00:20,161 --> 00:00:20,845
you spend.

12
00:00:21,025 --> 00:00:23,183
It has to do with seven little

13
00:00:23,183 --> 00:00:25,843
mistakes that almost everybody makes.

14
00:00:26,194 --> 00:00:29,297
Every year people send me pictures of

15
00:00:29,297 --> 00:00:30,303
their trees.

16
00:00:30,483 --> 00:00:33,583
Grandma, why does mine look thin?

17
00:00:33,763 --> 00:00:35,377
Why does it look cheap?

18
00:00:35,557 --> 00:00:37,302
Why does it look like a lamp

19
00:00:37,302 --> 00:00:39,296
post with things hanging off it?

20
00:00:39,476 --> 00:00:42,092
So tonight I'm giving you the seven

21
00:00:42,092 --> 00:00:43,886
Christmas tree mistakes,

22
00:00:43,886 --> 00:00:45,231
and for every one,

23
00:00:45,231 --> 00:00:47,324
the old trick that fixes it.

24
00:00:47,504 --> 00:00:49,781
Do these before you hang a single

25
00:00:49,781 --> 00:00:51,091
ornament this year.

26
00:00:51,271 --> 00:00:52,596
And stay with me,

27
00:00:52,596 --> 00:00:55,556
because the last one isn't about looks

28
00:00:55,556 --> 00:00:56,101
at all.

29
00:00:56,281 --> 00:00:58,847
It's about keeping your family safe.

30
00:00:59,197 --> 00:01:02,331
First, the question everybody asks me.

31
00:01:02,511 --> 00:01:04,485
When should you put up the tree?

32
00:01:04,665 --> 00:01:06,990
When I was a girl in Mansfield,

33
00:01:06,990 --> 00:01:09,616
nobody had a tree before the middle

34
00:01:09,616 --> 00:01:10,516
of December.

35
00:01:10,696 --> 00:01:12,878
Real trees dried out in a warm

36
00:01:12,878 --> 00:01:15,351
house, and they were a fire danger

37
00:01:15,351 --> 00:01:17,024
with the old hot bulbs.

38
00:01:17,204 --> 00:01:19,652
Most families put the tree up a

39
00:01:19,652 --> 00:01:21,942
week or two before Christmas,

40
00:01:21,942 --> 00:01:24,232
and some, like Grandma Pearl,

41
00:01:24,232 --> 00:01:26,364
waited until Christmas Eve.

42
00:01:26,714 --> 00:01:29,731
Today, with artificial trees and cool little

43
00:01:29,731 --> 00:01:32,269
lights, lots of families put the tree

44
00:01:32,269 --> 00:01:34,601
up the weekend after Thanksgiving,

45
00:01:34,601 --> 00:01:37,070
and there's nothing wrong with that.

46
00:01:37,250 --> 00:01:39,003
My rule is simple.

47
00:01:39,183 --> 00:01:42,727
Artificial tree, the day after Thanksgiving if

48
00:01:42,727 --> 00:01:43,420
you want.

49
00:01:43,600 --> 00:01:44,456
A real tree,

50
00:01:44,456 --> 00:01:47,024
no earlier than the first weekend of

51
00:01:47,024 --> 00:01:49,805
December, so it's still fresh and green

52
00:01:49,805 --> 00:01:51,303
on Christmas morning,

53
00:01:51,303 --> 00:01:53,942
and not dropping needles all over the

54
00:01:53,942 --> 00:01:54,583
presents.

55
00:01:54,934 --> 00:01:56,440
Mistake number one,

56
00:01:56,440 --> 00:01:59,613
and it's the biggest one with artificial

57
00:01:59,613 --> 00:02:00,088
trees.

58
00:02:00,268 --> 00:02:02,347
Not fluffing the branches.

59
00:02:02,527 --> 00:02:04,575
When the tree comes out of the

60
00:02:04,575 --> 00:02:07,238
box, the branches are flat and squished

61
00:02:07,238 --> 00:02:09,423
from eleven months in the attic.

62
00:02:09,603 --> 00:02:12,061
People bend them down and start hanging

63
00:02:12,061 --> 00:02:14,520
ornaments, and the tree looks thin with

64
00:02:14,520 --> 00:02:16,789
big holes you can see right through.

65
00:02:17,139 --> 00:02:19,136
The fix takes about an hour,

66
00:02:19,136 --> 00:02:21,133
and it's worth every minute.

67
00:02:21,313 --> 00:02:22,747
Start at the bottom,

68
00:02:22,747 --> 00:02:24,682
and work on one branch at a

69
00:02:24,682 --> 00:02:25,040
time.

70
00:02:25,220 --> 00:02:27,382
Pull every little tip out,

71
00:02:27,382 --> 00:02:28,962
some up, some down,

72
00:02:28,962 --> 00:02:30,458
some to the sides,

73
00:02:30,458 --> 00:02:32,952
like fingers on a spread hand.

74
00:02:33,132 --> 00:02:35,217
Work from the inside of the branch

75
00:02:35,217 --> 00:02:37,057
near the trunk out to the tip.

76
00:02:37,237 --> 00:02:38,595
Put on gloves.

77
00:02:38,775 --> 00:02:41,916
Those plastic needles are sharper than they

78
00:02:41,916 --> 00:02:42,281
look.

79
00:02:42,632 --> 00:02:44,187
Mistake number two.

80
00:02:44,367 --> 00:02:45,621
Too few lights.

81
00:02:45,801 --> 00:02:48,190
One string of a hundred lights on

82
00:02:48,190 --> 00:02:50,650
a seven-foot tree looks like a few

83
00:02:50,650 --> 00:02:52,605
fireflies lost in the dark.

84
00:02:52,785 --> 00:02:55,385
The old decorators' rule is about one

85
00:02:55,385 --> 00:02:58,056
hundred lights for every foot of tree.

86
00:02:58,236 --> 00:03:00,991
So a seven-foot tree wants about seven

87
00:03:00,991 --> 00:03:02,078
hundred lights.

88
00:03:02,258 --> 00:03:04,146
That sounds like a lot,

89
00:03:04,146 --> 00:03:04,638
honey.

90
00:03:04,818 --> 00:03:06,850
Hang them, and you'll see.

91
00:03:07,030 --> 00:03:08,974
In a minute I'll show you how

92
00:03:08,974 --> 00:03:10,985
to hang them so the tree glows

93
00:03:10,985 --> 00:03:12,057
from the inside.

94
00:03:12,408 --> 00:03:14,673
And mix your bulbs right,

95
00:03:14,673 --> 00:03:15,217
honey.

96
00:03:15,397 --> 00:03:17,928
Don't put warm white lights and cold

97
00:03:17,928 --> 00:03:20,389
blue-white lights on the same tree.

98
00:03:20,569 --> 00:03:22,926
The cold ones look like a hospital

99
00:03:22,926 --> 00:03:25,004
hallway next to the warm ones.

100
00:03:25,184 --> 00:03:27,698
Pick one color of white and stick

101
00:03:27,698 --> 00:03:28,308
with it.

102
00:03:28,488 --> 00:03:31,151
For the old-fashioned look I love,

103
00:03:31,151 --> 00:03:34,049
warm white, the color of candlelight.

104
00:03:34,229 --> 00:03:36,899
If you love the colored lights like

105
00:03:36,899 --> 00:03:38,120
I had as a girl,

106
00:03:38,120 --> 00:03:39,264
go all colored,

107
00:03:39,264 --> 00:03:40,103
and go big.

108
00:03:40,454 --> 00:03:42,299
Mistake number three.

109
00:03:42,479 --> 00:03:45,139
Wrapping the lights around the outside of

110
00:03:45,139 --> 00:03:47,344
the tree like a candy cane stripe.

111
00:03:47,524 --> 00:03:49,647
That's how most people do it,

112
00:03:49,647 --> 00:03:52,064
and it's why the tree looks flat.

113
00:03:52,244 --> 00:03:54,407
The light sits on the surface,

114
00:03:54,407 --> 00:03:56,498
and the inside of the tree is

115
00:03:56,498 --> 00:03:57,364
a dark hole.

116
00:03:57,544 --> 00:04:00,096
A tree that glows from the inside

117
00:04:00,096 --> 00:04:02,339
looks deep and full and rich.

118
00:04:02,689 --> 00:04:03,606
The fix.

119
00:04:03,786 --> 00:04:05,701
Work branch by branch.

120
00:04:05,881 --> 00:04:07,098
Start at the trunk,

121
00:04:07,098 --> 00:04:09,148
run the string out along the top

122
00:04:09,148 --> 00:04:10,622
of a branch to the tip,

123
00:04:10,622 --> 00:04:12,671
then back to the trunk along the

124
00:04:12,671 --> 00:04:15,042
underside, and on to the next branch.

125
00:04:15,222 --> 00:04:16,441
In and out,

126
00:04:16,441 --> 00:04:17,660
in and out.

127
00:04:17,840 --> 00:04:18,918
It takes longer,

128
00:04:18,918 --> 00:04:22,017
and it's the single biggest difference between

129
00:04:22,017 --> 00:04:23,971
a tree that looks cheap and a

130
00:04:23,971 --> 00:04:26,598
tree that looks like a department store

131
00:04:26,598 --> 00:04:27,070
window.

132
00:04:27,420 --> 00:04:29,977
And always check the lights before they

133
00:04:29,977 --> 00:04:30,961
go on the tree.

134
00:04:31,141 --> 00:04:33,479
Plug in every string on the floor

135
00:04:33,479 --> 00:04:33,904
first.

136
00:04:34,084 --> 00:04:36,951
There's nothing worse than finishing the whole

137
00:04:36,951 --> 00:04:39,133
tree and finding one string dead in

138
00:04:39,133 --> 00:04:39,819
the middle.

139
00:04:39,999 --> 00:04:41,787
My father had a ritual.

140
00:04:41,967 --> 00:04:44,326
He laid all the strings out across

141
00:04:44,326 --> 00:04:46,547
the living room rug on the first

142
00:04:46,547 --> 00:04:49,115
Saturday, plugged them in one by one,

143
00:04:49,115 --> 00:04:52,098
and replaced every burned-out bulb before a

144
00:04:52,098 --> 00:04:54,041
single one went on the tree.

145
00:04:54,221 --> 00:04:55,889
If this is helping you,

146
00:04:55,889 --> 00:04:58,355
honey, tap the like button for me.

147
00:04:58,535 --> 00:05:01,251
It helps Grandma more than you know.

148
00:05:01,602 --> 00:05:03,262
Mistake number four.

149
00:05:03,442 --> 00:05:05,485
Decorating in the wrong order.

150
00:05:05,665 --> 00:05:07,308
People put on ornaments,

151
00:05:07,308 --> 00:05:09,088
then remember the garland,

152
00:05:09,088 --> 00:05:11,210
and they have to wrap it around

153
00:05:11,210 --> 00:05:12,921
and knock everything off.

154
00:05:13,101 --> 00:05:15,379
The order is always the same,

155
00:05:15,379 --> 00:05:18,441
and it hasn't changed since my mother's

156
00:05:18,441 --> 00:05:18,755
day.

157
00:05:18,935 --> 00:05:20,352
Lights first.

158
00:05:20,532 --> 00:05:22,297
Then garland or ribbon.

159
00:05:22,477 --> 00:05:24,265
Then the big ornaments,

160
00:05:24,265 --> 00:05:25,820
then the small ones.

161
00:05:26,000 --> 00:05:28,377
And the topper goes on before the

162
00:05:28,377 --> 00:05:29,890
ornaments, not after.

163
00:05:30,240 --> 00:05:31,969
Why the topper early?

164
00:05:32,149 --> 00:05:34,304
Because you need to reach the very

165
00:05:34,304 --> 00:05:36,395
top, and you'll be leaning on the

166
00:05:36,395 --> 00:05:38,233
step ladder against the tree.

167
00:05:38,413 --> 00:05:40,708
If the ornaments are already on,

168
00:05:40,708 --> 00:05:42,860
you'll knock half of them off.

169
00:05:43,040 --> 00:05:45,447
My father learned that the hard way

170
00:05:45,447 --> 00:05:47,098
in nineteen fifty-three,

171
00:05:47,098 --> 00:05:49,849
when the ladder slipped and eleven glass

172
00:05:49,849 --> 00:05:51,225
balls hit the floor.

173
00:05:51,405 --> 00:05:53,959
My mother didn't speak to him until

174
00:05:53,959 --> 00:05:54,470
supper.

175
00:05:54,820 --> 00:05:56,596
Mistake number five.

176
00:05:56,776 --> 00:05:59,414
Every ornament hung on the very tips

177
00:05:59,414 --> 00:06:00,586
of the branches,

178
00:06:00,586 --> 00:06:02,198
all in a single layer.

179
00:06:02,378 --> 00:06:03,450
It looks flat,

180
00:06:03,450 --> 00:06:05,211
and the branches droop.

181
00:06:05,391 --> 00:06:08,572
Here's the trick the window decorators use.

182
00:06:08,752 --> 00:06:10,468
Hang some of your big,

183
00:06:10,468 --> 00:06:13,899
plain, cheap ornaments deep inside the tree,

184
00:06:13,899 --> 00:06:15,381
close to the trunk.

185
00:06:15,561 --> 00:06:18,167
They catch the light from inside and

186
00:06:18,167 --> 00:06:19,253
fill the holes.

187
00:06:19,433 --> 00:06:22,397
Then you'll see why the special ones

188
00:06:22,397 --> 00:06:23,055
go last.

189
00:06:23,406 --> 00:06:25,854
Then the medium ones in the middle,

190
00:06:25,854 --> 00:06:27,743
and your special ornaments,

191
00:06:27,743 --> 00:06:30,121
the pretty glass ones and the ones

192
00:06:30,121 --> 00:06:32,780
with memories, out near the tips where

193
00:06:32,780 --> 00:06:34,389
everybody can see them.

194
00:06:34,569 --> 00:06:36,528
Big ones on the bottom,

195
00:06:36,528 --> 00:06:38,062
small ones on top,

196
00:06:38,062 --> 00:06:40,362
so the tree looks balanced.

197
00:06:40,542 --> 00:06:43,143
And hang them in clusters of three

198
00:06:43,143 --> 00:06:44,443
of the same kind,

199
00:06:44,443 --> 00:06:47,044
not spaced evenly like polka dots.

200
00:06:47,394 --> 00:06:50,373
And here's something for the families with

201
00:06:50,373 --> 00:06:51,863
little ones and pets.

202
00:06:52,043 --> 00:06:54,677
Keep the glass and the heirloom ornaments

203
00:06:54,677 --> 00:06:56,476
on the top half of the tree,

204
00:06:56,476 --> 00:06:58,725
and put the unbreakable ones on the

205
00:06:58,725 --> 00:06:59,752
bottom two feet.

206
00:06:59,932 --> 00:07:01,989
Wooden ones, felt ones,

207
00:07:01,989 --> 00:07:05,296
the ones the children made at school.

208
00:07:05,476 --> 00:07:07,785
The cat will bat at them and

209
00:07:07,785 --> 00:07:10,093
the baby will pull them off,

210
00:07:10,093 --> 00:07:11,989
and nothing will break,

211
00:07:11,989 --> 00:07:13,638
and nobody will cry.

212
00:07:13,988 --> 00:07:15,845
Mistake number six.

213
00:07:16,025 --> 00:07:18,389
A tree topper that's too small,

214
00:07:18,389 --> 00:07:19,380
or too heavy.

215
00:07:19,560 --> 00:07:21,426
A tiny star on a big tree

216
00:07:21,426 --> 00:07:24,112
looks like a forgotten afterthought.

217
00:07:24,292 --> 00:07:26,457
And a big heavy angel makes the

218
00:07:26,457 --> 00:07:28,552
top bend over like it's tired.

219
00:07:28,732 --> 00:07:31,027
The topper should be about one tenth

220
00:07:31,027 --> 00:07:32,493
the height of the tree,

221
00:07:32,493 --> 00:07:34,788
and light enough that the top stands

222
00:07:34,788 --> 00:07:35,362
straight.

223
00:07:35,712 --> 00:07:38,066
If the top branch won't hold your

224
00:07:38,066 --> 00:07:40,634
topper up, here's my mother's trick.

225
00:07:40,814 --> 00:07:43,138
Tie a pencil or a wooden chopstick

226
00:07:43,138 --> 00:07:45,051
to the top of the trunk with

227
00:07:45,051 --> 00:07:47,238
a piece of wire or florist tape,

228
00:07:47,238 --> 00:07:48,947
so it sticks up straight,

229
00:07:48,947 --> 00:07:51,066
and slide the topper over that.

230
00:07:51,246 --> 00:07:53,486
It stands straight all season.

231
00:07:53,666 --> 00:07:56,164
And if you want a fuller look,

232
00:07:56,164 --> 00:07:58,661
tuck a few sprays of ribbon or

233
00:07:58,661 --> 00:08:00,493
picks behind the star,

234
00:08:00,493 --> 00:08:01,492
fanning out.

235
00:08:01,842 --> 00:08:03,798
And mistake number seven,

236
00:08:03,798 --> 00:08:04,971
for real trees,

237
00:08:04,971 --> 00:08:07,240
and this one is about safety.

238
00:08:07,420 --> 00:08:08,918
Forgetting the water.

239
00:08:09,098 --> 00:08:11,634
A fresh-cut tree can drink a gallon

240
00:08:11,634 --> 00:08:13,301
of water the first day.

241
00:08:13,481 --> 00:08:16,024
If the stand runs dry even once,

242
00:08:16,024 --> 00:08:18,567
the cut end seals over with sap,

243
00:08:18,567 --> 00:08:21,190
and the tree can't drink anymore.

244
00:08:21,370 --> 00:08:22,553
It dries out,

245
00:08:22,553 --> 00:08:24,100
the needles drop,

246
00:08:24,100 --> 00:08:26,466
and a dry tree burns fast.

247
00:08:26,646 --> 00:08:28,512
I'll show you how to keep that

248
00:08:28,512 --> 00:08:29,444
from happening.

249
00:08:29,795 --> 00:08:31,409
So when you buy the tree,

250
00:08:31,409 --> 00:08:33,218
ask them to cut half an inch

251
00:08:33,218 --> 00:08:35,026
off the bottom of the trunk,

252
00:08:35,026 --> 00:08:36,834
and put it in water within a

253
00:08:36,834 --> 00:08:37,480
few hours.

254
00:08:37,660 --> 00:08:40,290
Check the stand every single day,

255
00:08:40,290 --> 00:08:41,724
morning and night.

256
00:08:41,904 --> 00:08:44,545
Keep the tree away from the fireplace,

257
00:08:44,545 --> 00:08:46,908
the heater vents and the radiator.

258
00:08:47,088 --> 00:08:49,605
And always turn off the lights when

259
00:08:49,605 --> 00:08:51,474
you go to bed or leave the

260
00:08:51,474 --> 00:08:51,906
house.

261
00:08:52,086 --> 00:08:55,114
My father checked the water every morning

262
00:08:55,114 --> 00:08:56,443
before his coffee,

263
00:08:56,443 --> 00:08:57,403
without fail.

264
00:08:57,754 --> 00:08:59,116
And one last thing,

265
00:08:59,116 --> 00:09:01,625
the touch that makes the whole room

266
00:09:01,625 --> 00:09:03,059
feel like Christmas.

267
00:09:03,239 --> 00:09:04,309
A tree skirt,

268
00:09:04,309 --> 00:09:05,626
or an old quilt,

269
00:09:05,626 --> 00:09:08,506
or a white sheet bunched around the

270
00:09:08,506 --> 00:09:10,728
bottom, to cover the stand.

271
00:09:10,908 --> 00:09:13,038
A bare metal stand at the bottom

272
00:09:13,038 --> 00:09:14,969
of a beautiful tree is like a

273
00:09:14,969 --> 00:09:17,166
beautiful dress with muddy shoes.

274
00:09:17,346 --> 00:09:19,641
My mother used a white sheet with

275
00:09:19,641 --> 00:09:21,310
cotton batting for snow,

276
00:09:21,310 --> 00:09:23,883
and a little wooden train set running

277
00:09:23,883 --> 00:09:24,718
in a circle.

278
00:09:25,068 --> 00:09:27,381
Then turn off every other light in

279
00:09:27,381 --> 00:09:29,559
the room, sit down on the couch,

280
00:09:29,559 --> 00:09:31,600
and look at it from across the

281
00:09:31,600 --> 00:09:31,941
room.

282
00:09:32,121 --> 00:09:33,560
Squint your eyes.

283
00:09:33,740 --> 00:09:35,110
Any dark spots,

284
00:09:35,110 --> 00:09:37,119
you'll see right away.

285
00:09:37,299 --> 00:09:38,751
Move a few lights,

286
00:09:38,751 --> 00:09:40,445
move a few ornaments.

287
00:09:40,625 --> 00:09:42,600
That's what my mother did,

288
00:09:42,600 --> 00:09:45,258
every year, with her cup of coffee.

289
00:09:45,438 --> 00:09:46,695
Then she'd say,

290
00:09:46,695 --> 00:09:48,874
there, now it's Christmas.

291
00:09:49,224 --> 00:09:50,930
So, one more time.

292
00:09:51,110 --> 00:09:52,678
Fluff every branch.

293
00:09:52,858 --> 00:09:55,191
A hundred lights for every foot.

294
00:09:55,371 --> 00:09:57,371
Wrap them in and out of each

295
00:09:57,371 --> 00:09:59,586
branch, not around the outside.

296
00:09:59,766 --> 00:10:02,373
Lights, garland, topper,

297
00:10:02,373 --> 00:10:04,003
then ornaments.

298
00:10:04,183 --> 00:10:06,292
Plain ones deep inside,

299
00:10:06,292 --> 00:10:08,584
special ones on the tips,

300
00:10:08,584 --> 00:10:09,501
in threes.

301
00:10:09,681 --> 00:10:11,898
A topper one tenth the height.

302
00:10:12,078 --> 00:10:13,925
And for a real tree,

303
00:10:13,925 --> 00:10:16,049
water every single day.

304
00:10:16,229 --> 00:10:18,216
That's how you get a tree that

305
00:10:18,216 --> 00:10:19,607
looks like a picture.

306
00:10:19,958 --> 00:10:21,980
Tell me in the comments,

307
00:10:21,980 --> 00:10:22,907
sweetheart.

308
00:10:23,087 --> 00:10:25,211
What's on top of your tree?

309
00:10:25,391 --> 00:10:27,313
A star, an angel,

310
00:10:27,313 --> 00:10:27,992
a bow?

311
00:10:28,172 --> 00:10:30,352
And who in your family gets to

312
00:10:30,352 --> 00:10:31,515
put it up there?

313
00:10:31,695 --> 00:10:34,272
In my house it's always the youngest

314
00:10:34,272 --> 00:10:35,631
child who can walk.

315
00:10:35,811 --> 00:10:38,342
And if you want another one tonight,

316
00:10:38,342 --> 00:10:41,576
the whole playlist of Grandma's Christmas tips

317
00:10:41,576 --> 00:10:43,684
is right there on your screen,

318
00:10:43,684 --> 00:10:45,653
and I'll see you in the next

319
00:10:45,653 --> 00:10:46,074
video.

320
00:10:46,254 --> 00:10:47,950
Good night, honey.

321
00:10:48,130 --> 00:10:49,697
Merry Christmas.

45

00:01:39,110 --> 00:01:40,472

52

53
00:01:42,255 --> 00:01:45,421
Real tinsel, hung one strand at a

54
00:01:45,421 --> 00:01:45,901
time.

55
00:01:46,081 --> 00:01:47,856

56
00:01:47,856 --> 00:01:48,786

57
00:01:48,966 --> 00:01:51,315

58
00:01:51,315 --> 00:01:52,692

00:01:52,692 --> 00:01:55,769

60
00:01:55,949 --> 00:01:57,552

61
00:01:57,732 --> 00:02:00,177
And on New Year's Day she took

62
00:02:00,177 --> 00:02:01,074

63
00:02:01,074 --> 00:02:02,459

67

Number four.

68

The aluminum tree,

69

with the color wheel.

70

In nineteen sixty,

00:02:25,504 --> 00:02:27,250

My mother thought it was the ugliest

79
00:02:32,771 --> 00:02:34,409

00:02:34,589 --> 00:02:36,896

81
00:02:36,896 --> 00:02:37,434

00:02:37,783 --> 00:02:39,165
Number five.

83
00:02:39,345 --> 00:02:40,239
Plaid.

00:02:40,419 --> 00:02:42,713
Red tartan ribbon on the wreath,

00:02:42,713 --> 00:02:45,294

00:02:45,294 --> 00:02:47,373

89
00:02:51,968 --> 00:02:54,589

90
00:02:54,769 --> 00:02:57,178

00:02:57,178 --> 00:02:59,662

96

00:03:13,465 --> 00:03:15,884

00:03:16,922 --> 00:03:18,969
Go to the thrift store for an

00:03:31,279 --> 00:03:32,510
Number six.

107
00:03:32,690 --> 00:03:35,302
Felt ornaments, made by hand.

108

My mother cut little stockings,

109
00:03:37,876 --> 00:03:40,733

00:03:40,733 --> 00:03:42,277

00:03:42,277 --> 00:03:43,744

00:03:43,744 --> 00:03:46,446

00:03:46,446 --> 00:03:48,068

114
00:03:48,248 --> 00:03:50,859
The children's hands made them crooked,

115
00:03:50,859 --> 00:03:52,868

116
00:03:53,048 --> 00:03:54,656
Get a pack of felt and an

00:03:59,995 --> 00:04:00,316

00:04:00,666 --> 00:04:03,035

00:04:08,218 --> 00:04:10,413

124
00:04:10,593 --> 00:04:12,513
In a minute I'll tell you the

125
00:04:12,513 --> 00:04:15,161

126
00:04:15,161 --> 00:04:17,545

127
00:04:17,545 --> 00:04:17,942

00:04:18,292 --> 00:04:19,535
Number seven.

129
00:04:19,715 --> 00:04:22,431
Popcorn and cranberry garland.

130
00:04:22,611 --> 00:04:24,714
My mother popped a big pot of

131
00:04:24,714 --> 00:04:27,324

134

136
00:04:36,953 --> 00:04:38,604

00:04:38,784 --> 00:04:41,605
Three popcorns, one cranberry.

138
00:04:41,785 --> 00:04:44,479
Danny ate more than he strung.

139
00:04:44,828 --> 00:04:46,943
And when Christmas was over,

140
00:04:46,943 --> 00:04:49,512

141
00:04:49,512 --> 00:04:51,098

142
00:04:51,278 --> 00:04:53,155
The cardinals came first,

143
00:04:53,155 --> 00:04:54,656

144

00:04:57,641 --> 00:04:59,283

146
00:04:59,463 --> 00:05:02,472

00:05:02,472 --> 00:05:03,573

148
00:05:03,753 --> 00:05:05,204
Paper chains.

00:05:05,384 --> 00:05:08,404

00:05:08,404 --> 00:05:09,957

00:05:13,327 --> 00:05:15,662

154
00:05:15,662 --> 00:05:18,562

00:05:18,562 --> 00:05:21,037

156
00:05:21,037 --> 00:05:22,523

00:05:22,703 --> 00:05:24,424

158
00:05:24,424 --> 00:05:25,930

160

00:05:38,453 --> 00:05:40,450

166
00:05:40,630 --> 00:05:44,071

167
00:05:44,071 --> 00:05:46,791
with the orange bulb shaped like a

168
00:05:46,791 --> 00:05:47,271

00:05:47,451 --> 00:05:48,533
In the fifties,

170
00:05:48,533 --> 00:05:50,915

171
00:05:50,915 --> 00:05:53,512

172
00:05:53,512 --> 00:05:55,172

I'll take my candles.

176
00:06:03,480 --> 00:06:05,732
And here's how to do the window

177
00:06:05,732 --> 00:06:07,184
candles cheap today.

178
00:06:07,364 --> 00:06:09,658
The battery candles with a timer,

00:06:09,658 --> 00:06:12,021

00:06:12,021 --> 00:06:12,438
store.

00:06:12,618 --> 00:06:14,393

00:06:14,393 --> 00:06:15,773

00:06:18,452 --> 00:06:21,129
Put one in every front window,

00:06:21,129 --> 00:06:22,736

187
00:06:22,916 --> 00:06:24,144
From the street,

00:06:24,144 --> 00:06:26,986
your house will look exactly like Elm

189
00:06:26,986 --> 00:06:29,290
Street in nineteen fifty-five.

00:06:29,639 --> 00:06:30,719
Number nine.

191
00:06:30,899 --> 00:06:33,082
The ceramic Christmas tree.

192
00:06:33,262 --> 00:06:36,147
A little green ceramic tree with tiny

193
00:06:36,147 --> 00:06:39,110

194
00:06:39,110 --> 00:06:40,669

195
00:06:40,849 --> 00:06:42,141
In the seventies,

196
00:06:42,141 --> 00:06:45,181
every grandmother in America made one in

197
00:06:45,181 --> 00:06:48,221

198
00:06:48,401 --> 00:06:50,824
Mine is on my kitchen table right

199
00:06:50,824 --> 00:06:51,118

00:06:51,298 --> 00:06:53,959
Today they sell for a hundred dollars

201
00:06:53,959 --> 00:06:56,116

00:06:56,296 --> 00:06:57,910
Check your mother's attic.

203
00:06:58,259 --> 00:07:00,263
So far, glass birds,

204
00:07:00,263 --> 00:07:02,466
bubble lights, tinsel,

205
00:07:02,466 --> 00:07:04,269
the aluminum tree,

206
00:07:04,269 --> 00:07:07,174
plaid, felt, popcorn garland,

207
00:07:07,174 --> 00:07:10,879

208
00:07:11,059 --> 00:07:12,220
Number ten.

209
00:07:12,400 --> 00:07:14,618
Christmas cards on display.

210
00:07:14,798 --> 00:07:17,284
My mother strung a red ribbon across

211
00:07:17,284 --> 00:07:19,632

212
00:07:19,632 --> 00:07:21,980

213
00:07:21,980 --> 00:07:22,739

00:07:22,919 --> 00:07:25,857
By Christmas, the doorway was covered.

00:07:26,037 --> 00:07:28,022

216
00:07:28,022 --> 00:07:30,379

00:07:30,728 --> 00:07:32,405
And now number eleven,

218
00:07:32,405 --> 00:07:34,539

00:07:34,539 --> 00:07:35,454

00:07:35,634 --> 00:07:37,224
The nativity set.

00:07:37,404 --> 00:07:40,250

00:07:40,250 --> 00:07:42,147

00:07:46,559 --> 00:07:49,099
Mary has a chipped nose from when

226
00:07:49,099 --> 00:07:52,178

227
00:07:52,358 --> 00:07:54,804

228

229
00:07:56,409 --> 00:07:57,861

230
00:07:58,211 --> 00:08:00,769
My mother's rule was that the youngest

231
00:08:00,769 --> 00:08:02,922

00:08:02,922 --> 00:08:04,336

00:08:06,669 --> 00:08:09,032
Then the wise men moved a little

235
00:08:09,032 --> 00:08:11,617

236
00:08:11,617 --> 00:08:12,207
January.

237
00:08:12,387 --> 00:08:13,839
I still do it.

238
00:08:14,019 --> 00:08:17,134
My great-granddaughter put the baby in the

239
00:08:17,134 --> 00:08:18,395

240
00:08:18,395 --> 00:08:19,730

241
00:08:19,730 --> 00:08:20,694

242
00:08:20,874 --> 00:08:22,639
I'm still not over it.

243
00:08:22,988 --> 00:08:25,469
Now, how to get the vintage look

244
00:08:25,469 --> 00:08:27,795

245
00:08:27,975 --> 00:08:30,757

246
00:08:30,757 --> 00:08:31,295

248
00:08:34,958 --> 00:08:37,608

249
00:08:37,608 --> 00:08:38,592

251
00:08:41,419 --> 00:08:42,116

252
00:08:42,296 --> 00:08:44,200

253
00:08:44,380 --> 00:08:46,998

254
00:08:46,998 --> 00:08:50,562

255

256
00:08:53,034 --> 00:08:53,471

And mix them,

258
00:08:55,173 --> 00:08:56,421

00:08:56,601 --> 00:08:59,074

260
00:08:59,254 --> 00:09:01,178
A glass bird next to a felt

261
00:09:01,178 --> 00:09:03,317

262
00:09:03,317 --> 00:09:04,386

00:09:04,566 --> 00:09:06,986

264
00:09:06,986 --> 00:09:08,548

00:09:08,728 --> 00:09:10,843
A tree that looks like it came

00:09:12,786 --> 00:09:14,806
A tree that looks like it came

00:09:16,556 --> 00:09:17,163

00:09:17,512 --> 00:09:21,054

273
00:09:24,895 --> 00:09:25,893

274
00:09:25,893 --> 00:09:27,352

275
00:09:27,352 --> 00:09:29,425

276
00:09:29,425 --> 00:09:30,423

00:09:30,603 --> 00:09:32,468

00:09:32,468 --> 00:09:34,800

00:09:34,800 --> 00:09:37,209

00:09:37,209 --> 00:09:38,997

00:09:39,177 --> 00:09:42,509

282
00:09:42,858 --> 00:09:44,194
So one more time.

283
00:09:44,374 --> 00:09:46,931
Glass birds, bubble lights,

284
00:09:46,931 --> 00:09:50,056

00:09:50,056 --> 00:09:51,761

00:09:51,761 --> 00:09:54,508

00:09:54,508 --> 00:09:57,349

00:09:57,349 --> 00:09:58,865

00:09:58,865 --> 00:10:01,043

00:10:01,043 --> 00:10:02,653

00:10:02,653 --> 00:10:04,358

00:10:04,358 --> 00:10:05,968

00:10:13,568 --> 00:10:15,447
Tell me in the comments,

00:10:15,447 --> 00:10:16,308
sweetheart.

00:10:16,488 --> 00:10:18,694
Which one did your family have?

00:10:18,874 --> 00:10:20,757
I bet half of you had the

00:10:20,757 --> 00:10:21,812

00:10:21,992 --> 00:10:23,222
If you want more,

00:10:23,222 --> 00:10:26,553

00:10:26,553 --> 00:10:28,725

00:10:30,752 --> 00:10:31,187

52
00:01:40,804 --> 00:01:43,208
front door looks like a lost button.

53
00:01:43,388 --> 00:01:44,580
From the street,

54
00:01:44,580 --> 00:01:46,220
you can't even see it.

55
00:01:46,400 --> 00:01:48,905
The wreath should be about two thirds

56
00:01:48,905 --> 00:01:50,394
the width of the door.

57
00:01:50,574 --> 00:01:52,185
For most front doors,

58
00:01:52,185 --> 00:01:54,716
that's a twenty-four inch wreath,

59
00:01:54,716 --> 00:01:56,019
sometimes bigger.

60
00:01:56,370 --> 00:01:59,063
And make your own for almost nothing.

61
00:01:59,243 --> 00:02:00,799
Buy a plain wreath,

62
00:02:00,799 --> 00:02:03,829
then tuck in branches from your yard.

63
00:02:04,009 --> 00:02:05,672
Pine, cedar, holly,

64
00:02:05,672 --> 00:02:07,248
whatever you have.

65
00:02:07,428 --> 00:02:09,647
Add a few pinecones and a big

66
00:02:09,647 --> 00:02:11,712
bow made from wired ribbon.

67
00:02:11,892 --> 00:02:15,266
My mother wired real red apples into

68
00:02:15,266 --> 00:02:15,735
hers.

69
00:02:15,915 --> 00:02:18,226
A plain wreath from the store looks

70
00:02:18,226 --> 00:02:19,085
like a store.

71
00:02:19,265 --> 00:02:21,887
A full one with real greens looks

72
00:02:21,887 --> 00:02:22,841
like a home.

73
00:02:23,191 --> 00:02:24,909
Mistake number two.

74
00:02:25,089 --> 00:02:26,401
Mixed lights.

75
00:02:26,581 --> 00:02:28,562
Warm white along the roof,

76
00:02:28,562 --> 00:02:30,848
cold blue-white on the bushes,

77
00:02:30,848 --> 00:02:32,600
colored on the railing,

78
00:02:32,600 --> 00:02:34,429
and one string blinking.

79
00:02:34,609 --> 00:02:35,787
From the street,

80
00:02:35,787 --> 00:02:38,730
it looks like a hardware store clearance

81
00:02:38,730 --> 00:02:39,172
aisle.

82
00:02:39,352 --> 00:02:41,429
Pick one kind of light for the

83
00:02:41,429 --> 00:02:43,299
whole outside of the house.

84
00:02:43,479 --> 00:02:44,988
All warm white,

85
00:02:44,988 --> 00:02:46,498
or all colored.

86
00:02:46,678 --> 00:02:47,699
Never both.

87
00:02:48,050 --> 00:02:49,836
And hang them straight,

88
00:02:49,836 --> 00:02:50,302
honey.

89
00:02:50,482 --> 00:02:53,080
A droopy line of lights along the

90
00:02:53,080 --> 00:02:55,442
gutter, sagging between hooks,

91
00:02:55,442 --> 00:02:58,040
is the first thing people notice.

92
00:02:58,220 --> 00:03:00,987
Use the little plastic clips from the

93
00:03:00,987 --> 00:03:03,305
hardware store, one every foot,

94
00:03:03,305 --> 00:03:05,848
so the line is perfectly straight.

95
00:03:06,028 --> 00:03:08,779
My father measured with a yardstick.

96
00:03:08,959 --> 00:03:11,732
The neighbors laughed at him in November

97
00:03:11,732 --> 00:03:13,673
and admired him in December.

98
00:03:14,023 --> 00:03:16,401
And here's a little trick about the

99
00:03:16,401 --> 00:03:16,809
bulbs.

100
00:03:16,989 --> 00:03:18,555
The old big bulbs,

101
00:03:18,555 --> 00:03:21,339
the C9s, the size of your thumb,

102
00:03:21,339 --> 00:03:24,035
look wonderful from the street,

103
00:03:24,035 --> 00:03:26,732
much better than the tiny ones,

104
00:03:26,732 --> 00:03:29,342
which disappear from far away.

105
00:03:29,522 --> 00:03:31,440
They make them in LED now,

106
00:03:31,440 --> 00:03:33,653
so they don't get hot and they

107
00:03:33,653 --> 00:03:35,350
don't cost much to run.

108
00:03:35,530 --> 00:03:37,308
Big bulbs on the roof,

109
00:03:37,308 --> 00:03:39,489
small lights near the door.

110
00:03:39,669 --> 00:03:42,000
That's how my father did it,

111
00:03:42,000 --> 00:03:43,582
and it still works.

112
00:03:43,932 --> 00:03:45,754
Mistake number three.

113
00:03:45,934 --> 00:03:48,634
Lights only on the roofline and nothing

114
00:03:48,634 --> 00:03:49,603
near the door.

115
00:03:49,783 --> 00:03:52,186
The roof is high and far away.

116
00:03:52,366 --> 00:03:54,642
The door is where people come in.

117
00:03:54,822 --> 00:03:57,415
Put your warmest light at eye level,

118
00:03:57,415 --> 00:03:58,567
around the door,

119
00:03:58,567 --> 00:03:59,647
on the railing,

120
00:03:59,647 --> 00:04:00,727
in the windows,

121
00:04:00,727 --> 00:04:02,744
and in two lit trees or urns

122
00:04:02,744 --> 00:04:03,680
by the steps.

123
00:04:03,860 --> 00:04:06,507
That's what makes a house look welcoming

124
00:04:06,507 --> 00:04:08,028
instead of just bright.

125
00:04:08,379 --> 00:04:10,084
If this is helping you,

126
00:04:10,084 --> 00:04:12,605
honey, tap the like button for me.

127
00:04:12,785 --> 00:04:15,362
It helps Grandma more than you know.

128
00:04:15,542 --> 00:04:17,428
In a minute I'll tell you the

129
00:04:17,428 --> 00:04:19,640
cheapest thing on this whole list.

130
00:04:19,820 --> 00:04:21,796
It costs about ten dollars,

131
00:04:21,796 --> 00:04:24,869
and it makes more difference than anything

132
00:04:24,869 --> 00:04:26,113
else you can buy.

133
00:04:26,462 --> 00:04:28,239
Mistake number four.

134
00:04:28,419 --> 00:04:29,789
Bare steps.

135
00:04:29,969 --> 00:04:32,767
Here's the ten-dollar fix I promised.

136
00:04:32,947 --> 00:04:35,372
Two big pots or buckets on either

137
00:04:35,372 --> 00:04:37,136
side of the front steps,

138
00:04:37,136 --> 00:04:40,589
filled with cut evergreen branches standing up,

139
00:04:40,589 --> 00:04:42,868
a few tall birch or red dogwood

140
00:04:42,868 --> 00:04:45,587
sticks, and a string of little lights

141
00:04:45,587 --> 00:04:46,321
tucked in.

142
00:04:46,501 --> 00:04:47,778
It's the cheapest,

143
00:04:47,778 --> 00:04:49,692
prettiest thing you can do,

144
00:04:49,692 --> 00:04:51,961
and you can use the branches the

145
00:04:51,961 --> 00:04:54,443
Christmas tree lot gives away free.

146
00:04:54,793 --> 00:04:57,374
My father put two little live cedar

147
00:04:57,374 --> 00:04:59,955
trees in buckets on our steps every

148
00:04:59,955 --> 00:05:02,610
year, and in January he planted them

149
00:05:02,610 --> 00:05:03,790
in the backyard.

150
00:05:03,970 --> 00:05:05,840
By the time I left home,

151
00:05:05,840 --> 00:05:08,021
we had a row of eleven cedar

152
00:05:08,021 --> 00:05:10,124
trees along the back fence.

153
00:05:10,304 --> 00:05:13,043
Every Christmas of my childhood is still

154
00:05:13,043 --> 00:05:15,783
growing behind that house on Elm Street.

155
00:05:16,134 --> 00:05:19,051
And don't forget the mailbox and the

156
00:05:19,051 --> 00:05:20,429
lamp post, honey.

157
00:05:20,609 --> 00:05:22,728
A little swag of greens with a

158
00:05:22,728 --> 00:05:24,353
red bow on the mailbox,

159
00:05:24,353 --> 00:05:26,048
and a wreath or a bow on

160
00:05:26,048 --> 00:05:28,167
the lamp post by the driveway.

161
00:05:28,347 --> 00:05:30,944
They're the very first things people see

162
00:05:30,944 --> 00:05:31,854
from the road.

163
00:05:32,034 --> 00:05:34,679
My father tied a small wreath to

164
00:05:34,679 --> 00:05:36,581
our mailbox every year,

165
00:05:36,581 --> 00:05:37,904
and the mailman,

166
00:05:37,904 --> 00:05:38,152
Mr.

167
00:05:38,332 --> 00:05:40,654
Hoover, told him it was the only

168
00:05:40,654 --> 00:05:43,121
mailbox on his route that made him

169
00:05:43,121 --> 00:05:43,556
smile.

170
00:05:43,907 --> 00:05:45,834
Mistake number five.

171
00:05:46,014 --> 00:05:48,104
Too many things on the lawn.

172
00:05:48,284 --> 00:05:51,479
Inflatable snowmen, a plastic reindeer,

173
00:05:51,479 --> 00:05:53,446
a Santa on a motorcycle,

174
00:05:53,446 --> 00:05:55,658
a light-up candy cane path,

175
00:05:55,658 --> 00:05:59,099
and a projector throwing snowflakes on the

176
00:05:59,099 --> 00:05:59,673
garage.

177
00:05:59,853 --> 00:06:01,954
One or two of those is fun.

178
00:06:02,134 --> 00:06:04,412
All of them at once looks like

179
00:06:04,412 --> 00:06:05,931
a yard sale on fire.

180
00:06:06,111 --> 00:06:07,529
More isn't more,

181
00:06:07,529 --> 00:06:08,061
honey.

182
00:06:08,241 --> 00:06:09,611
Better is more.

183
00:06:09,962 --> 00:06:12,099
So far, a big full wreath,

184
00:06:12,099 --> 00:06:13,579
one kind of light,

185
00:06:13,579 --> 00:06:16,375
hung straight, light at eye level,

186
00:06:16,375 --> 00:06:19,006
and pots of greens on the steps.

187
00:06:19,186 --> 00:06:21,171
And here's the rule for the lawn.

188
00:06:21,351 --> 00:06:22,767
Pick one thing,

189
00:06:22,767 --> 00:06:24,184
and do it well.

190
00:06:24,364 --> 00:06:26,502
A single lit tree in the yard,

191
00:06:26,502 --> 00:06:28,070
or a pair of lit deer,

192
00:06:28,070 --> 00:06:30,137
or a sled leaning by the door

193
00:06:30,137 --> 00:06:31,562
with a wreath on it.

194
00:06:31,742 --> 00:06:33,833
Then leave the rest of the yard

195
00:06:33,833 --> 00:06:34,238
alone.

196
00:06:34,589 --> 00:06:36,365
Mistake number six.

197
00:06:36,545 --> 00:06:38,908
A muddy old doormat and a dead

198
00:06:38,908 --> 00:06:39,854
porch light.

199
00:06:40,034 --> 00:06:42,548
People forget, but the doormat is the

200
00:06:42,548 --> 00:06:45,130
first thing every guest looks down at.

201
00:06:45,310 --> 00:06:46,919
A clean, plain mat,

202
00:06:46,919 --> 00:06:49,121
maybe a red one or a plaid

203
00:06:49,121 --> 00:06:50,730
one for the season,

204
00:06:50,730 --> 00:06:53,610
layered on top of a bigger striped

205
00:06:53,610 --> 00:06:53,948
one.

206
00:06:54,128 --> 00:06:55,868
And put a warm bulb in the

207
00:06:55,868 --> 00:06:56,671
porch light.

208
00:06:56,851 --> 00:06:59,207
The bright white ones make the whole

209
00:06:59,207 --> 00:07:01,170
porch look like a gas station.

210
00:07:01,520 --> 00:07:03,180
And add a lantern.

211
00:07:03,360 --> 00:07:06,177
A plain metal lantern with a battery

212
00:07:06,177 --> 00:07:08,681
candle inside, by the door or on

213
00:07:08,681 --> 00:07:09,385
the step.

214
00:07:09,565 --> 00:07:10,888
Set it on a timer,

215
00:07:10,888 --> 00:07:12,944
so it comes on at dusk every

216
00:07:12,944 --> 00:07:13,385
night.

217
00:07:13,565 --> 00:07:15,778
It's the one thing that makes a

218
00:07:15,778 --> 00:07:17,919
porch look warm from far away.

219
00:07:18,099 --> 00:07:20,766
My mother had an oil lantern from

220
00:07:20,766 --> 00:07:22,464
Grandma Pearl's farm.

221
00:07:22,644 --> 00:07:25,163
I still light it every Christmas Eve.

222
00:07:25,514 --> 00:07:27,770
And if you live in an apartment

223
00:07:27,770 --> 00:07:29,226
with only a balcony,

224
00:07:29,226 --> 00:07:31,702
sweetheart, you can still do this.

225
00:07:31,882 --> 00:07:34,219
A string of warm lights along the

226
00:07:34,219 --> 00:07:36,061
railing, clipped straight.

227
00:07:36,241 --> 00:07:38,686
A small wreath hung on the outside

228
00:07:38,686 --> 00:07:39,765
of the railing,

229
00:07:39,765 --> 00:07:41,059
facing the street.

230
00:07:41,239 --> 00:07:43,784
And one potted evergreen in the corner

231
00:07:43,784 --> 00:07:44,989
with a few lights.

232
00:07:45,169 --> 00:07:47,902
Your neighbors walking by below will look

233
00:07:47,902 --> 00:07:48,769
up and smile.

234
00:07:48,949 --> 00:07:51,359
A little balcony done right is as

235
00:07:51,359 --> 00:07:52,966
warm as a whole house.

236
00:07:53,316 --> 00:07:55,506
And now mistake number seven,

237
00:07:55,506 --> 00:07:57,697
the one I see on almost every

238
00:07:57,697 --> 00:07:59,585
house in my neighborhood.

239
00:07:59,765 --> 00:08:01,657
Coming up the walk in the dark.

240
00:08:01,837 --> 00:08:04,110
People spend hundreds on the roof and

241
00:08:04,110 --> 00:08:06,198
forget the path to their own front

242
00:08:06,198 --> 00:08:06,505
door.

243
00:08:06,685 --> 00:08:09,464
Their guests stumble up a black sidewalk

244
00:08:09,464 --> 00:08:11,340
to get to all those lights.

245
00:08:11,691 --> 00:08:13,455
The five-minute fix.

246
00:08:13,635 --> 00:08:16,411
A row of little solar stake lights,

247
00:08:16,411 --> 00:08:18,314
or paper bag luminaries,

248
00:08:18,314 --> 00:08:21,089
along both sides of the front walk.

249
00:08:21,269 --> 00:08:22,542
In the fifties,

250
00:08:22,542 --> 00:08:26,020
we made luminaries with brown lunch bags,

251
00:08:26,020 --> 00:08:28,396
a cup of sand in the bottom,

252
00:08:28,396 --> 00:08:30,092
and a candle inside.

253
00:08:30,272 --> 00:08:32,902
Today use battery tea lights,

254
00:08:32,902 --> 00:08:35,079
so nothing catches fire.

255
00:08:35,259 --> 00:08:36,637
A lit path says,

256
00:08:36,637 --> 00:08:38,359
we're expecting you.

257
00:08:38,539 --> 00:08:41,213
And it keeps Aunt Margaret from falling

258
00:08:41,213 --> 00:08:42,173
in the bushes.

259
00:08:42,523 --> 00:08:44,684
And people always ask me,

260
00:08:44,684 --> 00:08:46,586
when do you put it up?

261
00:08:46,766 --> 00:08:49,439
My father's rule was the Saturday after

262
00:08:49,439 --> 00:08:51,426
Thanksgiving for the outside,

263
00:08:51,426 --> 00:08:53,962
while it's still warm enough to stand

264
00:08:53,962 --> 00:08:54,785
on a ladder,

265
00:08:54,785 --> 00:08:57,320
and everything came down on the sixth

266
00:08:57,320 --> 00:08:58,074
of January.

267
00:08:58,254 --> 00:09:00,294
Hang the lights in November,

268
00:09:00,294 --> 00:09:02,698
even early November on a dry day,

269
00:09:02,698 --> 00:09:05,102
and just don't turn them on until

270
00:09:05,102 --> 00:09:06,486
after Thanksgiving.

271
00:09:06,666 --> 00:09:08,721
Your fingers will thank you.

272
00:09:09,071 --> 00:09:10,998
And be safe out there,

273
00:09:10,998 --> 00:09:11,961
sweetheart.

274
00:09:12,141 --> 00:09:15,578
Only use lights marked for outdoor use.

275
00:09:15,758 --> 00:09:18,522
Plug them into an outdoor outlet with

276
00:09:18,522 --> 00:09:20,389
a cover, and use a timer,

277
00:09:20,389 --> 00:09:22,480
so they turn off at bedtime.

278
00:09:22,660 --> 00:09:25,098
Never staple through the wires.

279
00:09:25,278 --> 00:09:28,285
And always have somebody hold the ladder.

280
00:09:28,465 --> 00:09:30,781
My father fell off ours in nineteen

281
00:09:30,781 --> 00:09:32,765
sixty-two and broke his wrist,

282
00:09:32,765 --> 00:09:35,478
and my mother finished the lights herself

283
00:09:35,478 --> 00:09:37,727
with his cast pointing at her from

284
00:09:37,727 --> 00:09:38,322
the lawn.

285
00:09:38,672 --> 00:09:40,251
So one more time.

286
00:09:40,431 --> 00:09:42,359
A big, full wreath,

287
00:09:42,359 --> 00:09:44,390
two thirds the door.

288
00:09:44,570 --> 00:09:46,041
One kind of light,

289
00:09:46,041 --> 00:09:48,494
hung straight, never blinking.

290
00:09:48,674 --> 00:09:50,717
The warmest light at eye level by

291
00:09:50,717 --> 00:09:51,274
the door.

292
00:09:51,454 --> 00:09:53,509
Pots of greens on the steps.

293
00:09:53,689 --> 00:09:55,656
One thing on the lawn,

294
00:09:55,656 --> 00:09:56,371
not ten.

295
00:09:56,551 --> 00:09:57,854
A clean mat,

296
00:09:57,854 --> 00:09:59,157
a warm bulb,

297
00:09:59,157 --> 00:10:00,243
a lantern.

298
00:10:00,423 --> 00:10:02,583
And a lit path to your door.

299
00:10:02,763 --> 00:10:04,683
That's how you make your house the

300
00:10:04,683 --> 00:10:06,095
warmest one on the block.

301
00:10:06,445 --> 00:10:08,395
Tell me in the comments,

302
00:10:08,395 --> 00:10:09,289
sweetheart.

303
00:10:09,469 --> 00:10:11,814
White lights or colored lights?

304
00:10:11,994 --> 00:10:13,921
I know which one I am.

305
00:10:14,101 --> 00:10:15,284
If you want more,

306
00:10:15,284 --> 00:10:18,484
the whole playlist of Grandma's Christmas tips

307
00:10:18,484 --> 00:10:20,571
is right there on your screen,

308
00:10:20,571 --> 00:10:22,519
and I'll see you in the next

309
00:10:22,519 --> 00:10:22,937
video.

310
00:10:23,117 --> 00:10:24,742
Good night, honey.

311
00:10:24,922 --> 00:10:26,455
Merry Christmas.
