00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:03,250
Sweetheart, there's one Christmas cookie that every

2
00:00:03,250 --> 00:00:05,735
single grandmother in America has made.

3
00:00:05,915 --> 00:00:08,472
The little round peanut butter cookie,

4
00:00:08,472 --> 00:00:09,549
rolled in sugar,

5
00:00:09,549 --> 00:00:12,106
with a chocolate kiss pressed right in

6
00:00:12,106 --> 00:00:12,846
the middle.

7
00:00:13,026 --> 00:00:15,127
Peanut butter blossoms.

8
00:00:15,307 --> 00:00:17,652
On every cookie tray at every church

9
00:00:17,652 --> 00:00:19,800
party since I was a young mother.

10
00:00:19,980 --> 00:00:21,603
And every December,

11
00:00:21,603 --> 00:00:24,935
somebody tells me theirs came out flat,

12
00:00:24,935 --> 00:00:27,155
dry, or cracked to pieces.

13
00:00:27,505 --> 00:00:29,960
So tonight I'm giving you my peanut

14
00:00:29,960 --> 00:00:31,081
butter blossoms.

15
00:00:31,261 --> 00:00:32,372
Soft and chewy,

16
00:00:32,372 --> 00:00:33,557
thick and round,

17
00:00:33,557 --> 00:00:36,150
with the kiss sitting pretty in the

18
00:00:36,150 --> 00:00:37,705
middle and no cracks.

19
00:00:37,885 --> 00:00:40,690
Every step, and the four mistakes that

20
00:00:40,690 --> 00:00:42,018
make them go flat.

21
00:00:42,198 --> 00:00:43,384
And stay with me,

22
00:00:43,384 --> 00:00:45,965
because the last mistake is about the

23
00:00:45,965 --> 00:00:48,895
chocolate, and almost everybody does it at

24
00:00:48,895 --> 00:00:50,081
the wrong moment.

25
00:00:50,431 --> 00:00:52,848
This cookie is younger than me,

26
00:00:52,848 --> 00:00:54,251
believe it or not.

27
00:00:54,431 --> 00:00:56,813
It came from a baking contest in

28
00:00:56,813 --> 00:00:58,748
the late nineteen fifties,

29
00:00:58,748 --> 00:01:01,354
the big national one sponsored by a

30
00:01:01,354 --> 00:01:02,396
flour company.

31
00:01:02,576 --> 00:01:04,030
A woman from Ohio,

32
00:01:04,030 --> 00:01:07,504
Freda Smith, entered a peanut butter cookie

33
00:01:07,504 --> 00:01:10,575
with a chocolate candy pressed on top.

34
00:01:10,755 --> 00:01:13,054
She didn't win first prize.

35
00:01:13,234 --> 00:01:15,620
But her cookie became more famous than

36
00:01:15,620 --> 00:01:16,310
the winner.

37
00:01:16,660 --> 00:01:18,820
The first time I made them was

38
00:01:18,820 --> 00:01:22,419
nineteen sixty-four, for my son's first Christmas.

39
00:01:22,599 --> 00:01:24,685
I saw the recipe in a magazine

40
00:01:24,685 --> 00:01:26,910
at the beauty parlor and tore it

41
00:01:26,910 --> 00:01:28,857
out when nobody was looking.

42
00:01:29,037 --> 00:01:31,939
I've confessed that sin to my pastor.

43
00:01:32,119 --> 00:01:34,907
I've made them every December since,

44
00:01:34,907 --> 00:01:38,778
sixty-two Christmases, and that torn magazine page

45
00:01:38,778 --> 00:01:40,791
is still in my recipe box,

46
00:01:40,791 --> 00:01:42,650
held together with tape.

47
00:01:42,999 --> 00:01:44,950
My husband used to say they were

48
00:01:44,950 --> 00:01:47,205
the only cookie where you got dessert

49
00:01:47,205 --> 00:01:48,607
on top of your dessert.

50
00:01:48,787 --> 00:01:51,643
And the grandchildren fight over who gets

51
00:01:51,643 --> 00:01:53,803
to unwrap the chocolate kisses.

52
00:01:53,983 --> 00:01:56,039
Last year I had five of them

53
00:01:56,039 --> 00:01:57,581
at the kitchen table,

54
00:01:57,581 --> 00:01:59,197
unwrapping and eating,

55
00:01:59,197 --> 00:02:01,547
and by the end I had forty-eight

56
00:02:01,547 --> 00:02:04,118
cookies and only thirty-one kisses.

57
00:02:04,298 --> 00:02:06,092
In a minute I'll tell you how

58
00:02:06,092 --> 00:02:08,319
to keep the little helpers away from

59
00:02:08,319 --> 00:02:08,629
them.

60
00:02:08,978 --> 00:02:10,601
Here's what you need,

61
00:02:10,601 --> 00:02:12,763
honey, for about four dozen.

62
00:02:12,943 --> 00:02:14,642
Half a cup of butter,

63
00:02:14,642 --> 00:02:15,370
softened.

64
00:02:15,550 --> 00:02:18,034
Half a cup of creamy peanut butter.

65
00:02:18,214 --> 00:02:20,308
Half a cup of white sugar,

66
00:02:20,308 --> 00:02:22,080
plus more for rolling.

67
00:02:22,260 --> 00:02:24,896
Half a cup of packed brown sugar.

68
00:02:25,076 --> 00:02:26,063
One egg.

69
00:02:26,243 --> 00:02:28,216
Two tablespoons of milk.

70
00:02:28,396 --> 00:02:30,579
One teaspoon of vanilla.

71
00:02:30,759 --> 00:02:33,487
One and three quarter cups of flour.

72
00:02:33,667 --> 00:02:36,233
One teaspoon of baking soda.

73
00:02:36,413 --> 00:02:38,294
Half a teaspoon of salt.

74
00:02:38,474 --> 00:02:41,302
And about forty-eight chocolate kisses,

75
00:02:41,302 --> 00:02:42,027
unwrapped.

76
00:02:42,376 --> 00:02:44,420
Now, the peanut butter.

77
00:02:44,600 --> 00:02:47,680
Use the regular creamy kind from the

78
00:02:47,680 --> 00:02:50,160
jar, the one you stir with no

79
00:02:50,160 --> 00:02:51,101
oil on top.

80
00:02:51,281 --> 00:02:53,221
The natural peanut butter,

81
00:02:53,221 --> 00:02:55,011
where the oil floats up,

82
00:02:55,011 --> 00:02:58,144
sounds healthier, but it makes the cookies

83
00:02:58,144 --> 00:03:00,755
spread and turn greasy and crumbly.

84
00:03:00,935 --> 00:03:03,187
This is mistake number one.

85
00:03:03,367 --> 00:03:06,224
Save the natural kind for your toast.

86
00:03:06,573 --> 00:03:08,664
And measure the flour right,

87
00:03:08,664 --> 00:03:11,426
honey, because too much flour is what

88
00:03:11,426 --> 00:03:13,516
makes these dry and crumbly.

89
00:03:13,696 --> 00:03:16,007
Don't scoop the cup into the bag.

90
00:03:16,187 --> 00:03:18,977
Spoon the flour into the measuring cup,

91
00:03:18,977 --> 00:03:21,123
and level it off with the back

92
00:03:21,123 --> 00:03:21,910
of a knife.

93
00:03:22,090 --> 00:03:24,424
Scooping packs in up to a quarter

94
00:03:24,424 --> 00:03:26,686
cup extra, and with a dough this

95
00:03:26,686 --> 00:03:29,161
rich, that quarter cup turns a soft

96
00:03:29,161 --> 00:03:30,717
cookie into a dry one.

97
00:03:31,066 --> 00:03:32,065
Step one.

98
00:03:32,245 --> 00:03:33,461
Beat the butter,

99
00:03:33,461 --> 00:03:36,881
peanut butter, and both sugars together until

100
00:03:36,881 --> 00:03:38,249
smooth and creamy,

101
00:03:38,249 --> 00:03:39,617
about two minutes.

102
00:03:39,797 --> 00:03:41,430
Then beat in the egg,

103
00:03:41,430 --> 00:03:43,373
the milk and the vanilla.

104
00:03:43,553 --> 00:03:44,961
In another bowl,

105
00:03:44,961 --> 00:03:46,280
stir the flour,

106
00:03:46,280 --> 00:03:48,127
baking soda and salt.

107
00:03:48,307 --> 00:03:50,902
Add it to the peanut butter mixture

108
00:03:50,902 --> 00:03:53,866
slowly, mixing just until there's no dry

109
00:03:53,866 --> 00:03:54,681
flour left.

110
00:03:54,861 --> 00:03:56,943
The dough will be soft and a

111
00:03:56,943 --> 00:03:57,984
little sticky.

112
00:03:58,334 --> 00:04:00,943
Step two, and this is where most

113
00:04:00,943 --> 00:04:02,247
people go wrong.

114
00:04:02,427 --> 00:04:04,687
Cover the bowl and chill the dough

115
00:04:04,687 --> 00:04:06,681
in the icebox for at least one

116
00:04:06,681 --> 00:04:07,013
hour.

117
00:04:07,193 --> 00:04:09,863
Mistake number two is skipping this.

118
00:04:10,043 --> 00:04:12,906
Warm peanut butter dough spreads in the

119
00:04:12,906 --> 00:04:14,008
oven into thin,

120
00:04:14,008 --> 00:04:16,430
flat discs, and then the kiss has

121
00:04:16,430 --> 00:04:17,532
nowhere to sit.

122
00:04:17,712 --> 00:04:20,363
Cold dough holds its round shape and

123
00:04:20,363 --> 00:04:22,205
bakes up thick and puffy.

124
00:04:22,554 --> 00:04:23,762
Step three.

125
00:04:23,942 --> 00:04:26,926
Heat the oven to three hundred seventy-five.

126
00:04:27,106 --> 00:04:29,905
Roll the cold dough into balls about

127
00:04:29,905 --> 00:04:31,149
one inch across,

128
00:04:31,149 --> 00:04:33,015
about a tablespoon each.

129
00:04:33,195 --> 00:04:35,191
Then roll each ball in a little

130
00:04:35,191 --> 00:04:37,573
bowl of white sugar until it's coated

131
00:04:37,573 --> 00:04:38,153
all over.

132
00:04:38,333 --> 00:04:41,229
The sugar makes that pretty sparkly crust

133
00:04:41,229 --> 00:04:43,348
that crackles a little on top.

134
00:04:43,528 --> 00:04:45,565
Set them two inches apart on a

135
00:04:45,565 --> 00:04:47,534
parchment-lined baking sheet.

136
00:04:47,883 --> 00:04:49,607
If this is helping you,

137
00:04:49,607 --> 00:04:52,156
honey, tap the like button for me.

138
00:04:52,336 --> 00:04:55,018
It helps Grandma more than you know.

139
00:04:55,198 --> 00:04:57,195
Now, step four.

140
00:04:57,375 --> 00:04:59,535
Bake them for eight to ten minutes,

141
00:04:59,535 --> 00:05:01,881
just until they're puffed and the tops

142
00:05:01,881 --> 00:05:04,042
are starting to crack and the edges

143
00:05:04,042 --> 00:05:05,153
are barely golden.

144
00:05:05,333 --> 00:05:08,379
Mistake number three is baking them too

145
00:05:08,379 --> 00:05:08,770
long.

146
00:05:08,950 --> 00:05:11,093
If they look done in the oven,

147
00:05:11,093 --> 00:05:13,594
they'll be dry and hard by morning.

148
00:05:13,943 --> 00:05:15,650
How do you tell when they're done?

149
00:05:15,830 --> 00:05:18,631
The tops should have little cracks,

150
00:05:18,631 --> 00:05:19,832
like dry earth,

151
00:05:19,832 --> 00:05:21,832
and look just barely set.

152
00:05:22,012 --> 00:05:24,596
The middles should still look a tiny

153
00:05:24,596 --> 00:05:25,960
bit soft and shiny.

154
00:05:26,140 --> 00:05:27,189
Take one out,

155
00:05:27,189 --> 00:05:29,286
and press the edge gently.

156
00:05:29,466 --> 00:05:30,334
If it holds,

157
00:05:30,334 --> 00:05:31,347
they're ready.

158
00:05:31,527 --> 00:05:33,642
They keep baking on the hot pan

159
00:05:33,642 --> 00:05:35,689
for a minute or two after they

160
00:05:35,689 --> 00:05:37,736
come out, so trust me and take

161
00:05:37,736 --> 00:05:38,760
them out early.

162
00:05:39,109 --> 00:05:41,688
So far, regular peanut butter,

163
00:05:41,688 --> 00:05:43,063
chill the dough,

164
00:05:43,063 --> 00:05:44,266
roll in sugar,

165
00:05:44,266 --> 00:05:47,016
and bake them just until puffed.

166
00:05:47,196 --> 00:05:48,178
Now the kiss,

167
00:05:48,178 --> 00:05:51,050
and the fourth mistake I promised you.

168
00:05:51,230 --> 00:05:53,828
Most people press the chocolate kiss in

169
00:05:53,828 --> 00:05:56,225
right away, the second the pan comes

170
00:05:56,225 --> 00:05:57,291
out of the oven.

171
00:05:57,471 --> 00:05:59,704
And the cookie cracks all the way

172
00:05:59,704 --> 00:06:01,600
around, like a broken plate,

173
00:06:01,600 --> 00:06:04,239
because it's still too soft and puffed.

174
00:06:04,589 --> 00:06:05,925
Here's the trick.

175
00:06:06,105 --> 00:06:08,086
Let the cookies sit on the pan

176
00:06:08,086 --> 00:06:10,133
for two or three minutes first.

177
00:06:10,313 --> 00:06:12,908
Just long enough that the outside sets

178
00:06:12,908 --> 00:06:15,366
a little, but they're still warm and

179
00:06:15,366 --> 00:06:16,664
soft in the middle.

180
00:06:16,844 --> 00:06:19,286
Then press a kiss straight down into

181
00:06:19,286 --> 00:06:20,846
the center of each one,

182
00:06:20,846 --> 00:06:23,560
firmly, so the cookie crinkles around it

183
00:06:23,560 --> 00:06:25,052
like a flower opening.

184
00:06:25,232 --> 00:06:27,891
That's why they're called blossoms.

185
00:06:28,240 --> 00:06:30,413
And the other half of the kiss

186
00:06:30,413 --> 00:06:30,992
mistake.

187
00:06:31,172 --> 00:06:34,088
The chocolate melts from the warm cookie,

188
00:06:34,088 --> 00:06:36,221
and if you move the cookies or

189
00:06:36,221 --> 00:06:38,852
stack them, the kisses smear and lose

190
00:06:38,852 --> 00:06:39,705
their point.

191
00:06:39,885 --> 00:06:41,739
So once the kisses are in,

192
00:06:41,739 --> 00:06:44,305
move the whole sheet of parchment to

193
00:06:44,305 --> 00:06:46,800
the counter, and then put the whole

194
00:06:46,800 --> 00:06:49,580
tray in the icebox for fifteen minutes.

195
00:06:49,760 --> 00:06:52,217
The chocolate sets back up firm,

196
00:06:52,217 --> 00:06:55,135
with that perfect little point on top.

197
00:06:55,485 --> 00:06:57,744
And here's how I keep the little

198
00:06:57,744 --> 00:06:59,790
helpers away from the kisses,

199
00:06:59,790 --> 00:07:00,919
like I promised.

200
00:07:01,099 --> 00:07:02,824
Unwrap them yourself,

201
00:07:02,824 --> 00:07:04,220
the night before,

202
00:07:04,220 --> 00:07:06,683
and put them in a covered bowl

203
00:07:06,683 --> 00:07:07,833
in the icebox,

204
00:07:07,833 --> 00:07:08,901
out of sight.

205
00:07:09,081 --> 00:07:12,177
Cold kisses also hold their shape better

206
00:07:12,177 --> 00:07:13,957
when you press them in.

207
00:07:14,137 --> 00:07:16,820
Then give the children their own small

208
00:07:16,820 --> 00:07:19,151
bowl of kisses to unwrap and eat,

209
00:07:19,151 --> 00:07:20,987
so they leave yours alone.

210
00:07:21,336 --> 00:07:24,039
For Christmas, change the topping and you

211
00:07:24,039 --> 00:07:25,621
have a whole new cookie.

212
00:07:25,801 --> 00:07:27,847
Press in a peppermint kiss,

213
00:07:27,847 --> 00:07:29,667
or a caramel-filled one.

214
00:07:29,847 --> 00:07:31,854
Or roll the balls in red and

215
00:07:31,854 --> 00:07:33,933
green sugar instead of white.

216
00:07:34,113 --> 00:07:36,052
Or use a little piece of a

217
00:07:36,052 --> 00:07:37,469
dark chocolate bar.

218
00:07:37,649 --> 00:07:40,073
My grandson likes a whole peanut butter

219
00:07:40,073 --> 00:07:41,689
cup pressed in the middle.

220
00:07:41,869 --> 00:07:44,293
That's not a blossom anymore,

221
00:07:44,293 --> 00:07:44,795
honey.

222
00:07:44,975 --> 00:07:46,054
That's a dare.

223
00:07:46,404 --> 00:07:49,200
And if somebody in your family can't

224
00:07:49,200 --> 00:07:51,142
have peanuts, sweetheart,

225
00:07:51,142 --> 00:07:54,249
make the same cookie with sunflower seed

226
00:07:54,249 --> 00:07:55,414
butter instead.

227
00:07:55,594 --> 00:07:58,624
It bakes almost exactly the same.

228
00:07:58,804 --> 00:08:02,138
Be careful, because sunflower butter can turn

229
00:08:02,138 --> 00:08:04,731
a little green inside when it bakes

230
00:08:04,731 --> 00:08:05,991
with baking soda.

231
00:08:06,171 --> 00:08:08,098
It's perfectly safe,

232
00:08:08,098 --> 00:08:10,025
it's just chemistry.

233
00:08:10,205 --> 00:08:12,282
Use a little less baking soda,

234
00:08:12,282 --> 00:08:14,912
and tell the children it's a Christmas

235
00:08:14,912 --> 00:08:15,673
elf cookie.

236
00:08:16,023 --> 00:08:17,827
They keep a week in a tin,

237
00:08:17,827 --> 00:08:20,325
with wax paper between the layers so

238
00:08:20,325 --> 00:08:21,921
the kisses don't stick.

239
00:08:22,101 --> 00:08:24,725
Don't stack them while they're warm.

240
00:08:24,905 --> 00:08:27,366
And the dough freezes beautifully.

241
00:08:27,546 --> 00:08:29,141
Roll it into balls,

242
00:08:29,141 --> 00:08:30,736
roll them in sugar,

243
00:08:30,736 --> 00:08:32,582
freeze them on a tray,

244
00:08:32,582 --> 00:08:34,512
then put them in a bag.

245
00:08:34,692 --> 00:08:35,924
On Christmas Eve,

246
00:08:35,924 --> 00:08:38,532
bake them straight from the freezer,

247
00:08:38,532 --> 00:08:40,416
adding one or two minutes.

248
00:08:40,766 --> 00:08:43,446
And they're the perfect cookie for the

249
00:08:43,446 --> 00:08:44,575
cookie exchange.

250
00:08:44,755 --> 00:08:46,871
Everybody recognizes them,

251
00:08:46,871 --> 00:08:48,581
everybody loves them,

252
00:08:48,581 --> 00:08:51,267
and they look like Christmas on a

253
00:08:51,267 --> 00:08:51,755
plate.

254
00:08:51,935 --> 00:08:54,118
At my church's cookie swap,

255
00:08:54,118 --> 00:08:57,190
there are always three trays of peanut

256
00:08:57,190 --> 00:08:58,483
butter blossoms.

257
00:08:58,663 --> 00:09:01,450
Mine is always the one that runs

258
00:09:01,450 --> 00:09:02,320
out first.

259
00:09:02,500 --> 00:09:03,850
I'm not proud,

260
00:09:03,850 --> 00:09:04,428
honey.

261
00:09:04,608 --> 00:09:07,081
Well, I'm a little proud.

262
00:09:07,430 --> 00:09:09,230
And here's a good gift.

263
00:09:09,410 --> 00:09:12,111
A jar of the dry ingredients,

264
00:09:12,111 --> 00:09:15,463
flour, sugars, baking soda and salt,

265
00:09:15,463 --> 00:09:17,977
layered in a big mason jar,

266
00:09:17,977 --> 00:09:20,492
with a bag of kisses on top

267
00:09:20,492 --> 00:09:22,727
and the recipe on a tag.

268
00:09:22,907 --> 00:09:25,141
People just add the butter,

269
00:09:25,141 --> 00:09:27,458
peanut butter, egg and milk.

270
00:09:27,638 --> 00:09:29,590
I give them to the young mothers

271
00:09:29,590 --> 00:09:31,542
at church, and they tell me it's

272
00:09:31,542 --> 00:09:34,104
the first cookie their children ever made.

273
00:09:34,454 --> 00:09:35,975
So one more time.

274
00:09:36,155 --> 00:09:38,767
Regular creamy peanut butter,

275
00:09:38,767 --> 00:09:39,847
not natural.

276
00:09:40,027 --> 00:09:41,490
Chill the dough an hour.

277
00:09:41,670 --> 00:09:43,179
Roll in sugar.

278
00:09:43,359 --> 00:09:45,022
Eight to ten minutes,

279
00:09:45,022 --> 00:09:45,972
just puffed.

280
00:09:46,152 --> 00:09:48,459
Let them rest two or three minutes

281
00:09:48,459 --> 00:09:50,428
before you press in the kiss,

282
00:09:50,428 --> 00:09:52,871
then chill the tray so the chocolate

283
00:09:52,871 --> 00:09:54,093
sets with a point.

284
00:09:54,273 --> 00:09:57,071
That's how you get peanut butter blossoms

285
00:09:57,071 --> 00:09:59,323
that are thick and soft and never

286
00:09:59,323 --> 00:09:59,869
cracked.

287
00:10:00,218 --> 00:10:02,065
Tell me in the comments,

288
00:10:02,065 --> 00:10:02,912
sweetheart.

289
00:10:03,092 --> 00:10:06,124
Who made peanut butter blossoms in your

290
00:10:06,124 --> 00:10:06,668
family?

291
00:10:06,848 --> 00:10:09,009
And do you eat the kiss first,

292
00:10:09,009 --> 00:10:10,017
or the cookie?

293
00:10:10,197 --> 00:10:13,317
The whole playlist of Grandma's recipes is

294
00:10:13,317 --> 00:10:15,323
right there on your screen,

295
00:10:15,323 --> 00:10:17,403
and I'll see you in the next

296
00:10:17,403 --> 00:10:17,848
video.

297
00:10:18,028 --> 00:10:19,456
Good night, honey.

298
00:10:19,636 --> 00:10:21,099
Merry Christmas.

00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:02,927
Sweetheart, I was there when green bean

2
00:00:02,927 --> 00:00:04,353
casserole was born.

3
00:00:04,533 --> 00:00:06,263
Well, almost.

4
00:00:06,443 --> 00:00:08,096
In nineteen fifty-five,

5
00:00:08,096 --> 00:00:10,612
my mother clipped a recipe from the

6
00:00:10,612 --> 00:00:11,331
newspaper.

7
00:00:11,511 --> 00:00:14,608
Green beans, a can of mushroom soup,

8
00:00:14,608 --> 00:00:17,792
and those crispy fried onions on top.

9
00:00:17,972 --> 00:00:19,841
She made it for Thanksgiving,

10
00:00:19,841 --> 00:00:21,710
my father had three helpings,

11
00:00:21,710 --> 00:00:23,773
and it's been on our table every

12
00:00:23,773 --> 00:00:25,449
holiday for seventy years.

13
00:00:25,799 --> 00:00:28,847
But most green bean casserole today is

14
00:00:28,847 --> 00:00:30,050
gray and mushy,

15
00:00:30,050 --> 00:00:32,296
swimming in salty gray soup,

16
00:00:32,296 --> 00:00:33,740
with soggy onions.

17
00:00:33,920 --> 00:00:36,140
So tonight I'm giving you how to

18
00:00:36,140 --> 00:00:37,598
make it from scratch,

19
00:00:37,598 --> 00:00:40,027
the way that tastes like real food.

20
00:00:40,207 --> 00:00:43,040
Every step, and the four mistakes that

21
00:00:43,040 --> 00:00:44,084
make it mushy.

22
00:00:44,264 --> 00:00:45,463
And stay with me,

23
00:00:45,463 --> 00:00:47,789
because the last trick is for the

24
00:00:47,789 --> 00:00:50,257
onions, and it's the one that makes

25
00:00:50,257 --> 00:00:52,089
people ask for the recipe.

26
00:00:52,439 --> 00:00:55,319
The original recipe came from a test

27
00:00:55,319 --> 00:00:58,359
kitchen at the soup company in Camden,

28
00:00:58,359 --> 00:01:01,159
New Jersey, in nineteen fifty-five.

29
00:01:01,339 --> 00:01:03,599
A woman named Dorcas Reilly put it

30
00:01:03,599 --> 00:01:06,724
together from things every American kitchen had

31
00:01:06,724 --> 00:01:07,654
in the pantry.

32
00:01:07,834 --> 00:01:10,174
Canned beans, canned soup,

33
00:01:10,174 --> 00:01:11,793
and canned onions.

34
00:01:11,973 --> 00:01:14,219
It was the age of the can,

35
00:01:14,219 --> 00:01:14,737
honey.

36
00:01:14,917 --> 00:01:17,494
And she made something people still eat

37
00:01:17,494 --> 00:01:20,071
sixty million times every Thanksgiving.

38
00:01:20,421 --> 00:01:23,327
My mother was a little suspicious at

39
00:01:23,327 --> 00:01:23,812
first.

40
00:01:23,992 --> 00:01:26,904
Grandma Pearl grew her own green beans

41
00:01:26,904 --> 00:01:28,744
and canned them herself,

42
00:01:28,744 --> 00:01:31,120
and she thought soup from a can

43
00:01:31,120 --> 00:01:32,653
was for lazy people.

44
00:01:32,833 --> 00:01:34,883
But she ate two plates of it,

45
00:01:34,883 --> 00:01:37,076
and then she asked my mother to

46
00:01:37,076 --> 00:01:39,056
make it again for Christmas.

47
00:01:39,236 --> 00:01:42,150
Grandma Pearl never said she was wrong.

48
00:01:42,330 --> 00:01:44,152
She just asked for more.

49
00:01:44,502 --> 00:01:45,639
In the sixties,

50
00:01:45,639 --> 00:01:47,912
I made it the soup-can way for

51
00:01:47,912 --> 00:01:48,972
every holiday.

52
00:01:49,152 --> 00:01:51,372
Then in nineteen eighty-eight,

53
00:01:51,372 --> 00:01:54,776
my daughter-in-law Linda made it from scratch,

54
00:01:54,776 --> 00:01:57,514
with fresh beans and her own mushroom

55
00:01:57,514 --> 00:01:59,808
sauce, and I tasted it and went

56
00:01:59,808 --> 00:02:00,251
quiet.

57
00:02:00,431 --> 00:02:02,562
It was like going from a black

58
00:02:02,562 --> 00:02:04,692
and white television to color.

59
00:02:04,872 --> 00:02:07,163
In a minute I'll show you exactly

60
00:02:07,163 --> 00:02:08,274
how she made it.

61
00:02:08,623 --> 00:02:10,299
Here's what you need,

62
00:02:10,299 --> 00:02:13,252
honey, for one nine by thirteen dish,

63
00:02:13,252 --> 00:02:14,928
about eight servings.

64
00:02:15,108 --> 00:02:17,604
One and a half pounds of fresh

65
00:02:17,604 --> 00:02:18,602
green beans.

66
00:02:18,782 --> 00:02:21,225
Eight ounces of mushrooms,

67
00:02:21,225 --> 00:02:21,882
sliced.

68
00:02:22,062 --> 00:02:23,284
Half an onion,

69
00:02:23,284 --> 00:02:24,419
chopped fine.

70
00:02:24,599 --> 00:02:26,491
Two cloves of garlic.

71
00:02:26,671 --> 00:02:29,144
Three tablespoons of butter.

72
00:02:29,324 --> 00:02:31,704
Three tablespoons of flour.

73
00:02:31,884 --> 00:02:33,893
One cup of chicken broth.

74
00:02:34,073 --> 00:02:36,022
One cup of milk or half and

75
00:02:36,022 --> 00:02:36,383
half.

76
00:02:36,563 --> 00:02:39,559
Salt, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg.

77
00:02:39,908 --> 00:02:41,244
And for the topping.

78
00:02:41,424 --> 00:02:42,730
Two big onions,

79
00:02:42,730 --> 00:02:44,732
sliced into thin rings.

80
00:02:44,912 --> 00:02:46,573
Half a cup of flour.

81
00:02:46,753 --> 00:02:48,575
A teaspoon of salt.

82
00:02:48,755 --> 00:02:50,381
And oil for frying.

83
00:02:50,561 --> 00:02:52,780
Or, if you're short on time,

84
00:02:52,780 --> 00:02:55,871
a can of the store-bought crispy onions

85
00:02:55,871 --> 00:02:56,505
is fine.

86
00:02:56,685 --> 00:02:59,065
Nobody will call the police.

87
00:02:59,245 --> 00:03:01,120
But in a few minutes I'll show

88
00:03:01,120 --> 00:03:03,307
you why the homemade ones are worth

89
00:03:03,307 --> 00:03:03,494
it.

90
00:03:03,844 --> 00:03:06,681
You can use frozen green beans,

91
00:03:06,681 --> 00:03:07,687
sweetheart.

92
00:03:07,867 --> 00:03:09,295
They work fine.

93
00:03:09,475 --> 00:03:11,774
Thaw them and pat them dry.

94
00:03:11,954 --> 00:03:14,915
But please, not canned beans.

95
00:03:15,095 --> 00:03:18,241
Canned green beans are already cooked soft,

96
00:03:18,241 --> 00:03:20,290
and by the time they bake in

97
00:03:20,290 --> 00:03:21,388
the oven again,

98
00:03:21,388 --> 00:03:22,339
they're mush.

99
00:03:22,519 --> 00:03:24,632
That's mistake number one,

100
00:03:24,632 --> 00:03:27,477
and it's the reason most green bean

101
00:03:27,477 --> 00:03:28,940
casserole is gray.

102
00:03:29,289 --> 00:03:30,137
Step one.

103
00:03:30,317 --> 00:03:32,657
Snap the ends off the fresh beans

104
00:03:32,657 --> 00:03:34,926
and cut them in two-inch pieces.

105
00:03:35,106 --> 00:03:37,291
Bring a big pot of salted water

106
00:03:37,291 --> 00:03:37,996
to a boil,

107
00:03:37,996 --> 00:03:40,110
and drop in the beans for only

108
00:03:40,110 --> 00:03:41,591
four or five minutes,

109
00:03:41,591 --> 00:03:44,551
until they're bright green and just barely

110
00:03:44,551 --> 00:03:45,044
tender.

111
00:03:45,224 --> 00:03:46,357
Then drain them,

112
00:03:46,357 --> 00:03:48,409
and put them right into a big

113
00:03:48,409 --> 00:03:49,683
bowl of ice water.

114
00:03:49,863 --> 00:03:51,712
Leave them five minutes,

115
00:03:51,712 --> 00:03:53,253
and drain them well.

116
00:03:53,602 --> 00:03:55,170
Why the ice water?

117
00:03:55,350 --> 00:03:56,879
It stops the cooking,

118
00:03:56,879 --> 00:03:59,354
so the beans stay bright green and

119
00:03:59,354 --> 00:04:00,737
keep a little snap.

120
00:04:00,917 --> 00:04:03,644
Mistake number two is skipping this,

121
00:04:03,644 --> 00:04:05,538
or boiling them too long.

122
00:04:05,718 --> 00:04:08,278
Remember, they're going in the oven again

123
00:04:08,278 --> 00:04:09,340
for half an hour.

124
00:04:09,520 --> 00:04:11,837
If they're soft before they go in,

125
00:04:11,837 --> 00:04:14,222
they'll be mush when they come out.

126
00:04:14,571 --> 00:04:17,479
And pick good beans at the store,

127
00:04:17,479 --> 00:04:18,008
honey.

128
00:04:18,188 --> 00:04:20,742
Fresh green beans should be bright and

129
00:04:20,742 --> 00:04:23,095
firm, and they should snap clean in

130
00:04:23,095 --> 00:04:25,178
half with a little pop when you

131
00:04:25,178 --> 00:04:25,851
bend them.

132
00:04:26,031 --> 00:04:28,469
If they bend like a rubber band,

133
00:04:28,469 --> 00:04:31,975
they're old, and they'll taste like cardboard.

134
00:04:32,155 --> 00:04:34,748
Grandma Pearl used to snap one in

135
00:04:34,748 --> 00:04:36,556
the store, right there,

136
00:04:36,556 --> 00:04:39,307
before she bought a single handful.

137
00:04:39,487 --> 00:04:40,903
The grocer hated it.

138
00:04:41,253 --> 00:04:43,701
Step two, the mushroom sauce,

139
00:04:43,701 --> 00:04:45,305
instead of the can.

140
00:04:45,485 --> 00:04:47,877
Melt the butter in a big skillet.

141
00:04:48,057 --> 00:04:50,699
Add the mushrooms and leave them alone

142
00:04:50,699 --> 00:04:53,202
for three or four minutes until they

143
00:04:53,202 --> 00:04:54,454
brown on one side.

144
00:04:54,634 --> 00:04:57,245
Don't crowd them and don't stir too

145
00:04:57,245 --> 00:04:57,618
soon.

146
00:04:57,798 --> 00:05:00,712
Brown mushrooms taste rich and meaty.

147
00:05:00,892 --> 00:05:03,853
Gray mushrooms taste like wet paper.

148
00:05:04,033 --> 00:05:06,204
Then add the onion and garlic and

149
00:05:06,204 --> 00:05:07,783
cook three more minutes.

150
00:05:08,132 --> 00:05:09,819
If this is helping you,

151
00:05:09,819 --> 00:05:12,312
honey, tap the like button for me.

152
00:05:12,492 --> 00:05:15,302
It helps Grandma more than you know.

153
00:05:15,482 --> 00:05:18,470
Now sprinkle the flour over the mushrooms

154
00:05:18,470 --> 00:05:20,219
and stir for one minute.

155
00:05:20,399 --> 00:05:22,117
Slowly pour in the broth,

156
00:05:22,117 --> 00:05:23,767
stirring the whole time,

157
00:05:23,767 --> 00:05:24,729
then the milk.

158
00:05:24,909 --> 00:05:27,559
Let it bubble gently for five minutes

159
00:05:27,559 --> 00:05:29,565
until it's thick like gravy.

160
00:05:29,745 --> 00:05:32,923
Add salt, pepper and a little pinch

161
00:05:32,923 --> 00:05:33,831
of nutmeg.

162
00:05:34,181 --> 00:05:35,633
Taste it, honey.

163
00:05:35,813 --> 00:05:38,111
This is mistake number three.

164
00:05:38,291 --> 00:05:40,254
An unseasoned sauce.

165
00:05:40,434 --> 00:05:42,327
Green beans soak up salt,

166
00:05:42,327 --> 00:05:44,903
so the sauce should taste a little

167
00:05:44,903 --> 00:05:46,494
too salty on its own.

168
00:05:46,674 --> 00:05:49,510
A splash of soy sauce or Worcestershire

169
00:05:49,510 --> 00:05:51,182
gives it a deep flavor,

170
00:05:51,182 --> 00:05:53,582
the way the canned soup tried to.

171
00:05:53,762 --> 00:05:56,200
Linda's secret was a spoon of sour

172
00:05:56,200 --> 00:05:58,209
cream stirred in at the end.

173
00:05:58,389 --> 00:06:00,118
Don't tell her I told you.

174
00:06:00,468 --> 00:06:02,405
So far, fresh beans,

175
00:06:02,405 --> 00:06:03,664
a quick boil,

176
00:06:03,664 --> 00:06:06,472
ice water, browned mushrooms,

177
00:06:06,472 --> 00:06:08,990
and a well-seasoned sauce.

178
00:06:09,170 --> 00:06:11,562
Now the onion trick I promised.

179
00:06:11,742 --> 00:06:13,806
Toss the thin onion rings in a

180
00:06:13,806 --> 00:06:15,732
bag with the flour and salt,

181
00:06:15,732 --> 00:06:18,209
and shake them until they're coated.

182
00:06:18,389 --> 00:06:20,583
Shake off the extra flour.

183
00:06:20,763 --> 00:06:22,836
Heat about half an inch of oil

184
00:06:22,836 --> 00:06:25,186
in a heavy skillet to medium-high.

185
00:06:25,536 --> 00:06:27,918
Fry the onions in small batches,

186
00:06:27,918 --> 00:06:29,481
two or three minutes,

187
00:06:29,481 --> 00:06:32,607
stirring, until they're deep golden brown.

188
00:06:32,787 --> 00:06:35,360
Lift them out onto paper towels and

189
00:06:35,360 --> 00:06:37,419
sprinkle with a little salt.

190
00:06:37,599 --> 00:06:40,188
They get crispier as they cool.

191
00:06:40,368 --> 00:06:42,416
And they taste so good you'll have

192
00:06:42,416 --> 00:06:43,259
to guard them.

193
00:06:43,439 --> 00:06:45,709
My grandchildren eat a third of them

194
00:06:45,709 --> 00:06:48,041
off the paper towels before they ever

195
00:06:48,041 --> 00:06:49,302
reach the casserole.

196
00:06:49,652 --> 00:06:51,744
And here's the real secret,

197
00:06:51,744 --> 00:06:53,681
the one people ask about.

198
00:06:53,861 --> 00:06:56,291
Mistake number four is putting all the

199
00:06:56,291 --> 00:06:57,762
onions on at the start.

200
00:06:57,942 --> 00:07:00,369
They get soggy under the oven heat.

201
00:07:00,549 --> 00:07:02,858
Mix half of the onions into the

202
00:07:02,858 --> 00:07:04,050
beans and sauce,

203
00:07:04,050 --> 00:07:06,434
so you get onion flavor in every

204
00:07:06,434 --> 00:07:06,806
bite.

205
00:07:06,986 --> 00:07:09,145
Save the other half and put them

206
00:07:09,145 --> 00:07:11,102
on top only for the last five

207
00:07:11,102 --> 00:07:11,642
minutes.

208
00:07:11,822 --> 00:07:13,645
That's how they stay crispy.

209
00:07:13,994 --> 00:07:16,168
If frying makes you nervous,

210
00:07:16,168 --> 00:07:18,963
sweetheart, bake the onions instead.

211
00:07:19,143 --> 00:07:21,485
Toss the floured rings with a few

212
00:07:21,485 --> 00:07:22,478
spoons of oil,

213
00:07:22,478 --> 00:07:24,749
spread them on a baking sheet in

214
00:07:24,749 --> 00:07:27,019
one layer, and bake them at four

215
00:07:27,019 --> 00:07:30,212
hundred twenty-five for about twenty minutes,

216
00:07:30,212 --> 00:07:31,702
turning them halfway,

217
00:07:31,702 --> 00:07:33,192
until they're golden.

218
00:07:33,372 --> 00:07:35,560
Not quite as crisp as fried,

219
00:07:35,560 --> 00:07:38,217
but close, and no splatter on your

220
00:07:38,217 --> 00:07:40,953
stove the day before company comes.

221
00:07:41,302 --> 00:07:42,394
Step four.

222
00:07:42,574 --> 00:07:45,058
Heat the oven to three hundred fifty.

223
00:07:45,238 --> 00:07:47,943
Stir the beans into the mushroom sauce

224
00:07:47,943 --> 00:07:49,437
with half the onions,

225
00:07:49,437 --> 00:07:51,714
and spread it in a buttered nine

226
00:07:51,714 --> 00:07:52,924
by thirteen dish.

227
00:07:53,104 --> 00:07:55,048
Bake for twenty-five minutes,

228
00:07:55,048 --> 00:07:57,260
until it's bubbling at the edges.

229
00:07:57,440 --> 00:07:59,893
Then pile the rest of the crispy

230
00:07:59,893 --> 00:08:00,967
onions on top,

231
00:08:00,967 --> 00:08:03,036
and bake five more minutes.

232
00:08:03,216 --> 00:08:06,316
Let it rest five minutes before serving.

233
00:08:06,666 --> 00:08:08,406
And you can make it ahead,

234
00:08:08,406 --> 00:08:10,547
which is a blessing on a holiday

235
00:08:10,547 --> 00:08:12,019
when the oven is full.

236
00:08:12,199 --> 00:08:14,644
Make the beans and sauce the day

237
00:08:14,644 --> 00:08:15,942
before, mix them,

238
00:08:15,942 --> 00:08:17,547
put them in the dish,

239
00:08:17,547 --> 00:08:19,686
cover it, and keep it in the

240
00:08:19,686 --> 00:08:20,221
icebox.

241
00:08:20,401 --> 00:08:23,054
Fry the onions the day before too,

242
00:08:23,054 --> 00:08:25,239
and keep them in a paper bag

243
00:08:25,239 --> 00:08:26,409
on the counter,

244
00:08:26,409 --> 00:08:27,814
not in the icebox,

245
00:08:27,814 --> 00:08:29,062
or they go soft.

246
00:08:29,242 --> 00:08:31,645
Add ten minutes to the baking time.

247
00:08:31,995 --> 00:08:34,609
And don't save it only for Thanksgiving,

248
00:08:34,609 --> 00:08:35,327
sweetheart.

249
00:08:35,507 --> 00:08:38,840
Green bean casserole is a wonderful weeknight

250
00:08:38,840 --> 00:08:40,987
side dish with a pork chop or

251
00:08:40,987 --> 00:08:42,172
a roast chicken.

252
00:08:42,352 --> 00:08:44,839
Make half the recipe in an eight

253
00:08:44,839 --> 00:08:45,927
by eight dish.

254
00:08:46,107 --> 00:08:48,626
Add some shredded chicken or ham,

255
00:08:48,626 --> 00:08:50,916
and it's a whole supper in one

256
00:08:50,916 --> 00:08:51,297
dish.

257
00:08:51,477 --> 00:08:54,589
Linda calls that her lazy Tuesday casserole.

258
00:08:54,938 --> 00:08:56,906
And if you do want the quick

259
00:08:56,906 --> 00:08:58,382
version with the can,

260
00:08:58,382 --> 00:09:00,140
honey, I won't judge you.

261
00:09:00,320 --> 00:09:02,584
Here's how to make it taste better.

262
00:09:02,764 --> 00:09:05,317
Use fresh or frozen beans,

263
00:09:05,317 --> 00:09:06,398
not canned.

264
00:09:06,578 --> 00:09:09,262
Brown some fresh mushrooms in butter and

265
00:09:09,262 --> 00:09:10,873
stir them into the soup.

266
00:09:11,053 --> 00:09:13,467
Add a splash of soy sauce and

267
00:09:13,467 --> 00:09:14,966
some black pepper.

268
00:09:15,146 --> 00:09:17,561
And save half the onions for the

269
00:09:17,561 --> 00:09:17,862
end.

270
00:09:18,042 --> 00:09:20,267
It's ninety percent as good,

271
00:09:20,267 --> 00:09:21,618
in half the time.

272
00:09:21,968 --> 00:09:24,832
Leftovers keep three or four days in

273
00:09:24,832 --> 00:09:25,707
the icebox.

274
00:09:25,887 --> 00:09:27,517
Warm them in the oven,

275
00:09:27,517 --> 00:09:28,851
not the microwave,

276
00:09:28,851 --> 00:09:30,926
so the beans don't go mushy.

277
00:09:31,106 --> 00:09:33,677
And put fresh crispy onions on top

278
00:09:33,677 --> 00:09:34,962
when you warm it,

279
00:09:34,962 --> 00:09:36,551
if you have any left.

280
00:09:36,731 --> 00:09:37,543
You won't.

281
00:09:37,723 --> 00:09:40,133
Nobody ever has onions left,

282
00:09:40,133 --> 00:09:40,649
honey.

283
00:09:40,999 --> 00:09:42,358
So one more time.

284
00:09:42,538 --> 00:09:44,537
Fresh or frozen beans,

285
00:09:44,537 --> 00:09:45,719
never canned.

286
00:09:45,899 --> 00:09:47,533
Boil four minutes,

287
00:09:47,533 --> 00:09:48,894
then ice water.

288
00:09:49,074 --> 00:09:51,888
Brown the mushrooms in butter for a

289
00:09:51,888 --> 00:09:54,380
real sauce, and season it well.

290
00:09:54,560 --> 00:09:56,267
Fry your own onions.

291
00:09:56,447 --> 00:09:58,011
Half in the casserole,

292
00:09:58,011 --> 00:10:00,073
half on top for only the last

293
00:10:00,073 --> 00:10:00,998
five minutes.

294
00:10:01,178 --> 00:10:04,208
That's green bean casserole the way it

295
00:10:04,208 --> 00:10:06,361
should taste, bright green,

296
00:10:06,361 --> 00:10:08,434
creamy, and crispy on top.

297
00:10:08,784 --> 00:10:10,671
Tell me in the comments,

298
00:10:10,671 --> 00:10:11,536
sweetheart.

299
00:10:11,716 --> 00:10:15,182
Green bean casserole at your holiday table,

300
00:10:15,182 --> 00:10:15,988
yes or no?

301
00:10:16,168 --> 00:10:18,630
I know some families fight about it.

302
00:10:18,810 --> 00:10:21,901
The whole playlist of Grandma's recipes is

303
00:10:21,901 --> 00:10:23,888
right there on your screen,

304
00:10:23,888 --> 00:10:25,949
and I'll see you in the next

305
00:10:25,949 --> 00:10:26,391
video.

306
00:10:26,571 --> 00:10:28,208
Good night, honey.
