1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:03,577
Sweetheart, the best Christmas present I ever

2
00:00:03,577 --> 00:00:05,723
got cost about forty cents.

3
00:00:05,903 --> 00:00:07,990
It was a jar of my mother's

4
00:00:07,990 --> 00:00:10,617
apple butter, with a square of red

5
00:00:10,617 --> 00:00:13,322
calico tied on the lid with string.

6
00:00:13,502 --> 00:00:14,598
I was twenty,

7
00:00:14,598 --> 00:00:18,141
newly married, living in a tiny apartment,

8
00:00:18,141 --> 00:00:19,237
and homesick.

9
00:00:19,417 --> 00:00:21,674
I opened that jar and the whole

10
00:00:21,674 --> 00:00:24,003
kitchen smelled like Elm Street.

11
00:00:24,183 --> 00:00:26,215
I cried into my toast.

12
00:00:26,564 --> 00:00:29,291
So tonight I'm giving you nine homemade

13
00:00:29,291 --> 00:00:32,366
Christmas gifts from the kitchen that people

14
00:00:32,366 --> 00:00:35,232
actually love, all for under five dollars

15
00:00:35,232 --> 00:00:37,259
each, and how to wrap them so

16
00:00:37,259 --> 00:00:39,426
they look like they came from a

17
00:00:39,426 --> 00:00:40,195
fancy shop.

18
00:00:40,375 --> 00:00:41,699
And stay with me,

19
00:00:41,699 --> 00:00:44,193
because the last one is the gift

20
00:00:44,193 --> 00:00:45,908
people keep for years,

21
00:00:45,908 --> 00:00:47,700
and it isn't even food.

22
00:00:48,050 --> 00:00:49,786
When I was a girl in the

23
00:00:49,786 --> 00:00:52,607
fifties, nobody on our street had money

24
00:00:52,607 --> 00:00:54,993
for store presents for everybody.

25
00:00:55,173 --> 00:00:57,484
So the women gave from the kitchen.

26
00:00:57,664 --> 00:00:58,604
Mrs.

27
00:00:58,784 --> 00:01:01,594
Kowalski gave poppy seed bread.

28
00:01:01,774 --> 00:01:02,749
Mrs.

29
00:01:02,929 --> 00:01:05,321
MacLeod gave shortbread.

30
00:01:05,501 --> 00:01:08,566
My mother gave apple butter and fudge.

31
00:01:08,746 --> 00:01:10,878
And every one of those gifts was

32
00:01:10,878 --> 00:01:13,743
remembered longer than any sweater from the

33
00:01:13,743 --> 00:01:14,876
department store.

34
00:01:15,225 --> 00:01:16,693
A store gift says,

35
00:01:16,693 --> 00:01:19,057
I thought of you at the mall.

36
00:01:19,237 --> 00:01:20,790
A kitchen gift says,

37
00:01:20,790 --> 00:01:22,965
I thought of you for a whole

38
00:01:22,965 --> 00:01:23,741
afternoon.

39
00:01:23,921 --> 00:01:25,509
That's the difference,

40
00:01:25,509 --> 00:01:25,942
honey.

41
00:01:26,122 --> 00:01:28,875
And it's the one gift nobody can

42
00:01:28,875 --> 00:01:29,477
return.

43
00:01:29,657 --> 00:01:31,579
In a minute I'll tell you the

44
00:01:31,579 --> 00:01:33,699
one rule for every kitchen gift,

45
00:01:33,699 --> 00:01:36,019
the one that makes a two-dollar jar

46
00:01:36,019 --> 00:01:37,145
look like twenty.

47
00:01:37,496 --> 00:01:38,587
Number one.

48
00:01:38,767 --> 00:01:40,950
Sugared spiced pecans.

49
00:01:41,130 --> 00:01:43,320
Whisk one egg white with a spoon

50
00:01:43,320 --> 00:01:45,100
of water until it's foamy.

51
00:01:45,280 --> 00:01:47,846
Toss in a pound of pecan halves.

52
00:01:48,026 --> 00:01:50,240
Then toss them with a cup of

53
00:01:50,240 --> 00:01:52,612
sugar, a teaspoon of cinnamon,

54
00:01:52,612 --> 00:01:54,114
a teaspoon of salt,

55
00:01:54,114 --> 00:01:55,932
and a pinch of cayenne.

56
00:01:56,112 --> 00:01:58,392
Spread them on a baking sheet and

57
00:01:58,392 --> 00:02:00,603
bake at two hundred fifty for an

58
00:02:00,603 --> 00:02:03,160
hour, stirring every fifteen minutes.

59
00:02:03,510 --> 00:02:05,812
They come out crackly and sweet and

60
00:02:05,812 --> 00:02:07,654
a little bit hot at the end.

61
00:02:07,834 --> 00:02:11,217
A pound of pecans fills four little

62
00:02:11,217 --> 00:02:11,700
jars.

63
00:02:11,880 --> 00:02:14,390
My husband used to hide one jar

64
00:02:14,390 --> 00:02:16,494
in the garage for himself,

65
00:02:16,494 --> 00:02:18,275
behind the paint cans,

66
00:02:18,275 --> 00:02:20,460
and pretend I'd miscounted.

67
00:02:20,640 --> 00:02:22,484
I never miscounted,

68
00:02:22,484 --> 00:02:23,067
honey.

69
00:02:23,247 --> 00:02:25,487
I just let him think I did.

70
00:02:25,838 --> 00:02:26,964
Number two.

71
00:02:27,144 --> 00:02:28,897
Cookie mix in a jar.

72
00:02:29,077 --> 00:02:30,629
In a quart mason jar,

73
00:02:30,629 --> 00:02:33,807
layer the dry ingredients for your favorite

74
00:02:33,807 --> 00:02:34,324
cookie.

75
00:02:34,504 --> 00:02:37,198
Flour with the baking soda and salt

76
00:02:37,198 --> 00:02:38,276
on the bottom,

77
00:02:38,276 --> 00:02:39,584
then brown sugar,

78
00:02:39,584 --> 00:02:41,894
packed down, then white sugar,

79
00:02:41,894 --> 00:02:44,895
then oats, then chocolate chips on top.

80
00:02:45,075 --> 00:02:48,164
The stripes look beautiful through the glass.

81
00:02:48,344 --> 00:02:50,303
Then tie a card on the lid

82
00:02:50,303 --> 00:02:52,489
with what to add and how long

83
00:02:52,489 --> 00:02:53,092
to bake.

84
00:02:53,442 --> 00:02:55,983
Pack every layer down hard with the

85
00:02:55,983 --> 00:02:57,726
bottom of a small glass,

86
00:02:57,726 --> 00:03:00,049
so they stay neat and don't mix.

87
00:03:00,229 --> 00:03:02,887
That's the mistake most people make.

88
00:03:03,067 --> 00:03:05,290
And write the card by hand,

89
00:03:05,290 --> 00:03:05,784
honey.

90
00:03:05,964 --> 00:03:07,983
Add one stick of butter,

91
00:03:07,983 --> 00:03:10,759
one egg, one teaspoon of vanilla.

92
00:03:10,939 --> 00:03:13,830
Bake at three seventy-five for ten minutes.

93
00:03:14,010 --> 00:03:16,576
The young mothers at my church love

94
00:03:16,576 --> 00:03:19,803
these, because their children can make them.

95
00:03:20,154 --> 00:03:21,465
Number three.

96
00:03:21,645 --> 00:03:23,403
Fudge or chocolate bark,

97
00:03:23,403 --> 00:03:25,673
cut in squares and stacked in a

98
00:03:25,673 --> 00:03:27,870
little tin or a paper box with

99
00:03:27,870 --> 00:03:29,993
wax paper between the layers.

100
00:03:30,173 --> 00:03:32,975
A batch of fudge costs about six

101
00:03:32,975 --> 00:03:35,514
dollars and fills five boxes.

102
00:03:35,694 --> 00:03:37,354
Bark is even easier.

103
00:03:37,534 --> 00:03:40,008
Melt chocolate, spread it thin,

104
00:03:40,008 --> 00:03:42,562
and scatter crushed candy canes,

105
00:03:42,562 --> 00:03:45,196
nuts or dried cranberries on top.

106
00:03:45,376 --> 00:03:47,662
I have whole videos on both on

107
00:03:47,662 --> 00:03:48,500
my channel.

108
00:03:48,850 --> 00:03:51,060
And a word about fudge as a

109
00:03:51,060 --> 00:03:52,042
gift, honey.

110
00:03:52,222 --> 00:03:53,260
Cut it small,

111
00:03:53,260 --> 00:03:56,692
one-inch squares, because fudge is rich and

112
00:03:56,692 --> 00:03:58,847
people eat it a little at a

113
00:03:58,847 --> 00:03:59,246
time.

114
00:03:59,426 --> 00:04:01,791
Put each square in a tiny paper

115
00:04:01,791 --> 00:04:04,460
candy cup, the kind for muffins but

116
00:04:04,460 --> 00:04:04,918
small.

117
00:04:05,098 --> 00:04:06,870
Twelve squares in a box,

118
00:04:06,870 --> 00:04:08,789
each in its own paper cup,

119
00:04:08,789 --> 00:04:11,595
looks like something from a candy shop

120
00:04:11,595 --> 00:04:12,702
on Main Street.

121
00:04:12,882 --> 00:04:15,119
My mother learned that from the lady

122
00:04:15,119 --> 00:04:16,423
at the five and dime.

123
00:04:16,774 --> 00:04:19,740
Number four, and this is the cheapest

124
00:04:19,740 --> 00:04:21,023
one on the list.

125
00:04:21,203 --> 00:04:22,491
Flavored sugar.

126
00:04:22,671 --> 00:04:24,632
Put two cups of sugar in a

127
00:04:24,632 --> 00:04:26,895
jar with a split vanilla bean,

128
00:04:26,895 --> 00:04:28,781
or the peel of an orange,

129
00:04:28,781 --> 00:04:30,666
or a few cinnamon sticks,

130
00:04:30,666 --> 00:04:32,552
and let it sit two weeks.

131
00:04:32,732 --> 00:04:35,691
Or mix coarse salt with dried rosemary

132
00:04:35,691 --> 00:04:37,794
and lemon zest for cooking.

133
00:04:37,974 --> 00:04:39,900
It costs about a dollar a jar,

134
00:04:39,900 --> 00:04:42,084
and it looks like something from a

135
00:04:42,084 --> 00:04:42,919
gourmet shop.

136
00:04:43,270 --> 00:04:44,947
If this is helping you,

137
00:04:44,947 --> 00:04:47,426
honey, tap the like button for me.

138
00:04:47,606 --> 00:04:50,427
It helps Grandma more than you know.

139
00:04:50,607 --> 00:04:53,049
And now the one rule I promised

140
00:04:53,049 --> 00:04:55,728
you, for every single gift on this

141
00:04:55,728 --> 00:04:56,122
list.

142
00:04:56,302 --> 00:04:57,959
Make the jar beautiful,

143
00:04:57,959 --> 00:04:59,831
and keep the label simple.

144
00:05:00,011 --> 00:05:00,977
A clean jar,

145
00:05:00,977 --> 00:05:03,632
a square of fabric or brown paper

146
00:05:03,632 --> 00:05:04,517
on the lid,

147
00:05:04,517 --> 00:05:06,287
real string or ribbon,

148
00:05:06,287 --> 00:05:08,057
and a handwritten tag.

149
00:05:08,237 --> 00:05:10,662
That's what makes it look like twenty

150
00:05:10,662 --> 00:05:11,186
dollars.

151
00:05:11,536 --> 00:05:12,731
Number five.

152
00:05:12,911 --> 00:05:15,187
Homemade hot cocoa mix.

153
00:05:15,367 --> 00:05:17,655
Mix two cups of powdered milk,

154
00:05:17,655 --> 00:05:19,639
one cup of powdered sugar,

155
00:05:19,639 --> 00:05:22,003
three quarters of a cup of good

156
00:05:22,003 --> 00:05:24,597
cocoa powder, and a pinch of salt.

157
00:05:24,777 --> 00:05:26,004
Put it in a jar,

158
00:05:26,004 --> 00:05:28,919
with a little bag of mini marshmallows

159
00:05:28,919 --> 00:05:29,456
on top.

160
00:05:29,636 --> 00:05:32,017
Three big spoons in a mug of

161
00:05:32,017 --> 00:05:33,548
hot water or milk.

162
00:05:33,728 --> 00:05:35,690
Add a candy cane tied to the

163
00:05:35,690 --> 00:05:37,862
side, and you have a gift every

164
00:05:37,862 --> 00:05:39,684
child in the family wants.

165
00:05:40,035 --> 00:05:41,315
Sift the cocoa,

166
00:05:41,315 --> 00:05:43,877
sweetheart, that's the secret.

167
00:05:44,057 --> 00:05:47,181
Unsifted cocoa makes lumps that float on

168
00:05:47,181 --> 00:05:49,758
top of the mug like little rocks,

169
00:05:49,758 --> 00:05:51,476
and nobody likes that.

170
00:05:51,656 --> 00:05:54,090
Sift it with the sugar right into

171
00:05:54,090 --> 00:05:56,376
the bowl, then stir in the milk

172
00:05:56,376 --> 00:05:56,892
powder.

173
00:05:57,072 --> 00:06:00,126
It'll dissolve smooth every time.

174
00:06:00,306 --> 00:06:04,323
My grandson calls it Grandma's magic dust.

175
00:06:04,673 --> 00:06:05,834
Number six.

176
00:06:06,014 --> 00:06:07,750
A loaf of quick bread,

177
00:06:07,750 --> 00:06:11,064
wrapped in parchment and tied with string.

178
00:06:11,244 --> 00:06:13,899
Pumpkin bread, banana bread,

179
00:06:13,899 --> 00:06:15,795
or cranberry orange.

180
00:06:15,975 --> 00:06:18,677
One batch makes four little loaves in

181
00:06:18,677 --> 00:06:19,846
small foil pans,

182
00:06:19,846 --> 00:06:22,256
and they freeze for three months.

183
00:06:22,436 --> 00:06:24,466
So I bake them the first week

184
00:06:24,466 --> 00:06:26,846
of December and pull one out every

185
00:06:26,846 --> 00:06:29,646
time somebody surprises me with a visit.

186
00:06:29,996 --> 00:06:31,923
So far, spiced nuts,

187
00:06:31,923 --> 00:06:33,850
cookie mix in a jar,

188
00:06:33,850 --> 00:06:35,295
fudge and bark,

189
00:06:35,295 --> 00:06:37,800
flavored sugar, cocoa mix,

190
00:06:37,800 --> 00:06:39,342
and quick bread.

191
00:06:39,522 --> 00:06:41,844
And here's a tip for the bread.

192
00:06:42,024 --> 00:06:44,436
Let the loaves cool completely,

193
00:06:44,436 --> 00:06:45,370
all the way,

194
00:06:45,370 --> 00:06:47,004
before you wrap them.

195
00:06:47,184 --> 00:06:48,214
Wrap them warm,

196
00:06:48,214 --> 00:06:50,411
and the steam makes the tops wet

197
00:06:50,411 --> 00:06:51,921
and sticky by morning.

198
00:06:52,101 --> 00:06:54,155
Cool bread, then parchment,

199
00:06:54,155 --> 00:06:56,665
then string, then a sprig of pine

200
00:06:56,665 --> 00:06:58,034
tucked in the bow.

201
00:06:58,383 --> 00:06:59,556
Number seven.

202
00:06:59,736 --> 00:07:01,350
The one my mother made.

203
00:07:01,530 --> 00:07:03,922
Apple butter in the slow cooker.

204
00:07:04,102 --> 00:07:06,922
Peel and slice six pounds of apples,

205
00:07:06,922 --> 00:07:08,881
add a cup of brown sugar,

206
00:07:08,881 --> 00:07:10,918
two teaspoons of cinnamon,

207
00:07:10,918 --> 00:07:13,034
a little nutmeg and cloves,

208
00:07:13,034 --> 00:07:15,071
and cook it on low for ten

209
00:07:15,071 --> 00:07:18,126
hours, until it's dark brown and thick.

210
00:07:18,306 --> 00:07:19,627
Blend it smooth,

211
00:07:19,627 --> 00:07:22,022
and spoon it into clean jars.

212
00:07:22,202 --> 00:07:25,197
It keeps three weeks in the icebox.

213
00:07:25,546 --> 00:07:27,731
And you don't have to know how

214
00:07:27,731 --> 00:07:28,751
to can, honey.

215
00:07:28,931 --> 00:07:30,987
Just tell people to keep it in

216
00:07:30,987 --> 00:07:33,318
the icebox and use it within three

217
00:07:33,318 --> 00:07:34,689
weeks, or freeze it.

218
00:07:34,869 --> 00:07:36,908
Nobody has ever let a jar of

219
00:07:36,908 --> 00:07:39,456
apple butter last three weeks in my

220
00:07:39,456 --> 00:07:39,966
family.

221
00:07:40,146 --> 00:07:42,452
My brother Danny eats his with a

222
00:07:42,452 --> 00:07:44,686
spoon, standing at the counter.

223
00:07:45,035 --> 00:07:45,964
Number eight.

224
00:07:46,144 --> 00:07:48,153
For the young cook in the family.

225
00:07:48,333 --> 00:07:50,964
A basket, or a big mixing bowl,

226
00:07:50,964 --> 00:07:53,256
filled with a wooden spoon,

227
00:07:53,256 --> 00:07:54,529
a good spatula,

228
00:07:54,529 --> 00:07:56,567
a set of measuring cups,

229
00:07:56,567 --> 00:07:58,689
a bag of chocolate chips,

230
00:07:58,689 --> 00:08:01,914
and your best cookie recipe written on

231
00:08:01,914 --> 00:08:02,509
a card.

232
00:08:02,689 --> 00:08:04,070
Put a bow on the bowl.

233
00:08:04,250 --> 00:08:05,996
It costs a little more,

234
00:08:05,996 --> 00:08:07,667
maybe fifteen dollars,

235
00:08:07,667 --> 00:08:10,552
but it starts somebody cooking for the

236
00:08:10,552 --> 00:08:11,994
rest of their life.

237
00:08:12,343 --> 00:08:14,729
And put a little something extra in

238
00:08:14,729 --> 00:08:15,478
the basket.

239
00:08:15,658 --> 00:08:18,488
A dish towel with a Christmas print,

240
00:08:18,488 --> 00:08:19,431
or an apron.

241
00:08:19,611 --> 00:08:20,714
A pot holder.

242
00:08:20,894 --> 00:08:23,508
For my granddaughter's first apartment,

243
00:08:23,508 --> 00:08:25,519
I tucked in a little card with

244
00:08:25,519 --> 00:08:27,530
my phone number and the words,

245
00:08:27,530 --> 00:08:29,474
call me when it doesn't work.

246
00:08:29,654 --> 00:08:32,593
She called me eleven times that first

247
00:08:32,593 --> 00:08:33,149
winter.

248
00:08:33,329 --> 00:08:35,279
Best gift I ever gave,

249
00:08:35,279 --> 00:08:38,205
because I got eleven phone calls.

250
00:08:38,554 --> 00:08:39,735
And number nine,

251
00:08:39,735 --> 00:08:42,023
the gift people keep for years,

252
00:08:42,023 --> 00:08:44,016
the one I told you about at

253
00:08:44,016 --> 00:08:44,754
the start.

254
00:08:44,934 --> 00:08:46,443
It isn't food at all.

255
00:08:46,623 --> 00:08:48,620
It's the recipe itself.

256
00:08:48,800 --> 00:08:51,367
Write your family's best recipe on a

257
00:08:51,367 --> 00:08:53,506
card, in your own handwriting,

258
00:08:53,506 --> 00:08:54,861
with a little note.

259
00:08:55,041 --> 00:08:56,573
Who taught it to you,

260
00:08:56,573 --> 00:08:58,617
and one memory of eating it.

261
00:08:58,797 --> 00:09:01,023
Then tuck it in with whatever you're

262
00:09:01,023 --> 00:09:01,455
giving.

263
00:09:01,805 --> 00:09:04,615
My mother's apple butter is long gone,

264
00:09:04,615 --> 00:09:05,428
sweetheart.

265
00:09:05,608 --> 00:09:07,511
But I still have the card she

266
00:09:07,511 --> 00:09:10,136
tied to that jar in nineteen sixty-four.

267
00:09:10,316 --> 00:09:12,498
Her handwriting, in blue ink.

268
00:09:12,678 --> 00:09:15,785
To Ruthie, so you're never homesick at

269
00:09:15,785 --> 00:09:16,603
Christmas.

270
00:09:16,783 --> 00:09:18,512
Love, Mama.

271
00:09:18,692 --> 00:09:20,638
It's in my recipe box,

272
00:09:20,638 --> 00:09:23,644
and it's the most valuable thing I

273
00:09:23,644 --> 00:09:23,998
own.

274
00:09:24,178 --> 00:09:26,919
Your handwriting is a gift nobody else

275
00:09:26,919 --> 00:09:27,568
can give.

276
00:09:27,919 --> 00:09:29,579
A few last tips.

277
00:09:29,759 --> 00:09:32,256
Buy your jars after Christmas,

278
00:09:32,256 --> 00:09:34,171
on sale, for next year.

279
00:09:34,351 --> 00:09:36,963
Save the pretty tins people give you.

280
00:09:37,143 --> 00:09:38,937
Brown paper lunch bags,

281
00:09:38,937 --> 00:09:41,901
folded over and punched with two holes

282
00:09:41,901 --> 00:09:45,177
for ribbon, make perfect bags for cookies.

283
00:09:45,357 --> 00:09:48,236
And always label anything with nuts.

284
00:09:48,416 --> 00:09:51,035
Somebody at the church party always has

285
00:09:51,035 --> 00:09:53,185
an allergy, and you want them to

286
00:09:53,185 --> 00:09:53,722
be safe.

287
00:09:54,072 --> 00:09:55,662
So one more time.

288
00:09:55,842 --> 00:09:57,386
Spiced pecans.

289
00:09:57,566 --> 00:09:59,575
Cookie mix in a jar.

290
00:09:59,755 --> 00:10:01,113
Fudge and bark.

291
00:10:01,293 --> 00:10:02,501
Flavored sugar.

292
00:10:02,681 --> 00:10:03,830
Cocoa mix.

293
00:10:04,010 --> 00:10:05,124
Quick bread.

294
00:10:05,304 --> 00:10:06,500
Apple butter.

295
00:10:06,680 --> 00:10:09,176
A baking bowl for the young cook.

296
00:10:09,356 --> 00:10:11,040
And your own recipe,

297
00:10:11,040 --> 00:10:13,060
in your own handwriting.

298
00:10:13,240 --> 00:10:14,909
Make the jar beautiful,

299
00:10:14,909 --> 00:10:16,505
keep the label simple,

300
00:10:16,505 --> 00:10:18,174
and give it with a hug.

301
00:10:18,354 --> 00:10:20,874
That's how my mother did Christmas on

302
00:10:20,874 --> 00:10:21,895
almost nothing.

303
00:10:22,246 --> 00:10:24,236
Tell me in the comments,

304
00:10:24,236 --> 00:10:25,148
sweetheart.

305
00:10:25,328 --> 00:10:28,397
What's the best homemade gift anybody ever

306
00:10:28,397 --> 00:10:29,055
gave you?

307
00:10:29,235 --> 00:10:31,011
I read every one.

308
00:10:31,191 --> 00:10:34,425
The whole playlist of Grandma's Christmas tips

309
00:10:34,425 --> 00:10:36,533
is right there on your screen,

310
00:10:36,533 --> 00:10:38,502
and I'll see you in the next

311
00:10:38,502 --> 00:10:38,923
video.

312
00:10:39,103 --> 00:10:40,775
Good night, honey.

313
00:10:40,955 --> 00:10:42,488
Merry Christmas.
uEAq4TsCpUk:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:02,302
Sweetheart, in nineteen sixty-eight,

2
00:00:02,302 --> 00:00:04,924
there wasn't a Christmas party in America

3
00:00:04,924 --> 00:00:07,163
without a cheese ball on the table.

4
00:00:07,343 --> 00:00:08,798
Round as a snowball,

5
00:00:08,798 --> 00:00:10,617
rolled in chopped pecans,

6
00:00:10,617 --> 00:00:13,164
sitting on a plate of crackers with

7
00:00:13,164 --> 00:00:15,493
a little knife stuck in the top.

8
00:00:15,673 --> 00:00:18,007
People stood around it all night.

9
00:00:18,187 --> 00:00:20,360
The cheese ball was where all the

10
00:00:20,360 --> 00:00:21,414
gossip happened.

11
00:00:21,764 --> 00:00:24,761
But today, people tell me theirs tastes

12
00:00:24,761 --> 00:00:26,605
like plain cream cheese,

13
00:00:26,605 --> 00:00:28,603
or it melts into a puddle,

14
00:00:28,603 --> 00:00:30,217
or the nuts fall off.

15
00:00:30,397 --> 00:00:33,059
So tonight I'm giving you my Christmas

16
00:00:33,059 --> 00:00:34,741
cheese ball, every step,

17
00:00:34,741 --> 00:00:37,123
and the four mistakes that make it

18
00:00:37,123 --> 00:00:38,315
bland and sloppy.

19
00:00:38,495 --> 00:00:39,547
And stay with me,

20
00:00:39,547 --> 00:00:41,529
because the last trick is how to

21
00:00:41,529 --> 00:00:43,820
make it look like a Christmas present

22
00:00:43,820 --> 00:00:44,625
on the table.

23
00:00:44,975 --> 00:00:47,351
The cheese ball came into fashion in

24
00:00:47,351 --> 00:00:48,935
the fifties and sixties,

25
00:00:48,935 --> 00:00:51,443
when cream cheese was new and exciting

26
00:00:51,443 --> 00:00:54,347
and every hostess wanted something she could

27
00:00:54,347 --> 00:00:55,667
make the day before.

28
00:00:55,847 --> 00:00:59,325
Women's magazines printed a new cheese ball

29
00:00:59,325 --> 00:01:00,538
every December.

30
00:01:00,718 --> 00:01:02,542
Port wine cheese balls,

31
00:01:02,542 --> 00:01:04,049
bacon cheese balls,

32
00:01:04,049 --> 00:01:05,873
pineapple cheese balls.

33
00:01:06,053 --> 00:01:08,160
My mother tried every one,

34
00:01:08,160 --> 00:01:10,430
and my father ate every one.

35
00:01:10,780 --> 00:01:13,847
Mine came from my neighbor Betty Hartman,

36
00:01:13,847 --> 00:01:15,493
in nineteen sixty-six.

37
00:01:15,673 --> 00:01:18,296
She brought it to the church Christmas

38
00:01:18,296 --> 00:01:20,781
party, and people kept going back to

39
00:01:20,781 --> 00:01:23,266
it until the plate was licked clean.

40
00:01:23,446 --> 00:01:25,833
I followed her into the kitchen and

41
00:01:25,833 --> 00:01:27,266
asked for the recipe.

42
00:01:27,446 --> 00:01:29,686
She made me promise never to tell.

43
00:01:29,866 --> 00:01:32,612
Betty passed in two thousand nine,

44
00:01:32,612 --> 00:01:35,439
honey, so I think it's alright now.

45
00:01:35,790 --> 00:01:38,680
And Betty's secret wasn't one thing.

46
00:01:38,860 --> 00:01:40,312
It was three.

47
00:01:40,492 --> 00:01:42,512
In a minute I'll tell you all

48
00:01:42,512 --> 00:01:45,298
three, and they're the reason her cheese

49
00:01:45,298 --> 00:01:47,179
ball tasted like something,

50
00:01:47,179 --> 00:01:49,965
and everybody else's tasted like a block

51
00:01:49,965 --> 00:01:52,195
of cream cheese with nuts on it.

52
00:01:52,545 --> 00:01:55,209
My mother's favorite was a port wine

53
00:01:55,209 --> 00:01:58,392
cheese ball, pink as a ballerina's slipper,

54
00:01:58,392 --> 00:02:00,464
from a recipe on the back of

55
00:02:00,464 --> 00:02:01,426
a cheese box.

56
00:02:01,606 --> 00:02:04,455
My father called it the strawberry cheese,

57
00:02:04,455 --> 00:02:06,760
and he wouldn't touch it for three

58
00:02:06,760 --> 00:02:07,167
years.

59
00:02:07,347 --> 00:02:09,796
Then one Christmas he tried it by

60
00:02:09,796 --> 00:02:11,280
mistake in the dark,

61
00:02:11,280 --> 00:02:12,913
thinking it was fudge,

62
00:02:12,913 --> 00:02:14,991
and from then on he ate half

63
00:02:14,991 --> 00:02:16,252
of it every year.

64
00:02:16,603 --> 00:02:18,400
Here's what you need,

65
00:02:18,400 --> 00:02:18,913
honey.

66
00:02:19,093 --> 00:02:21,426
Two packages of cream cheese,

67
00:02:21,426 --> 00:02:22,874
eight ounces each,

68
00:02:22,874 --> 00:02:23,598
softened.

69
00:02:23,778 --> 00:02:26,560
Two cups of sharp cheddar cheese,

70
00:02:26,560 --> 00:02:27,319
shredded.

71
00:02:27,499 --> 00:02:29,426
Half a stick of butter,

72
00:02:29,426 --> 00:02:30,181
softened.

73
00:02:30,361 --> 00:02:32,021
Two green onions,

74
00:02:32,021 --> 00:02:33,193
sliced thin.

75
00:02:33,373 --> 00:02:36,462
One tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce.

76
00:02:36,642 --> 00:02:39,265
Half a teaspoon of garlic powder.

77
00:02:39,445 --> 00:02:40,990
A pinch of cayenne.

78
00:02:41,170 --> 00:02:43,183
And one cup of pecans,

79
00:02:43,183 --> 00:02:45,930
chopped fine, for the outside.

80
00:02:46,280 --> 00:02:48,787
And now Betty's first secret.

81
00:02:48,967 --> 00:02:51,899
Sharp cheddar, the sharpest you can find,

82
00:02:51,899 --> 00:02:54,401
and shred it yourself from a block.

83
00:02:54,581 --> 00:02:56,780
That's mistake number one,

84
00:02:56,780 --> 00:02:59,910
using mild cheese or the bagged kind.

85
00:03:00,090 --> 00:03:03,387
Mild cheddar disappears into the cream cheese.

86
00:03:03,567 --> 00:03:06,134
And the bagged shredded cheese has a

87
00:03:06,134 --> 00:03:07,062
powder on it,

88
00:03:07,062 --> 00:03:08,987
so it won't stick together,

89
00:03:08,987 --> 00:03:11,055
and it makes the ball dry and

90
00:03:11,055 --> 00:03:11,555
grainy.

91
00:03:11,905 --> 00:03:12,961
Step one.

92
00:03:13,141 --> 00:03:15,962
Make sure the cream cheese and butter

93
00:03:15,962 --> 00:03:17,181
are really soft.

94
00:03:17,361 --> 00:03:19,400
Leave them on the counter for an

95
00:03:19,400 --> 00:03:19,718
hour.

96
00:03:19,898 --> 00:03:22,110
Cold cream cheese makes lumps,

97
00:03:22,110 --> 00:03:24,322
and you'll never get them out.

98
00:03:24,502 --> 00:03:26,246
Put them in a big bowl and

99
00:03:26,246 --> 00:03:29,131
beat them together until they're smooth and

100
00:03:29,131 --> 00:03:30,875
fluffy, about two minutes.

101
00:03:31,055 --> 00:03:32,640
Then add the cheddar,

102
00:03:32,640 --> 00:03:33,923
the green onions,

103
00:03:33,923 --> 00:03:35,432
and everything else.

104
00:03:35,783 --> 00:03:38,232
And here's Betty's second secret.

105
00:03:38,412 --> 00:03:40,995
Worcestershire sauce and a little bit of

106
00:03:40,995 --> 00:03:41,512
cayenne.

107
00:03:41,692 --> 00:03:44,022
That's what gives it that deep,

108
00:03:44,022 --> 00:03:46,879
savory taste that makes people go back

109
00:03:46,879 --> 00:03:47,555
for more.

110
00:03:47,735 --> 00:03:50,173
Mistake number two is a cheese ball

111
00:03:50,173 --> 00:03:51,427
with no seasoning.

112
00:03:51,607 --> 00:03:53,958
Taste the mixture with a cracker before

113
00:03:53,958 --> 00:03:54,742
you shape it.

114
00:03:54,922 --> 00:03:57,461
It should taste a little too strong,

115
00:03:57,461 --> 00:04:00,142
because the flavor goes flat when it's

116
00:04:00,142 --> 00:04:00,495
cold.

117
00:04:00,845 --> 00:04:02,587
If this is helping you,

118
00:04:02,587 --> 00:04:05,163
honey, tap the like button for me.

119
00:04:05,343 --> 00:04:08,095
It helps Grandma more than you know.

120
00:04:08,275 --> 00:04:10,521
Now mix it all together with a

121
00:04:10,521 --> 00:04:13,291
spoon, just until everything is even.

122
00:04:13,471 --> 00:04:15,437
Don't beat it after you add the

123
00:04:15,437 --> 00:04:17,847
cheddar, or the cheese turns to paste.

124
00:04:18,027 --> 00:04:20,110
You want to still see little bits

125
00:04:20,110 --> 00:04:22,320
of orange cheese and green onion in

126
00:04:22,320 --> 00:04:22,509
it.

127
00:04:22,859 --> 00:04:24,658
Step two, shaping.

128
00:04:24,838 --> 00:04:27,571
Scrape the mixture onto a big piece

129
00:04:27,571 --> 00:04:28,820
of plastic wrap.

130
00:04:29,000 --> 00:04:31,320
Pull up the corners and twist them

131
00:04:31,320 --> 00:04:33,639
together, and press it into a ball

132
00:04:33,639 --> 00:04:35,004
through the plastic,

133
00:04:35,004 --> 00:04:36,709
so your hands stay clean.

134
00:04:36,889 --> 00:04:39,300
Then twist the top tight and put

135
00:04:39,300 --> 00:04:41,484
it in the icebox for at least

136
00:04:41,484 --> 00:04:43,368
four hours, or overnight.

137
00:04:43,548 --> 00:04:46,590
Betty always made hers the night before.

138
00:04:46,940 --> 00:04:49,582
Mistake number three is rolling it in

139
00:04:49,582 --> 00:04:51,010
the nuts right away,

140
00:04:51,010 --> 00:04:52,152
while it's soft.

141
00:04:52,332 --> 00:04:53,568
The nuts sink in,

142
00:04:53,568 --> 00:04:55,675
the ball sags into a pancake,

143
00:04:55,675 --> 00:04:58,073
and the whole thing slumps on the

144
00:04:58,073 --> 00:05:00,471
plate by the middle of the party.

145
00:05:00,651 --> 00:05:02,019
Chill it first,

146
00:05:02,019 --> 00:05:03,205
so it's firm.

147
00:05:03,385 --> 00:05:05,467
Then roll it in the nuts right

148
00:05:05,467 --> 00:05:06,646
before the party,

149
00:05:06,646 --> 00:05:08,936
and the nuts stay crisp and stuck

150
00:05:08,936 --> 00:05:09,144
on.

151
00:05:09,494 --> 00:05:12,400
So far, sharp cheddar from the block,

152
00:05:12,400 --> 00:05:13,814
soft cream cheese,

153
00:05:13,814 --> 00:05:15,935
Worcestershire and cayenne,

154
00:05:15,935 --> 00:05:16,957
a gentle mix,

155
00:05:16,957 --> 00:05:20,256
and chilling it overnight before the nuts.

156
00:05:20,436 --> 00:05:22,619
Now Betty's third secret.

157
00:05:22,799 --> 00:05:24,366
Toast the pecans.

158
00:05:24,546 --> 00:05:26,871
Spread them on a baking sheet and

159
00:05:26,871 --> 00:05:29,126
bake them at three fifty for six

160
00:05:29,126 --> 00:05:30,324
or seven minutes,

161
00:05:30,324 --> 00:05:32,719
until they smell like warm butter.

162
00:05:32,899 --> 00:05:34,116
Let them cool,

163
00:05:34,116 --> 00:05:35,767
and chop them fine.

164
00:05:36,117 --> 00:05:39,307
Raw pecans taste like cardboard next to

165
00:05:39,307 --> 00:05:41,353
toasted ones, sweetheart.

166
00:05:41,533 --> 00:05:43,980
Toasting brings out all the oil and

167
00:05:43,980 --> 00:05:44,749
the flavor.

168
00:05:44,929 --> 00:05:47,291
And that's mistake number four,

169
00:05:47,291 --> 00:05:49,120
raw nuts on the outside.

170
00:05:49,300 --> 00:05:52,239
Some people also add chopped fresh parsley

171
00:05:52,239 --> 00:05:54,548
to the pecans for a little green.

172
00:05:54,728 --> 00:05:56,818
Betty did, and it made the whole

173
00:05:56,818 --> 00:05:59,104
thing look like a Christmas wreath.

174
00:05:59,455 --> 00:06:01,254
And if a ball is too much

175
00:06:01,254 --> 00:06:02,406
for your family,

176
00:06:02,406 --> 00:06:03,773
make a log instead.

177
00:06:03,953 --> 00:06:06,426
Shape it in the plastic wrap like

178
00:06:06,426 --> 00:06:07,474
a fat sausage,

179
00:06:07,474 --> 00:06:09,272
about two inches across,

180
00:06:09,272 --> 00:06:10,246
and chill it.

181
00:06:10,426 --> 00:06:12,793
Then roll it in the pecans and

182
00:06:12,793 --> 00:06:14,449
slice it into rounds,

183
00:06:14,449 --> 00:06:16,579
one round for each cracker.

184
00:06:16,759 --> 00:06:18,266
It's neater on a buffet,

185
00:06:18,266 --> 00:06:20,464
and people don't have to fight over

186
00:06:20,464 --> 00:06:21,531
the little knife.

187
00:06:21,881 --> 00:06:23,702
Now the trick I promised you,

188
00:06:23,702 --> 00:06:25,336
how to make it look like a

189
00:06:25,336 --> 00:06:26,466
Christmas present.

190
00:06:26,646 --> 00:06:28,819
Roll the cold ball in the toasted

191
00:06:28,819 --> 00:06:31,452
pecans, pressing them on with your hands

192
00:06:31,452 --> 00:06:33,032
so they cover every bit.

193
00:06:33,212 --> 00:06:34,899
Put it in the middle of a

194
00:06:34,899 --> 00:06:35,708
big platter.

195
00:06:35,888 --> 00:06:38,017
Then lay a few sprigs of fresh

196
00:06:38,017 --> 00:06:40,926
rosemary around the bottom like a wreath,

197
00:06:40,926 --> 00:06:44,189
and scatter some fresh cranberries in between.

198
00:06:44,540 --> 00:06:45,814
And for the top,

199
00:06:45,814 --> 00:06:46,850
a little bow.

200
00:06:47,030 --> 00:06:49,326
Cut a strip of red bell pepper,

201
00:06:49,326 --> 00:06:50,141
and tie it,

202
00:06:50,141 --> 00:06:52,215
or lay two strips in a cross

203
00:06:52,215 --> 00:06:53,178
over the top,

204
00:06:53,178 --> 00:06:55,029
like ribbon on a package.

205
00:06:55,209 --> 00:06:57,400
Stick a little sprig of rosemary in

206
00:06:57,400 --> 00:06:58,088
the middle.

207
00:06:58,268 --> 00:07:01,291
My grandchildren call it the cheese present,

208
00:07:01,291 --> 00:07:03,557
and they won't let anybody cut it

209
00:07:03,557 --> 00:07:05,618
until Grandpa takes a picture.

210
00:07:05,968 --> 00:07:08,387
Serve it with a good variety of

211
00:07:08,387 --> 00:07:09,636
crackers, honey.

212
00:07:09,816 --> 00:07:12,288
Butter crackers, wheat crackers,

213
00:07:12,288 --> 00:07:15,377
and some little slices of toasted bread.

214
00:07:15,557 --> 00:07:18,142
Celery sticks and apple slices too,

215
00:07:18,142 --> 00:07:20,875
for the people watching their figure.

216
00:07:21,055 --> 00:07:23,281
Take it out of the icebox about

217
00:07:23,281 --> 00:07:25,578
twenty minutes before the party,

218
00:07:25,578 --> 00:07:27,732
so it's soft enough to spread,

219
00:07:27,732 --> 00:07:30,029
but still holds its round shape.

220
00:07:30,380 --> 00:07:32,756
And always put out two knives,

221
00:07:32,756 --> 00:07:33,944
honey, not one.

222
00:07:34,124 --> 00:07:35,645
Betty taught me that.

223
00:07:35,825 --> 00:07:37,144
With one knife,

224
00:07:37,144 --> 00:07:38,287
a line forms,

225
00:07:38,287 --> 00:07:41,189
and people get shy and walk away.

226
00:07:41,369 --> 00:07:44,083
With two knives on opposite sides of

227
00:07:44,083 --> 00:07:46,797
the platter, everybody can dig in at

228
00:07:46,797 --> 00:07:47,174
once.

229
00:07:47,354 --> 00:07:49,967
Small things like that are the difference

230
00:07:49,967 --> 00:07:52,325
between a party people talk about and

231
00:07:52,325 --> 00:07:53,727
a party people forget.

232
00:07:54,078 --> 00:07:55,975
Once you know the method,

233
00:07:55,975 --> 00:07:58,327
you can make it a hundred ways.

234
00:07:58,507 --> 00:07:59,736
For a sweet one,

235
00:07:59,736 --> 00:08:02,426
leave out the onions and garlic and

236
00:08:02,426 --> 00:08:03,887
use powdered sugar,

237
00:08:03,887 --> 00:08:06,423
vanilla and mini chocolate chips,

238
00:08:06,423 --> 00:08:09,420
and roll it in crushed graham crackers.

239
00:08:09,600 --> 00:08:12,085
The children go wild for that one.

240
00:08:12,265 --> 00:08:15,539
Serve it with vanilla wafers and pretzels.

241
00:08:15,889 --> 00:08:18,327
Or make a cranberry pecan one,

242
00:08:18,327 --> 00:08:21,334
with dried cranberries and a spoon of

243
00:08:21,334 --> 00:08:22,553
honey mixed in.

244
00:08:22,733 --> 00:08:24,358
Or a bacon ranch one,

245
00:08:24,358 --> 00:08:27,067
with crumbled bacon and a packet of

246
00:08:27,067 --> 00:08:28,305
ranch seasoning.

247
00:08:28,485 --> 00:08:31,013
Or roll little cheese balls the size

248
00:08:31,013 --> 00:08:33,050
of a walnut and put a pretzel

249
00:08:33,050 --> 00:08:34,314
stick in each one.

250
00:08:34,494 --> 00:08:36,353
Those are cheese ball pops,

251
00:08:36,353 --> 00:08:38,694
and they're gone in ten minutes at

252
00:08:38,694 --> 00:08:39,521
every party.

253
00:08:39,871 --> 00:08:42,933
And here's why every busy hostess loved

254
00:08:42,933 --> 00:08:44,189
the cheese ball.

255
00:08:44,369 --> 00:08:46,514
You can make it three days ahead

256
00:08:46,514 --> 00:08:48,793
and keep it wrapped in the icebox.

257
00:08:48,973 --> 00:08:50,756
Or freeze it for a month,

258
00:08:50,756 --> 00:08:51,968
without the nuts.

259
00:08:52,148 --> 00:08:54,401
Thaw it overnight in the icebox,

260
00:08:54,401 --> 00:08:56,513
then roll it in the pecans the

261
00:08:56,513 --> 00:08:57,709
day of the party.

262
00:08:57,889 --> 00:09:00,116
I make two in early December,

263
00:09:00,116 --> 00:09:03,265
and freeze one for the surprise visitors.

264
00:09:03,615 --> 00:09:05,633
And it's a lovely gift,

265
00:09:05,633 --> 00:09:06,598
sweetheart.

266
00:09:06,778 --> 00:09:08,860
Wrap a cheese ball in plastic,

267
00:09:08,860 --> 00:09:10,941
tuck it in a small basket with

268
00:09:10,941 --> 00:09:13,023
a box of crackers and a little

269
00:09:13,023 --> 00:09:15,451
spreading knife tied with a ribbon.

270
00:09:15,631 --> 00:09:18,440
My neighbor across the street gets one

271
00:09:18,440 --> 00:09:19,253
every year.

272
00:09:19,433 --> 00:09:21,547
She says it's the only present she

273
00:09:21,547 --> 00:09:23,598
doesn't have to find a place for,

274
00:09:23,598 --> 00:09:25,587
because it's gone by New Year's.

275
00:09:25,937 --> 00:09:27,330
So one more time.

276
00:09:27,510 --> 00:09:30,238
Sharp cheddar, shredded from the block.

277
00:09:30,418 --> 00:09:32,879
Really soft cream cheese.

278
00:09:33,059 --> 00:09:35,473
Worcestershire and a little cayenne,

279
00:09:35,473 --> 00:09:36,345
and taste it.

280
00:09:36,525 --> 00:09:38,104
Mix it gently.

281
00:09:38,284 --> 00:09:40,585
Shape it in plastic wrap and chill

282
00:09:40,585 --> 00:09:41,465
it overnight.

283
00:09:41,645 --> 00:09:45,140
Toasted pecans, rolled on right before the

284
00:09:45,140 --> 00:09:45,639
party.

285
00:09:45,819 --> 00:09:48,313
And a rosemary wreath and a red

286
00:09:48,313 --> 00:09:49,197
pepper bow.

287
00:09:49,377 --> 00:09:51,924
That's Betty Hartman's cheese ball,

288
00:09:51,924 --> 00:09:53,453
and it's never bland.

289
00:09:53,803 --> 00:09:55,825
Tell me in the comments,

290
00:09:55,825 --> 00:09:56,751
sweetheart.

291
00:09:56,931 --> 00:09:58,947
Was there a cheese ball at your

292
00:09:58,947 --> 00:10:00,182
family's Christmas?

293
00:10:00,362 --> 00:10:01,535
What kind?

294
00:10:01,715 --> 00:10:04,910
The whole playlist of Grandma's recipes is

295
00:10:04,910 --> 00:10:06,965
right there on your screen,

296
00:10:06,965 --> 00:10:09,095
and I'll see you in the next

297
00:10:09,095 --> 00:10:09,552
video.

298
00:10:09,732 --> 00:10:11,427
Good night, honey.

299
00:10:11,607 --> 00:10:13,035
Merry Christmas.
_DlrMyhVQ8k:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:03,904
Sweetheart, my granddaughter Emily called me last

2
00:00:03,904 --> 00:00:05,020
week and said,

3
00:00:05,020 --> 00:00:09,163
Grandma, everybody online is making tortellini soup,

4
00:00:09,163 --> 00:00:12,271
and mine came out like wallpaper paste.

5
00:00:12,451 --> 00:00:14,000
The pasta was mushy,

6
00:00:14,000 --> 00:00:15,472
the broth was gone,

7
00:00:15,472 --> 00:00:17,409
and the spinach was gray.

8
00:00:17,589 --> 00:00:19,935
I laughed, because I made the same

9
00:00:19,935 --> 00:00:22,143
mistakes in nineteen eighty-one,

10
00:00:22,143 --> 00:00:24,903
the first time I ever cooked tortellini.

11
00:00:25,253 --> 00:00:27,719
So tonight I'm giving you my creamy

12
00:00:27,719 --> 00:00:29,410
sausage tortellini soup,

13
00:00:29,410 --> 00:00:31,383
a whole supper in one pot in

14
00:00:31,383 --> 00:00:34,342
thirty minutes, and the four mistakes that

15
00:00:34,342 --> 00:00:35,469
turn it to mush.

16
00:00:35,649 --> 00:00:36,901
And stay with me,

17
00:00:36,901 --> 00:00:39,919
because the last mistake happens the next

18
00:00:39,919 --> 00:00:42,717
day, and it's the reason most leftover

19
00:00:42,717 --> 00:00:45,146
tortellini soup gets thrown away.

20
00:00:45,497 --> 00:00:48,207
When I was growing up in Mansfield,

21
00:00:48,207 --> 00:00:51,305
pasta meant spaghetti or elbow macaroni,

22
00:00:51,305 --> 00:00:52,544
and that was it.

23
00:00:52,724 --> 00:00:54,798
Then in the late seventies,

24
00:00:54,798 --> 00:00:58,640
the grocery store started selling fresh tortellini

25
00:00:58,640 --> 00:00:59,946
in the cold case,

26
00:00:59,946 --> 00:01:03,173
little rings of pasta stuffed with cheese.

27
00:01:03,353 --> 00:01:06,114
My husband said they looked like tiny

28
00:01:06,114 --> 00:01:06,487
hats.

29
00:01:06,667 --> 00:01:09,253
He was suspicious of them for about

30
00:01:09,253 --> 00:01:09,918
one bite.

31
00:01:10,269 --> 00:01:12,916
The Italians in Bologna have a story

32
00:01:12,916 --> 00:01:16,004
that tortellini were shaped like the belly

33
00:01:16,004 --> 00:01:17,180
button of Venus,

34
00:01:17,180 --> 00:01:18,651
the goddess of love.

35
00:01:18,831 --> 00:01:20,739
I told my husband that at the

36
00:01:20,739 --> 00:01:22,976
dinner table, and he turned red as

37
00:01:22,976 --> 00:01:25,213
a beet and didn't say another word

38
00:01:25,213 --> 00:01:26,726
for the rest of supper.

39
00:01:26,906 --> 00:01:28,163
Forty years later,

40
00:01:28,163 --> 00:01:31,305
my grandchildren still call them belly button

41
00:01:31,305 --> 00:01:31,654
soup.

42
00:01:32,005 --> 00:01:34,349
And what I love most about this

43
00:01:34,349 --> 00:01:36,921
soup is that it costs about twelve

44
00:01:36,921 --> 00:01:39,114
dollars and feeds six people,

45
00:01:39,114 --> 00:01:39,946
with bread.

46
00:01:40,126 --> 00:01:41,851
In a minute I'll tell you how

47
00:01:41,851 --> 00:01:43,813
to make it with what's already in

48
00:01:43,813 --> 00:01:45,716
your freezer, so it's a soup you

49
00:01:45,716 --> 00:01:47,501
can make on a Tuesday when you

50
00:01:47,501 --> 00:01:49,820
thought there was nothing in the house.

51
00:01:50,170 --> 00:01:51,858
Here's what you need,

52
00:01:51,858 --> 00:01:52,341
honey.

53
00:01:52,521 --> 00:01:55,293
One pound of Italian sausage,

54
00:01:55,293 --> 00:01:56,440
mild or hot,

55
00:01:56,440 --> 00:01:58,256
out of the casings.

56
00:01:58,436 --> 00:02:00,282
One onion, chopped.

57
00:02:00,462 --> 00:02:02,215
Three cloves of garlic.

58
00:02:02,395 --> 00:02:04,694
One can of diced tomatoes.

59
00:02:04,874 --> 00:02:06,847
Six cups of chicken broth.

60
00:02:07,027 --> 00:02:09,884
One teaspoon of Italian seasoning.

61
00:02:10,064 --> 00:02:12,828
One package of cheese tortellini,

62
00:02:12,828 --> 00:02:14,336
about nine ounces.

63
00:02:14,516 --> 00:02:17,256
Three big handfuls of fresh spinach.

64
00:02:17,436 --> 00:02:19,177
Half a cup of heavy cream.

65
00:02:19,357 --> 00:02:21,993
And Parmesan cheese for the top.

66
00:02:22,343 --> 00:02:24,026
Now the tortellini.

67
00:02:24,206 --> 00:02:26,772
The fresh kind from the cold case,

68
00:02:26,772 --> 00:02:28,206
or the frozen kind,

69
00:02:28,206 --> 00:02:29,338
both work fine.

70
00:02:29,518 --> 00:02:32,452
The dried tortellini on the shelf takes

71
00:02:32,452 --> 00:02:33,957
much longer to cook,

72
00:02:33,957 --> 00:02:35,913
so if that's all you have,

73
00:02:35,913 --> 00:02:37,192
add five minutes.

74
00:02:37,372 --> 00:02:39,844
And remember the trick with the freezer

75
00:02:39,844 --> 00:02:40,541
I promised.

76
00:02:40,721 --> 00:02:43,724
A bag of frozen tortellini lasts months,

77
00:02:43,724 --> 00:02:46,050
and so does a pound of sausage.

78
00:02:46,230 --> 00:02:47,860
Keep both in the freezer,

79
00:02:47,860 --> 00:02:50,793
and you're always thirty minutes from supper.

80
00:02:51,143 --> 00:02:53,027
And pick a good pot,

81
00:02:53,027 --> 00:02:53,592
honey.

82
00:02:53,772 --> 00:02:55,167
A big heavy one,

83
00:02:55,167 --> 00:02:57,607
a Dutch oven if you have it,

84
00:02:57,607 --> 00:02:59,438
at least five quarts.

85
00:02:59,618 --> 00:03:01,884
A thin pot burns the sausage in

86
00:03:01,884 --> 00:03:04,003
one spot and leaves it raw in

87
00:03:04,003 --> 00:03:07,000
another, and the bottom scorches when you

88
00:03:07,000 --> 00:03:08,024
add the cream.

89
00:03:08,204 --> 00:03:10,628
My Dutch oven was a wedding present

90
00:03:10,628 --> 00:03:12,290
in nineteen sixty-three.

91
00:03:12,470 --> 00:03:15,056
It's orange, it weighs as much as

92
00:03:15,056 --> 00:03:15,997
a small dog,

93
00:03:15,997 --> 00:03:18,740
and it's made ten thousand suppers.

94
00:03:19,090 --> 00:03:20,042
Step one.

95
00:03:20,222 --> 00:03:21,674
In a big heavy pot,

96
00:03:21,674 --> 00:03:24,731
brown the sausage over medium-high heat,

97
00:03:24,731 --> 00:03:27,406
breaking it up with a wooden spoon,

98
00:03:27,406 --> 00:03:30,005
until it's deep brown and a little

99
00:03:30,005 --> 00:03:31,228
crispy in spots.

100
00:03:31,408 --> 00:03:32,917
About eight minutes.

101
00:03:33,097 --> 00:03:34,862
Don't rush this part.

102
00:03:35,042 --> 00:03:37,158
Those brown bits on the bottom of

103
00:03:37,158 --> 00:03:39,210
the pot are where all the flavor

104
00:03:39,210 --> 00:03:40,684
of the soup comes from.

105
00:03:41,035 --> 00:03:44,041
Mistake number one is pale sausage.

106
00:03:44,221 --> 00:03:46,599
If you just cook it until it's

107
00:03:46,599 --> 00:03:49,690
gray, the soup tastes like boiled meat.

108
00:03:49,870 --> 00:03:52,132
Let it sit still in the pot

109
00:03:52,132 --> 00:03:52,970
and brown.

110
00:03:53,150 --> 00:03:55,529
Then take out most of the grease

111
00:03:55,529 --> 00:03:56,496
with a spoon,

112
00:03:56,496 --> 00:03:58,653
but leave about a tablespoon.

113
00:03:58,833 --> 00:03:59,845
Add the onion,

114
00:03:59,845 --> 00:04:02,085
and cook it in that sausage fat

115
00:04:02,085 --> 00:04:03,313
for five minutes,

116
00:04:03,313 --> 00:04:05,265
until it's soft and golden.

117
00:04:05,445 --> 00:04:06,679
Then the garlic,

118
00:04:06,679 --> 00:04:07,836
for one minute.

119
00:04:08,187 --> 00:04:09,220
Step two.

120
00:04:09,400 --> 00:04:10,989
Pour in the tomatoes,

121
00:04:10,989 --> 00:04:13,788
the broth, and the Italian seasoning.

122
00:04:13,968 --> 00:04:16,238
Scrape the bottom of the pot with

123
00:04:16,238 --> 00:04:18,438
your spoon, to lift up all those

124
00:04:18,438 --> 00:04:20,226
brown bits into the broth.

125
00:04:20,406 --> 00:04:21,769
Bring it to a boil,

126
00:04:21,769 --> 00:04:23,777
then turn it down and let it

127
00:04:23,777 --> 00:04:25,427
simmer for ten minutes,

128
00:04:25,427 --> 00:04:27,650
so the flavors get to know each

129
00:04:27,650 --> 00:04:28,080
other.

130
00:04:28,260 --> 00:04:31,058
Taste it, and add salt and pepper.

131
00:04:31,409 --> 00:04:33,015
If this is helping you,

132
00:04:33,015 --> 00:04:35,391
honey, tap the like button for me.

133
00:04:35,571 --> 00:04:38,160
It helps Grandma more than you know.

134
00:04:38,340 --> 00:04:40,333
And while the soup simmers,

135
00:04:40,333 --> 00:04:43,065
here's a little secret from my friend

136
00:04:43,065 --> 00:04:45,724
Rosa, whose family came from Naples.

137
00:04:45,904 --> 00:04:48,142
If you have the hard rind from

138
00:04:48,142 --> 00:04:50,454
the end of a piece of Parmesan,

139
00:04:50,454 --> 00:04:51,871
drop it in the pot.

140
00:04:52,051 --> 00:04:54,502
It melts a little and makes the

141
00:04:54,502 --> 00:04:56,637
broth taste rich and nutty.

142
00:04:56,817 --> 00:04:58,977
Take it out before serving.

143
00:04:59,327 --> 00:05:01,858
Step three, the tortellini.

144
00:05:02,038 --> 00:05:04,278
Here's mistake number two.

145
00:05:04,458 --> 00:05:05,991
Adding them too early.

146
00:05:06,171 --> 00:05:09,282
Fresh tortellini only need about three to

147
00:05:09,282 --> 00:05:10,269
five minutes.

148
00:05:10,449 --> 00:05:12,031
If you put them in at the

149
00:05:12,031 --> 00:05:14,182
start and let them simmer with the

150
00:05:14,182 --> 00:05:15,637
broth for half an hour,

151
00:05:15,637 --> 00:05:17,662
they swell up and split open and

152
00:05:17,662 --> 00:05:18,991
the cheese leaks out,

153
00:05:18,991 --> 00:05:21,205
and you get that wallpaper paste my

154
00:05:21,205 --> 00:05:22,407
granddaughter made.

155
00:05:22,758 --> 00:05:25,168
So add the tortellini only at the

156
00:05:25,168 --> 00:05:27,505
very end, when the broth is done

157
00:05:27,505 --> 00:05:28,528
and simmering.

158
00:05:28,708 --> 00:05:31,177
Cook them just until they float and

159
00:05:31,177 --> 00:05:33,363
are tender, about four minutes.

160
00:05:33,543 --> 00:05:34,867
Taste one.

161
00:05:35,047 --> 00:05:37,373
It should be soft but still have

162
00:05:37,373 --> 00:05:38,391
a little chew.

163
00:05:38,571 --> 00:05:40,896
And keep the soup at a gentle

164
00:05:40,896 --> 00:05:42,820
simmer, not a hard boil.

165
00:05:43,000 --> 00:05:45,869
A hard boil bangs the pasta around

166
00:05:45,869 --> 00:05:47,388
and tears it open.

167
00:05:47,739 --> 00:05:49,213
Step four.

168
00:05:49,393 --> 00:05:51,193
Turn the heat down to low.

169
00:05:51,373 --> 00:05:53,335
Then stir in the cream.

170
00:05:53,515 --> 00:05:56,692
Mistake number three is pouring cold cream

171
00:05:56,692 --> 00:05:58,054
into boiling soup.

172
00:05:58,234 --> 00:06:00,488
It can curdle and turn grainy,

173
00:06:00,488 --> 00:06:03,192
little white flecks floating on top.

174
00:06:03,372 --> 00:06:05,664
So turn the heat low first,

175
00:06:05,664 --> 00:06:08,552
and pour the cream in slowly while

176
00:06:08,552 --> 00:06:09,316
you stir.

177
00:06:09,496 --> 00:06:11,846
You can also warm the cream for

178
00:06:11,846 --> 00:06:13,362
a few seconds first.

179
00:06:13,712 --> 00:06:15,134
Then the spinach,

180
00:06:15,134 --> 00:06:16,138
last of all.

181
00:06:16,318 --> 00:06:18,479
Just stir in the handfuls,

182
00:06:18,479 --> 00:06:20,474
and in about one minute,

183
00:06:20,474 --> 00:06:23,133
it wilts down to almost nothing.

184
00:06:23,313 --> 00:06:24,277
That's it.

185
00:06:24,457 --> 00:06:25,687
Turn off the heat.

186
00:06:25,867 --> 00:06:28,226
If you cook spinach any longer,

187
00:06:28,226 --> 00:06:31,192
it turns that sad gray-green and tastes

188
00:06:31,192 --> 00:06:33,170
like the bottom of a pond.

189
00:06:33,350 --> 00:06:36,077
Bright green spinach means you did it

190
00:06:36,077 --> 00:06:36,520
right.

191
00:06:36,870 --> 00:06:39,493
So far, brown the sausage dark,

192
00:06:39,493 --> 00:06:41,693
cook the onion in the fat,

193
00:06:41,693 --> 00:06:43,216
scrape the bottom,

194
00:06:43,216 --> 00:06:46,178
add the tortellini at the very end,

195
00:06:46,178 --> 00:06:47,701
then cream on low,

196
00:06:47,701 --> 00:06:50,070
then spinach for one minute.

197
00:06:50,250 --> 00:06:52,255
Ladle it into big bowls,

198
00:06:52,255 --> 00:06:55,262
and grate plenty of Parmesan on top,

199
00:06:55,262 --> 00:06:57,518
with a little black pepper.

200
00:06:57,698 --> 00:07:00,070
Serve it with warm crusty bread for

201
00:07:00,070 --> 00:07:00,612
dipping.

202
00:07:00,792 --> 00:07:03,656
My husband dipped until the bread was

203
00:07:03,656 --> 00:07:06,133
gone, then asked for more bread.

204
00:07:06,483 --> 00:07:08,291
And here's how to make it a

205
00:07:08,291 --> 00:07:09,095
real supper.

206
00:07:09,275 --> 00:07:11,504
Put out a little bowl of extra

207
00:07:11,504 --> 00:07:13,882
Parmesan, a bottle of olive oil,

208
00:07:13,882 --> 00:07:15,888
and some red pepper flakes,

209
00:07:15,888 --> 00:07:18,563
so everybody can fix their own bowl.

210
00:07:18,743 --> 00:07:20,890
And a simple green salad on the

211
00:07:20,890 --> 00:07:22,760
side with a lemon dressing.

212
00:07:22,940 --> 00:07:25,134
Emily made it this way for her

213
00:07:25,134 --> 00:07:26,669
new husband's family,

214
00:07:26,669 --> 00:07:29,302
and his mother asked for the recipe.

215
00:07:29,482 --> 00:07:32,340
That's the highest compliment there is,

216
00:07:32,340 --> 00:07:32,779
honey.

217
00:07:33,130 --> 00:07:35,831
You can change this soup a hundred

218
00:07:35,831 --> 00:07:37,181
ways, sweetheart.

219
00:07:37,361 --> 00:07:39,587
Use kale instead of spinach,

220
00:07:39,587 --> 00:07:42,130
but add it five minutes earlier,

221
00:07:42,130 --> 00:07:44,037
because kale is tougher.

222
00:07:44,217 --> 00:07:45,703
Use chicken sausage,

223
00:07:45,703 --> 00:07:48,302
or ground turkey with a teaspoon of

224
00:07:48,302 --> 00:07:49,268
fennel seeds.

225
00:07:49,448 --> 00:07:51,051
Or leave out the meat,

226
00:07:51,051 --> 00:07:53,091
and add a can of white beans

227
00:07:53,091 --> 00:07:54,985
and some sliced mushrooms.

228
00:07:55,165 --> 00:07:57,953
My daughter-in-law Linda makes it that way

229
00:07:57,953 --> 00:07:58,683
on Fridays.

230
00:07:59,034 --> 00:08:01,449
And if you want it without cream,

231
00:08:01,449 --> 00:08:03,718
leave the cream out and stir in

232
00:08:03,718 --> 00:08:05,767
a spoon of pesto at the end.

233
00:08:05,947 --> 00:08:08,866
Or a few spoons of cream cheese,

234
00:08:08,866 --> 00:08:09,779
melted in.

235
00:08:09,959 --> 00:08:12,223
It's lighter and still creamy.

236
00:08:12,403 --> 00:08:13,712
For a spicy one,

237
00:08:13,712 --> 00:08:16,166
use hot sausage and a pinch of

238
00:08:16,166 --> 00:08:17,639
red pepper flakes.

239
00:08:17,819 --> 00:08:20,363
My grandson puts so much pepper in

240
00:08:20,363 --> 00:08:21,860
his, his eyes water,

241
00:08:21,860 --> 00:08:24,030
and he says that's the point.

242
00:08:24,380 --> 00:08:27,204
And now the last mistake I promised,

243
00:08:27,204 --> 00:08:29,871
the one that happens the next day.

244
00:08:30,051 --> 00:08:32,325
You put the leftover soup in the

245
00:08:32,325 --> 00:08:34,741
icebox, with the tortellini in it.

246
00:08:34,921 --> 00:08:37,896
Overnight, the pasta drinks up all the

247
00:08:37,896 --> 00:08:40,557
broth, and in the morning you have

248
00:08:40,557 --> 00:08:41,888
a pot of swollen,

249
00:08:41,888 --> 00:08:44,314
soggy pasta and no soup at all.

250
00:08:44,494 --> 00:08:46,570
That's mistake number four,

251
00:08:46,570 --> 00:08:48,568
and it's why so much of it

252
00:08:48,568 --> 00:08:50,183
ends up in the trash.

253
00:08:50,533 --> 00:08:51,798
Here's the fix.

254
00:08:51,978 --> 00:08:54,498
If you know you'll have leftovers,

255
00:08:54,498 --> 00:08:57,240
cook the tortellini in a separate pot

256
00:08:57,240 --> 00:08:58,425
of salted water,

257
00:08:58,425 --> 00:09:00,797
drain them, and put them in each

258
00:09:00,797 --> 00:09:03,391
bowl, then ladle the hot soup over.

259
00:09:03,571 --> 00:09:06,261
Keep the leftover soup and the leftover

260
00:09:06,261 --> 00:09:08,261
pasta in separate containers.

261
00:09:08,441 --> 00:09:09,375
The next day,

262
00:09:09,375 --> 00:09:11,602
heat the soup and add the pasta

263
00:09:11,602 --> 00:09:13,039
for the last minute.

264
00:09:13,219 --> 00:09:15,993
It tastes like it was just made.

265
00:09:16,344 --> 00:09:18,545
And if it's already too late,

266
00:09:18,545 --> 00:09:20,899
and your pasta drank the broth,

267
00:09:20,899 --> 00:09:22,721
just add a cup or two of

268
00:09:22,721 --> 00:09:25,303
broth or water when you reheat it,

269
00:09:25,303 --> 00:09:26,897
and a spoon of cream.

270
00:09:27,077 --> 00:09:28,949
And it freezes well too,

271
00:09:28,949 --> 00:09:32,069
without the pasta and without the cream.

272
00:09:32,249 --> 00:09:35,158
Freeze the sausage and tomato broth for

273
00:09:35,158 --> 00:09:36,127
three months.

274
00:09:36,307 --> 00:09:37,385
Then thaw it,

275
00:09:37,385 --> 00:09:39,127
bring it to a simmer,

276
00:09:39,127 --> 00:09:41,200
and add fresh tortellini,

277
00:09:41,200 --> 00:09:42,693
cream and spinach.

278
00:09:43,043 --> 00:09:44,552
So one more time.

279
00:09:44,732 --> 00:09:47,147
Brown the sausage until it's dark.

280
00:09:47,327 --> 00:09:49,277
Cook the onion in the fat.

281
00:09:49,457 --> 00:09:52,011
Scrape the brown bits into the broth.

282
00:09:52,191 --> 00:09:53,678
Simmer ten minutes.

283
00:09:53,858 --> 00:09:56,562
Add the tortellini only at the very

284
00:09:56,562 --> 00:09:58,339
end, and simmer gently.

285
00:09:58,519 --> 00:10:00,992
Turn the heat low before the cream.

286
00:10:01,172 --> 00:10:02,948
Spinach for one minute.

287
00:10:03,128 --> 00:10:05,895
And keep the leftover pasta and soup

288
00:10:05,895 --> 00:10:06,356
apart.

289
00:10:06,536 --> 00:10:09,752
That's tortellini soup that's never mushy.

290
00:10:10,102 --> 00:10:11,869
Tell me in the comments,

291
00:10:11,869 --> 00:10:12,679
sweetheart.

292
00:10:12,859 --> 00:10:15,730
What's your family's favorite soup on a

293
00:10:15,730 --> 00:10:16,539
cold night?

294
00:10:16,719 --> 00:10:19,053
I'm always looking for a new one.

295
00:10:19,233 --> 00:10:22,410
The whole playlist of Grandma's recipes is

296
00:10:22,410 --> 00:10:24,452
right there on your screen,

297
00:10:24,452 --> 00:10:26,569
and I'll see you in the next

298
00:10:26,569 --> 00:10:27,023
video.

299
00:10:27,203 --> 00:10:28,898
Good night, honey.

1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:02,476
Sweetheart, you can always tell a home

2
00:00:02,476 --> 00:00:05,082
that's been decorated with love from one

3
00:00:05,082 --> 00:00:07,233
that's been decorated from a box.

4
00:00:07,413 --> 00:00:08,981
And most of the time,

5
00:00:08,981 --> 00:00:11,221
the difference is the garland.

6
00:00:11,401 --> 00:00:13,973
That long rope of green over the

7
00:00:13,973 --> 00:00:16,224
fireplace, or up the stairs,

8
00:00:16,224 --> 00:00:17,751
or around the door.

9
00:00:17,931 --> 00:00:20,243
Done right, it makes a room look

10
00:00:20,243 --> 00:00:21,832
like a Christmas card.

11
00:00:22,012 --> 00:00:24,716
Done wrong, it looks like a sad

12
00:00:24,716 --> 00:00:25,762
green snake.

13
00:00:26,113 --> 00:00:29,160
So tonight I'm giving you seven Christmas

14
00:00:29,160 --> 00:00:31,984
garland mistakes that make a home look

15
00:00:31,984 --> 00:00:34,511
cheap, and the old fixes my mother

16
00:00:34,511 --> 00:00:36,294
used, most of them free.

17
00:00:36,474 --> 00:00:37,682
And stay with me,

18
00:00:37,682 --> 00:00:40,025
because the last one is the trick

19
00:00:40,025 --> 00:00:43,007
decorators charge hundreds of dollars for,

20
00:00:43,007 --> 00:00:45,137
and you can do it this weekend

21
00:00:45,137 --> 00:00:47,481
with branches from your own yard.

22
00:00:47,831 --> 00:00:50,168
We didn't have a fireplace on Elm

23
00:00:50,168 --> 00:00:50,663
Street.

24
00:00:50,843 --> 00:00:52,759
We had a coal furnace in the

25
00:00:52,759 --> 00:00:53,374
basement.

26
00:00:53,554 --> 00:00:55,923
But my mother made a mantel anyway,

27
00:00:55,923 --> 00:00:57,886
on the top of the old upright

28
00:00:57,886 --> 00:00:59,510
piano in the front room.

29
00:00:59,690 --> 00:01:02,659
Every December, she draped it with cedar

30
00:01:02,659 --> 00:01:05,702
branches my father cut from the fencerow,

31
00:01:05,702 --> 00:01:08,226
with pinecones and a row of little

32
00:01:08,226 --> 00:01:11,343
red candles, and our family photographs in

33
00:01:11,343 --> 00:01:12,159
the middle.

34
00:01:12,510 --> 00:01:14,958
She never bought a single thing for

35
00:01:14,958 --> 00:01:15,168
it.

36
00:01:15,348 --> 00:01:18,082
And when the piano teacher came on

37
00:01:18,082 --> 00:01:21,379
Thursdays, she'd stand in the doorway and

38
00:01:21,379 --> 00:01:24,354
say, Dorothy, your piano looks like a

39
00:01:24,354 --> 00:01:25,077
magazine.

40
00:01:25,257 --> 00:01:27,088
My mother would say,

41
00:01:27,088 --> 00:01:28,827
it's just branches,

42
00:01:28,827 --> 00:01:29,193
Mrs.

43
00:01:29,373 --> 00:01:30,256
Fenwick.

44
00:01:30,436 --> 00:01:32,064
But she was proud,

45
00:01:32,064 --> 00:01:32,607
honey.

46
00:01:32,787 --> 00:01:33,825
I could tell,

47
00:01:33,825 --> 00:01:36,938
because she dusted the piano twice that

48
00:01:36,938 --> 00:01:37,338
week.

49
00:01:37,688 --> 00:01:39,174
Before you start,

50
00:01:39,174 --> 00:01:40,486
measure, honey.

51
00:01:40,666 --> 00:01:42,937
A garland for a mantel should be

52
00:01:42,937 --> 00:01:45,067
about one and a half times the

53
00:01:45,067 --> 00:01:46,487
width of the mantel,

54
00:01:46,487 --> 00:01:48,617
so it has enough to drape down

55
00:01:48,617 --> 00:01:49,327
the sides.

56
00:01:49,507 --> 00:01:50,773
For a staircase,

57
00:01:50,773 --> 00:01:53,384
measure the rail and add a third.

58
00:01:53,564 --> 00:01:56,536
Most people buy one six-foot garland for

59
00:01:56,536 --> 00:01:57,948
a five-foot mantel,

60
00:01:57,948 --> 00:02:00,623
and that's where the trouble starts.

61
00:02:00,803 --> 00:02:02,847
In a minute you'll see why.

62
00:02:03,197 --> 00:02:04,961
Mistake number one.

63
00:02:05,141 --> 00:02:06,302
A thin garland.

64
00:02:06,482 --> 00:02:09,426
Most store garland is skinny and flat,

65
00:02:09,426 --> 00:02:10,975
like a pipe cleaner.

66
00:02:11,155 --> 00:02:12,874
Stretched across a mantel,

67
00:02:12,874 --> 00:02:14,725
it looks like you ran out of

68
00:02:14,725 --> 00:02:16,972
money in the middle of decorating.

69
00:02:17,152 --> 00:02:19,597
A garland should be big and full,

70
00:02:19,597 --> 00:02:21,523
eight or ten inches thick,

71
00:02:21,523 --> 00:02:24,931
with branches sticking out in every direction.

72
00:02:25,111 --> 00:02:27,885
Fullness is what makes it look rich.

73
00:02:28,236 --> 00:02:30,116
Here's the free fix.

74
00:02:30,296 --> 00:02:33,054
Take two or three cheap garlands and

75
00:02:33,054 --> 00:02:35,276
twist them together into one,

76
00:02:35,276 --> 00:02:38,034
and fluff every branch out with your

77
00:02:38,034 --> 00:02:40,409
fingers, up, down and sideways.

78
00:02:40,589 --> 00:02:41,903
It takes an hour,

79
00:02:41,903 --> 00:02:43,758
but it doubles the size.

80
00:02:43,938 --> 00:02:46,257
My mother would put the radio on

81
00:02:46,257 --> 00:02:48,576
and fluff for a whole afternoon,

82
00:02:48,576 --> 00:02:50,823
singing along with Bing Crosby.

83
00:02:51,173 --> 00:02:52,821
Mistake number two.

84
00:02:53,001 --> 00:02:55,370
All fake and all one kind.

85
00:02:55,550 --> 00:02:57,010
A plastic garland,

86
00:02:57,010 --> 00:02:58,552
all the same green,

87
00:02:58,552 --> 00:03:00,094
all the same shape,

88
00:03:00,094 --> 00:03:03,340
looks like plastic from across the room.

89
00:03:03,520 --> 00:03:05,676
The fix is to tuck in real

90
00:03:05,676 --> 00:03:06,422
branches.

91
00:03:06,602 --> 00:03:09,122
Cedar, pine, spruce,

92
00:03:09,122 --> 00:03:12,523
boxwood, holly, eucalyptus.

93
00:03:12,703 --> 00:03:14,898
Mix two or three kinds.

94
00:03:15,078 --> 00:03:17,693
The different shapes and greens make it

95
00:03:17,693 --> 00:03:20,108
look natural, and the real ones make

96
00:03:20,108 --> 00:03:22,589
the whole house smell like Christmas.

97
00:03:22,940 --> 00:03:25,754
And here's where you get them free,

98
00:03:25,754 --> 00:03:26,237
honey.

99
00:03:26,417 --> 00:03:29,050
The Christmas tree lot trims the bottom

100
00:03:29,050 --> 00:03:31,346
branches off every tree they sell,

101
00:03:31,346 --> 00:03:33,304
and they throw them in a pile

102
00:03:33,304 --> 00:03:34,114
in the back.

103
00:03:34,294 --> 00:03:35,502
Just ask.

104
00:03:35,682 --> 00:03:37,468
They'll give you an armful,

105
00:03:37,468 --> 00:03:39,982
and sometimes they'll even help you to

106
00:03:39,982 --> 00:03:40,511
the car.

107
00:03:40,691 --> 00:03:43,771
Real branches stay fresh about two weeks

108
00:03:43,771 --> 00:03:45,927
indoors, away from the heat.

109
00:03:46,107 --> 00:03:48,717
Mist them with water every couple of

110
00:03:48,717 --> 00:03:49,080
days.

111
00:03:49,430 --> 00:03:51,543
Mistake number three.

112
00:03:51,723 --> 00:03:53,975
Hanging it straight and flat,

113
00:03:53,975 --> 00:03:54,985
like a shelf.

114
00:03:55,165 --> 00:03:57,792
A garland across a mantel should drape

115
00:03:57,792 --> 00:03:59,867
a little, or hang down at both

116
00:03:59,867 --> 00:04:02,148
ends, longer on the sides than in

117
00:04:02,148 --> 00:04:02,909
the middle.

118
00:04:03,089 --> 00:04:05,243
Let the ends fall about a third

119
00:04:05,243 --> 00:04:07,189
of the way down the sides of

120
00:04:07,189 --> 00:04:08,162
the fireplace.

121
00:04:08,342 --> 00:04:11,581
That loose, generous look is what you

122
00:04:11,581 --> 00:04:13,857
see in the fancy catalogs.

123
00:04:14,207 --> 00:04:15,860
If this is helping you,

124
00:04:15,860 --> 00:04:18,305
honey, tap the like button for me.

125
00:04:18,485 --> 00:04:21,353
It helps Grandma more than you know.

126
00:04:21,533 --> 00:04:23,622
And how do you hang it without

127
00:04:23,622 --> 00:04:25,085
nails in your mantel?

128
00:04:25,265 --> 00:04:27,498
Command hooks on the underside,

129
00:04:27,498 --> 00:04:29,370
or a heavy book or a brick

130
00:04:29,370 --> 00:04:30,738
at each end on top,

131
00:04:30,738 --> 00:04:33,043
with the garland tied to it with

132
00:04:33,043 --> 00:04:35,563
wire and hidden under the branches.

133
00:04:35,743 --> 00:04:38,607
My father used two bricks wrapped in

134
00:04:38,607 --> 00:04:39,482
green felt.

135
00:04:39,832 --> 00:04:41,527
Mistake number four.

136
00:04:41,707 --> 00:04:44,462
Lights wrapped around the outside of the

137
00:04:44,462 --> 00:04:46,803
garland, like a candy cane stripe.

138
00:04:46,983 --> 00:04:49,205
You see the wires and the plugs,

139
00:04:49,205 --> 00:04:50,524
and it looks cheap.

140
00:04:50,704 --> 00:04:52,121
Here's the fix.

141
00:04:52,301 --> 00:04:54,858
Tuck the lights deep inside the garland,

142
00:04:54,858 --> 00:04:57,286
pushing the strands into the middle of

143
00:04:57,286 --> 00:04:58,117
the branches.

144
00:04:58,297 --> 00:05:00,784
Then it glows from inside,

145
00:05:00,784 --> 00:05:02,698
softly, like a fire.

146
00:05:02,878 --> 00:05:04,997
And use warm white lights,

147
00:05:04,997 --> 00:05:07,034
never the cold blue ones.

148
00:05:07,384 --> 00:05:09,892
And use more lights than you think,

149
00:05:09,892 --> 00:05:10,681
sweetheart.

150
00:05:10,861 --> 00:05:13,438
One hundred little lights for every six

151
00:05:13,438 --> 00:05:14,495
feet of garland.

152
00:05:14,675 --> 00:05:16,446
That sounds like a lot,

153
00:05:16,446 --> 00:05:18,911
but tucked deep in the branches,

154
00:05:18,911 --> 00:05:20,143
it's just right.

155
00:05:20,323 --> 00:05:22,348
Buy the ones on a battery pack

156
00:05:22,348 --> 00:05:23,225
with a timer,

157
00:05:23,225 --> 00:05:25,453
and hide the battery box behind a

158
00:05:25,453 --> 00:05:27,208
picture frame or a candle.

159
00:05:27,388 --> 00:05:29,781
Then there's no cord hanging down to

160
00:05:29,781 --> 00:05:31,776
the floor for the cat to chew.

161
00:05:32,127 --> 00:05:34,028
So far, make it full,

162
00:05:34,028 --> 00:05:35,749
mix real greens in,

163
00:05:35,749 --> 00:05:36,926
let it drape,

164
00:05:36,926 --> 00:05:39,371
and tuck the lights inside.

165
00:05:39,551 --> 00:05:41,862
Now mistake number five.

166
00:05:42,042 --> 00:05:43,957
Too many things stuck in it.

167
00:05:44,137 --> 00:05:46,653
Ornaments, ribbons, signs,

168
00:05:46,653 --> 00:05:50,232
little figures, all different colors.

169
00:05:50,412 --> 00:05:52,479
It looks like a junk drawer.

170
00:05:52,659 --> 00:05:54,881
Pick two or three things and repeat

171
00:05:54,881 --> 00:05:56,595
them all along the garland.

172
00:05:56,775 --> 00:05:58,671
Pinecones, red berries,

173
00:05:58,671 --> 00:06:00,731
and a few gold ornaments,

174
00:06:00,731 --> 00:06:01,721
for example.

175
00:06:02,071 --> 00:06:04,336
Repetition is the secret,

176
00:06:04,336 --> 00:06:04,880
honey.

177
00:06:05,060 --> 00:06:06,836
The same three things,

178
00:06:06,836 --> 00:06:07,966
over and over,

179
00:06:07,966 --> 00:06:10,064
every eight or ten inches.

180
00:06:10,244 --> 00:06:12,563
Your eye reads it as a pattern,

181
00:06:12,563 --> 00:06:14,807
and a pattern looks expensive.

182
00:06:14,987 --> 00:06:17,471
My mother used pinecones,

183
00:06:17,471 --> 00:06:21,047
red candles and dried orange slices.

184
00:06:21,227 --> 00:06:22,493
Three things.

185
00:06:22,673 --> 00:06:24,205
Every year the same.

186
00:06:24,385 --> 00:06:25,697
And every year,

187
00:06:25,697 --> 00:06:29,459
somebody asked her who decorated the piano.

188
00:06:29,809 --> 00:06:32,625
And here's how to dry orange slices

189
00:06:32,625 --> 00:06:33,350
for free.

190
00:06:33,530 --> 00:06:34,932
Slice oranges thin,

191
00:06:34,932 --> 00:06:36,040
a quarter inch,

192
00:06:36,040 --> 00:06:38,255
and pat them dry with a towel.

193
00:06:38,435 --> 00:06:40,186
Lay them on a rack over a

194
00:06:40,186 --> 00:06:42,707
baking sheet and bake at two hundred

195
00:06:42,707 --> 00:06:44,809
degrees for about three hours,

196
00:06:44,809 --> 00:06:46,490
turning them every hour,

197
00:06:46,490 --> 00:06:49,081
until they're dry like stained glass.

198
00:06:49,261 --> 00:06:50,917
Hold one up to the window,

199
00:06:50,917 --> 00:06:53,336
and the light shines right through it.

200
00:06:53,687 --> 00:06:55,463
Mistake number six.

201
00:06:55,643 --> 00:06:57,015
A bare stair rail,

202
00:06:57,015 --> 00:06:59,759
or a garland wrapped round and round

203
00:06:59,759 --> 00:07:01,436
it like a barber pole.

204
00:07:01,616 --> 00:07:03,253
The old way is better.

205
00:07:03,433 --> 00:07:05,597
Lay the garland along the top of

206
00:07:05,597 --> 00:07:07,761
the rail, and tie it with ribbon

207
00:07:07,761 --> 00:07:09,993
or twine every two or three feet.

208
00:07:10,173 --> 00:07:12,617
Then let it swag down a little

209
00:07:12,617 --> 00:07:14,002
between the ties,

210
00:07:14,002 --> 00:07:15,061
like a smile.

211
00:07:15,241 --> 00:07:17,135
Put a bow at every tie,

212
00:07:17,135 --> 00:07:19,606
or just at the top and bottom.

213
00:07:19,956 --> 00:07:21,291
And be careful,

214
00:07:21,291 --> 00:07:21,825
honey.

215
00:07:22,005 --> 00:07:24,280
Never cover the part of the rail

216
00:07:24,280 --> 00:07:25,987
where people's hands go.

217
00:07:26,167 --> 00:07:28,448
Leave the top of the rail clear,

218
00:07:28,448 --> 00:07:30,871
and tie the garland on the outside

219
00:07:30,871 --> 00:07:31,798
of the posts.

220
00:07:31,978 --> 00:07:35,102
My granddaughter Emily nearly went down the

221
00:07:35,102 --> 00:07:38,008
stairs on Christmas morning because of a

222
00:07:38,008 --> 00:07:40,333
garland, with a cup of coffee in

223
00:07:40,333 --> 00:07:40,987
her hand.

224
00:07:41,167 --> 00:07:43,710
Safety first, then pretty.

225
00:07:44,060 --> 00:07:46,463
And now mistake number seven,

226
00:07:46,463 --> 00:07:50,357
the trick decorators charge hundreds of dollars

227
00:07:50,357 --> 00:07:50,689
for.

228
00:07:50,869 --> 00:07:52,076
Forgetting the height.

229
00:07:52,256 --> 00:07:54,857
A garland all alone on a mantel,

230
00:07:54,857 --> 00:07:55,913
flat and low,

231
00:07:55,913 --> 00:07:56,889
looks small.

232
00:07:57,069 --> 00:07:59,704
The decorators add tall things.

233
00:07:59,884 --> 00:08:01,267
Two tall vases,

234
00:08:01,267 --> 00:08:02,743
one at each end,

235
00:08:02,743 --> 00:08:04,772
full of tall branches.

236
00:08:04,952 --> 00:08:06,630
Or big candlesticks,

237
00:08:06,630 --> 00:08:09,399
or a pair of little potted trees.

238
00:08:09,579 --> 00:08:11,086
Now the eye goes up,

239
00:08:11,086 --> 00:08:13,421
and the whole wall looks grand.

240
00:08:13,772 --> 00:08:15,683
And you can do it for free

241
00:08:15,683 --> 00:08:16,639
this weekend.

242
00:08:16,819 --> 00:08:18,873
Go out in the yard with your

243
00:08:18,873 --> 00:08:21,219
clippers, and cut tall branches.

244
00:08:21,399 --> 00:08:24,473
Bare birch, red twig dogwood,

245
00:08:24,473 --> 00:08:28,818
magnolia, pine, even dry hydrangea heads.

246
00:08:28,998 --> 00:08:30,785
Put them in two big jars or

247
00:08:30,785 --> 00:08:33,233
crocks with some stones in the bottom

248
00:08:33,233 --> 00:08:34,292
to hold them up.

249
00:08:34,472 --> 00:08:36,164
Then put a big wreath or a

250
00:08:36,164 --> 00:08:38,702
mirror in the middle above the garland,

251
00:08:38,702 --> 00:08:39,743
and you're done.

252
00:08:40,094 --> 00:08:43,081
And a word about candles in garland,

253
00:08:43,081 --> 00:08:43,994
sweetheart.

254
00:08:44,174 --> 00:08:47,102
Real flames and dry branches are a

255
00:08:47,102 --> 00:08:48,308
terrible pair.

256
00:08:48,488 --> 00:08:51,906
Every December, the fire department in Mansfield

257
00:08:51,906 --> 00:08:53,828
used to put a notice in the

258
00:08:53,828 --> 00:08:54,896
paper about it.

259
00:08:55,076 --> 00:08:57,885
Use battery candles inside the garland,

260
00:08:57,885 --> 00:09:00,765
the good ones with the flickering light.

261
00:09:00,945 --> 00:09:03,525
Keep any real candles in tall glass

262
00:09:03,525 --> 00:09:05,809
holders, well above the greens,

263
00:09:05,809 --> 00:09:08,536
and never leave them burning when you

264
00:09:08,536 --> 00:09:09,641
leave the room.

265
00:09:09,991 --> 00:09:13,268
And garland isn't only for the fireplace,

266
00:09:13,268 --> 00:09:14,147
sweetheart.

267
00:09:14,327 --> 00:09:16,405
Over the kitchen window.

268
00:09:16,585 --> 00:09:19,046
Across the top of a bookshelf.

269
00:09:19,226 --> 00:09:21,873
Along the middle of the dinner table,

270
00:09:21,873 --> 00:09:23,232
with candles in it.

271
00:09:23,412 --> 00:09:25,211
Over the front door,

272
00:09:25,211 --> 00:09:25,931
outside.

273
00:09:26,111 --> 00:09:28,527
Or across the headboard of the guest

274
00:09:28,527 --> 00:09:30,138
bed, with little lights,

275
00:09:30,138 --> 00:09:31,614
for the grandchildren.

276
00:09:31,794 --> 00:09:33,246
That's their favorite.

277
00:09:33,426 --> 00:09:35,725
They say it's like sleeping in the

278
00:09:35,725 --> 00:09:36,131
woods.

279
00:09:36,481 --> 00:09:38,701
And when you take it down,

280
00:09:38,701 --> 00:09:41,007
after the sixth of January,

281
00:09:41,007 --> 00:09:42,715
save the best parts.

282
00:09:42,895 --> 00:09:44,960
Pull out the lights and wind them

283
00:09:44,960 --> 00:09:46,713
around a piece of cardboard,

284
00:09:46,713 --> 00:09:48,027
so they don't tangle.

285
00:09:48,207 --> 00:09:51,404
Keep the pinecones and dried oranges in

286
00:09:51,404 --> 00:09:52,224
a shoebox.

287
00:09:52,404 --> 00:09:55,008
Throw the real branches in the yard

288
00:09:55,008 --> 00:09:56,049
for the birds.

289
00:09:56,229 --> 00:09:57,296
And next year,

290
00:09:57,296 --> 00:10:00,039
you start with half the work already

291
00:10:00,039 --> 00:10:00,421
done.

292
00:10:00,771 --> 00:10:02,036
So one more time.

293
00:10:02,216 --> 00:10:03,309
Make it full,

294
00:10:03,309 --> 00:10:05,745
twist two together and fluff.

295
00:10:05,925 --> 00:10:07,643
Mix in real greens,

296
00:10:07,643 --> 00:10:09,722
free from the tree lot.

297
00:10:09,902 --> 00:10:11,992
Let it drape at the ends.

298
00:10:12,172 --> 00:10:14,598
Tuck warm lights deep inside.

299
00:10:14,778 --> 00:10:17,193
Pick three things and repeat them.

300
00:10:17,373 --> 00:10:18,845
Swag the stairs,

301
00:10:18,845 --> 00:10:21,053
and keep the rail clear.

302
00:10:21,233 --> 00:10:23,939
And add height with tall branches.

303
00:10:24,119 --> 00:10:26,354
That's how my mother made a piano

304
00:10:26,354 --> 00:10:27,776
look like a magazine.

305
00:10:28,126 --> 00:10:30,076
Tell me in the comments,

306
00:10:30,076 --> 00:10:30,970
sweetheart.

307
00:10:31,150 --> 00:10:33,774
Real garland, or fake garland?

308
00:10:33,954 --> 00:10:36,241
And where do you hang yours?

309
00:10:36,421 --> 00:10:39,509
The whole playlist of Grandma's Christmas tips

310
00:10:39,509 --> 00:10:41,523
is right there on your screen,

311
00:10:41,523 --> 00:10:43,402
and I'll see you in the next

312
00:10:43,402 --> 00:10:43,805
video.

313
00:10:43,985 --> 00:10:45,576
Good night, honey.

314
00:10:45,756 --> 00:10:47,149
Merry Christmas.
