1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:03,674
Sweetheart, every family has one Christmas dessert

2
00:00:03,674 --> 00:00:06,025
that makes the grown-ups giggle.

3
00:00:06,205 --> 00:00:08,666
In ours, it was the rum cake.

4
00:00:08,846 --> 00:00:11,132
A golden ring of butter cake,

5
00:00:11,132 --> 00:00:14,048
soaked through with a warm butter and

6
00:00:14,048 --> 00:00:16,648
rum glaze, and covered in pecans.

7
00:00:16,828 --> 00:00:19,656
My Aunt Margaret ate three slices one

8
00:00:19,656 --> 00:00:23,249
Christmas Eve in nineteen seventy-four and sang

9
00:00:23,249 --> 00:00:26,000
Silent Night in four different keys.

10
00:00:26,351 --> 00:00:28,857
But most rum cakes today come out

11
00:00:28,857 --> 00:00:31,136
dry, or the glaze just sits on

12
00:00:31,136 --> 00:00:32,882
top in a sticky puddle,

13
00:00:32,882 --> 00:00:35,465
or the cake falls apart coming out

14
00:00:35,465 --> 00:00:36,300
of the pan.

15
00:00:36,480 --> 00:00:38,914
So tonight I'm giving you my rum

16
00:00:38,914 --> 00:00:40,207
cake, every step,

17
00:00:40,207 --> 00:00:42,794
and the four mistakes that make it

18
00:00:42,794 --> 00:00:43,098
dry.

19
00:00:43,278 --> 00:00:44,612
And stay with me,

20
00:00:44,612 --> 00:00:47,514
because the last secret is about when

21
00:00:47,514 --> 00:00:48,926
to pour the glaze,

22
00:00:48,926 --> 00:00:51,672
and almost everybody does it wrong.

23
00:00:52,022 --> 00:00:53,941
Rum cake came to us from the

24
00:00:53,941 --> 00:00:57,163
Caribbean, honey, where they've made rich cakes

25
00:00:57,163 --> 00:01:00,042
soaked with rum for Christmas for hundreds

26
00:01:00,042 --> 00:01:00,659
of years.

27
00:01:00,839 --> 00:01:02,147
In the seventies,

28
00:01:02,147 --> 00:01:04,838
a quick version became all the rage

29
00:01:04,838 --> 00:01:07,145
in America, made with a box of

30
00:01:07,145 --> 00:01:09,298
yellow cake mix and a box of

31
00:01:09,298 --> 00:01:10,220
pudding mix.

32
00:01:10,400 --> 00:01:13,442
Every church cookbook in Ohio had it.

33
00:01:13,622 --> 00:01:15,297
Mine had four of them,

34
00:01:15,297 --> 00:01:17,048
all slightly different,

35
00:01:17,048 --> 00:01:19,485
all claiming to be the original.

36
00:01:19,835 --> 00:01:22,131
I got mine from my friend Joyce,

37
00:01:22,131 --> 00:01:24,355
who went on a cruise to Jamaica

38
00:01:24,355 --> 00:01:27,369
in nineteen seventy-two and came home with

39
00:01:27,369 --> 00:01:28,732
a tan, a straw hat,

40
00:01:28,732 --> 00:01:30,884
and this recipe on the back of

41
00:01:30,884 --> 00:01:32,176
a cocktail napkin.

42
00:01:32,356 --> 00:01:35,129
Joyce told everybody the chef gave it

43
00:01:35,129 --> 00:01:35,653
to her.

44
00:01:35,833 --> 00:01:37,989
Her husband told me she bribed a

45
00:01:37,989 --> 00:01:39,606
waiter with two dollars.

46
00:01:39,786 --> 00:01:41,435
I believe her husband.

47
00:01:41,785 --> 00:01:44,490
And here's something people don't know.

48
00:01:44,670 --> 00:01:46,948
The rum cooks off in the oven,

49
00:01:46,948 --> 00:01:49,303
but the glaze doesn't go in the

50
00:01:49,303 --> 00:01:51,961
oven, so most of the alcohol stays.

51
00:01:52,141 --> 00:01:54,026
This is a grown-up cake,

52
00:01:54,026 --> 00:01:54,498
honey.

53
00:01:54,678 --> 00:01:56,740
In a minute I'll tell you how

54
00:01:56,740 --> 00:01:59,016
to make one the children can eat

55
00:01:59,016 --> 00:02:01,363
too, so nobody at the table feels

56
00:02:01,363 --> 00:02:02,003
left out.

57
00:02:02,354 --> 00:02:04,618
Here's what you need for the cake.

58
00:02:04,798 --> 00:02:07,572
One box of yellow cake mix.

59
00:02:07,752 --> 00:02:10,832
One small box of instant vanilla pudding

60
00:02:10,832 --> 00:02:13,219
mix, the three and a half ounce

61
00:02:13,219 --> 00:02:13,604
size.

62
00:02:13,784 --> 00:02:14,840
Four eggs.

63
00:02:15,020 --> 00:02:17,075
Half a cup of cold water.

64
00:02:17,255 --> 00:02:19,496
Half a cup of vegetable oil.

65
00:02:19,676 --> 00:02:21,568
Half a cup of dark rum.

66
00:02:21,748 --> 00:02:24,146
And one cup of chopped pecans or

67
00:02:24,146 --> 00:02:26,694
walnuts for the bottom of the pan.

68
00:02:27,045 --> 00:02:28,693
And for the glaze.

69
00:02:28,873 --> 00:02:30,441
One stick of butter.

70
00:02:30,621 --> 00:02:32,327
A quarter cup of water.

71
00:02:32,507 --> 00:02:34,643
One cup of white sugar.

72
00:02:34,823 --> 00:02:37,203
And half a cup of dark rum.

73
00:02:37,383 --> 00:02:38,568
That's all.

74
00:02:38,748 --> 00:02:40,559
Now, about the rum.

75
00:02:40,739 --> 00:02:42,933
Use a dark or gold rum,

76
00:02:42,933 --> 00:02:44,268
not white rum.

77
00:02:44,448 --> 00:02:47,220
Dark rum has that warm molasses and

78
00:02:47,220 --> 00:02:48,407
vanilla flavor.

79
00:02:48,587 --> 00:02:51,413
White rum just tastes like alcohol,

80
00:02:51,413 --> 00:02:53,835
and that's mistake number one.

81
00:02:54,185 --> 00:02:56,494
Step one, and this is where most

82
00:02:56,494 --> 00:02:59,165
rum cakes are lost before they start.

83
00:02:59,345 --> 00:03:00,262
The pan.

84
00:03:00,442 --> 00:03:03,322
Use a ten-inch Bundt pan or tube

85
00:03:03,322 --> 00:03:03,682
pan.

86
00:03:03,862 --> 00:03:06,285
Grease every inch of it with soft

87
00:03:06,285 --> 00:03:08,634
butter, with a pastry brush or a

88
00:03:08,634 --> 00:03:12,012
paper towel, getting into every little groove.

89
00:03:12,192 --> 00:03:14,255
Then dust it with flour,

90
00:03:14,255 --> 00:03:15,803
tap out the extra.

91
00:03:15,983 --> 00:03:17,596
If you miss one groove,

92
00:03:17,596 --> 00:03:20,193
the cake sticks right there and tears

93
00:03:20,193 --> 00:03:20,754
in half.

94
00:03:21,105 --> 00:03:24,071
Then sprinkle the chopped nuts evenly in

95
00:03:24,071 --> 00:03:25,702
the bottom of the pan.

96
00:03:25,882 --> 00:03:28,241
When you turn the cake out later,

97
00:03:28,241 --> 00:03:29,957
the nuts will be on top,

98
00:03:29,957 --> 00:03:30,886
like a crown.

99
00:03:31,066 --> 00:03:33,374
Joyce toasted hers first in a dry

100
00:03:33,374 --> 00:03:35,122
skillet for five minutes,

101
00:03:35,122 --> 00:03:37,010
and that's how I do it too.

102
00:03:37,190 --> 00:03:40,488
Toasted pecans taste twice as rich.

103
00:03:40,838 --> 00:03:43,314
And if you don't trust your pan,

104
00:03:43,314 --> 00:03:46,178
honey, use baking spray with flour in

105
00:03:46,178 --> 00:03:48,732
it, the kind made for Bundt pans.

106
00:03:48,912 --> 00:03:50,588
And never use a dark,

107
00:03:50,588 --> 00:03:53,062
thin, cheap pan if you can help

108
00:03:53,062 --> 00:03:53,301
it.

109
00:03:53,481 --> 00:03:56,164
Dark pans bake the outside too fast

110
00:03:56,164 --> 00:03:58,847
and burn the nuts before the middle

111
00:03:58,847 --> 00:03:59,460
is done.

112
00:03:59,640 --> 00:04:02,639
A heavy, light-colored pan is worth the

113
00:04:02,639 --> 00:04:03,100
money.

114
00:04:03,280 --> 00:04:05,839
Mine is from nineteen seventy-one,

115
00:04:05,839 --> 00:04:07,796
and it's never stuck once.

116
00:04:08,146 --> 00:04:09,144
Step two.

117
00:04:09,324 --> 00:04:12,328
Heat the oven to three hundred twenty-five

118
00:04:12,328 --> 00:04:12,900
degrees.

119
00:04:13,080 --> 00:04:14,296
In a big bowl,

120
00:04:14,296 --> 00:04:15,773
put the cake mix,

121
00:04:15,773 --> 00:04:17,163
the pudding mix,

122
00:04:17,163 --> 00:04:18,901
the eggs, the water,

123
00:04:18,901 --> 00:04:20,638
the oil and the rum.

124
00:04:20,818 --> 00:04:22,699
Beat it with a mixer on low

125
00:04:22,699 --> 00:04:24,022
for thirty seconds,

126
00:04:24,022 --> 00:04:26,182
then on medium for two minutes.

127
00:04:26,362 --> 00:04:28,742
The pudding mix is the secret,

128
00:04:28,742 --> 00:04:29,218
honey.

129
00:04:29,398 --> 00:04:32,074
It makes the cake dense and moist,

130
00:04:32,074 --> 00:04:34,042
almost like a pound cake.

131
00:04:34,392 --> 00:04:36,190
If this is helping you,

132
00:04:36,190 --> 00:04:38,850
honey, tap the like button for me.

133
00:04:39,030 --> 00:04:42,048
It helps Grandma more than you know.

134
00:04:42,228 --> 00:04:44,296
Now pour the batter over the nuts

135
00:04:44,296 --> 00:04:46,176
in the pan and smooth the top.

136
00:04:46,356 --> 00:04:48,523
Then tap the pan hard on the

137
00:04:48,523 --> 00:04:50,071
counter three times.

138
00:04:50,251 --> 00:04:52,556
That knocks out the big air bubbles,

139
00:04:52,556 --> 00:04:54,412
so you don't get holes in the

140
00:04:54,412 --> 00:04:54,732
cake.

141
00:04:55,083 --> 00:04:57,837
Bake it for about fifty-five minutes to

142
00:04:57,837 --> 00:04:58,473
one hour.

143
00:04:58,653 --> 00:05:01,477
Mistake number two is overbaking it,

144
00:05:01,477 --> 00:05:02,968
which makes it dry,

145
00:05:02,968 --> 00:05:05,557
no matter how much glaze you pour

146
00:05:05,557 --> 00:05:05,793
on.

147
00:05:05,973 --> 00:05:08,028
Start checking at fifty minutes.

148
00:05:08,208 --> 00:05:10,604
Stick a long wooden skewer into the

149
00:05:10,604 --> 00:05:11,563
thickest part.

150
00:05:11,743 --> 00:05:14,110
It should come out with just a

151
00:05:14,110 --> 00:05:15,451
few moist crumbs,

152
00:05:15,451 --> 00:05:16,635
not wet batter,

153
00:05:16,635 --> 00:05:19,081
and not perfectly clean either.

154
00:05:19,431 --> 00:05:21,544
Step three, the glaze.

155
00:05:21,724 --> 00:05:24,012
Start it about ten minutes before the

156
00:05:24,012 --> 00:05:24,940
cake comes out.

157
00:05:25,120 --> 00:05:26,771
In a small saucepan,

158
00:05:26,771 --> 00:05:28,092
melt the butter.

159
00:05:28,272 --> 00:05:30,292
Stir in the water and the sugar.

160
00:05:30,472 --> 00:05:32,310
Bring it to a boil and let

161
00:05:32,310 --> 00:05:34,077
it boil for five minutes,

162
00:05:34,077 --> 00:05:35,774
stirring the whole time,

163
00:05:35,774 --> 00:05:38,601
until the sugar is completely melted and

164
00:05:38,601 --> 00:05:40,015
it's a little thick.

165
00:05:40,195 --> 00:05:42,000
Then take it off the heat,

166
00:05:42,000 --> 00:05:43,388
and stir in the rum.

167
00:05:43,738 --> 00:05:45,467
Careful, sweetheart.

168
00:05:45,647 --> 00:05:47,965
Always take the pot off the stove

169
00:05:47,965 --> 00:05:49,581
before you add the rum,

170
00:05:49,581 --> 00:05:51,267
and stand back a little.

171
00:05:51,447 --> 00:05:54,183
Rum near a gas flame can catch

172
00:05:54,183 --> 00:05:54,639
fire.

173
00:05:54,819 --> 00:05:57,384
My friend Joyce singed her eyebrows in

174
00:05:57,384 --> 00:06:00,285
nineteen seventy-three, and she had to draw

175
00:06:00,285 --> 00:06:02,242
them on with a pencil for the

176
00:06:02,242 --> 00:06:03,794
whole New Year's party.

177
00:06:03,974 --> 00:06:06,644
She looked surprised until February.

178
00:06:06,995 --> 00:06:09,470
And now the secret I promised you,

179
00:06:09,470 --> 00:06:11,580
about when to pour the glaze.

180
00:06:11,760 --> 00:06:14,080
Most people turn the cake out of

181
00:06:14,080 --> 00:06:15,095
the pan first,

182
00:06:15,095 --> 00:06:17,415
and then pour the glaze over the

183
00:06:17,415 --> 00:06:17,705
top.

184
00:06:17,885 --> 00:06:20,249
And the glaze runs right off the

185
00:06:20,249 --> 00:06:21,948
outside onto the plate,

186
00:06:21,948 --> 00:06:24,312
and the inside of the cake stays

187
00:06:24,312 --> 00:06:24,607
dry.

188
00:06:24,787 --> 00:06:26,888
That's mistake number three.

189
00:06:27,239 --> 00:06:29,920
Here's how Joyce's waiter did it.

190
00:06:30,100 --> 00:06:31,952
Take the cake out of the oven,

191
00:06:31,952 --> 00:06:33,433
and leave it in the pan.

192
00:06:33,613 --> 00:06:35,878
Right away, while it's hot,

193
00:06:35,878 --> 00:06:38,815
poke holes all over the bottom with

194
00:06:38,815 --> 00:06:39,990
a long skewer,

195
00:06:39,990 --> 00:06:41,416
all the way down,

196
00:06:41,416 --> 00:06:42,842
every inch or so.

197
00:06:43,022 --> 00:06:45,524
Then slowly spoon half of the hot

198
00:06:45,524 --> 00:06:46,585
glaze over it,

199
00:06:46,585 --> 00:06:48,025
a little at a time,

200
00:06:48,025 --> 00:06:50,527
letting it soak in before you add

201
00:06:50,527 --> 00:06:50,906
more.

202
00:06:51,256 --> 00:06:53,074
Let it sit in the pan for

203
00:06:53,074 --> 00:06:54,820
thirty minutes, soaking.

204
00:06:55,000 --> 00:06:56,979
Then put a plate on top,

205
00:06:56,979 --> 00:06:58,051
turn it over,

206
00:06:58,051 --> 00:06:59,783
and lift the pan off.

207
00:06:59,963 --> 00:07:02,071
Poke a few holes in the top,

208
00:07:02,071 --> 00:07:04,480
and slowly spoon the rest of the

209
00:07:04,480 --> 00:07:06,964
glaze over the top and the sides,

210
00:07:06,964 --> 00:07:09,599
brushing it on with a pastry brush.

211
00:07:09,779 --> 00:07:11,831
The whole cake drinks it up,

212
00:07:11,831 --> 00:07:13,297
all the way through.

213
00:07:13,477 --> 00:07:15,567
Not a single dry crumb.

214
00:07:15,917 --> 00:07:17,300
So far, dark rum,

215
00:07:17,300 --> 00:07:19,008
every groove greased,

216
00:07:19,008 --> 00:07:20,798
pudding in the batter,

217
00:07:20,798 --> 00:07:23,890
no overbaking, and the glaze soaked in

218
00:07:23,890 --> 00:07:26,168
while it's still in the pan.

219
00:07:26,348 --> 00:07:28,833
And here's mistake number four.

220
00:07:29,013 --> 00:07:30,766
Cutting it the same day.

221
00:07:30,946 --> 00:07:33,249
A rum cake gets better every day

222
00:07:33,249 --> 00:07:34,905
for three or four days,

223
00:07:34,905 --> 00:07:37,424
as the glaze settles into the cake.

224
00:07:37,604 --> 00:07:39,603
Wrap it tight in plastic,

225
00:07:39,603 --> 00:07:41,842
and wait at least one night.

226
00:07:42,192 --> 00:07:44,609
And if you'd like it even prettier

227
00:07:44,609 --> 00:07:45,605
for the table,

228
00:07:45,605 --> 00:07:48,307
sweetheart, dust the top with a little

229
00:07:48,307 --> 00:07:50,867
powdered sugar right before serving,

230
00:07:50,867 --> 00:07:53,000
like fresh snow on the pecans.

231
00:07:53,180 --> 00:07:55,072
Or tuck a few sprigs of holly

232
00:07:55,072 --> 00:07:57,420
or rosemary around the bottom of the

233
00:07:57,420 --> 00:08:00,029
plate, and put a few sugared cranberries

234
00:08:00,029 --> 00:08:01,725
in the hole in the middle.

235
00:08:01,905 --> 00:08:04,280
It looks like a Christmas wreath you

236
00:08:04,280 --> 00:08:04,808
can eat.

237
00:08:05,158 --> 00:08:07,621
And here's the version for the children,

238
00:08:07,621 --> 00:08:08,606
like I promised.

239
00:08:08,786 --> 00:08:11,624
Use water or apple juice instead of

240
00:08:11,624 --> 00:08:12,921
rum in the cake,

241
00:08:12,921 --> 00:08:14,300
and in the glaze,

242
00:08:14,300 --> 00:08:17,056
use orange juice and a teaspoon of

243
00:08:17,056 --> 00:08:19,002
rum extract, or vanilla.

244
00:08:19,182 --> 00:08:20,785
It's not quite the same,

245
00:08:20,785 --> 00:08:22,921
but it's moist and sweet and the

246
00:08:22,921 --> 00:08:24,256
little ones love it.

247
00:08:24,436 --> 00:08:25,709
I make one of each,

248
00:08:25,709 --> 00:08:27,384
and I put a red ribbon on

249
00:08:27,384 --> 00:08:29,394
the plate of the grown-up one.

250
00:08:29,744 --> 00:08:31,914
It keeps for a week at room

251
00:08:31,914 --> 00:08:34,084
temperature, wrapped tight,

252
00:08:34,084 --> 00:08:36,013
or longer in the icebox.

253
00:08:36,193 --> 00:08:39,270
And it freezes beautifully for three months.

254
00:08:39,450 --> 00:08:41,269
Wrap it in plastic,

255
00:08:41,269 --> 00:08:42,515
then in foil.

256
00:08:42,695 --> 00:08:45,156
It's the perfect cake for mailing to

257
00:08:45,156 --> 00:08:46,251
family far away,

258
00:08:46,251 --> 00:08:48,576
because it only gets better on the

259
00:08:48,576 --> 00:08:48,918
trip.

260
00:08:49,098 --> 00:08:51,191
I've mailed one to my son in

261
00:08:51,191 --> 00:08:54,554
Arizona every December since nineteen ninety.

262
00:08:54,905 --> 00:08:56,932
Serve it in thin slices,

263
00:08:56,932 --> 00:08:59,467
sweetheart, because it's rich.

264
00:08:59,647 --> 00:09:01,764
With a spoon of whipped cream,

265
00:09:01,764 --> 00:09:04,023
or a scoop of vanilla ice cream,

266
00:09:04,023 --> 00:09:05,928
and a cup of strong coffee.

267
00:09:06,108 --> 00:09:08,430
Some people warm a slice for a

268
00:09:08,430 --> 00:09:11,294
few seconds, so the butter glaze gets

269
00:09:11,294 --> 00:09:12,145
soft again.

270
00:09:12,325 --> 00:09:14,896
My husband liked his with a slice

271
00:09:14,896 --> 00:09:17,155
of sharp cheddar on the side.

272
00:09:17,335 --> 00:09:19,355
Ohio men, honey.

273
00:09:19,535 --> 00:09:21,544
I don't ask questions.

274
00:09:21,894 --> 00:09:23,356
So one more time.

275
00:09:23,536 --> 00:09:25,765
Dark rum, not white.

276
00:09:25,945 --> 00:09:27,455
Grease every groove.

277
00:09:27,635 --> 00:09:29,690
Toasted nuts in the bottom.

278
00:09:29,870 --> 00:09:31,658
Pudding mix in the batter,

279
00:09:31,658 --> 00:09:32,621
for moistness.

280
00:09:32,801 --> 00:09:34,827
Bake at three twenty-five,

281
00:09:34,827 --> 00:09:36,308
and don't overbake.

282
00:09:36,488 --> 00:09:38,792
Poke holes and soak it with half

283
00:09:38,792 --> 00:09:41,169
the glaze while it's still in the

284
00:09:41,169 --> 00:09:41,457
pan.

285
00:09:41,637 --> 00:09:42,746
Turn it out,

286
00:09:42,746 --> 00:09:44,133
glaze the rest.

287
00:09:44,313 --> 00:09:46,899
And wait one night before you cut

288
00:09:46,899 --> 00:09:47,134
it.

289
00:09:47,314 --> 00:09:49,838
That's a rum cake that never dries

290
00:09:49,838 --> 00:09:50,135
out.

291
00:09:50,486 --> 00:09:52,468
Tell me in the comments,

292
00:09:52,468 --> 00:09:53,376
sweetheart.

293
00:09:53,556 --> 00:09:56,049
What's the dessert in your family that

294
00:09:56,049 --> 00:09:58,607
made the grown-ups giggle at Christmas?

295
00:09:58,787 --> 00:10:01,750
The whole playlist of Grandma's recipes is

296
00:10:01,750 --> 00:10:03,656
right there on your screen,

297
00:10:03,656 --> 00:10:05,631
and I'll see you in the next

298
00:10:05,631 --> 00:10:06,055
video.

299
00:10:06,235 --> 00:10:07,964
Good night, honey.

300
00:10:08,144 --> 00:10:09,549
Merry Christmas.

1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:02,261
Sweetheart, when I was a girl,

2
00:00:02,261 --> 00:00:05,578
oxtail was what the butcher practically gave

3
00:00:05,578 --> 00:00:05,955
away.

4
00:00:06,135 --> 00:00:09,491
Fifteen cents a pound in nineteen fifty-two.

5
00:00:09,671 --> 00:00:12,395
Nobody wanted those knobby bones with a

6
00:00:12,395 --> 00:00:13,792
little meat on them.

7
00:00:13,972 --> 00:00:16,259
Except my Grandma Pearl.

8
00:00:16,439 --> 00:00:18,766
She'd buy three pounds on Saturday,

9
00:00:18,766 --> 00:00:19,697
and on Sunday,

10
00:00:19,697 --> 00:00:22,024
the whole house smelled so good the

11
00:00:22,024 --> 00:00:24,617
neighbors found excuses to knock on our

12
00:00:24,617 --> 00:00:24,950
door.

13
00:00:25,300 --> 00:00:28,075
Today oxtail costs more than steak,

14
00:00:28,075 --> 00:00:30,770
and people tell me theirs came out

15
00:00:30,770 --> 00:00:33,070
tough, or swimming in grease,

16
00:00:33,070 --> 00:00:35,052
or the gravy tastes thin.

17
00:00:35,232 --> 00:00:38,227
So tonight I'm giving you Grandma Pearl's

18
00:00:38,227 --> 00:00:39,615
Sunday oxtail stew,

19
00:00:39,615 --> 00:00:42,392
every step, and the four mistakes that

20
00:00:42,392 --> 00:00:44,218
make it greasy and tough.

21
00:00:44,398 --> 00:00:45,690
And stay with me,

22
00:00:45,690 --> 00:00:48,501
because the last trick takes away all

23
00:00:48,501 --> 00:00:51,236
the grease, and it costs nothing but

24
00:00:51,236 --> 00:00:52,908
a night in the icebox.

25
00:00:53,259 --> 00:00:56,513
Grandma Pearl lived through the Depression on

26
00:00:56,513 --> 00:00:58,320
a farm outside Mansfield.

27
00:00:58,500 --> 00:01:00,734
She said nobody in her house ever

28
00:01:00,734 --> 00:01:02,764
threw away a single part of an

29
00:01:02,764 --> 00:01:03,237
animal.

30
00:01:03,417 --> 00:01:04,870
Oxtail, neck bones,

31
00:01:04,870 --> 00:01:08,005
shanks, the pieces the city people didn't

32
00:01:08,005 --> 00:01:10,604
want, were the best eating of all,

33
00:01:10,604 --> 00:01:12,821
if you knew how to cook them.

34
00:01:13,001 --> 00:01:14,112
And the secret,

35
00:01:14,112 --> 00:01:16,333
she said, was always the same.

36
00:01:16,513 --> 00:01:17,164
Time.

37
00:01:17,514 --> 00:01:19,542
She'd put the pot on the back

38
00:01:19,542 --> 00:01:21,711
of her wood stove after church,

39
00:01:21,711 --> 00:01:24,369
and leave it there all afternoon while

40
00:01:24,369 --> 00:01:25,699
the family visited.

41
00:01:25,879 --> 00:01:28,544
By supper, the meat was falling off

42
00:01:28,544 --> 00:01:30,904
the bones, and the gravy was so

43
00:01:30,904 --> 00:01:31,970
rich and dark,

44
00:01:31,970 --> 00:01:33,646
it stuck to your lips.

45
00:01:33,826 --> 00:01:35,967
My father said it was the only

46
00:01:35,967 --> 00:01:38,679
food that made him forget his manners.

47
00:01:38,859 --> 00:01:41,029
He'd pick up the bones and suck

48
00:01:41,029 --> 00:01:43,410
them clean, and my mother let him.

49
00:01:43,759 --> 00:01:47,170
And oxtail isn't only a Grandma Pearl

50
00:01:47,170 --> 00:01:48,276
dish, honey.

51
00:01:48,456 --> 00:01:51,710
Jamaican families make it with butter beans

52
00:01:51,710 --> 00:01:52,693
and allspice.

53
00:01:52,873 --> 00:01:55,886
Korean families make a clear soup with

54
00:01:55,886 --> 00:01:56,124
it.

55
00:01:56,304 --> 00:01:59,701
Italians in Rome braise it with tomatoes

56
00:01:59,701 --> 00:02:00,635
and celery.

57
00:02:00,815 --> 00:02:03,111
Every kitchen in the world that ever

58
00:02:03,111 --> 00:02:05,470
had to stretch a dollar found oxtail.

59
00:02:05,650 --> 00:02:07,642
In a minute I'll tell you how

60
00:02:07,642 --> 00:02:09,358
to make yours go further,

61
00:02:09,358 --> 00:02:11,281
so three pounds feeds eight.

62
00:02:11,632 --> 00:02:13,465
Here's what you need,

63
00:02:13,465 --> 00:02:13,988
honey.

64
00:02:14,168 --> 00:02:16,552
Three to four pounds of oxtail,

65
00:02:16,552 --> 00:02:17,628
cut in pieces.

66
00:02:17,808 --> 00:02:20,300
Ask the butcher for big pieces from

67
00:02:20,300 --> 00:02:22,081
the thick end if you can.

68
00:02:22,261 --> 00:02:24,330
Two onions, three carrots,

69
00:02:24,330 --> 00:02:26,321
and three ribs of celery,

70
00:02:26,321 --> 00:02:27,276
all chopped.

71
00:02:27,456 --> 00:02:29,383
Four cloves of garlic.

72
00:02:29,563 --> 00:02:32,292
Two tablespoons of tomato paste.

73
00:02:32,472 --> 00:02:34,573
Three cups of beef broth.

74
00:02:34,753 --> 00:02:36,477
One cup of red wine,

75
00:02:36,477 --> 00:02:38,631
or one more cup of broth.

76
00:02:38,811 --> 00:02:40,051
Two bay leaves,

77
00:02:40,051 --> 00:02:42,201
and a few sprigs of thyme.

78
00:02:42,551 --> 00:02:43,890
And for the gravy,

79
00:02:43,890 --> 00:02:46,420
a quarter cup of flour for dusting

80
00:02:46,420 --> 00:02:47,090
the meat.

81
00:02:47,270 --> 00:02:48,756
Salt and pepper.

82
00:02:48,936 --> 00:02:52,141
And potatoes, either whole small ones in

83
00:02:52,141 --> 00:02:54,625
the pot, or mashed on the side.

84
00:02:54,805 --> 00:02:58,015
Grandma Pearl always made mashed potatoes,

85
00:02:58,015 --> 00:03:00,920
because she said a good gravy deserves

86
00:03:00,920 --> 00:03:02,142
somewhere to go.

87
00:03:02,322 --> 00:03:04,817
I've never found a reason to argue

88
00:03:04,817 --> 00:03:05,550
with that.

89
00:03:05,899 --> 00:03:07,445
When you buy oxtail,

90
00:03:07,445 --> 00:03:10,305
honey, look for pieces with plenty of

91
00:03:10,305 --> 00:03:12,623
deep red meat around the bone,

92
00:03:12,623 --> 00:03:14,787
and a thin rim of white fat,

93
00:03:14,787 --> 00:03:16,023
not a thick one.

94
00:03:16,203 --> 00:03:18,259
The pieces from the wide end of

95
00:03:18,259 --> 00:03:20,116
the tail have the most meat.

96
00:03:20,296 --> 00:03:22,387
The little ones from the tip are

97
00:03:22,387 --> 00:03:24,870
mostly bone, but don't throw them out.

98
00:03:25,050 --> 00:03:26,943
They make the gravy rich.

99
00:03:27,123 --> 00:03:29,536
Ask the butcher for a mix of

100
00:03:29,536 --> 00:03:29,967
both.

101
00:03:30,318 --> 00:03:31,316
Step one.

102
00:03:31,496 --> 00:03:34,500
Pat the oxtail very dry with paper

103
00:03:34,500 --> 00:03:35,118
towels.

104
00:03:35,298 --> 00:03:38,051
Season it well with salt and pepper

105
00:03:38,051 --> 00:03:39,152
on every side,

106
00:03:39,152 --> 00:03:41,747
then roll it lightly in the flour

107
00:03:41,747 --> 00:03:43,634
and shake off the extra.

108
00:03:43,814 --> 00:03:46,833
Mistake number one is skipping the drying.

109
00:03:47,013 --> 00:03:49,172
Wet meat steams in the pot.

110
00:03:49,352 --> 00:03:51,923
It turns gray instead of brown,

111
00:03:51,923 --> 00:03:54,743
and the stew never gets that deep,

112
00:03:54,743 --> 00:03:55,738
dark flavor.

113
00:03:56,088 --> 00:03:58,679
Heat two tablespoons of oil in a

114
00:03:58,679 --> 00:03:59,812
big heavy pot,

115
00:03:59,812 --> 00:04:00,865
a Dutch oven,

116
00:04:00,865 --> 00:04:02,485
until it's very hot.

117
00:04:02,665 --> 00:04:05,065
Brown the oxtail a few pieces at

118
00:04:05,065 --> 00:04:07,165
a time, so they don't touch,

119
00:04:07,165 --> 00:04:09,565
about four minutes on each side,

120
00:04:09,565 --> 00:04:12,115
until they're dark brown all over.

121
00:04:12,295 --> 00:04:13,874
Don't crowd the pot.

122
00:04:14,054 --> 00:04:16,865
It takes about twenty minutes to brown

123
00:04:16,865 --> 00:04:18,048
them all, honey.

124
00:04:18,228 --> 00:04:20,920
It's the most important twenty minutes of

125
00:04:20,920 --> 00:04:22,036
the whole recipe.

126
00:04:22,386 --> 00:04:24,334
Take the browned meat out and set

127
00:04:24,334 --> 00:04:25,160
it on a plate.

128
00:04:25,340 --> 00:04:27,996
Pour off all but two tablespoons of

129
00:04:27,996 --> 00:04:28,603
the fat.

130
00:04:28,783 --> 00:04:30,236
Then add the onions,

131
00:04:30,236 --> 00:04:31,618
carrots and celery,

132
00:04:31,618 --> 00:04:33,944
and cook them for eight minutes,

133
00:04:33,944 --> 00:04:36,342
scraping up all the brown bits on

134
00:04:36,342 --> 00:04:37,142
the bottom.

135
00:04:37,322 --> 00:04:39,779
Add the garlic and tomato paste,

136
00:04:39,779 --> 00:04:41,699
and stir for two minutes,

137
00:04:41,699 --> 00:04:44,080
until the paste turns dark red,

138
00:04:44,080 --> 00:04:45,693
almost brick colored.

139
00:04:46,043 --> 00:04:47,738
If this is helping you,

140
00:04:47,738 --> 00:04:50,245
honey, tap the like button for me.

141
00:04:50,425 --> 00:04:53,130
It helps Grandma more than you know.

142
00:04:53,310 --> 00:04:54,962
Now pour in the wine,

143
00:04:54,962 --> 00:04:57,636
and let it bubble for two minutes,

144
00:04:57,636 --> 00:04:59,208
scraping the bottom.

145
00:04:59,388 --> 00:05:00,405
Add the broth,

146
00:05:00,405 --> 00:05:02,511
the bay leaves and the thyme.

147
00:05:02,691 --> 00:05:04,475
Put the oxtail back in,

148
00:05:04,475 --> 00:05:06,801
with any juice from the plate.

149
00:05:06,981 --> 00:05:09,869
The liquid should come about three quarters

150
00:05:09,869 --> 00:05:11,414
of the way up the meat,

151
00:05:11,414 --> 00:05:12,287
not cover it.

152
00:05:12,637 --> 00:05:13,763
Step two.

153
00:05:13,943 --> 00:05:15,738
Cover the pot and put it in

154
00:05:15,738 --> 00:05:18,198
the oven at three hundred degrees for

155
00:05:18,198 --> 00:05:20,259
three and a half to four hours.

156
00:05:20,439 --> 00:05:22,935
Mistake number two is rushing it.

157
00:05:23,115 --> 00:05:24,649
Oxtail is all bone,

158
00:05:24,649 --> 00:05:26,667
gristle and tough muscle.

159
00:05:26,847 --> 00:05:28,880
If you cook it for two hours,

160
00:05:28,880 --> 00:05:30,632
it's like chewing a shoe.

161
00:05:30,812 --> 00:05:32,871
At three and a half hours,

162
00:05:32,871 --> 00:05:35,881
all that gristle melts into the gravy,

163
00:05:35,881 --> 00:05:38,415
and the meat falls right off the

164
00:05:38,415 --> 00:05:38,811
bone.

165
00:05:39,162 --> 00:05:41,323
And keep it low and gentle,

166
00:05:41,323 --> 00:05:42,203
sweetheart.

167
00:05:42,383 --> 00:05:45,440
Mistake number three is cooking it too

168
00:05:45,440 --> 00:05:47,532
hot, on a hard boil on the

169
00:05:47,532 --> 00:05:48,014
stove.

170
00:05:48,194 --> 00:05:51,060
Boiling makes the meat stringy and dry,

171
00:05:51,060 --> 00:05:53,558
even while it's sitting in liquid.

172
00:05:53,738 --> 00:05:56,451
The oven is better than the stovetop,

173
00:05:56,451 --> 00:05:59,237
because the heat comes from all sides,

174
00:05:59,237 --> 00:06:02,097
the way Grandma Pearl's wood stove did.

175
00:06:02,277 --> 00:06:03,685
Check it every hour,

176
00:06:03,685 --> 00:06:05,798
and add a little broth if it's

177
00:06:05,798 --> 00:06:06,643
getting low.

178
00:06:06,993 --> 00:06:08,560
How do you know it's done?

179
00:06:08,740 --> 00:06:11,079
Take one piece out and poke the

180
00:06:11,079 --> 00:06:12,362
meat with a fork.

181
00:06:12,542 --> 00:06:15,175
If it slides off the bone with

182
00:06:15,175 --> 00:06:17,105
no pulling, it's done.

183
00:06:17,285 --> 00:06:18,750
If you have to tug,

184
00:06:18,750 --> 00:06:21,139
give it another thirty minutes.

185
00:06:21,319 --> 00:06:22,801
Pearl used to say,

186
00:06:22,801 --> 00:06:25,516
oxtail tells you when it's ready,

187
00:06:25,516 --> 00:06:26,010
honey.

188
00:06:26,190 --> 00:06:28,071
Your job is to listen.

189
00:06:28,421 --> 00:06:30,846
So far, dry the meat and flour

190
00:06:30,846 --> 00:06:33,190
it, brown it dark in batches,

191
00:06:33,190 --> 00:06:36,181
cook the vegetables in the drippings,

192
00:06:36,181 --> 00:06:38,526
and braise it low in the oven

193
00:06:38,526 --> 00:06:39,334
for hours.

194
00:06:39,514 --> 00:06:40,768
Now the grease.

195
00:06:40,948 --> 00:06:42,798
Oxtail has a lot of fat,

196
00:06:42,798 --> 00:06:44,802
and it melts into the pot.

197
00:06:44,982 --> 00:06:47,631
And mistake number four is serving it

198
00:06:47,631 --> 00:06:49,849
right away, with a half inch of

199
00:06:49,849 --> 00:06:51,925
shiny grease floating on top.

200
00:06:52,105 --> 00:06:54,552
It coats your mouth and hides all

201
00:06:54,552 --> 00:06:55,367
the flavor.

202
00:06:55,718 --> 00:06:57,822
Here's the trick I promised,

203
00:06:57,822 --> 00:06:59,851
the one that costs nothing.

204
00:07:00,031 --> 00:07:01,761
Make it the day before.

205
00:07:01,941 --> 00:07:03,155
Let the pot cool,

206
00:07:03,155 --> 00:07:05,370
then put the whole thing in the

207
00:07:05,370 --> 00:07:06,585
icebox overnight.

208
00:07:06,765 --> 00:07:07,835
In the morning,

209
00:07:07,835 --> 00:07:09,975
all the fat will have risen to

210
00:07:09,975 --> 00:07:12,400
the top and turned hard and white,

211
00:07:12,400 --> 00:07:14,183
like a lid of candle wax.

212
00:07:14,363 --> 00:07:17,060
Just lift it off with a spoon,

213
00:07:17,060 --> 00:07:18,318
in big pieces,

214
00:07:18,318 --> 00:07:19,936
and throw it away.

215
00:07:20,116 --> 00:07:22,011
Every bit of grease,

216
00:07:22,011 --> 00:07:22,485
gone.

217
00:07:22,835 --> 00:07:24,808
And here's the best part.

218
00:07:24,988 --> 00:07:27,693
It tastes better the next day anyway.

219
00:07:27,873 --> 00:07:29,473
The gravy thickens up,

220
00:07:29,473 --> 00:07:32,308
the meat soaks up the flavor overnight.

221
00:07:32,488 --> 00:07:35,606
Pearl always made hers on Saturday for

222
00:07:35,606 --> 00:07:36,180
Sunday.

223
00:07:36,360 --> 00:07:38,106
On the day you serve it,

224
00:07:38,106 --> 00:07:40,142
heat it slowly on the stove,

225
00:07:40,142 --> 00:07:42,614
covered, for about thirty minutes,

226
00:07:42,614 --> 00:07:45,159
until it's bubbling and hot all the

227
00:07:45,159 --> 00:07:46,031
way through.

228
00:07:46,382 --> 00:07:48,552
And if you can't wait a day,

229
00:07:48,552 --> 00:07:51,110
honey, tilt the pot and spoon off

230
00:07:51,110 --> 00:07:53,203
as much fat as you can from

231
00:07:53,203 --> 00:07:53,824
the top.

232
00:07:54,004 --> 00:07:56,216
Then lay a paper towel flat on

233
00:07:56,216 --> 00:07:58,060
the surface for a second,

234
00:07:58,060 --> 00:07:59,240
and lift it off.

235
00:07:59,420 --> 00:08:01,743
It soaks up the last of the

236
00:08:01,743 --> 00:08:02,345
grease.

237
00:08:02,525 --> 00:08:04,545
Do it two or three times.

238
00:08:04,725 --> 00:08:07,088
It's not as clean as the icebox

239
00:08:07,088 --> 00:08:09,451
trick, but it works in a pinch.

240
00:08:09,801 --> 00:08:11,211
Before you serve it,

241
00:08:11,211 --> 00:08:13,256
take out the meat and keep it

242
00:08:13,256 --> 00:08:13,609
warm.

243
00:08:13,789 --> 00:08:16,549
Fish out the bay leaves and thyme

244
00:08:16,549 --> 00:08:17,051
stems.

245
00:08:17,231 --> 00:08:18,824
If the gravy is thin,

246
00:08:18,824 --> 00:08:21,099
simmer it on the stove for ten

247
00:08:21,099 --> 00:08:23,753
minutes, until it coats the back of

248
00:08:23,753 --> 00:08:24,360
a spoon.

249
00:08:24,540 --> 00:08:28,034
Taste it, and add salt and pepper.

250
00:08:28,214 --> 00:08:30,864
Pearl added a splash of vinegar at

251
00:08:30,864 --> 00:08:32,812
the end, just a teaspoon.

252
00:08:32,992 --> 00:08:35,128
It wakes the whole gravy up.

253
00:08:35,478 --> 00:08:37,787
And here's how to make three pounds

254
00:08:37,787 --> 00:08:39,634
feed eight, like I promised.

255
00:08:39,814 --> 00:08:42,161
Pull all the meat off the bones,

256
00:08:42,161 --> 00:08:44,435
and stir it back into the gravy

257
00:08:44,435 --> 00:08:46,416
with a can of butter beans,

258
00:08:46,416 --> 00:08:47,883
or some egg noodles.

259
00:08:48,063 --> 00:08:51,337
Serve it over mashed potatoes or rice.

260
00:08:51,517 --> 00:08:53,886
Two pieces of oxtail on a plate

261
00:08:53,886 --> 00:08:55,186
feeds one person.

262
00:08:55,366 --> 00:08:58,075
The same meat pulled off the bones,

263
00:08:58,075 --> 00:08:59,932
with beans and potatoes,

264
00:08:59,932 --> 00:09:00,706
feeds two.

265
00:09:01,057 --> 00:09:03,793
Oxtail stew keeps four days in the

266
00:09:03,793 --> 00:09:07,012
icebox, and it freezes for three months.

267
00:09:07,192 --> 00:09:08,970
Freeze it in the gravy,

268
00:09:08,970 --> 00:09:11,674
in containers with the meat off the

269
00:09:11,674 --> 00:09:14,147
bones, so it takes up less room.

270
00:09:14,327 --> 00:09:16,846
And save any leftover gravy.

271
00:09:17,026 --> 00:09:18,483
A spoon of it in a pot

272
00:09:18,483 --> 00:09:20,469
of soup, or over a hot biscuit

273
00:09:20,469 --> 00:09:21,661
on a cold morning,

274
00:09:21,661 --> 00:09:23,514
is a little bit of Sunday in

275
00:09:23,514 --> 00:09:25,037
the middle of the week.

276
00:09:25,387 --> 00:09:26,826
So one more time.

277
00:09:27,006 --> 00:09:28,072
Dry the meat,

278
00:09:28,072 --> 00:09:30,530
flour it, and brown it dark in

279
00:09:30,530 --> 00:09:31,186
batches.

280
00:09:31,366 --> 00:09:34,074
Cook the vegetables and tomato paste in

281
00:09:34,074 --> 00:09:35,046
the drippings.

282
00:09:35,226 --> 00:09:36,625
Wine and broth,

283
00:09:36,625 --> 00:09:38,303
three quarters up.

284
00:09:38,483 --> 00:09:40,634
Three and a half hours in a

285
00:09:40,634 --> 00:09:41,350
low oven.

286
00:09:41,530 --> 00:09:43,356
Make it the day before,

287
00:09:43,356 --> 00:09:45,420
and lift the fat off cold.

288
00:09:45,600 --> 00:09:48,061
A splash of vinegar in the gravy.

289
00:09:48,241 --> 00:09:50,510
That's Grandma Pearl's oxtail,

290
00:09:50,510 --> 00:09:53,384
and it's never greasy and never tough.

291
00:09:53,735 --> 00:09:55,757
Tell me in the comments,

292
00:09:55,757 --> 00:09:56,683
sweetheart.

293
00:09:56,863 --> 00:09:59,397
Did your family eat oxtail when you

294
00:09:59,397 --> 00:10:00,555
were growing up?

295
00:10:00,735 --> 00:10:02,848
How did your grandmother make it?

296
00:10:03,028 --> 00:10:06,205
The whole playlist of Grandma's recipes is

297
00:10:06,205 --> 00:10:08,247
right there on your screen,

298
00:10:08,247 --> 00:10:10,365
and I'll see you in the next

299
00:10:10,365 --> 00:10:10,819
video.

300
00:10:10,999 --> 00:10:12,752
Good night, honey.

1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:03,479
Sweetheart, every Christmas cookie tray in America

2
00:00:03,479 --> 00:00:05,845
has a little round white cookie on

3
00:00:05,845 --> 00:00:07,932
it, covered in powdered sugar,

4
00:00:07,932 --> 00:00:10,507
that melts the second it touches your

5
00:00:10,507 --> 00:00:10,994
tongue.

6
00:00:11,174 --> 00:00:13,902
Some families call them snowballs.

7
00:00:14,082 --> 00:00:16,683
Some call them Russian tea cakes,

8
00:00:16,683 --> 00:00:18,810
or Mexican wedding cookies,

9
00:00:18,810 --> 00:00:19,992
or butterballs.

10
00:00:20,172 --> 00:00:21,146
In our house,

11
00:00:21,146 --> 00:00:24,441
my brother Danny called them sneeze cookies,

12
00:00:24,441 --> 00:00:27,138
because he always inhaled the sugar.

13
00:00:27,487 --> 00:00:29,956
But people tell me theirs go flat

14
00:00:29,956 --> 00:00:30,853
in the oven,

15
00:00:30,853 --> 00:00:33,247
or the sugar melts into a sticky

16
00:00:33,247 --> 00:00:36,090
glaze, or the whole cookie crumbles to

17
00:00:36,090 --> 00:00:37,286
dust in the tin.

18
00:00:37,466 --> 00:00:40,039
So tonight I'm giving you my snowball

19
00:00:40,039 --> 00:00:41,430
cookies, every step,

20
00:00:41,430 --> 00:00:44,003
and the four mistakes that ruin them.

21
00:00:44,183 --> 00:00:45,376
And stay with me,

22
00:00:45,376 --> 00:00:47,623
because the last trick is how to

23
00:00:47,623 --> 00:00:49,730
keep that snowy coat of sugar,

24
00:00:49,730 --> 00:00:51,555
and it's all about timing.

25
00:00:51,904 --> 00:00:54,521
This little cookie is very old,

26
00:00:54,521 --> 00:00:55,028
honey.

27
00:00:55,208 --> 00:00:58,040
Nobody knows exactly where it started.

28
00:00:58,220 --> 00:01:00,681
Something like it was baked in the

29
00:01:00,681 --> 00:01:03,720
Middle East with ground almonds and butter

30
00:01:03,720 --> 00:01:05,312
hundreds of years ago,

31
00:01:05,312 --> 00:01:07,121
and it traveled to Spain,

32
00:01:07,121 --> 00:01:09,510
to Mexico, to Russia and all over

33
00:01:09,510 --> 00:01:10,016
Europe.

34
00:01:10,196 --> 00:01:12,573
Every country that made it gave it

35
00:01:12,573 --> 00:01:13,482
its own name.

36
00:01:13,662 --> 00:01:16,770
And every grandmother thinks hers is the

37
00:01:16,770 --> 00:01:17,470
original.

38
00:01:17,819 --> 00:01:19,758
Mine came from Mrs.

39
00:01:19,938 --> 00:01:22,807
Kowalski, two doors down on Elm Street,

40
00:01:22,807 --> 00:01:24,647
who called them kolaczki,

41
00:01:24,647 --> 00:01:28,031
though I think she called everything kolaczki.

42
00:01:28,211 --> 00:01:29,964
She made them with walnuts.

43
00:01:30,144 --> 00:01:32,409
The first time I tried to make

44
00:01:32,409 --> 00:01:34,600
them, in nineteen sixty-five,

45
00:01:34,600 --> 00:01:37,168
I used margarine to save a nickel.

46
00:01:37,348 --> 00:01:39,981
They spread out flat like pancakes,

47
00:01:39,981 --> 00:01:42,990
and my husband called them snow puddles.

48
00:01:43,340 --> 00:01:45,114
That was my first lesson,

49
00:01:45,114 --> 00:01:47,172
and I'll tell you about it in

50
00:01:47,172 --> 00:01:47,810
a minute.

51
00:01:47,990 --> 00:01:50,045
But here's the good news.

52
00:01:50,225 --> 00:01:53,088
This is one of the easiest Christmas

53
00:01:53,088 --> 00:01:54,440
cookies there is.

54
00:01:54,620 --> 00:01:56,531
Only six ingredients,

55
00:01:56,531 --> 00:01:58,715
no eggs, no rolling pin,

56
00:01:58,715 --> 00:02:00,353
no cookie cutters,

57
00:02:00,353 --> 00:02:03,629
and the children can roll the balls.

58
00:02:03,809 --> 00:02:06,675
It costs about five dollars for four

59
00:02:06,675 --> 00:02:07,153
dozen.

60
00:02:07,502 --> 00:02:08,637
In our house,

61
00:02:08,637 --> 00:02:11,953
snowball day was the first Saturday of

62
00:02:11,953 --> 00:02:12,739
December.

63
00:02:12,919 --> 00:02:14,586
My mother made the dough,

64
00:02:14,586 --> 00:02:16,653
Danny and I rolled the balls at

65
00:02:16,653 --> 00:02:17,853
the kitchen table,

66
00:02:17,853 --> 00:02:19,854
and my father was in charge of

67
00:02:19,854 --> 00:02:20,854
the sugar bowl,

68
00:02:20,854 --> 00:02:22,922
because he said it was the most

69
00:02:22,922 --> 00:02:23,855
important job.

70
00:02:24,035 --> 00:02:25,832
By the end of the morning,

71
00:02:25,832 --> 00:02:28,457
there was powdered sugar on the floor,

72
00:02:28,457 --> 00:02:29,217
on the dog,

73
00:02:29,217 --> 00:02:31,152
and in my father's eyebrows.

74
00:02:31,502 --> 00:02:33,149
Here's what you need,

75
00:02:33,149 --> 00:02:35,345
honey, for about four dozen.

76
00:02:35,525 --> 00:02:37,149
One cup of butter,

77
00:02:37,149 --> 00:02:39,043
two sticks, softened.

78
00:02:39,223 --> 00:02:41,322
Half a cup of powdered sugar,

79
00:02:41,322 --> 00:02:43,276
plus about a cup and a half

80
00:02:43,276 --> 00:02:44,506
more for rolling.

81
00:02:44,686 --> 00:02:46,729
One teaspoon of vanilla.

82
00:02:46,909 --> 00:02:49,301
Two and a quarter cups of flour.

83
00:02:49,481 --> 00:02:51,663
A quarter teaspoon of salt.

84
00:02:51,843 --> 00:02:54,377
And three quarters of a cup of

85
00:02:54,377 --> 00:02:55,896
pecans or walnuts,

86
00:02:55,896 --> 00:02:57,416
chopped very fine.

87
00:02:57,766 --> 00:03:00,473
And here's the lesson from my snow

88
00:03:00,473 --> 00:03:01,110
puddles.

89
00:03:01,290 --> 00:03:02,974
Mistake number one.

90
00:03:03,154 --> 00:03:05,267
Margarine, or a spread.

91
00:03:05,447 --> 00:03:07,215
Use real butter,

92
00:03:07,215 --> 00:03:08,430
every time.

93
00:03:08,610 --> 00:03:11,398
Margarine and spreads have water in them,

94
00:03:11,398 --> 00:03:13,710
and the cookies melt and spread in

95
00:03:13,710 --> 00:03:14,322
the oven.

96
00:03:14,502 --> 00:03:16,460
With only six ingredients,

97
00:03:16,460 --> 00:03:18,945
butter is the whole flavor of the

98
00:03:18,945 --> 00:03:19,472
cookie.

99
00:03:19,652 --> 00:03:20,673
Mrs.

100
00:03:20,853 --> 00:03:23,964
Kowalski laughed at my snow puddles for

101
00:03:23,964 --> 00:03:24,522
a week.

102
00:03:24,871 --> 00:03:27,066
And toast the nuts first.

103
00:03:27,246 --> 00:03:29,650
Spread them on a baking sheet and

104
00:03:29,650 --> 00:03:31,982
bake them at three fifty for six

105
00:03:31,982 --> 00:03:33,220
or seven minutes,

106
00:03:33,220 --> 00:03:35,698
until they smell warm and buttery.

107
00:03:35,878 --> 00:03:38,132
Let them cool all the way,

108
00:03:38,132 --> 00:03:40,299
then chop them very fine,

109
00:03:40,299 --> 00:03:42,379
almost like coarse sand.

110
00:03:42,559 --> 00:03:45,236
Big chunks of nut make the cookies

111
00:03:45,236 --> 00:03:46,890
crack and fall apart.

112
00:03:47,070 --> 00:03:49,694
Fine nuts hold together and melt in

113
00:03:49,694 --> 00:03:50,518
your mouth.

114
00:03:50,868 --> 00:03:51,879
Step one.

115
00:03:52,059 --> 00:03:54,211
Beat the soft butter with half a

116
00:03:54,211 --> 00:03:56,699
cup of powdered sugar and the vanilla

117
00:03:56,699 --> 00:03:58,650
until it's smooth and creamy,

118
00:03:58,650 --> 00:03:59,860
about two minutes.

119
00:04:00,040 --> 00:04:01,482
Then add the flour,

120
00:04:01,482 --> 00:04:03,833
the salt, and the chopped nuts,

121
00:04:03,833 --> 00:04:05,198
and mix it on low,

122
00:04:05,198 --> 00:04:06,943
or with a wooden spoon,

123
00:04:06,943 --> 00:04:09,143
just until it comes together.

124
00:04:09,323 --> 00:04:11,691
It'll look crumbly at first.

125
00:04:11,871 --> 00:04:14,736
Keep going, and it'll turn into a

126
00:04:14,736 --> 00:04:15,691
soft dough.

127
00:04:16,040 --> 00:04:17,811
If this is helping you,

128
00:04:17,811 --> 00:04:20,429
honey, tap the like button for me.

129
00:04:20,609 --> 00:04:23,012
It helps Grandma more than you know.

130
00:04:23,192 --> 00:04:25,398
Now, mistake number two.

131
00:04:25,578 --> 00:04:26,948
Skipping the chill.

132
00:04:27,128 --> 00:04:29,322
This dough is mostly butter.

133
00:04:29,502 --> 00:04:31,673
If it's warm when it goes in

134
00:04:31,673 --> 00:04:34,541
the oven, the balls slump into little

135
00:04:34,541 --> 00:04:35,006
domes.

136
00:04:35,186 --> 00:04:37,209
Cover the bowl and put it in

137
00:04:37,209 --> 00:04:39,521
the icebox for at least an hour,

138
00:04:39,521 --> 00:04:40,677
until it's firm.

139
00:04:41,027 --> 00:04:42,165
Step two.

140
00:04:42,345 --> 00:04:45,213
Heat the oven to three hundred seventy-five.

141
00:04:45,393 --> 00:04:48,125
Roll the cold dough into balls about

142
00:04:48,125 --> 00:04:49,339
one inch across,

143
00:04:49,339 --> 00:04:51,161
about a tablespoon each,

144
00:04:51,161 --> 00:04:52,603
between your palms.

145
00:04:52,783 --> 00:04:54,181
Roll them quickly,

146
00:04:54,181 --> 00:04:56,744
so your warm hands don't melt the

147
00:04:56,744 --> 00:04:57,287
butter.

148
00:04:57,467 --> 00:04:59,882
Set them on a baking sheet lined

149
00:04:59,882 --> 00:05:02,599
with parchment, about an inch apart.

150
00:05:02,779 --> 00:05:04,656
They don't spread much if you did

151
00:05:04,656 --> 00:05:05,565
the chill right.

152
00:05:05,915 --> 00:05:08,689
And make them all the same size,

153
00:05:08,689 --> 00:05:09,642
sweetheart.

154
00:05:09,822 --> 00:05:12,017
A little cookie scoop helps.

155
00:05:12,197 --> 00:05:14,137
If some are big and some are

156
00:05:14,137 --> 00:05:16,492
small, the small ones burn and the

157
00:05:16,492 --> 00:05:18,710
big ones stay raw in the middle.

158
00:05:18,890 --> 00:05:19,935
Mrs.

159
00:05:20,115 --> 00:05:23,451
Kowalski weighed hers on her kitchen scale,

160
00:05:23,451 --> 00:05:24,770
every single one.

161
00:05:24,950 --> 00:05:27,666
She was a very serious woman about

162
00:05:27,666 --> 00:05:28,306
cookies.

163
00:05:28,655 --> 00:05:30,570
And if your kitchen is warm,

164
00:05:30,570 --> 00:05:33,443
sweetheart, put the baking sheet of rolled

165
00:05:33,443 --> 00:05:35,631
balls back in the icebox for ten

166
00:05:35,631 --> 00:05:38,025
minutes before they go in the oven.

167
00:05:38,205 --> 00:05:40,580
Especially if the oven has been on

168
00:05:40,580 --> 00:05:41,978
and the room is hot.

169
00:05:42,158 --> 00:05:44,237
Cold dough in a hot oven is

170
00:05:44,237 --> 00:05:45,931
what keeps them round.

171
00:05:46,111 --> 00:05:47,902
Warm dough in a hot oven is

172
00:05:47,902 --> 00:05:49,559
how you get snow puddles.

173
00:05:49,909 --> 00:05:51,117
Step three.

174
00:05:51,297 --> 00:05:53,735
Bake for ten to twelve minutes.

175
00:05:53,915 --> 00:05:56,632
And here's mistake number three.

176
00:05:56,812 --> 00:05:59,041
Baking them until they're brown.

177
00:05:59,221 --> 00:06:02,438
Snowball cookies should stay pale on top,

178
00:06:02,438 --> 00:06:05,263
with just the bottoms a light golden

179
00:06:05,263 --> 00:06:05,734
color.

180
00:06:05,914 --> 00:06:07,850
Lift one up and peek at the

181
00:06:07,850 --> 00:06:08,352
bottom.

182
00:06:08,532 --> 00:06:11,516
Light gold underneath means they're done.

183
00:06:11,696 --> 00:06:13,184
If the tops brown,

184
00:06:13,184 --> 00:06:15,167
they'll be dry and hard.

185
00:06:15,517 --> 00:06:17,252
So far, real butter,

186
00:06:17,252 --> 00:06:19,506
toasted nuts chopped fine,

187
00:06:19,506 --> 00:06:20,893
chill the dough,

188
00:06:20,893 --> 00:06:24,448
same-size balls, and bake them just until

189
00:06:24,448 --> 00:06:26,442
the bottoms are golden.

190
00:06:26,622 --> 00:06:27,891
Now the sugar coat,

191
00:06:27,891 --> 00:06:29,827
and the trick I promised you.

192
00:06:30,007 --> 00:06:32,573
Mistake number four is rolling them in

193
00:06:32,573 --> 00:06:34,802
powdered sugar while they're hot.

194
00:06:34,982 --> 00:06:37,340
The sugar melts into a sticky,

195
00:06:37,340 --> 00:06:40,799
see-through glaze, and they look wet instead

196
00:06:40,799 --> 00:06:41,507
of snowy.

197
00:06:41,856 --> 00:06:43,273
Here's the timing.

198
00:06:43,453 --> 00:06:45,657
Let the cookies cool on the pan

199
00:06:45,657 --> 00:06:47,293
for about five minutes,

200
00:06:47,293 --> 00:06:49,640
until you can pick one up without

201
00:06:49,640 --> 00:06:51,986
it breaking, but it's still warm.

202
00:06:52,166 --> 00:06:54,460
Then roll each one gently in a

203
00:06:54,460 --> 00:06:56,218
bowl of powdered sugar.

204
00:06:56,398 --> 00:06:58,964
This first coat melts just a little

205
00:06:58,964 --> 00:07:01,163
and sticks, like a primer on a

206
00:07:01,163 --> 00:07:01,530
wall.

207
00:07:01,710 --> 00:07:03,476
Set them on a rack and let

208
00:07:03,476 --> 00:07:04,902
them cool completely.

209
00:07:05,252 --> 00:07:07,814
Then, when they're completely cool,

210
00:07:07,814 --> 00:07:10,448
roll them in powdered sugar a second

211
00:07:10,448 --> 00:07:10,814
time.

212
00:07:10,994 --> 00:07:13,687
This coat stays white and fluffy,

213
00:07:13,687 --> 00:07:16,299
like fresh snow on a fence post.

214
00:07:16,479 --> 00:07:19,161
Two coats, warm and then cold.

215
00:07:19,341 --> 00:07:21,496
That's the whole secret,

216
00:07:21,496 --> 00:07:22,035
honey.

217
00:07:22,215 --> 00:07:24,442
The first one is the glue,

218
00:07:24,442 --> 00:07:26,754
the second one is the snow.

219
00:07:26,934 --> 00:07:27,875
Mrs.

220
00:07:28,055 --> 00:07:30,848
Kowalski did it this way for sixty

221
00:07:30,848 --> 00:07:31,340
years.

222
00:07:31,690 --> 00:07:33,737
And for a coat that lasts for

223
00:07:33,737 --> 00:07:34,866
days in the tin,

224
00:07:34,866 --> 00:07:37,760
mix a tablespoon of cornstarch into every

225
00:07:37,760 --> 00:07:40,301
cup of powdered sugar for the second

226
00:07:40,301 --> 00:07:40,653
coat.

227
00:07:40,833 --> 00:07:44,248
Or use the special non-melting snow sugar

228
00:07:44,248 --> 00:07:45,663
that bakers sell.

229
00:07:45,843 --> 00:07:48,974
Regular powdered sugar slowly soaks into the

230
00:07:48,974 --> 00:07:50,824
butter after a day or two.

231
00:07:51,004 --> 00:07:53,639
A light dusting on top right before

232
00:07:53,639 --> 00:07:55,822
serving brings back the snow.

233
00:07:56,171 --> 00:07:58,788
And sift your powdered sugar first,

234
00:07:58,788 --> 00:07:59,237
honey.

235
00:07:59,417 --> 00:08:01,967
Powdered sugar sits in the box and

236
00:08:01,967 --> 00:08:04,142
gets little hard lumps in it.

237
00:08:04,322 --> 00:08:06,832
If you roll your cookies in lumpy

238
00:08:06,832 --> 00:08:08,963
sugar, they come out spotty,

239
00:08:08,963 --> 00:08:10,637
like a dog with mange,

240
00:08:10,637 --> 00:08:11,474
Danny said.

241
00:08:11,654 --> 00:08:14,090
Sift it into a wide shallow bowl,

242
00:08:14,090 --> 00:08:16,527
and roll three or four cookies at

243
00:08:16,527 --> 00:08:19,259
a time, turning them gently with your

244
00:08:19,259 --> 00:08:19,850
fingers.

245
00:08:20,200 --> 00:08:22,630
You can change these a hundred ways

246
00:08:22,630 --> 00:08:23,602
for Christmas.

247
00:08:23,782 --> 00:08:27,077
Use almonds and a little almond extract,

248
00:08:27,077 --> 00:08:28,972
the way the Spanish do.

249
00:08:29,152 --> 00:08:31,856
Or hazelnuts and a spoon of cocoa

250
00:08:31,856 --> 00:08:32,921
in the dough,

251
00:08:32,921 --> 00:08:34,887
for chocolate snowballs.

252
00:08:35,067 --> 00:08:37,482
Or add the zest of an orange.

253
00:08:37,662 --> 00:08:40,261
Or press a chocolate kiss inside each

254
00:08:40,261 --> 00:08:41,946
ball before you bake it.

255
00:08:42,126 --> 00:08:45,453
My grandson calls those snowballs with a

256
00:08:45,453 --> 00:08:46,201
surprise.

257
00:08:46,551 --> 00:08:48,888
And if somebody can't have nuts,

258
00:08:48,888 --> 00:08:51,151
honey, leave them out and use a

259
00:08:51,151 --> 00:08:52,831
quarter cup more flour,

260
00:08:52,831 --> 00:08:55,313
or a cup of finely chopped toasted

261
00:08:55,313 --> 00:08:55,898
coconut.

262
00:08:56,078 --> 00:08:59,087
And add mini chocolate chips for the

263
00:08:59,087 --> 00:08:59,839
children.

264
00:09:00,019 --> 00:09:01,996
A friend at church with a nut

265
00:09:01,996 --> 00:09:04,518
allergy told me the coconut ones were

266
00:09:04,518 --> 00:09:07,109
the first snowball cookie she'd had in

267
00:09:07,109 --> 00:09:07,995
thirty years.

268
00:09:08,175 --> 00:09:10,149
She took the whole plate home.

269
00:09:10,498 --> 00:09:12,647
They keep two weeks in a tin,

270
00:09:12,647 --> 00:09:15,166
with wax paper between the layers.

271
00:09:15,346 --> 00:09:17,935
And they're perfect for freezing.

272
00:09:18,115 --> 00:09:19,829
Freeze the dough balls,

273
00:09:19,829 --> 00:09:21,245
unbaked, on a tray,

274
00:09:21,245 --> 00:09:23,183
then put them in a bag for

275
00:09:23,183 --> 00:09:24,152
three months.

276
00:09:24,332 --> 00:09:26,621
Bake them straight from frozen,

277
00:09:26,621 --> 00:09:28,024
adding two minutes.

278
00:09:28,204 --> 00:09:30,958
Or freeze the baked cookies without the

279
00:09:30,958 --> 00:09:33,430
second coat, and roll them in sugar

280
00:09:33,430 --> 00:09:35,054
the day you serve them.

281
00:09:35,403 --> 00:09:37,987
And put them in little paper candy

282
00:09:37,987 --> 00:09:39,810
cups, in a box or a tin,

283
00:09:39,810 --> 00:09:40,570
for gifts.

284
00:09:40,750 --> 00:09:43,083
They look like a box of snow.

285
00:09:43,263 --> 00:09:45,197
I give a tin to the mailman

286
00:09:45,197 --> 00:09:46,270
every year, Mr.

287
00:09:46,450 --> 00:09:48,260
Hoover's grandson now,

288
00:09:48,260 --> 00:09:51,056
who carries our mail just like his

289
00:09:51,056 --> 00:09:52,372
grandfather did.

290
00:09:52,552 --> 00:09:54,882
He says his wife hides them from

291
00:09:54,882 --> 00:09:57,794
the children, and the children hide them

292
00:09:57,794 --> 00:09:58,449
from her.

293
00:09:58,799 --> 00:10:00,286
So one more time.

294
00:10:00,466 --> 00:10:02,973
Real butter, never margarine.

295
00:10:03,153 --> 00:10:05,858
Toasted nuts, chopped fine.

296
00:10:06,038 --> 00:10:07,594
Chill the dough an hour.

297
00:10:07,774 --> 00:10:09,957
Roll same-size balls.

298
00:10:10,137 --> 00:10:12,807
Bake until just the bottoms are golden.

299
00:10:12,987 --> 00:10:15,649
Roll them in powdered sugar while they're

300
00:10:15,649 --> 00:10:17,921
warm, then again when they're cool.

301
00:10:18,101 --> 00:10:20,365
The glue, and then the snow.

302
00:10:20,545 --> 00:10:23,372
That's how you get snowball cookies that

303
00:10:23,372 --> 00:10:24,644
stay round, snowy,

304
00:10:24,644 --> 00:10:26,269
and melt in your mouth.

305
00:10:26,618 --> 00:10:28,457
Tell me in the comments,

306
00:10:28,457 --> 00:10:29,300
sweetheart.

307
00:10:29,480 --> 00:10:32,093
What did your family call these cookies?

308
00:10:32,273 --> 00:10:34,045
Snowballs, tea cakes,

309
00:10:34,045 --> 00:10:36,998
wedding cookies, or something else?

310
00:10:37,178 --> 00:10:40,255
The whole playlist of Grandma's recipes is

311
00:10:40,255 --> 00:10:42,233
right there on your screen,

312
00:10:42,233 --> 00:10:44,285
and I'll see you in the next

313
00:10:44,285 --> 00:10:44,724
video.

314
00:10:44,904 --> 00:10:46,611
Good night, honey.

315
00:10:46,791 --> 00:10:48,207
Merry Christmas.

1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:03,212
Sweetheart, on Christmas Day in our house,

2
00:00:03,212 --> 00:00:05,353
the ham came out of the oven

3
00:00:05,353 --> 00:00:07,418
shining like stained glass.

4
00:00:07,598 --> 00:00:08,848
Dark amber glaze,

5
00:00:08,848 --> 00:00:11,420
a diamond pattern cut into the top,

6
00:00:11,420 --> 00:00:13,477
and a clove in the middle of

7
00:00:13,477 --> 00:00:14,506
every diamond.

8
00:00:14,686 --> 00:00:16,829
My father carried it to the table

9
00:00:16,829 --> 00:00:19,426
on my grandmother's blue platter like he

10
00:00:19,426 --> 00:00:21,374
was carrying the crown jewels.

11
00:00:21,554 --> 00:00:23,585
And the whole family clapped.

12
00:00:23,765 --> 00:00:24,961
Every year.

13
00:00:25,312 --> 00:00:28,161
But today, people tell me their Christmas

14
00:00:28,161 --> 00:00:30,245
ham comes out dry and stringy,

15
00:00:30,245 --> 00:00:32,330
or so salty you need a pitcher

16
00:00:32,330 --> 00:00:34,762
of water, or the glaze burns black.

17
00:00:34,942 --> 00:00:37,503
So tonight I'm giving you my brown

18
00:00:37,503 --> 00:00:38,783
sugar glazed ham,

19
00:00:38,783 --> 00:00:41,644
every step, and the five mistakes that

20
00:00:41,644 --> 00:00:43,301
make it dry and salty.

21
00:00:43,481 --> 00:00:44,724
And stay with me,

22
00:00:44,724 --> 00:00:47,137
because the last trick is when to

23
00:00:47,137 --> 00:00:48,380
put on the glaze,

24
00:00:48,380 --> 00:00:51,086
and it's the reason most glazes burn.

25
00:00:51,436 --> 00:00:54,354
Ham at Christmas is an old tradition,

26
00:00:54,354 --> 00:00:56,405
honey, older than America.

27
00:00:56,585 --> 00:00:57,768
In the old days,

28
00:00:57,768 --> 00:01:00,505
farm families butchered a hog in late

29
00:01:00,505 --> 00:01:03,167
fall, and salted and smoked the hams

30
00:01:03,167 --> 00:01:05,164
to keep through the winter.

31
00:01:05,344 --> 00:01:08,084
The best ham was saved for Christmas.

32
00:01:08,264 --> 00:01:09,997
On Grandma Pearl's farm,

33
00:01:09,997 --> 00:01:12,596
the hams hung in the smokehouse from

34
00:01:12,596 --> 00:01:14,834
November, and on Christmas Eve,

35
00:01:14,834 --> 00:01:17,650
my grandfather would take one down like

36
00:01:17,650 --> 00:01:19,816
he was picking the best apple.

37
00:01:20,167 --> 00:01:22,054
By the time I was cooking,

38
00:01:22,054 --> 00:01:23,143
in the sixties,

39
00:01:23,143 --> 00:01:26,119
everybody bought their ham at the grocery

40
00:01:26,119 --> 00:01:28,514
store, already cooked and smoked.

41
00:01:28,694 --> 00:01:31,376
That's what most hams are today.

42
00:01:31,556 --> 00:01:34,356
And that changes everything about how you

43
00:01:34,356 --> 00:01:37,224
cook it, because you're not really cooking

44
00:01:37,224 --> 00:01:37,907
it, honey.

45
00:01:38,087 --> 00:01:39,640
You're only warming it,

46
00:01:39,640 --> 00:01:40,652
and glazing it.

47
00:01:40,832 --> 00:01:42,869
In a minute I'll tell you why

48
00:01:42,869 --> 00:01:45,186
that's the secret to a juicy ham.

49
00:01:45,537 --> 00:01:48,141
And my mother's Christmas ham was the

50
00:01:48,141 --> 00:01:50,746
one dinner she never let anybody help

51
00:01:50,746 --> 00:01:51,098
with.

52
00:01:51,278 --> 00:01:53,268
She'd shoo us all out of the

53
00:01:53,268 --> 00:01:55,328
kitchen on Christmas morning,

54
00:01:55,328 --> 00:01:57,744
while we played with our presents.

55
00:01:57,924 --> 00:02:00,067
Danny and I would sneak to the

56
00:02:00,067 --> 00:02:02,709
kitchen door and smell it through the

57
00:02:02,709 --> 00:02:03,137
crack.

58
00:02:03,317 --> 00:02:05,307
Brown sugar, cloves,

59
00:02:05,307 --> 00:02:06,301
and smoke.

60
00:02:06,481 --> 00:02:07,445
To this day,

61
00:02:07,445 --> 00:02:10,418
that smell means Christmas to me more

62
00:02:10,418 --> 00:02:12,588
than any tree or any carol.

63
00:02:12,938 --> 00:02:15,422
First, choosing the ham.

64
00:02:15,602 --> 00:02:17,581
Look for a fully cooked,

65
00:02:17,581 --> 00:02:20,384
bone-in ham, either a shank end or

66
00:02:20,384 --> 00:02:21,291
a butt end,

67
00:02:21,291 --> 00:02:22,940
eight to ten pounds.

68
00:02:23,120 --> 00:02:26,278
That feeds twelve people with leftovers.

69
00:02:26,458 --> 00:02:29,138
Bone-in is juicier and has more flavor

70
00:02:29,138 --> 00:02:31,607
than boneless, and you get the bone

71
00:02:31,607 --> 00:02:32,947
for soup afterward.

72
00:02:33,127 --> 00:02:34,768
My mother always said,

73
00:02:34,768 --> 00:02:36,855
the bone is the best part of

74
00:02:36,855 --> 00:02:38,943
the ham, and the soup is the

75
00:02:38,943 --> 00:02:40,732
best part of New Year's.

76
00:02:41,082 --> 00:02:43,531
And here's mistake number one.

77
00:02:43,711 --> 00:02:45,964
Buying a ham with water added.

78
00:02:46,144 --> 00:02:47,423
Read the label,

79
00:02:47,423 --> 00:02:48,361
sweetheart.

80
00:02:48,541 --> 00:02:51,360
If it says ham with natural juices,

81
00:02:51,360 --> 00:02:52,326
that's good.

82
00:02:52,506 --> 00:02:53,808
If it says ham,

83
00:02:53,808 --> 00:02:57,107
water added, or ham and water product,

84
00:02:57,107 --> 00:03:00,319
it's been pumped full of salty water.

85
00:03:00,499 --> 00:03:02,357
It shrinks in the oven,

86
00:03:02,357 --> 00:03:03,729
tastes like salt,

87
00:03:03,729 --> 00:03:05,828
and the texture is spongy.

88
00:03:06,008 --> 00:03:08,473
Pay the extra dollar for a better

89
00:03:08,473 --> 00:03:08,772
ham.

90
00:03:09,122 --> 00:03:11,414
And spiral-cut hams are easy,

91
00:03:11,414 --> 00:03:13,707
but they dry out the fastest,

92
00:03:13,707 --> 00:03:16,712
because all those slices let the juice

93
00:03:16,712 --> 00:03:17,028
out.

94
00:03:17,208 --> 00:03:18,585
If you buy one,

95
00:03:18,585 --> 00:03:20,238
cook it face down,

96
00:03:20,238 --> 00:03:22,258
wrapped tight in foil,

97
00:03:22,258 --> 00:03:24,186
and watch it closely.

98
00:03:24,366 --> 00:03:26,252
I like a whole ham that I

99
00:03:26,252 --> 00:03:27,233
score myself.

100
00:03:27,413 --> 00:03:28,696
It stays juicier,

101
00:03:28,696 --> 00:03:31,337
and it looks prettier on the table.

102
00:03:31,517 --> 00:03:33,561
That's how my father liked it.

103
00:03:33,911 --> 00:03:35,048
Step one.

104
00:03:35,228 --> 00:03:37,398
Take the ham out of the icebox

105
00:03:37,398 --> 00:03:39,641
two hours before it goes in the

106
00:03:39,641 --> 00:03:41,811
oven, so it warms up a little.

107
00:03:41,991 --> 00:03:45,056
Mistake number two is putting an ice-cold

108
00:03:45,056 --> 00:03:46,252
ham in the oven.

109
00:03:46,432 --> 00:03:48,987
The outside dries out while you wait

110
00:03:48,987 --> 00:03:50,832
for the middle to warm up.

111
00:03:51,012 --> 00:03:53,822
Heat the oven to three hundred twenty-five.

112
00:03:54,002 --> 00:03:55,012
Not hotter.

113
00:03:55,362 --> 00:03:57,196
Step two, scoring.

114
00:03:57,376 --> 00:03:58,812
With a sharp knife,

115
00:03:58,812 --> 00:04:01,382
cut a diamond pattern into the fat

year.

00:06:36,415 --> 00:06:39,206

00:06:54,042 --> 00:06:54,974

00:07:06,834 --> 00:07:09,140

00:07:55,380 --> 00:07:56,840

248
00:08:28,673 --> 00:08:30,377

250

The houses that feel the coziest at

Seventy-five years later,

00:01:38,174 --> 00:01:40,519

If you like colored lights,

00:03:15,951 --> 00:03:19,348
the old-fashioned soft colors look warmer than

95
00:03:19,348 --> 00:03:20,899
the bright neon ones.

96
00:03:21,079 --> 00:03:23,833
My grandson bought blue lights one year,

97
00:03:23,833 --> 00:03:26,106
and his wife said the living room

98
00:03:26,106 --> 00:03:28,033
looked like a swimming pool.

99
00:03:28,383 --> 00:03:30,195
Mistake number three.

100
00:03:30,375 --> 00:03:32,761
All the lights on the tree,

101
00:03:32,761 --> 00:03:34,264
and nowhere else.

102
00:03:34,444 --> 00:03:36,358
The tree glows in the corner,

103
00:03:36,358 --> 00:03:38,273
and the rest of the room sits

104
00:03:38,273 --> 00:03:39,065
in the dark.

105
00:03:39,245 --> 00:03:41,033
Spread a little light around.

106
00:03:41,213 --> 00:03:43,390
A string of small lights tucked in

107
00:03:43,390 --> 00:03:45,056
the garland on the mantel.

108
00:03:45,236 --> 00:03:47,082
A few in a glass jar on

109
00:03:47,082 --> 00:03:48,045
a bookshelf.

110
00:03:48,225 --> 00:03:50,129
A string around a mirror.

111
00:03:50,309 --> 00:03:52,224
A little lit tree in the kitchen

112
00:03:52,224 --> 00:03:52,643
window.

113
00:03:52,992 --> 00:03:54,646
If this is helping you,

114
00:03:54,646 --> 00:03:57,091
honey, tap the like button for me.

115
00:03:57,271 --> 00:04:00,034
It helps Grandma more than you know.

116
00:04:00,214 --> 00:04:02,716
And a tip for those little lights

117
00:04:02,716 --> 00:04:04,080
in jars and bowls.

118
00:04:04,260 --> 00:04:06,927
Buy the tiny battery strings with the

119
00:04:06,927 --> 00:04:08,153
thin copper wire,

120
00:04:08,153 --> 00:04:10,460
the ones they call fairy lights.

121
00:04:10,640 --> 00:04:12,771
They cost about two dollars,

122
00:04:12,771 --> 00:04:14,142
they have a timer,

123
00:04:14,142 --> 00:04:15,969
and the wire disappears.

124
00:04:16,149 --> 00:04:18,692
Tuck them in a bowl of pinecones

125
00:04:18,692 --> 00:04:19,725
or ornaments.

126
00:04:19,905 --> 00:04:21,948
It glows like magic.

127
00:04:22,297 --> 00:04:23,993
Mistake number four.

128
00:04:24,173 --> 00:04:26,239
Too few lights on the tree.

129
00:04:26,419 --> 00:04:29,414
People put one string on a seven-foot

130
00:04:29,414 --> 00:04:32,247
tree, and it looks thin and spotty.

131
00:04:32,427 --> 00:04:34,976
The old rule is one hundred lights

132
00:04:34,976 --> 00:04:36,700
for every foot of tree.

133
00:04:36,880 --> 00:04:40,265
A seven-foot tree needs about seven hundred

134
00:04:40,265 --> 00:04:40,816
lights.

135
00:04:40,996 --> 00:04:42,660
That sounds like a lot,

136
00:04:42,660 --> 00:04:45,193
honey, but that's what makes a tree

137
00:04:45,193 --> 00:04:46,713
glow from the inside,

138
00:04:46,713 --> 00:04:49,029
instead of looking like it has a

139
00:04:49,029 --> 00:04:49,970
few freckles.

140
00:04:50,320 --> 00:04:52,492
And put them on the right way.

141
00:04:52,672 --> 00:04:55,472
Don't just wrap them around the outside

142
00:04:55,472 --> 00:04:56,549
like a bandage.

143
00:04:56,729 --> 00:04:58,853
Start at the trunk at the bottom,

144
00:04:58,853 --> 00:05:00,977
and run the lights out along each

145
00:05:00,977 --> 00:05:02,392
big branch to the tip,

146
00:05:02,392 --> 00:05:04,001
and back in to the trunk,

147
00:05:04,001 --> 00:05:05,739
then on to the next branch.

148
00:05:05,919 --> 00:05:07,611
It takes an hour longer,

149
00:05:07,611 --> 00:05:09,798
but the lights go deep into the

150
00:05:09,798 --> 00:05:12,196
tree, and it glows from the middle

151
00:05:12,196 --> 00:05:12,478
out.

152
00:05:12,828 --> 00:05:15,262
And here's a little trick for an

153
00:05:15,262 --> 00:05:16,479
old tree, honey,

154
00:05:16,479 --> 00:05:18,076
or a skinny fake one.

155
00:05:18,256 --> 00:05:20,858
Put a second string of lights deep

156
00:05:20,858 --> 00:05:23,308
inside, right against the trunk,

157
00:05:23,308 --> 00:05:24,456
all the way up.

158
00:05:24,636 --> 00:05:27,024
It lights the tree from the center,

159
00:05:27,024 --> 00:05:29,275
so you can't see the gaps between

160
00:05:29,275 --> 00:05:30,708
the branches anymore.

161
00:05:30,888 --> 00:05:33,728
The whole tree looks fuller and richer,

162
00:05:33,728 --> 00:05:35,694
like it cost twice as much.

163
00:05:35,874 --> 00:05:39,738
My daughter-in-law's fake tree is thirty years

164
00:05:39,738 --> 00:05:41,587
old, and nobody knows.

165
00:05:41,936 --> 00:05:44,285
So far, the ceiling light off,

166
00:05:44,285 --> 00:05:47,573
warm bulbs, lights spread around the room,

167
00:05:47,573 --> 00:05:50,078
and plenty of lights deep in the

168
00:05:50,078 --> 00:05:50,470
tree.

169
00:05:50,650 --> 00:05:52,740
Now mistake number five.

170
00:05:52,920 --> 00:05:57,227
Blinking, chasing, flashing lights inside the house.

171
00:05:57,407 --> 00:06:00,770
My father always said blinking lights belong

172
00:06:00,770 --> 00:06:01,993
on a fire truck.

173
00:06:02,173 --> 00:06:04,703
They make a room feel busy and

174
00:06:04,703 --> 00:06:05,377
nervous.

175
00:06:05,557 --> 00:06:07,426
Set every string to steady.

176
00:06:07,606 --> 00:06:09,621
Steady light is calm,

177
00:06:09,621 --> 00:06:11,252
and calm is cozy.

178
00:06:11,601 --> 00:06:13,494
Mistake number six.

179
00:06:13,674 --> 00:06:15,137
Cords everywhere.

180
00:06:15,317 --> 00:06:17,624
A tangle of green and white wires

181
00:06:17,624 --> 00:06:20,211
running across the floor and down the

182
00:06:20,211 --> 00:06:21,540
wall to the outlet.

183
00:06:21,720 --> 00:06:23,072
It looks messy,

184
00:06:23,072 --> 00:06:24,785
and it's dangerous.

185
00:06:24,965 --> 00:06:26,942
Run the cords along the back of

186
00:06:26,942 --> 00:06:29,493
the furniture and behind the tree skirt.

187
00:06:29,673 --> 00:06:30,911
Use a cord cover,

188
00:06:30,911 --> 00:06:33,095
or tape them under the edge of

189
00:06:33,095 --> 00:06:33,678
the rug.

190
00:06:33,858 --> 00:06:36,933
And use battery lights wherever you can,

191
00:06:36,933 --> 00:06:38,932
so there's no cord at all.

192
00:06:39,281 --> 00:06:40,444
And be safe,

193
00:06:40,444 --> 00:06:41,511
sweetheart.

194
00:06:41,691 --> 00:06:44,185
Never run cords under a rug where

195
00:06:44,185 --> 00:06:47,360
people walk, because they can wear through

196
00:06:47,360 --> 00:06:48,645
and start a fire.

197
00:06:48,825 --> 00:06:51,770
Don't plug too many strings into one

198
00:06:51,770 --> 00:06:52,343
outlet.

199
00:06:52,523 --> 00:06:55,061
Use a power strip with a switch,

200
00:06:55,061 --> 00:06:55,933
or a timer,

201
00:06:55,933 --> 00:06:58,630
so everything goes off at bedtime.

202
00:06:58,810 --> 00:07:01,480
And keep the tree watered every day.

203
00:07:01,660 --> 00:07:03,833
A dry tree and hot lights is

204
00:07:03,833 --> 00:07:05,851
how Christmas fires start.

205
00:07:06,201 --> 00:07:08,551
And now mistake number seven,

206
00:07:08,551 --> 00:07:10,253
the trick I promised.

207
00:07:10,433 --> 00:07:12,047
Forgetting the candles.

208
00:07:12,227 --> 00:07:14,491
Nothing in the world makes a room

209
00:07:14,491 --> 00:07:17,579
feel like Christmas the way candlelight does.

210
00:07:17,759 --> 00:07:20,446
My mother's trick on Christmas Eve was

211
00:07:20,446 --> 00:07:20,940
simple.

212
00:07:21,120 --> 00:07:23,505
Turn off every lamp in the house,

213
00:07:23,505 --> 00:07:24,661
except the tree.

214
00:07:24,841 --> 00:07:26,444
Then light candles.

215
00:07:26,624 --> 00:07:27,735
In the windows,

216
00:07:27,735 --> 00:07:28,698
on the table,

217
00:07:28,698 --> 00:07:29,735
on the mantel.

218
00:07:29,915 --> 00:07:31,153
Then sit down,

219
00:07:31,153 --> 00:07:33,363
and let your eyes adjust.

220
00:07:33,713 --> 00:07:35,174
In two minutes,

221
00:07:35,174 --> 00:07:37,510
honey, the room changes.

222
00:07:37,690 --> 00:07:40,767
Everybody's face looks soft and young.

223
00:07:40,947 --> 00:07:42,618
The ornaments sparkle.

224
00:07:42,798 --> 00:07:44,714
The children get quiet.

225
00:07:44,894 --> 00:07:47,471
That's the Christmas card I promised.

226
00:07:47,651 --> 00:07:50,963
And today, use the good battery candles

227
00:07:50,963 --> 00:07:53,002
with a flickering flame,

228
00:07:53,002 --> 00:07:55,295
especially around children,

229
00:07:55,295 --> 00:07:56,823
pets and greenery.

230
00:07:57,003 --> 00:07:59,917
Put them in glass holders or lanterns.

231
00:08:00,097 --> 00:08:02,767
Nobody can tell the difference across the

232
00:08:02,767 --> 00:08:03,093
room.

233
00:08:03,442 --> 00:08:05,497
If you do use real candles,

234
00:08:05,497 --> 00:08:07,476
keep them on a plate or in

235
00:08:07,476 --> 00:08:08,998
a tall glass holder,

236
00:08:08,998 --> 00:08:10,825
well away from the tree,

237
00:08:10,825 --> 00:08:13,032
the curtains and the garland.

238
00:08:13,212 --> 00:08:15,851
Never leave them burning when you leave

239
00:08:15,851 --> 00:08:17,678
the room, or when you go to

240
00:08:17,678 --> 00:08:17,949
bed.

241
00:08:18,129 --> 00:08:20,996
My mother kept a little brass snuffer

242
00:08:20,996 --> 00:08:22,236
by every candle,

243
00:08:22,236 --> 00:08:24,793
and the last job of Christmas Eve

244
00:08:24,793 --> 00:08:25,490
was mine.

245
00:08:25,670 --> 00:08:27,621
Snuffing out the candles,

246
00:08:27,621 --> 00:08:28,479
one by one.

247
00:08:28,829 --> 00:08:30,958
And one more kind of light,

248
00:08:30,958 --> 00:08:31,825
sweetheart.

249
00:08:32,005 --> 00:08:33,468
The fireplace.

250
00:08:33,648 --> 00:08:35,134
If you have one,

251
00:08:35,134 --> 00:08:37,363
use it on Christmas Eve.

252
00:08:37,543 --> 00:08:38,469
If you don't,

253
00:08:38,469 --> 00:08:41,103
there's no shame in a little tabletop

254
00:08:41,103 --> 00:08:43,311
lantern, or a row of candles in

255
00:08:43,311 --> 00:08:44,735
the empty fireplace,

256
00:08:44,735 --> 00:08:47,156
or even the fireplace video on the

257
00:08:47,156 --> 00:08:49,791
television with the sound turned low.

258
00:08:49,971 --> 00:08:53,447
My grandchildren insist on the television fire

259
00:08:53,447 --> 00:08:54,279
every year.

260
00:08:54,459 --> 00:08:56,026
They say it's tradition.

261
00:08:56,206 --> 00:08:58,934
It's been on since two thousand nine.

262
00:08:59,284 --> 00:09:01,529
And don't forget the windows,

263
00:09:01,529 --> 00:09:05,167
sweetheart, because that's what people see from

264
00:09:05,167 --> 00:09:06,018
the street.

265
00:09:06,198 --> 00:09:08,891
A single candle in every window,

266
00:09:08,891 --> 00:09:10,658
the old American way,

267
00:09:10,658 --> 00:09:13,350
on a timer from dusk to bedtime.

268
00:09:13,530 --> 00:09:14,912
In colonial days,

269
00:09:14,912 --> 00:09:17,350
a candle in the window meant a

270
00:09:17,350 --> 00:09:19,056
traveler was welcome.

271
00:09:19,236 --> 00:09:21,654
My mother kept one burning in our

272
00:09:21,654 --> 00:09:24,364
front window every night in December,

273
00:09:24,364 --> 00:09:25,609
for my uncle Ray,

274
00:09:25,609 --> 00:09:28,466
who was overseas in nineteen fifty-two.

275
00:09:28,816 --> 00:09:30,864
He came home that Christmas,

276
00:09:30,864 --> 00:09:33,497
honey, the day before Christmas Eve,

277
00:09:33,497 --> 00:09:35,179
on the afternoon train.

278
00:09:35,359 --> 00:09:37,464
He walked up Elm Street in his

279
00:09:37,464 --> 00:09:39,991
uniform, and the first thing he said

280
00:09:39,991 --> 00:09:42,377
when he came through the door was,

281
00:09:42,377 --> 00:09:44,693
I saw the candle from the corner.

282
00:09:44,873 --> 00:09:46,807
My mother put her face in her

283
00:09:46,807 --> 00:09:49,141

284
00:09:49,141 --> 00:09:49,807
long time.

285
00:09:50,157 --> 00:09:51,516
So one more time.

286
00:09:51,696 --> 00:09:53,472
Turn off the ceiling light.

287
00:09:53,652 --> 00:09:56,183
Warm white bulbs in every lamp.

288
00:09:56,363 --> 00:09:57,748
Layers of light,

289
00:09:57,748 --> 00:09:59,740
five or six small ones,

290
00:09:59,740 --> 00:10:01,471
all around the room.

291
00:10:01,651 --> 00:10:04,208
A hundred lights for every foot of

292
00:10:04,208 --> 00:10:06,237
tree, deep in the branches.

293
00:10:06,417 --> 00:10:08,658
Steady, never blinking.

294
00:10:08,838 --> 00:10:10,347
Hide the cords.

295
00:10:10,527 --> 00:10:13,326
And candles, in the windows and on

296
00:10:13,326 --> 00:10:14,150
the table.

297
00:10:14,330 --> 00:10:16,893
That's how my mother turned our little

298
00:10:16,893 --> 00:10:19,322
front room gold every Christmas Eve.

299
00:10:19,672 --> 00:10:21,416
Tell me in the comments,

300
00:10:21,416 --> 00:10:22,215
sweetheart.

301
00:10:22,395 --> 00:10:25,011
White lights or colored lights on your

302
00:10:25,011 --> 00:10:25,356
tree?

303
00:10:25,536 --> 00:10:27,286
And do you leave a candle in

304
00:10:27,286 --> 00:10:27,974
the window?

305
00:10:28,154 --> 00:10:31,343
The whole playlist of Grandma's Christmas tips

306
00:10:31,343 --> 00:10:33,424

307
00:10:33,424 --> 00:10:35,365

308
00:10:35,365 --> 00:10:35,781
video.

309
00:10:35,961 --> 00:10:37,517
Good night, honey.

310
00:10:37,697 --> 00:10:39,090
Merry Christmas.
