00:02:25,110 --> 00:02:27,178
The men ate it with spoons,

70
00:02:27,178 --> 00:02:29,857
and my husband's boss asked for the

71
00:02:29,857 --> 00:02:30,393
recipe.

72
00:02:30,573 --> 00:02:32,651
I never told him the truth.

73
00:02:33,002 --> 00:02:34,675
Here's what you need,

74
00:02:34,675 --> 00:02:36,508
for about forty pieces.

75
00:02:36,688 --> 00:02:39,002
Two and a half cups of white

76
00:02:39,002 --> 00:02:39,497
sugar.

77
00:02:39,677 --> 00:02:42,197
Half a cup of light corn syrup.

78
00:02:42,377 --> 00:02:43,991
Half a cup of water.

79
00:02:44,171 --> 00:02:46,365
A quarter teaspoon of salt.

80
00:02:46,545 --> 00:02:47,674
Two egg whites,

81
00:02:47,674 --> 00:02:49,180
at room temperature.

82
00:02:49,360 --> 00:02:51,404
One teaspoon of vanilla.

83
00:02:51,584 --> 00:02:54,376
And about a cup of pecan halves,

84
00:02:54,376 --> 00:02:55,947
or chopped pecans,

85
00:02:55,947 --> 00:02:56,646
toasted.

86
00:02:56,826 --> 00:02:58,056
That's all.

87
00:02:58,236 --> 00:03:00,593
But every one of these matters.

88
00:03:00,943 --> 00:03:02,487
And the tool I promised.

89
00:03:02,667 --> 00:03:04,443
A candy thermometer.

90
00:03:04,623 --> 00:03:06,968
Mistake number one is guessing.

91
00:03:07,148 --> 00:03:09,852
Divinity has to be cooked to exactly

92
00:03:09,852 --> 00:03:11,505
the right temperature,

93
00:03:11,505 --> 00:03:13,457
and a few degrees too low,

94
00:03:13,457 --> 00:03:14,509
it never sets.

95
00:03:14,689 --> 00:03:16,428
A few degrees too high,

96
00:03:16,428 --> 00:03:17,789
it turns to chalk.

97
00:03:17,969 --> 00:03:20,796
Grandma Pearl tested it by dropping a

98
00:03:20,796 --> 00:03:22,172
bit in cold water.

99
00:03:22,352 --> 00:03:23,907
You can do that too,

100
00:03:23,907 --> 00:03:26,473
but a thermometer is much easier.

101
00:03:26,824 --> 00:03:29,471
And check your thermometer first,

102
00:03:29,471 --> 00:03:30,353
sweetheart.

103
00:03:30,533 --> 00:03:32,561
Put it in a pot of boiling

104
00:03:32,561 --> 00:03:33,029
water.

105
00:03:33,209 --> 00:03:36,599
It should read two hundred twelve degrees.

106
00:03:36,779 --> 00:03:38,789
If it reads two hundred ten,

107
00:03:38,789 --> 00:03:40,654
then it's two degrees off,

108
00:03:40,654 --> 00:03:43,094
and you'll need to cook your candy

109
00:03:43,094 --> 00:03:45,893
two degrees lower than the recipe says.

110
00:03:46,073 --> 00:03:48,710
My thermometer was three degrees off for

111
00:03:48,710 --> 00:03:51,017
ten years, and I blamed the weather

112
00:03:51,017 --> 00:03:52,006
the whole time.

113
00:03:52,356 --> 00:03:53,470
Step one.

114
00:03:53,650 --> 00:03:56,587
Line two baking sheets with wax paper,

115
00:03:56,587 --> 00:03:58,596
and set them by the mixer.

116
00:03:58,776 --> 00:04:01,610
Have everything ready before you start,

117
00:04:01,610 --> 00:04:03,863
because once the candy is done,

118
00:04:03,863 --> 00:04:06,334
you have about one minute to work.

119
00:04:06,514 --> 00:04:08,712
Then, in a heavy saucepan,

120
00:04:08,712 --> 00:04:09,979
stir the sugar,

121
00:04:09,979 --> 00:04:13,360
corn syrup, water and salt together over

122
00:04:13,360 --> 00:04:17,079
medium heat, just until the sugar dissolves.

123
00:04:17,429 --> 00:04:19,263
Then stop stirring.

124
00:04:19,443 --> 00:04:22,483
Mistake number two is stirring the syrup

125
00:04:22,483 --> 00:04:23,623
while it boils.

126
00:04:23,803 --> 00:04:26,078
It makes sugar crystals form,

127
00:04:26,078 --> 00:04:28,667
and the whole batch turns grainy.

128
00:04:28,847 --> 00:04:30,384
Clip on the thermometer,

129
00:04:30,384 --> 00:04:32,690
and let it boil without touching it.

130
00:04:32,870 --> 00:04:35,155
If you see sugar crystals on the

131
00:04:35,155 --> 00:04:36,369
sides of the pan,

132
00:04:36,369 --> 00:04:38,868
brush them down with a pastry brush

133
00:04:38,868 --> 00:04:40,010
dipped in water.

134
00:04:40,361 --> 00:04:42,024
If this is helping you,

135
00:04:42,024 --> 00:04:44,482
honey, tap the like button for me.

136
00:04:44,662 --> 00:04:47,263
It helps Grandma more than you know.

137
00:04:47,443 --> 00:04:49,113
While the syrup boils,

138
00:04:49,113 --> 00:04:51,390
put the egg whites in the bowl

139
00:04:51,390 --> 00:04:52,377
of the mixer.

140
00:04:52,557 --> 00:04:55,378
When the syrup reaches about two hundred

141
00:04:55,378 --> 00:04:58,340
forty degrees, start beating the whites on

142
00:04:58,340 --> 00:05:01,019
high, until they form stiff peaks that

143
00:05:01,019 --> 00:05:03,488
stand up straight when you lift the

144
00:05:03,488 --> 00:05:03,981
beater.

145
00:05:04,161 --> 00:05:06,623
Then turn the mixer off and wait.

146
00:05:06,973 --> 00:05:10,054
Keep boiling the syrup until it reaches

147
00:05:10,054 --> 00:05:13,056
exactly two hundred fifty-two degrees.

148
00:05:13,236 --> 00:05:15,872
That's called the hard ball stage.

149
00:05:16,052 --> 00:05:17,869
If you drop a little in cold

150
00:05:17,869 --> 00:05:19,947
water, it makes a firm ball that

151
00:05:19,947 --> 00:05:22,089
holds its shape but still gives a

152
00:05:22,089 --> 00:05:23,842
little when you squeeze it.

153
00:05:24,022 --> 00:05:25,337
That's the number,

154
00:05:25,337 --> 00:05:25,775
honey.

155
00:05:25,955 --> 00:05:27,348
Two fifty-two.

156
00:05:27,528 --> 00:05:29,632
Write it on your hand if you

157
00:05:29,632 --> 00:05:30,233
have to.

158
00:05:30,584 --> 00:05:32,813
Now, mistake number three.

159
00:05:32,993 --> 00:05:35,162
Pouring the hot syrup in all at

160
00:05:35,162 --> 00:05:35,512
once.

161
00:05:35,692 --> 00:05:38,770
It cooks the egg whites into scrambled

162
00:05:38,770 --> 00:05:39,175
eggs.

163
00:05:39,355 --> 00:05:41,104
Turn the mixer on high,

164
00:05:41,104 --> 00:05:43,461
and pour the hot syrup into the

165
00:05:43,461 --> 00:05:45,666
whites in a very thin stream,

166
00:05:45,666 --> 00:05:46,730
like a pencil,

167
00:05:46,730 --> 00:05:48,707
down the side of the bowl,

168
00:05:48,707 --> 00:05:50,303
not onto the beaters.

169
00:05:50,483 --> 00:05:52,004
It takes about a minute.

170
00:05:52,184 --> 00:05:54,792
Be careful, the syrup is hotter than

171
00:05:54,792 --> 00:05:55,807
boiling water.

172
00:05:56,157 --> 00:05:57,329
Step three.

173
00:05:57,509 --> 00:05:58,683
Add the vanilla,

174
00:05:58,683 --> 00:06:00,516
and keep beating on high.

175
00:06:00,696 --> 00:06:03,013
It will be shiny and runny at

176
00:06:03,013 --> 00:06:05,410
first, like marshmallow cream.

177
00:06:05,590 --> 00:06:06,635
Keep going.

178
00:06:06,815 --> 00:06:09,379
Five minutes, eight minutes,

179
00:06:09,379 --> 00:06:10,936
sometimes twelve.

180
00:06:11,116 --> 00:06:14,611
Mistake number four is stopping too soon.

181
00:06:14,791 --> 00:06:17,352
You'll know it's ready when it starts

182
00:06:17,352 --> 00:06:18,598
to lose its shine,

183
00:06:18,598 --> 00:06:20,674
turns dull and a little matte,

184
00:06:20,674 --> 00:06:22,958
and holds its shape when you lift

185
00:06:22,958 --> 00:06:23,719
the beater.

186
00:06:24,069 --> 00:06:27,157
Here's the test Grandma Pearl used.

187
00:06:27,337 --> 00:06:29,903
Drop a spoonful on the wax paper.

188
00:06:30,083 --> 00:06:32,411
If it holds a soft little peak

189
00:06:32,411 --> 00:06:33,885
and doesn't spread,

190
00:06:33,885 --> 00:06:34,738
it's ready.

191
00:06:34,918 --> 00:06:37,134
If it flattens into a puddle,

192
00:06:37,134 --> 00:06:40,038
beat it another minute and test again.

193
00:06:40,218 --> 00:06:41,857
And when it's ready,

194
00:06:41,857 --> 00:06:44,068
stir in the chopped pecans,

195
00:06:44,068 --> 00:06:45,789
if you're using them,

196
00:06:45,789 --> 00:06:47,591
quickly, with a spoon.

197
00:06:47,941 --> 00:06:50,573
So far, a tested thermometer,

198
00:06:50,573 --> 00:06:53,024
no stirring while it boils,

199
00:06:53,024 --> 00:06:54,567
stiff egg whites,

200
00:06:54,567 --> 00:06:56,564
two fifty-two exactly,

201
00:06:56,564 --> 00:06:58,651
a thin stream of syrup,

202
00:06:58,651 --> 00:07:01,375
and beat it until it loses its

203
00:07:01,375 --> 00:07:01,919
shine.

204
00:07:02,099 --> 00:07:03,536
Now work fast,

205
00:07:03,536 --> 00:07:04,665
sweetheart.

206
00:07:04,845 --> 00:07:06,038
Use two spoons,

207
00:07:06,038 --> 00:07:08,344
one to scoop and one to push,

208
00:07:08,344 --> 00:07:11,127
and drop little mounds onto the wax

209
00:07:11,127 --> 00:07:13,274
paper, with a swirl on top.

210
00:07:13,454 --> 00:07:15,753
Press a pecan half on each one.

211
00:07:16,103 --> 00:07:18,235
If it starts to stiffen in the

212
00:07:18,235 --> 00:07:19,940
bowl before you're done,

213
00:07:19,940 --> 00:07:21,930
add a few drops of hot water

214
00:07:21,930 --> 00:07:22,569
and stir.

215
00:07:22,749 --> 00:07:25,583
Let the pieces sit at room temperature

216
00:07:25,583 --> 00:07:28,043
until they're firm and dry on the

217
00:07:28,043 --> 00:07:29,907
outside, about two hours,

218
00:07:29,907 --> 00:07:30,876
or overnight.

219
00:07:31,056 --> 00:07:33,661
They should be crisp on the outside

220
00:07:33,661 --> 00:07:35,669
and soft and creamy inside,

221
00:07:35,669 --> 00:07:37,976
like a cloud with a thin shell.

222
00:07:38,326 --> 00:07:40,706
And now the secret I promised,

223
00:07:40,706 --> 00:07:43,641
the one that makes most divinity fail

224
00:07:43,641 --> 00:07:44,990
before you start.

225
00:07:45,170 --> 00:07:46,075
The weather.

226
00:07:46,255 --> 00:07:48,911
Mistake number five is making it on

227
00:07:48,911 --> 00:07:50,505
a humid or rainy day.

228
00:07:50,685 --> 00:07:53,209
Sugar soaks up the water from the

229
00:07:53,209 --> 00:07:54,968
air, and on a damp day,

230
00:07:54,968 --> 00:07:56,804
divinity just won't set,

231
00:07:56,804 --> 00:07:58,487
no matter what you do.

232
00:07:58,667 --> 00:08:00,652
It stays sticky forever.

233
00:08:00,832 --> 00:08:03,917
Grandma Pearl always looked out the window

234
00:08:03,917 --> 00:08:05,313
before she started.

235
00:08:05,664 --> 00:08:07,621
Make it on a cold,

236
00:08:07,621 --> 00:08:09,251
clear, dry day.

237
00:08:09,431 --> 00:08:11,556
Winter is perfect for that.

238
00:08:11,736 --> 00:08:13,682
Don't boil a pot of soup or

239
00:08:13,682 --> 00:08:16,278
run the dishwasher at the same time,

240
00:08:16,278 --> 00:08:19,306
because the steam makes the kitchen humid.

241
00:08:19,486 --> 00:08:21,506
And if you must make it on

242
00:08:21,506 --> 00:08:22,361
a damp day,

243
00:08:22,361 --> 00:08:25,081
cook the syrup two or three degrees

244
00:08:25,081 --> 00:08:27,102
higher, to two fifty-five.

245
00:08:27,282 --> 00:08:30,161
Pearl said, a good candy maker reads

246
00:08:30,161 --> 00:08:33,040
the sky before she reads the recipe.

247
00:08:33,390 --> 00:08:35,139
And if it does fail,

248
00:08:35,139 --> 00:08:37,500
honey, don't throw it away.

249
00:08:37,680 --> 00:08:39,040
If it never sets,

250
00:08:39,040 --> 00:08:41,761
spread it on a cake like frosting,

251
00:08:41,761 --> 00:08:43,922
or spoon it over ice cream,

252
00:08:43,922 --> 00:08:45,923
like my divinity pudding.

253
00:08:46,103 --> 00:08:48,437
If it goes too hard and crumbly,

254
00:08:48,437 --> 00:08:50,479
break it up and stir it into

255
00:08:50,479 --> 00:08:53,615
softened vanilla ice cream with the pecans,

256
00:08:53,615 --> 00:08:54,636
and freeze it.

257
00:08:54,816 --> 00:08:56,299
Grandma Pearl said,

258
00:08:56,299 --> 00:08:59,265
there's no wasted sugar in my kitchen,

259
00:08:59,265 --> 00:09:01,840
just sugar that changed its mind.

260
00:09:02,190 --> 00:09:04,627
You can make it pretty for Christmas,

261
00:09:04,627 --> 00:09:05,023
honey.

262
00:09:05,203 --> 00:09:06,953
Add a few drops of red or

263
00:09:06,953 --> 00:09:09,544
green food coloring with the vanilla,

264
00:09:09,544 --> 00:09:11,785
for pink or pale green divinity.

265
00:09:11,965 --> 00:09:15,604
Or use peppermint extract instead of vanilla,

266
00:09:15,604 --> 00:09:18,839
and sprinkle crushed candy canes on top.

267
00:09:19,019 --> 00:09:21,786
Or chopped maraschino cherries,

268
00:09:21,786 --> 00:09:22,769
well dried.

269
00:09:22,949 --> 00:09:25,286
My mother made a plate of white,

270
00:09:25,286 --> 00:09:26,381
pink and green,

271
00:09:26,381 --> 00:09:29,230
and called it the Christmas tree plate.

272
00:09:29,580 --> 00:09:32,397
Divinity keeps about two weeks in an

273
00:09:32,397 --> 00:09:35,527
airtight tin, with wax paper between the

274
00:09:35,527 --> 00:09:36,936
layers, in a cool,

275
00:09:36,936 --> 00:09:37,718
dry place.

276
00:09:37,898 --> 00:09:39,555
Never in the icebox,

277
00:09:39,555 --> 00:09:42,206
because it gets damp and sticky.

278
00:09:42,386 --> 00:09:44,725
And it freezes for a month,

279
00:09:44,725 --> 00:09:45,938
wrapped tight.

280
00:09:46,118 --> 00:09:48,741
It makes a beautiful gift in paper

281
00:09:48,741 --> 00:09:49,590
candy cups.

282
00:09:49,770 --> 00:09:52,160
Old folks especially love it,

283
00:09:52,160 --> 00:09:53,067
sweetheart.

284
00:09:53,247 --> 00:09:56,027
One bite, and they're seven years old

285
00:09:56,027 --> 00:09:57,380
on the farm again.

286
00:09:57,730 --> 00:09:59,262
So one more time.

287
00:09:59,442 --> 00:10:01,253
A cold, dry day.

288
00:10:01,433 --> 00:10:03,697
A tested candy thermometer.

289
00:10:03,877 --> 00:10:06,333
Stir only until the sugar dissolves,

290
00:10:06,333 --> 00:10:07,697
then don't touch it.

291
00:10:07,877 --> 00:10:09,201
Stiff egg whites.

292
00:10:09,381 --> 00:10:11,691
Exactly two fifty-two.

293
00:10:11,871 --> 00:10:13,810
A thin stream of syrup.

294
00:10:13,990 --> 00:10:16,649
Beat it until it loses its shine.

295
00:10:16,829 --> 00:10:19,341
Work fast, two spoons,

296
00:10:19,341 --> 00:10:21,055
a pecan on top.

297
00:10:21,235 --> 00:10:23,661
That's Grandma Pearl's divinity,

298
00:10:23,661 --> 00:10:25,936
and with a little divine help,

299
00:10:25,936 --> 00:10:27,376
it sets every time.

300
00:10:27,726 --> 00:10:29,549
Tell me in the comments,

301
00:10:29,549 --> 00:10:30,384
sweetheart.

302
00:10:30,564 --> 00:10:33,827
Did somebody in your family make divinity?

303
00:10:34,007 --> 00:10:35,888
And did it ever fail?

304
00:10:36,068 --> 00:10:38,459
Be honest, mine has.

305
00:10:38,639 --> 00:10:41,778
The whole playlist of Grandma's recipes is

306
00:10:41,778 --> 00:10:43,796
right there on your screen,

307
00:10:43,796 --> 00:10:45,888
and I'll see you in the next

308
00:10:45,888 --> 00:10:46,337
video.

309
00:10:46,517 --> 00:10:48,107
Good night, honey.

310
00:10:48,287 --> 00:10:49,797
Merry Christmas.
0xtAc-8nWy0:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:02,509
Sweetheart, I can walk into any house

2
00:00:02,509 --> 00:00:04,679
in December and tell if the tree

3
00:00:04,679 --> 00:00:06,646
was done by a decorator or by

4
00:00:06,646 --> 00:00:09,020
a tired family at eleven o'clock at

5
00:00:09,020 --> 00:00:09,427
night.

6
00:00:09,607 --> 00:00:11,348
It's not the ornaments.

7
00:00:11,528 --> 00:00:13,270
It's the ribbon and the top.

8
00:00:13,450 --> 00:00:16,508
A decorator's tree has ribbon that tumbles

9
00:00:16,508 --> 00:00:18,110
down like a waterfall,

10
00:00:18,110 --> 00:00:20,367
and a topper that looks like it

11
00:00:20,367 --> 00:00:20,950
belongs.

12
00:00:21,130 --> 00:00:23,471
A tired tree has a ribbon wrapped

13
00:00:23,471 --> 00:00:25,670
like a mummy and a star leaning

14
00:00:25,670 --> 00:00:26,308
sideways.

15
00:00:26,658 --> 00:00:29,166
So tonight I'm giving you seven ribbon

16
00:00:29,166 --> 00:00:31,543
and tree topper mistakes that make a

17
00:00:31,543 --> 00:00:32,599
tree look cheap,

18
00:00:32,599 --> 00:00:33,854
and the easy fixes,

19
00:00:33,854 --> 00:00:35,900
so yours looks like it came out

20
00:00:35,900 --> 00:00:37,815
of a department store window.

21
00:00:37,995 --> 00:00:39,100
And stay with me,

22
00:00:39,100 --> 00:00:41,246
because the last one is the trick

23
00:00:41,246 --> 00:00:43,327
for keeping the topper straight,

24
00:00:43,327 --> 00:00:45,799
and it uses something you already have

25
00:00:45,799 --> 00:00:47,294
in your kitchen drawer.

26
00:00:47,644 --> 00:00:48,863
When I was a girl,

27
00:00:48,863 --> 00:00:51,299
my mother took me to Cleveland every

28
00:00:51,299 --> 00:00:54,006
December to see the Christmas windows at

29
00:00:54,006 --> 00:00:56,375
the big department stores downtown.

30
00:00:56,555 --> 00:00:58,610
Halle Brothers and Higbee's.

31
00:00:58,790 --> 00:01:01,052
There was a tree in one window,

32
00:01:01,052 --> 00:01:02,803
in nineteen fifty-three,

33
00:01:02,803 --> 00:01:05,795
with wide red velvet ribbon tumbling down

34
00:01:05,795 --> 00:01:07,911
from the top in long streams,

35
00:01:07,911 --> 00:01:10,465
and a gold star that almost touched

36
00:01:10,465 --> 00:01:11,341
the ceiling.

37
00:01:11,521 --> 00:01:13,666
I stood there so long my feet

38
00:01:13,666 --> 00:01:15,294
went numb in the snow.

39
00:01:15,643 --> 00:01:17,001
On the bus home,

40
00:01:17,001 --> 00:01:19,631
my mother asked me what I liked

41
00:01:19,631 --> 00:01:20,055
best.

42
00:01:20,235 --> 00:01:21,617
I said the ribbon.

43
00:01:21,797 --> 00:01:22,727
The next year,

44
00:01:22,727 --> 00:01:24,986
she bought two yards of red ribbon

45
00:01:24,986 --> 00:01:26,382
at the five and dime,

46
00:01:26,382 --> 00:01:28,442
and we tried to make our little

47
00:01:28,442 --> 00:01:29,970
tree look like Halle's.

48
00:01:30,150 --> 00:01:31,845
It didn't, honey.

49
00:01:32,025 --> 00:01:33,503
But we kept trying,

50
00:01:33,503 --> 00:01:35,759
every year, and by the time I

51
00:01:35,759 --> 00:01:39,026
was twenty, we'd figured out every secret.

52
00:01:39,206 --> 00:01:41,399
In a minute I'll show you the

53
00:01:41,399 --> 00:01:42,155
first one.

54
00:01:42,505 --> 00:01:44,456
Mistake number one.

55
00:01:44,636 --> 00:01:47,287
Wrapping the ribbon around the tree in

56
00:01:47,287 --> 00:01:49,101
a spiral, round and round,

57
00:01:49,101 --> 00:01:50,985
tight against the branches,

58
00:01:50,985 --> 00:01:52,032
like a bandage.

59
00:01:52,212 --> 00:01:54,820
It flattens the tree and looks like

60
00:01:54,820 --> 00:01:56,310
a candy cane stripe.

61
00:01:56,490 --> 00:01:59,079
The decorator's way is vertical.

62
00:01:59,259 --> 00:02:00,415
Start at the top,

63
00:02:00,415 --> 00:02:02,592
and let the ribbon fall down the

64
00:02:02,592 --> 00:02:03,476
tree in long,

65
00:02:03,476 --> 00:02:05,789
loose streams, from the top to the

66
00:02:05,789 --> 00:02:08,442
bottom, like water running down a hill.

67
00:02:08,792 --> 00:02:09,837
Here's how.

68
00:02:10,017 --> 00:02:11,925
Cut the ribbon into lengths,

69
00:02:11,925 --> 00:02:14,104
each one the height of the tree.

70
00:02:14,284 --> 00:02:16,807
Tuck one end into the branches near

71
00:02:16,807 --> 00:02:17,384
the top.

72
00:02:17,564 --> 00:02:19,177
Then let it fall down,

73
00:02:19,177 --> 00:02:21,743
tucking it into the tree every foot

74
00:02:21,743 --> 00:02:23,796
or so, pushing it in deep so

75
00:02:23,796 --> 00:02:26,656
it disappears, then letting it puff out

76
00:02:26,656 --> 00:02:27,096
again.

77
00:02:27,276 --> 00:02:28,901
In, out, in,

78
00:02:28,901 --> 00:02:32,152
out, like a gentle wave.

79
00:02:32,332 --> 00:02:34,408
Do five or six streams,

80
00:02:34,408 --> 00:02:37,115
evenly spaced around the tree.

81
00:02:37,465 --> 00:02:39,137
Mistake number two.

82
00:02:39,317 --> 00:02:41,233
Ribbon that's too skinny.

83
00:02:41,413 --> 00:02:43,157
A thin little ribbon,

84
00:02:43,157 --> 00:02:44,236
an inch wide,

85
00:02:44,236 --> 00:02:46,312
disappears into the tree.

86
00:02:46,492 --> 00:02:48,910
You can't even see it from across

87
00:02:48,910 --> 00:02:49,569
the room.

88
00:02:49,749 --> 00:02:50,682
For a tree,

89
00:02:50,682 --> 00:02:52,464
you want wide ribbon,

90
00:02:52,464 --> 00:02:55,095
two and a half inches at least,

91
00:02:55,095 --> 00:02:57,725
and four inches for a big tree.

92
00:02:57,905 --> 00:02:59,287
And wired ribbon,

93
00:02:59,287 --> 00:03:02,131
with thin wire sewn into the edges,

94
00:03:02,131 --> 00:03:04,407
so you can bend it and shape

95
00:03:04,407 --> 00:03:07,332
it, and it holds those pretty waves.

96
00:03:07,682 --> 00:03:08,843
How much?

97
00:03:09,023 --> 00:03:10,734
For a seven-foot tree,

98
00:03:10,734 --> 00:03:13,301
plan on about three or four rolls

99
00:03:13,301 --> 00:03:14,701
of ten yards each.

100
00:03:14,881 --> 00:03:16,678
It sounds like a lot,

101
00:03:16,678 --> 00:03:17,191
honey.

102
00:03:17,371 --> 00:03:19,708
But skimping on ribbon is like putting

103
00:03:19,708 --> 00:03:21,307
half a frosting on a cake.

104
00:03:21,487 --> 00:03:24,447
And buy it the day after Christmas,

105
00:03:24,447 --> 00:03:25,632
at half price,

106
00:03:25,632 --> 00:03:26,816
for next year.

107
00:03:26,996 --> 00:03:29,460
That's the only way I ever bought

108
00:03:29,460 --> 00:03:30,804
ribbon in my life.

109
00:03:31,154 --> 00:03:33,069
Mistake number three.

110
00:03:33,249 --> 00:03:35,049
Too many kinds of ribbon.

111
00:03:35,229 --> 00:03:37,614
Red plaid, gold glitter,

112
00:03:37,614 --> 00:03:40,396
silver mesh, and polka dots,

113
00:03:40,396 --> 00:03:41,986
all on one tree.

114
00:03:42,166 --> 00:03:45,242
It looks like a craft store exploded.

115
00:03:45,422 --> 00:03:46,676
Pick one ribbon,

116
00:03:46,676 --> 00:03:48,557
or two that go together.

117
00:03:48,737 --> 00:03:50,756
A red velvet and a gold,

118
00:03:50,756 --> 00:03:53,532
or a plaid with a matching solid.

119
00:03:53,712 --> 00:03:56,336
Then repeat them all around the tree.

120
00:03:56,516 --> 00:03:59,465
Repetition is what makes it look planned.

121
00:03:59,815 --> 00:04:01,412
If this is helping you,

122
00:04:01,412 --> 00:04:03,774
honey, tap the like button for me.

123
00:04:03,954 --> 00:04:06,693
It helps Grandma more than you know.

124
00:04:06,873 --> 00:04:08,116
And a little trick.

125
00:04:08,296 --> 00:04:10,006
If you use two ribbons,

126
00:04:10,006 --> 00:04:12,236
lay them on top of each other,

127
00:04:12,236 --> 00:04:15,061
the wide one underneath and the narrow

128
00:04:15,061 --> 00:04:15,879
one on top,

129
00:04:15,879 --> 00:04:17,514
and treat them as one.

130
00:04:17,694 --> 00:04:19,864
It looks rich and layered,

131
00:04:19,864 --> 00:04:21,699
and it's no more work.

132
00:04:21,879 --> 00:04:24,071
My mother did a red velvet with

133
00:04:24,071 --> 00:04:25,909
a thin gold ribbon on top,

134
00:04:25,909 --> 00:04:28,242
and it looked like a king's robe.

135
00:04:28,592 --> 00:04:30,414
Mistake number four.

136
00:04:30,594 --> 00:04:32,451
Putting the ribbon on last,

137
00:04:32,451 --> 00:04:34,100
after all the ornaments.

138
00:04:34,280 --> 00:04:36,835
Then it sits on top of everything

139
00:04:36,835 --> 00:04:38,924
and squashes the ornaments.

140
00:04:39,104 --> 00:04:41,538
The right order is lights first,

141
00:04:41,538 --> 00:04:42,754
then the ribbon,

142
00:04:42,754 --> 00:04:44,503
then the big ornaments,

143
00:04:44,503 --> 00:04:46,024
then the small ones.

144
00:04:46,204 --> 00:04:49,144
The ribbon goes on before the ornaments,

145
00:04:49,144 --> 00:04:51,202
so they can hang in front of

146
00:04:51,202 --> 00:04:52,451
it and around it,

147
00:04:52,451 --> 00:04:55,097
and everything looks woven together.

148
00:04:55,448 --> 00:04:58,154
So far, ribbon falling down,

149
00:04:58,154 --> 00:04:59,894
not wrapped round.

150
00:05:00,074 --> 00:05:01,734
Wide and wired.

151
00:05:01,914 --> 00:05:03,660
One or two kinds,

152
00:05:03,660 --> 00:05:04,585
repeated.

153
00:05:04,765 --> 00:05:07,063
And the ribbon before the ornaments.

154
00:05:07,243 --> 00:05:09,078
Now, the tree topper.

155
00:05:09,258 --> 00:05:11,800
And here's mistake number five.

156
00:05:11,980 --> 00:05:14,440
A topper that's too small for the

157
00:05:14,440 --> 00:05:14,813
tree.

158
00:05:14,993 --> 00:05:17,651
A little four-inch star on a seven-foot

159
00:05:17,651 --> 00:05:19,695
tree looks like a lost button.

160
00:05:19,875 --> 00:05:22,053
The topper should be about a tenth

161
00:05:22,053 --> 00:05:23,718
of the height of the tree.

162
00:05:24,069 --> 00:05:26,169
So for a seven-foot tree,

163
00:05:26,169 --> 00:05:29,110
a topper about eight or nine inches

164
00:05:29,110 --> 00:05:30,454
tall, or bigger.

165
00:05:30,634 --> 00:05:32,259
A star, an angel,

166
00:05:32,259 --> 00:05:33,215
a big bow,

167
00:05:33,215 --> 00:05:36,369
or a spray of branches and picks.

168
00:05:36,549 --> 00:05:38,860
And it doesn't have to be fancy.

169
00:05:39,040 --> 00:05:41,750
My mother's angel was made from a

170
00:05:41,750 --> 00:05:44,378
paper doily, a wooden bead for a

171
00:05:44,378 --> 00:05:46,842
head, and a pipe cleaner halo.

172
00:05:47,022 --> 00:05:49,032
I made it in second grade,

173
00:05:49,032 --> 00:05:50,733
in nineteen fifty-one,

174
00:05:50,733 --> 00:05:52,666
and it went on top of her

175
00:05:52,666 --> 00:05:54,289
tree for forty years.

176
00:05:54,640 --> 00:05:57,203
And here's a decorator's trick for a

177
00:05:57,203 --> 00:05:58,912
topper that looks grand.

178
00:05:59,092 --> 00:06:01,243
Make a big bow from your tree

179
00:06:01,243 --> 00:06:03,022
ribbon, with long tails,

180
00:06:03,022 --> 00:06:05,025
and put it at the very top.

181
00:06:05,205 --> 00:06:07,539
Then let the tails fall down the

182
00:06:07,539 --> 00:06:10,385
tree, and they become the first streams

183
00:06:10,385 --> 00:06:11,114
of ribbon.

184
00:06:11,294 --> 00:06:13,469
Then tuck a few tall sprays of

185
00:06:13,469 --> 00:06:16,587
glittery picks or dried branches behind the

186
00:06:16,587 --> 00:06:18,399
bow, sticking up and out.

187
00:06:18,579 --> 00:06:20,790
It looks like a firework at the

188
00:06:20,790 --> 00:06:21,076
top.

189
00:06:21,426 --> 00:06:23,434
Mistake number six.

190
00:06:23,614 --> 00:06:26,170
A bare, skinny top of the tree,

191
00:06:26,170 --> 00:06:28,726
with a topper stuck on a single

192
00:06:28,726 --> 00:06:30,127
stick, all alone.

193
00:06:30,307 --> 00:06:32,699
Most trees get thin at the top.

194
00:06:32,879 --> 00:06:34,637
The fix is to fill in the

195
00:06:34,637 --> 00:06:36,606
space just under the topper.

196
00:06:36,786 --> 00:06:38,130
Put your biggest,

197
00:06:38,130 --> 00:06:40,344
shiniest ornaments up there,

198
00:06:40,344 --> 00:06:42,875
cluster a few sprays of picks or

199
00:06:42,875 --> 00:06:44,693
ribbon loops around it,

200
00:06:44,693 --> 00:06:46,828
and add a few extra lights.

201
00:06:47,008 --> 00:06:49,201
Then the topper sits in a nest

202
00:06:49,201 --> 00:06:50,735
instead of on a pole.

203
00:06:51,086 --> 00:06:53,341
And now mistake number seven,

204
00:06:53,341 --> 00:06:54,975
the trick I promised.

205
00:06:55,155 --> 00:06:56,502
The leaning topper.

206
00:06:56,682 --> 00:06:59,098
Every year, it starts straight,

207
00:06:59,098 --> 00:07:02,371
and by Christmas morning it's tipped over,

208
00:07:02,371 --> 00:07:04,553
like it had too much eggnog.

209
00:07:04,733 --> 00:07:07,218
Here's the fix from your kitchen drawer.

210
00:07:07,398 --> 00:07:08,755
A wooden spoon,

211
00:07:08,755 --> 00:07:10,475
or a paint stirrer,

212
00:07:10,475 --> 00:07:11,833
or a chopstick.

213
00:07:12,013 --> 00:07:13,741
Tie it to the top of the

214
00:07:13,741 --> 00:07:15,901
trunk with a few twist ties or

215
00:07:15,901 --> 00:07:18,349
zip ties, so it sticks up straight

216
00:07:18,349 --> 00:07:19,141
and strong.

217
00:07:19,492 --> 00:07:21,775
Then slide the topper over it,

218
00:07:21,775 --> 00:07:23,907
or tie the topper to it with

219
00:07:23,907 --> 00:07:24,820
floral wire.

220
00:07:25,000 --> 00:07:28,177
The wooden spoon gives the skinny treetop

221
00:07:28,177 --> 00:07:29,029
a backbone.

222
00:07:29,209 --> 00:07:32,365
Your star or angel will stand straight

223
00:07:32,365 --> 00:07:34,608
until the sixth of January.

224
00:07:34,788 --> 00:07:37,894
My father figured that out in nineteen

225
00:07:37,894 --> 00:07:38,712
fifty-six.

226
00:07:38,892 --> 00:07:42,070
Before that, our angel spent every Christmas

227
00:07:42,070 --> 00:07:44,670
looking at the floor like she'd lost

228
00:07:44,670 --> 00:07:45,753
a contact lens.

229
00:07:46,104 --> 00:07:48,605
And put the topper on first,

230
00:07:48,605 --> 00:07:50,480
sweetheart, not last.

231
00:07:50,660 --> 00:07:52,574
Do it right after the lights,

232
00:07:52,574 --> 00:07:54,751
while you can still reach the top

233
00:07:54,751 --> 00:07:57,325
without knocking off a dozen ornaments.

234
00:07:57,505 --> 00:07:59,781
Stand on a sturdy step stool,

235
00:07:59,781 --> 00:08:00,723
not a chair,

236
00:08:00,723 --> 00:08:02,764
and have somebody hold it.

237
00:08:02,944 --> 00:08:05,221
And turn the lights on before you

238
00:08:05,221 --> 00:08:07,844
start decorating, so you can see where

239
00:08:07,844 --> 00:08:09,155
the dark spots are.

240
00:08:09,506 --> 00:08:11,044
When you're finished,

241
00:08:11,044 --> 00:08:12,948
step back across the room,

242
00:08:12,948 --> 00:08:14,486
and squint your eyes.

243
00:08:14,666 --> 00:08:15,915
It sounds silly,

244
00:08:15,915 --> 00:08:16,930
but it works.

245
00:08:17,110 --> 00:08:18,183
When you squint,

246
00:08:18,183 --> 00:08:20,328
you see the shapes and the light

247
00:08:20,328 --> 00:08:21,870
instead of the details.

248
00:08:22,050 --> 00:08:23,998
If one side looks empty,

249
00:08:23,998 --> 00:08:26,433
or a ribbon stream is crooked,

250
00:08:26,433 --> 00:08:28,299
or there's a dark hole,

251
00:08:28,299 --> 00:08:30,328
you'll see it right away.

252
00:08:30,508 --> 00:08:33,151
My mother squinted at our tree every

253
00:08:33,151 --> 00:08:35,720
year, and my father said she looked

254
00:08:35,720 --> 00:08:37,114
like a sea captain.

255
00:08:37,465 --> 00:08:39,797
And don't forget the bottom,

256
00:08:39,797 --> 00:08:40,297
honey.

257
00:08:40,477 --> 00:08:43,153
Fill the space under the tree with

258
00:08:43,153 --> 00:08:44,176
a tree skirt,

259
00:08:44,176 --> 00:08:46,773
a basket, or a few wrapped boxes,

260
00:08:46,773 --> 00:08:49,291
so the trunk and the stand don't

261
00:08:49,291 --> 00:08:49,684
show.

262
00:08:49,864 --> 00:08:51,973
A tree with a bare plastic stand

263
00:08:51,973 --> 00:08:54,740
looks like it's standing in its underwear.

264
00:08:54,920 --> 00:08:57,071
My grandson said that once,

265
00:08:57,071 --> 00:09:00,338
at Thanksgiving, and the whole family has

266
00:09:00,338 --> 00:09:01,851
said it ever since.

267
00:09:02,202 --> 00:09:04,430
And when you take it all down,

268
00:09:04,430 --> 00:09:07,177
wind each ribbon around a paper towel

269
00:09:07,177 --> 00:09:09,554
tube, and keep the topper in its

270
00:09:09,554 --> 00:09:11,559
own box, wrapped in tissue.

271
00:09:11,739 --> 00:09:14,606
Next year, you'll be finished in half

272
00:09:14,606 --> 00:09:15,303
the time.

273
00:09:15,483 --> 00:09:17,782
And the ribbon will come out smooth

274
00:09:17,782 --> 00:09:20,277
and ready, not crushed and wrinkled in

275
00:09:20,277 --> 00:09:21,590
the bottom of a box.

276
00:09:21,941 --> 00:09:23,438
So one more time.

277
00:09:23,618 --> 00:09:26,025
Ribbon falling down the tree,

278
00:09:26,025 --> 00:09:27,519
not wrapped round.

279
00:09:27,699 --> 00:09:29,278
Wide and wired.

280
00:09:29,458 --> 00:09:31,281
One or two kinds.

281
00:09:31,461 --> 00:09:33,644
The ribbon before the ornaments.

282
00:09:33,824 --> 00:09:35,842
A topper a tenth the height of

283
00:09:35,842 --> 00:09:36,447
the tree.

284
00:09:36,627 --> 00:09:38,522
Fill in the top so it sits

285
00:09:38,522 --> 00:09:39,251
in a nest.

286
00:09:39,431 --> 00:09:41,428
And a wooden spoon tied to the

287
00:09:41,428 --> 00:09:43,158
trunk to hold it straight.

288
00:09:43,338 --> 00:09:45,486
That's how my mother and I finally

289
00:09:45,486 --> 00:09:47,634
made our little tree look like the

290
00:09:47,634 --> 00:09:48,772
window at Halle's.

291
00:09:49,122 --> 00:09:51,040
Tell me in the comments,

292
00:09:51,040 --> 00:09:51,920
sweetheart.

293
00:09:52,100 --> 00:09:54,073
What's on top of your tree?

294
00:09:54,253 --> 00:09:55,843
A star, an angel,

295
00:09:55,843 --> 00:09:57,527
or something else?

296
00:09:57,707 --> 00:10:01,062
The whole playlist of Grandma's Christmas tips

297
00:10:01,062 --> 00:10:03,250
is right there on your screen,

298
00:10:03,250 --> 00:10:05,292
and I'll see you in the next

299
00:10:05,292 --> 00:10:05,730
video.

300
00:10:05,910 --> 00:10:07,407
Good night, honey.

301
00:10:07,587 --> 00:10:09,050
Merry Christmas.
4_IOj3-JGuk:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:03,863
Sweetheart, everybody decorates the living room for

2
00:00:03,863 --> 00:00:04,620
Christmas.

3
00:00:04,800 --> 00:00:06,493
The tree, the mantel,

4
00:00:06,493 --> 00:00:07,703
the front door.

5
00:00:07,883 --> 00:00:10,233
And then they forget the one room

6
00:00:10,233 --> 00:00:13,723
where the whole family actually spends Christmas.

7
00:00:13,903 --> 00:00:14,855
The kitchen.

8
00:00:15,035 --> 00:00:17,408
That's where the cookies get baked,

9
00:00:17,408 --> 00:00:19,375
where the coffee gets poured,

10
00:00:19,375 --> 00:00:21,681
where the aunts sit and talk until

11
00:00:21,681 --> 00:00:22,291
midnight.

12
00:00:22,471 --> 00:00:23,997
My mother always said,

13
00:00:23,997 --> 00:00:26,634
the kitchen is the heart of Christmas,

14
00:00:26,634 --> 00:00:28,438
so it should look like it.

15
00:00:28,788 --> 00:00:31,172
So tonight I'm giving you nine ways

16
00:00:31,172 --> 00:00:33,964
to make your kitchen feel like Christmas,

17
00:00:33,964 --> 00:00:35,190
most of them free,

18
00:00:35,190 --> 00:00:38,118
without cluttering up the counters you need

19
00:00:38,118 --> 00:00:38,936
for cooking.

20
00:00:39,116 --> 00:00:40,369
And stay with me,

21
00:00:40,369 --> 00:00:43,320
because the last one isn't something you

22
00:00:43,320 --> 00:00:44,131
see at all.

23
00:00:44,311 --> 00:00:45,955
It's something you smell,

24
00:00:45,955 --> 00:00:48,125
and it makes the whole house feel

25
00:00:48,125 --> 00:00:50,755
like Christmas the minute people walk in

26
00:00:50,755 --> 00:00:51,347
the door.

27
00:00:51,696 --> 00:00:54,395
Our kitchen on Elm Street was small,

28
00:00:54,395 --> 00:00:57,169
yellow, with a white enamel stove and

29
00:00:57,169 --> 00:00:59,717
a window over the sink that looked

30
00:00:59,717 --> 00:01:01,217
out on the backyard.

31
00:01:01,397 --> 00:01:04,544
Every December, my mother turned it into

32
00:01:04,544 --> 00:01:06,510
the coziest room in Ohio,

33
00:01:06,510 --> 00:01:08,084
with almost nothing.

34
00:01:08,264 --> 00:01:09,640
A few branches,

35
00:01:09,640 --> 00:01:11,109
some red ribbon,

36
00:01:11,109 --> 00:01:12,761
a bowl of oranges,

37
00:01:12,761 --> 00:01:14,963
and her good tablecloth.

38
00:01:15,143 --> 00:01:17,976
And the smell of something always baking.

39
00:01:18,325 --> 00:01:19,835
She had one rule.

40
00:01:20,015 --> 00:01:22,140
Nothing on the counters that gets in

41
00:01:22,140 --> 00:01:23,498
the way of the cooking.

42
00:01:23,678 --> 00:01:25,986
A kitchen has to work at Christmas

43
00:01:25,986 --> 00:01:28,226
harder than any other time of the

44
00:01:28,226 --> 00:01:28,566
year.

45
00:01:28,746 --> 00:01:30,749
So she decorated up high,

46
00:01:30,749 --> 00:01:31,791
on the walls,

47
00:01:31,791 --> 00:01:34,756
the windows and the tops of cabinets,

48
00:01:34,756 --> 00:01:37,000
and left the counters clear.

49
00:01:37,180 --> 00:01:39,129
In a minute I'll show you how,

50
00:01:39,129 --> 00:01:41,662
starting with the window over the sink.

51
00:01:42,011 --> 00:01:42,975
Number one.

52
00:01:43,155 --> 00:01:44,870
The window over the sink,

53
00:01:44,870 --> 00:01:47,546
because that's where you spend the most

54
00:01:47,546 --> 00:01:48,438
time looking.

55
00:01:48,618 --> 00:01:50,933
Hang a small wreath in the window

56
00:01:50,933 --> 00:01:51,776
on a ribbon.

57
00:01:51,956 --> 00:01:54,425
Or lay a little garland of cedar

58
00:01:54,425 --> 00:01:55,583
along the sill,

59
00:01:55,583 --> 00:01:57,203
with a few pinecones.

60
00:01:57,383 --> 00:01:59,830
Or hang a row of three dried

61
00:01:59,830 --> 00:02:02,888
orange slices, or paper snowflakes,

62
00:02:02,888 --> 00:02:04,198
on thin thread.

63
00:02:04,378 --> 00:02:06,505
My mother hung a little red bell

64
00:02:06,505 --> 00:02:08,964
that rang when she opened the window.

65
00:02:09,314 --> 00:02:11,802
And put a small potted plant on

66
00:02:11,802 --> 00:02:13,006
the windowsill.

67
00:02:13,186 --> 00:02:16,357
A little rosemary plant trimmed like a

68
00:02:16,357 --> 00:02:19,443
Christmas tree, or a paperwhite bulb,

69
00:02:19,443 --> 00:02:21,279
or a Christmas cactus.

70
00:02:21,459 --> 00:02:23,096
Rosemary is my favorite,

71
00:02:23,096 --> 00:02:25,485
honey, because it looks like a tiny

72
00:02:25,485 --> 00:02:27,395
tree and you can snip it for

73
00:02:27,395 --> 00:02:28,146
the turkey.

74
00:02:28,326 --> 00:02:30,741
Mine is eleven years old now.

75
00:02:30,921 --> 00:02:33,845
Every December, I tie a little red

76
00:02:33,845 --> 00:02:34,706
bow on it.

77
00:02:35,055 --> 00:02:36,158
Number two.

78
00:02:36,338 --> 00:02:38,196
The tops of the cabinets.

79
00:02:38,376 --> 00:02:40,773
That's the most wasted space in the

80
00:02:40,773 --> 00:02:41,731
whole kitchen.

81
00:02:41,911 --> 00:02:44,775
Lay a long garland of greenery across

82
00:02:44,775 --> 00:02:47,174
the tops, with a string of warm

83
00:02:47,174 --> 00:02:49,109
battery lights tucked in.

84
00:02:49,289 --> 00:02:51,599
It makes the whole room glow at

85
00:02:51,599 --> 00:02:54,355
night, and it's completely out of the

86
00:02:54,355 --> 00:02:54,653
way.

87
00:02:54,833 --> 00:02:57,527
My granddaughter does this every year,

88
00:02:57,527 --> 00:03:00,149
and she says it's the only decoration

89
00:03:00,149 --> 00:03:01,567
the cat can't reach.

90
00:03:01,917 --> 00:03:03,311
Number three.

91
00:03:03,491 --> 00:03:05,523
If you have an open shelf,

92
00:03:05,523 --> 00:03:06,382
or a hutch,

93
00:03:06,382 --> 00:03:09,509
swap a few everyday things for Christmas

94
00:03:09,509 --> 00:03:09,899
ones.

95
00:03:10,079 --> 00:03:12,923
Put out the red and white dishes,

96
00:03:12,923 --> 00:03:14,818
a few old cookie tins,

97
00:03:14,818 --> 00:03:16,628
a jar of candy canes,

98
00:03:16,628 --> 00:03:18,868
a stack of Christmas mugs.

99
00:03:19,048 --> 00:03:22,125
Mix in a few sprigs of greenery.

100
00:03:22,305 --> 00:03:24,097
You're not adding clutter,

101
00:03:24,097 --> 00:03:24,511
honey.

102
00:03:24,691 --> 00:03:27,390
You're just trading what's already there for

103
00:03:27,390 --> 00:03:28,801
something more festive.

104
00:03:29,150 --> 00:03:31,453
And if you have any old Christmas

105
00:03:31,453 --> 00:03:34,174
dishes from your mother or grandmother,

106
00:03:34,174 --> 00:03:36,198
this is the time to use them.

107
00:03:36,378 --> 00:03:38,351
Don't keep them in a box.

108
00:03:38,531 --> 00:03:41,327
My mother's Christmas plates are white with

109
00:03:41,327 --> 00:03:42,757
a little holly border,

110
00:03:42,757 --> 00:03:45,358
from Woolworth's in nineteen fifty-five.

111
00:03:45,538 --> 00:03:47,221
They cost a dollar each.

112
00:03:47,401 --> 00:03:50,216
I eat breakfast off them every day

113
00:03:50,216 --> 00:03:52,534
in December, and every time,

114
00:03:52,534 --> 00:03:53,775
I think of her.

115
00:03:54,125 --> 00:03:56,905
Number four, and this is the easiest

116
00:03:56,905 --> 00:03:57,214
one.

117
00:03:57,394 --> 00:03:59,843
Change the towels and the linens.

118
00:04:00,023 --> 00:04:02,675
A red and white checked dish towel,

119
00:04:02,675 --> 00:04:04,039
a plaid oven mitt,

120
00:04:04,039 --> 00:04:07,373
a Christmas tablecloth on the kitchen table.

121
00:04:07,553 --> 00:04:08,983
That's all it takes,

122
00:04:08,983 --> 00:04:11,488
and it changes the whole feeling of

123
00:04:11,488 --> 00:04:13,276
the room in five minutes.

124
00:04:13,456 --> 00:04:15,945
And it costs almost nothing if you

125
00:04:15,945 --> 00:04:18,434
buy them the week after Christmas,

126
00:04:18,434 --> 00:04:19,459
for next year.

127
00:04:19,808 --> 00:04:21,490
If this is helping you,

128
00:04:21,490 --> 00:04:23,976
honey, tap the like button for me.

129
00:04:24,156 --> 00:04:26,850
It helps Grandma more than you know.

130
00:04:27,030 --> 00:04:29,410
And put a small rug in front

131
00:04:29,410 --> 00:04:30,430
of the sink,

132
00:04:30,430 --> 00:04:31,790
in red or plaid.

133
00:04:31,970 --> 00:04:34,199
It's soft on your feet when you're

134
00:04:34,199 --> 00:04:37,215
standing there doing dishes for the fourteenth

135
00:04:37,215 --> 00:04:38,657
time on Christmas Day.

136
00:04:38,837 --> 00:04:39,763
In my family,

137
00:04:39,763 --> 00:04:42,541
the dishes take longer than the dinner.

138
00:04:42,890 --> 00:04:44,121
Number five.

139
00:04:44,301 --> 00:04:45,627
The kitchen table,

140
00:04:45,627 --> 00:04:48,574
the one where the family eats breakfast.

141
00:04:48,754 --> 00:04:49,874
Keep it simple,

142
00:04:49,874 --> 00:04:51,668
so you can still use it.

143
00:04:51,848 --> 00:04:54,465
A small bowl of clementines with a

144
00:04:54,465 --> 00:04:56,236
few sprigs of greenery.

145
00:04:56,416 --> 00:04:59,216
Or a pitcher of evergreen branches with

146
00:04:59,216 --> 00:04:59,934
a red bow.

147
00:05:00,114 --> 00:05:02,644
Or a little row of three candles

148
00:05:02,644 --> 00:05:03,435
on a tray.

149
00:05:03,615 --> 00:05:05,696
Something you can lift off in one

150
00:05:05,696 --> 00:05:07,651
move when it's time to roll out

151
00:05:07,651 --> 00:05:08,723
the cookie dough.

152
00:05:09,072 --> 00:05:11,826
So far, the window over the sink,

153
00:05:11,826 --> 00:05:13,912
the tops of the cabinets,

154
00:05:13,912 --> 00:05:15,164
the open shelf,

155
00:05:15,164 --> 00:05:18,000
the towels, and the kitchen table.

156
00:05:18,180 --> 00:05:20,650
And here's a tip about that bowl

157
00:05:20,650 --> 00:05:22,348
of clementines, honey.

158
00:05:22,528 --> 00:05:25,533
They're food and decoration at the same

159
00:05:25,533 --> 00:05:25,919
time.

160
00:05:26,099 --> 00:05:28,208
My mother put a bowl of oranges

161
00:05:28,208 --> 00:05:29,976
on the table all December,

162
00:05:29,976 --> 00:05:32,085
and we were allowed to take one

163
00:05:32,085 --> 00:05:33,378
any time we wanted.

164
00:05:33,558 --> 00:05:34,643
In the fifties,

165
00:05:34,643 --> 00:05:37,031
an orange in December felt like a

166
00:05:37,031 --> 00:05:37,610
present.

167
00:05:37,959 --> 00:05:40,414
And hang a few things on the

168
00:05:40,414 --> 00:05:42,255
cabinet doors, honey.

169
00:05:42,435 --> 00:05:44,426
A small wreath on a ribbon over

170
00:05:44,426 --> 00:05:46,480
the door of the cabinet with the

171
00:05:46,480 --> 00:05:48,856
glasses, or a sprig of mistletoe tied

172
00:05:48,856 --> 00:05:50,782
with red string to the knob of

173
00:05:50,782 --> 00:05:51,874
the kitchen door.

174
00:05:52,054 --> 00:05:55,132
My mother hung mistletoe there every year,

175
00:05:55,132 --> 00:05:57,697
and my father would stand under it,

176
00:05:57,697 --> 00:05:59,823
waiting, with his coffee cup,

177
00:05:59,823 --> 00:06:01,435
until she noticed him.

178
00:06:01,615 --> 00:06:04,295
She always pretended not to see him

179
00:06:04,295 --> 00:06:05,980
for a good long while.

180
00:06:06,330 --> 00:06:07,631
Number six.

181
00:06:07,811 --> 00:06:09,471
The refrigerator door.

182
00:06:09,651 --> 00:06:12,274
That's where the family's whole life goes

183
00:06:12,274 --> 00:06:13,041
in December.

184
00:06:13,221 --> 00:06:15,924
Clear off the old magnets and papers,

185
00:06:15,924 --> 00:06:18,626
and hang the Christmas cards there as

186
00:06:18,626 --> 00:06:19,575
they come in,

187
00:06:19,575 --> 00:06:21,548
or the children's drawings,

188
00:06:21,548 --> 00:06:23,008
or the family photo.

189
00:06:23,188 --> 00:06:25,384
My mother tied a red ribbon around

190
00:06:25,384 --> 00:06:26,933
the refrigerator handle,

191
00:06:26,933 --> 00:06:27,902
like a present.

192
00:06:28,082 --> 00:06:30,125
My father said it was the only

193
00:06:30,125 --> 00:06:32,440
present in the house he could open

194
00:06:32,440 --> 00:06:33,121
every day.

195
00:06:33,470 --> 00:06:34,840
Number seven.

196
00:06:35,020 --> 00:06:36,518
Bring out something old.

197
00:06:36,698 --> 00:06:38,707
A vintage cookie jar.

198
00:06:38,887 --> 00:06:41,301
An old rolling pin with a ribbon

199
00:06:41,301 --> 00:06:42,132
tied on it,

200
00:06:42,132 --> 00:06:43,415
hung on the wall.

201
00:06:43,595 --> 00:06:46,582
Your grandmother's tin cookie cutters on a

202
00:06:46,582 --> 00:06:46,938
hook.

203
00:06:47,118 --> 00:06:50,075
A handwritten recipe card in a little

204
00:06:50,075 --> 00:06:50,555
frame.

205
00:06:50,735 --> 00:06:53,531
Old kitchen things have a warmth that

206
00:06:53,531 --> 00:06:55,042
nothing new can buy.

207
00:06:55,222 --> 00:06:57,358
And they start conversations.

208
00:06:57,538 --> 00:07:00,158
Every child who comes in my kitchen

209
00:07:00,158 --> 00:07:03,076
asks about Grandma Pearl's rolling pin.

210
00:07:03,426 --> 00:07:04,332
Number eight.

211
00:07:04,512 --> 00:07:06,416
Soft light at night.

212
00:07:06,596 --> 00:07:09,607
After supper, turn off the bright overhead

213
00:07:09,607 --> 00:07:11,112
light in the kitchen,

214
00:07:11,112 --> 00:07:13,549
and leave on only the little light

215
00:07:13,549 --> 00:07:14,625
over the stove,

216
00:07:14,625 --> 00:07:17,062
the lights on top of the cabinets,

217
00:07:17,062 --> 00:07:18,926
and a candle on the table.

218
00:07:19,106 --> 00:07:22,368
That's when the kitchen feels the coziest.

219
00:07:22,548 --> 00:07:25,284
The whole family drifts in for cocoa

220
00:07:25,284 --> 00:07:28,249
and cookies, and nobody wants to leave.

221
00:07:28,598 --> 00:07:29,947
And now number nine,

222
00:07:29,947 --> 00:07:31,497
the one I promised you,

223
00:07:31,497 --> 00:07:33,451
the one you don't see at all.

224
00:07:33,631 --> 00:07:34,688
The smell.

225
00:07:34,868 --> 00:07:36,876
Put a small pot of water on

226
00:07:36,876 --> 00:07:38,885
the stove on very low heat.

227
00:07:39,065 --> 00:07:41,042
Add a few orange peels,

228
00:07:41,042 --> 00:07:42,504
a cinnamon stick,

229
00:07:42,504 --> 00:07:44,653
five or six whole cloves,

230
00:07:44,653 --> 00:07:46,716
a slice of fresh ginger,

231
00:07:46,716 --> 00:07:49,468
and a sprig of pine or rosemary.

232
00:07:49,648 --> 00:07:52,282
Let it simmer gently all afternoon,

233
00:07:52,282 --> 00:07:54,466
adding water as it goes down.

234
00:07:54,815 --> 00:07:56,023
In half an hour,

235
00:07:56,023 --> 00:07:58,891
the whole house smells like Christmas,

236
00:07:58,891 --> 00:07:59,343
honey.

237
00:07:59,523 --> 00:08:02,530
Like oranges and spice and pine.

238
00:08:02,710 --> 00:08:05,218
Better than any candle you can buy.

239
00:08:05,398 --> 00:08:07,777
People walk in the front door and

240
00:08:07,777 --> 00:08:09,868
say, oh, what are you baking?

241
00:08:10,048 --> 00:08:11,600
And you can say,

242
00:08:11,600 --> 00:08:12,765
nothing yet.

243
00:08:12,945 --> 00:08:15,001
Keep it on the back burner on

244
00:08:15,001 --> 00:08:17,200
low, and never leave it on when

245
00:08:17,200 --> 00:08:19,186
you leave the house or go to

246
00:08:19,186 --> 00:08:19,469
bed.

247
00:08:19,819 --> 00:08:21,812
And use your scraps,

248
00:08:21,812 --> 00:08:22,908
sweetheart.

249
00:08:23,088 --> 00:08:25,806
Save the peels from the clementines in

250
00:08:25,806 --> 00:08:27,237
a bag in the icebox,

251
00:08:27,237 --> 00:08:29,813
with the ends of the cinnamon sticks

252
00:08:29,813 --> 00:08:31,459
and the rosemary stems.

253
00:08:31,639 --> 00:08:33,125
Toss them in the pot.

254
00:08:33,305 --> 00:08:35,569
It costs nothing at all.

255
00:08:35,749 --> 00:08:38,519
My mother made hers with apple peels

256
00:08:38,519 --> 00:08:40,982
and cloves, and she said it kept

257
00:08:40,982 --> 00:08:43,368
the whole family in a good mood

258
00:08:43,368 --> 00:08:44,677
until New Year's.

259
00:08:45,026 --> 00:08:47,309
And make a little cocoa station,

260
00:08:47,309 --> 00:08:50,163
sweetheart, on one corner of the counter

261
00:08:50,163 --> 00:08:51,447
you don't cook on.

262
00:08:51,627 --> 00:08:53,648
A tray with a jar of cocoa

263
00:08:53,648 --> 00:08:56,135
mix, a jar of mini marshmallows,

264
00:08:56,135 --> 00:08:57,767
a jar of candy canes,

265
00:08:57,767 --> 00:09:00,487
and a few Christmas mugs hanging on

266
00:09:00,487 --> 00:09:01,809
hooks or stacked.

267
00:09:01,989 --> 00:09:04,234
It's a decoration and a treat at

268
00:09:04,234 --> 00:09:05,216
the same time.

269
00:09:05,396 --> 00:09:08,660
The grandchildren make their own all December,

270
00:09:08,660 --> 00:09:10,788
and the tray is always a happy

271
00:09:10,788 --> 00:09:11,143
mess.

272
00:09:11,493 --> 00:09:13,714
And a word about keeping it all

273
00:09:13,714 --> 00:09:14,431
practical.

274
00:09:14,611 --> 00:09:17,612
Keep every decoration away from the stove,

275
00:09:17,612 --> 00:09:19,684
the toaster and anything hot.

276
00:09:19,864 --> 00:09:22,621
No paper or dried greens near the

277
00:09:22,621 --> 00:09:23,289
burners.

278
00:09:23,469 --> 00:09:25,919
Keep the counters clear for cooking.

279
00:09:26,099 --> 00:09:28,847
And put everything away by the sixth

280
00:09:28,847 --> 00:09:31,595
of January, so the kitchen goes back

281
00:09:31,595 --> 00:09:32,206
to work.

282
00:09:32,386 --> 00:09:35,056
A Christmas kitchen should be beautiful,

283
00:09:35,056 --> 00:09:37,192
but it should still make supper.

284
00:09:37,542 --> 00:09:39,203
So one more time.

285
00:09:39,383 --> 00:09:41,523
A wreath or greens in the window

286
00:09:41,523 --> 00:09:42,459
over the sink.

287
00:09:42,639 --> 00:09:45,008
A garland on top of the cabinets.

288
00:09:45,188 --> 00:09:47,115
Christmas dishes on the shelf.

289
00:09:47,295 --> 00:09:49,861
Red towels and a plaid rug.

290
00:09:50,041 --> 00:09:52,421
A bowl of oranges on the table.

291
00:09:52,601 --> 00:09:54,563
Cards on the refrigerator.

292
00:09:54,743 --> 00:09:56,542
Something old on the wall.

293
00:09:56,722 --> 00:09:58,301
Soft light at night.

294
00:09:58,481 --> 00:10:00,435
And a pot of orange peels and

295
00:10:00,435 --> 00:10:02,591
cinnamon simmering on the stove.

296
00:10:02,771 --> 00:10:04,559
That's the heart of Christmas.

297
00:10:04,909 --> 00:10:06,653
Tell me in the comments,

298
00:10:06,653 --> 00:10:07,452
sweetheart.

299
00:10:07,632 --> 00:10:10,710
What did your grandmother's kitchen smell like

300
00:10:10,710 --> 00:10:11,579
at Christmas?

301
00:10:11,759 --> 00:10:13,164
I'd love to know.

302
00:10:13,344 --> 00:10:16,476
The whole playlist of Grandma's Christmas tips

303
00:10:16,476 --> 00:10:18,518
is right there on your screen,

304
00:10:18,518 --> 00:10:20,424
and I'll see you in the next

305
00:10:20,424 --> 00:10:20,833
video.

306
00:10:21,013 --> 00:10:22,650
Good night, honey.

307
00:10:22,830 --> 00:10:24,409
Merry Christmas.
