00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:03,250
Sweetheart, the first time I tasted real

2
00:00:03,250 --> 00:00:06,257
homemade eggnog, I was six years old,

3
00:00:06,257 --> 00:00:09,589
at Grandma Pearl's farm on Christmas Eve,

4
00:00:09,589 --> 00:00:10,808
nineteen fifty.

5
00:00:10,988 --> 00:00:12,952
She ladled it out of a big

6
00:00:12,952 --> 00:00:15,520
glass punch bowl into little cups,

7
00:00:15,520 --> 00:00:17,483
thick and cold and creamy,

8
00:00:17,483 --> 00:00:18,918
with nutmeg on top.

9
00:00:19,098 --> 00:00:21,257
Mine had no whiskey in it.

10
00:00:21,437 --> 00:00:23,353
My father's had plenty.

11
00:00:23,533 --> 00:00:25,975
He sang Jingle Bells all the way

12
00:00:25,975 --> 00:00:27,272
home in the snow.

13
00:00:27,621 --> 00:00:30,382
Today most people only know the carton

14
00:00:30,382 --> 00:00:31,472
from the store,

15
00:00:31,472 --> 00:00:33,941
which is thin and sweet and tastes

16
00:00:33,941 --> 00:00:35,539
like melted ice cream.

17
00:00:35,719 --> 00:00:38,145
And when they make it at home,

18
00:00:38,145 --> 00:00:39,681
it comes out runny,

19
00:00:39,681 --> 00:00:42,430
or it curdles into scrambled eggs.

20
00:00:42,610 --> 00:00:45,707
So tonight I'm giving you Grandma Pearl's

21
00:00:45,707 --> 00:00:47,142
eggnog, every step,

22
00:00:47,142 --> 00:00:49,785
and the five mistakes that ruin it.

23
00:00:49,965 --> 00:00:51,202
And stay with me,

24
00:00:51,202 --> 00:00:53,676
because the last secret is the one

25
00:00:53,676 --> 00:00:55,131
that makes it thick,

26
00:00:55,131 --> 00:00:57,314
and it takes nothing but time.

27
00:00:57,664 --> 00:01:00,346
Eggnog is older than the country,

28
00:01:00,346 --> 00:01:00,834
honey.

29
00:01:01,014 --> 00:01:03,731
In England, rich people drank a hot

30
00:01:03,731 --> 00:01:06,138
milk and egg drink with wine or

31
00:01:06,138 --> 00:01:07,458
sherry in winter.

32
00:01:07,638 --> 00:01:10,615
When it came to the American colonies,

33
00:01:10,615 --> 00:01:12,495
people made it with rum,

34
00:01:12,495 --> 00:01:14,610
because rum was cheap here,

35
00:01:14,610 --> 00:01:17,274
and later with whiskey and brandy.

36
00:01:17,454 --> 00:01:20,068
George Washington had his own recipe,

37
00:01:20,068 --> 00:01:22,117
and they say it was so strong

38
00:01:22,117 --> 00:01:24,095
only the brave would try it.

39
00:01:24,444 --> 00:01:25,459
On the farm,

40
00:01:25,459 --> 00:01:28,502
Grandma Pearl made it with eggs from

41
00:01:28,502 --> 00:01:31,122
her own hens and milk and cream

42
00:01:31,122 --> 00:01:32,559
from her own cow,

43
00:01:32,559 --> 00:01:33,489
still warm.

44
00:01:33,669 --> 00:01:35,907
Nothing in it came from a store

45
00:01:35,907 --> 00:01:37,134
except the sugar,

46
00:01:37,134 --> 00:01:39,950
the nutmeg and my grandfather's bottle.

47
00:01:40,130 --> 00:01:42,066
She made it in the morning and

48
00:01:42,066 --> 00:01:44,260
set it in the cold springhouse all

49
00:01:44,260 --> 00:01:45,099
day to chill.

50
00:01:45,279 --> 00:01:47,779
By evening, it was thick enough to

51
00:01:47,779 --> 00:01:49,029
stand a spoon in.

52
00:01:49,379 --> 00:01:50,830
In the old days,

53
00:01:50,830 --> 00:01:53,825
people made eggnog with raw eggs.

54
00:01:54,005 --> 00:01:56,511
Today, we cook it gently into a

55
00:01:56,511 --> 00:01:59,906
custard first, so it's safe for everybody,

56
00:01:59,906 --> 00:02:03,544
the children and the grandparents and anybody

57
00:02:03,544 --> 00:02:04,919
expecting a baby.

58
00:02:05,099 --> 00:02:08,489
And honestly, it tastes better cooked.

59
00:02:08,669 --> 00:02:10,689
In a minute I'll show you how,

60
00:02:10,689 --> 00:02:12,844
and the trick that keeps it from

61
00:02:12,844 --> 00:02:14,729
turning into scrambled eggs.

62
00:02:15,079 --> 00:02:17,132
In our house on Elm Street,

63
00:02:17,132 --> 00:02:19,566
eggnog was only for two nights a

64
00:02:19,566 --> 00:02:22,532
year, Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve.

65
00:02:22,712 --> 00:02:24,753
My mother made it in her big

66
00:02:24,753 --> 00:02:27,159
yellow mixing bowl and kept it on

67
00:02:27,159 --> 00:02:28,253
the back porch,

68
00:02:28,253 --> 00:02:30,804
because the icebox was full of ham.

69
00:02:30,984 --> 00:02:33,088
One year the dog got to it

70
00:02:33,088 --> 00:02:33,573
first.

71
00:02:33,753 --> 00:02:36,803
He spent Christmas Day sleeping under the

72
00:02:36,803 --> 00:02:38,737
kitchen table, very happy,

73
00:02:38,737 --> 00:02:39,779
and very full.

74
00:02:40,129 --> 00:02:42,922
Here's what you need for about six

75
00:02:42,922 --> 00:02:43,333
cups.

76
00:02:43,513 --> 00:02:45,220
Six egg yolks.

77
00:02:45,400 --> 00:02:46,979
Half a cup of sugar.

78
00:02:47,159 --> 00:02:48,842
Two cups of whole milk.

79
00:02:49,022 --> 00:02:50,938
One cup of heavy cream.

80
00:02:51,118 --> 00:02:52,546
A pinch of salt.

81
00:02:52,726 --> 00:02:54,955
One teaspoon of vanilla.

82
00:02:55,135 --> 00:02:58,429
Half a teaspoon of freshly grated nutmeg,

83
00:02:58,429 --> 00:03:00,197
plus more for the top.

84
00:03:00,377 --> 00:03:02,072
And a cinnamon stick.

85
00:03:02,252 --> 00:03:04,596
If you want it for grown-ups,

86
00:03:04,596 --> 00:03:06,374
half a cup to a cup of

87
00:03:06,374 --> 00:03:08,719
bourbon, brandy, or dark rum.

88
00:03:09,069 --> 00:03:11,286
And here's mistake number one.

89
00:03:11,466 --> 00:03:14,461
Using skim milk or low fat milk.

90
00:03:14,641 --> 00:03:17,563
Eggnog is supposed to be rich,

91
00:03:17,563 --> 00:03:18,148
honey.

92
00:03:18,328 --> 00:03:20,116
It's a once-a-year treat.

93
00:03:20,296 --> 00:03:22,088
Thin milk makes thin,

94
00:03:22,088 --> 00:03:25,416
watery eggnog that tastes like nothing.

95
00:03:25,596 --> 00:03:28,881
Use whole milk and real heavy cream.

96
00:03:29,061 --> 00:03:31,260
If you want it a little lighter,

97
00:03:31,260 --> 00:03:33,459
use half and half instead of the

98
00:03:33,459 --> 00:03:34,971
cream, but never skim.

99
00:03:35,321 --> 00:03:38,100
And grate the nutmeg yourself if you

100
00:03:38,100 --> 00:03:38,409
can.

101
00:03:38,589 --> 00:03:41,410
A whole nutmeg costs about the same

102
00:03:41,410 --> 00:03:43,666
as a jar of the ground kind,

103
00:03:43,666 --> 00:03:45,520
and it lasts for years.

104
00:03:45,700 --> 00:03:47,538
Rub it on a small grater,

105
00:03:47,538 --> 00:03:50,332
and the smell fills the whole kitchen.

106
00:03:50,512 --> 00:03:53,039
Ground nutmeg from a jar that's been

107
00:03:53,039 --> 00:03:56,126
in the cupboard since nineteen ninety tastes

108
00:03:56,126 --> 00:03:56,828
like dust.

109
00:03:57,008 --> 00:03:59,226
That's mistake number two.

110
00:03:59,576 --> 00:04:00,574
Step one.

111
00:04:00,754 --> 00:04:01,482
In a bowl,

112
00:04:01,482 --> 00:04:04,248
whisk the egg yolks and sugar together

113
00:04:04,248 --> 00:04:05,849
for about two minutes,

114
00:04:05,849 --> 00:04:08,615
until they turn pale yellow and thick,

115
00:04:08,615 --> 00:04:10,871
like a ribbon when you lift the

116
00:04:10,871 --> 00:04:11,307
whisk.

117
00:04:11,487 --> 00:04:12,594
In a saucepan,

118
00:04:12,594 --> 00:04:13,701
warm the milk,

119
00:04:13,701 --> 00:04:16,073
the cream, the cinnamon stick,

120
00:04:16,073 --> 00:04:18,841
the nutmeg and the salt over medium

121
00:04:18,841 --> 00:04:22,319
heat, until it's steaming and little bubbles

122
00:04:22,319 --> 00:04:23,980
form around the edge.

123
00:04:24,160 --> 00:04:25,832
Don't let it boil.

124
00:04:26,182 --> 00:04:29,363
Step two, and here's mistake number three.

125
00:04:29,543 --> 00:04:31,988
Pouring the hot milk into the eggs

126
00:04:31,988 --> 00:04:32,852
all at once.

127
00:04:33,032 --> 00:04:36,279
The eggs cook instantly into little scrambled

128
00:04:36,279 --> 00:04:36,712
lumps.

129
00:04:36,892 --> 00:04:38,707
It's called tempering,

130
00:04:38,707 --> 00:04:39,202
honey.

131
00:04:39,382 --> 00:04:41,630
Pour the hot milk into the eggs

132
00:04:41,630 --> 00:04:43,806
very slowly, just a ladle at a

133
00:04:43,806 --> 00:04:46,416
time, while you whisk the whole time

134
00:04:46,416 --> 00:04:47,939
with your other hand.

135
00:04:48,119 --> 00:04:49,998
Warm the eggs up gently,

136
00:04:49,998 --> 00:04:51,486
a little at a time.

137
00:04:51,836 --> 00:04:53,513
If this is helping you,

138
00:04:53,513 --> 00:04:55,992
honey, tap the like button for me.

139
00:04:56,172 --> 00:04:58,958
It helps Grandma more than you know.

140
00:04:59,138 --> 00:05:01,287
When about half the milk is in,

141
00:05:01,287 --> 00:05:03,991
pour everything back into the saucepan.

142
00:05:04,171 --> 00:05:06,634
Now cook it over medium-low heat,

143
00:05:06,634 --> 00:05:09,767
stirring constantly with a wooden spoon or

144
00:05:09,767 --> 00:05:12,976
a spatula, scraping the bottom and corners,

145
00:05:12,976 --> 00:05:15,363
for about five to eight minutes.

146
00:05:15,714 --> 00:05:18,218
Mistake number four is cooking it too

147
00:05:18,218 --> 00:05:19,301
hot or too long.

148
00:05:19,481 --> 00:05:20,921
It curdles.

149
00:05:21,101 --> 00:05:23,152
You want it to reach one hundred

150
00:05:23,152 --> 00:05:25,652
sixty to one hundred seventy degrees on

151
00:05:25,652 --> 00:05:27,126
a thermometer, no more.

152
00:05:27,306 --> 00:05:29,350
Or use the old test.

153
00:05:29,530 --> 00:05:30,629
Dip a spoon in,

154
00:05:30,629 --> 00:05:33,268
and run your finger across the back.

155
00:05:33,448 --> 00:05:36,338
If the line stays clean and doesn't

156
00:05:36,338 --> 00:05:37,824
run back together,

157
00:05:37,824 --> 00:05:38,649
it's done.

158
00:05:38,829 --> 00:05:41,012
Take it off the heat right away.

159
00:05:41,362 --> 00:05:44,021
And if it does start to curdle

160
00:05:44,021 --> 00:05:45,882
a little, sweetheart,

161
00:05:45,882 --> 00:05:46,946
don't panic.

162
00:05:47,126 --> 00:05:49,634
Take it off the heat immediately and

163
00:05:49,634 --> 00:05:51,375
pour it into a cold bowl.

164
00:05:51,555 --> 00:05:53,135
Then whisk it hard,

165
00:05:53,135 --> 00:05:55,630
or blend it for a few seconds.

166
00:05:55,810 --> 00:05:58,515
Small lumps will smooth right out.

167
00:05:58,695 --> 00:06:00,978
Then pour it through a fine strainer

168
00:06:00,978 --> 00:06:02,817
into a clean pitcher or bowl.

169
00:06:02,997 --> 00:06:05,145
Always strain it anyway.

170
00:06:05,325 --> 00:06:07,854
It catches the cinnamon stick and any

171
00:06:07,854 --> 00:06:09,632
little bits of cooked egg.

172
00:06:09,982 --> 00:06:12,604
So far, whole milk and cream,

173
00:06:12,604 --> 00:06:14,866
fresh nutmeg, pale yolks,

174
00:06:14,866 --> 00:06:16,946
temper the eggs slowly,

175
00:06:16,946 --> 00:06:19,840
and cook it gently to one sixty,

176
00:06:19,840 --> 00:06:21,197
then strain it.

177
00:06:21,377 --> 00:06:22,573
Stir in the vanilla.

178
00:06:22,753 --> 00:06:24,530
Now the secret I promised,

179
00:06:24,530 --> 00:06:26,445
the one that makes it thick.

180
00:06:26,625 --> 00:06:29,784
Mistake number five is drinking it right

181
00:06:29,784 --> 00:06:30,653
away, warm.

182
00:06:30,833 --> 00:06:32,993
Warm eggnog is thin.

183
00:06:33,173 --> 00:06:36,100
Cold eggnog is thick and velvety,

184
00:06:36,100 --> 00:06:38,583
the way Grandma Pearl's was.

185
00:06:38,933 --> 00:06:41,026
Cover it, and put it in the

186
00:06:41,026 --> 00:06:43,429
icebox for at least four hours,

187
00:06:43,429 --> 00:06:45,678
and overnight is even better.

188
00:06:45,858 --> 00:06:48,217
The custard thickens as it chills,

189
00:06:48,217 --> 00:06:50,507
and the flavors of the nutmeg and

190
00:06:50,507 --> 00:06:51,686
vanilla come out.

191
00:06:51,866 --> 00:06:54,920
That's Grandma Pearl's springhouse.

192
00:06:55,100 --> 00:06:57,388
And if you want it extra light

193
00:06:57,388 --> 00:06:59,676
and fluffy, whip a half cup of

194
00:06:59,676 --> 00:07:02,803
cream to soft peaks right before serving,

195
00:07:02,803 --> 00:07:04,480
and fold it in gently.

196
00:07:04,831 --> 00:07:06,223
For the grown-ups,

197
00:07:06,223 --> 00:07:07,770
stir in the bourbon,

198
00:07:07,770 --> 00:07:10,401
brandy, or rum after it's chilled,

199
00:07:10,401 --> 00:07:11,871
a little at a time,

200
00:07:11,871 --> 00:07:12,876
and taste it.

201
00:07:13,056 --> 00:07:15,204
My father liked bourbon.

202
00:07:15,384 --> 00:07:18,210
Grandma Pearl liked a mix of brandy

203
00:07:18,210 --> 00:07:20,067
and rum, half and half,

204
00:07:20,067 --> 00:07:22,489
and she said it was medicinal.

205
00:07:22,669 --> 00:07:24,968
Some people make a big batch with

206
00:07:24,968 --> 00:07:26,919
the spirits in it and let it

207
00:07:26,919 --> 00:07:28,869
age in the icebox for weeks.

208
00:07:29,049 --> 00:07:31,574
That's a little too brave for me,

209
00:07:31,574 --> 00:07:32,033
honey.

210
00:07:32,383 --> 00:07:34,918
And always keep a pitcher without any

211
00:07:34,918 --> 00:07:37,454
spirits, for the children and for the

212
00:07:37,454 --> 00:07:38,002
drivers.

213
00:07:38,182 --> 00:07:40,483
I put a little red ribbon around

214
00:07:40,483 --> 00:07:43,143
the handle of the children's pitcher,

215
00:07:43,143 --> 00:07:44,869
so nobody mixes them up.

216
00:07:45,049 --> 00:07:47,189
Learned that one the hard way in

217
00:07:47,189 --> 00:07:50,667
nineteen seventy-three, when my nephew Michael drank

218
00:07:50,667 --> 00:07:52,606
two cups of the wrong one and

219
00:07:52,606 --> 00:07:55,080
fell asleep under the Christmas tree.

220
00:07:55,431 --> 00:07:57,968
And save those egg whites,

221
00:07:57,968 --> 00:07:58,554
honey.

222
00:07:58,734 --> 00:08:00,429
Don't throw them away.

223
00:08:00,609 --> 00:08:02,485
Put them in a jar in the

224
00:08:02,485 --> 00:08:04,986
icebox, and they keep four days.

225
00:08:05,166 --> 00:08:07,942
Use them for a batch of divinity,

226
00:08:07,942 --> 00:08:09,625
or meringue cookies,

227
00:08:09,625 --> 00:08:10,971
or a white cake.

228
00:08:11,151 --> 00:08:13,361
Or whip two of them to soft

229
00:08:13,361 --> 00:08:16,227
peaks and fold them into the eggnog

230
00:08:16,227 --> 00:08:17,947
right before serving,

231
00:08:17,947 --> 00:08:19,011
for a frothy,

232
00:08:19,011 --> 00:08:20,485
old-fashioned nog.

233
00:08:20,665 --> 00:08:23,674
That's how my grandmother's mother made it,

234
00:08:23,674 --> 00:08:25,773
back in the eighteen nineties.

235
00:08:26,124 --> 00:08:27,018
To serve it,

236
00:08:27,018 --> 00:08:29,106
pour it into a punch bowl or

237
00:08:29,106 --> 00:08:32,238
small glasses, and grate fresh nutmeg over

238
00:08:32,238 --> 00:08:32,834
the top.

239
00:08:33,014 --> 00:08:35,357
Add a cinnamon stick in each glass

240
00:08:35,357 --> 00:08:36,253
for stirring.

241
00:08:36,433 --> 00:08:39,127
Or a little dollop of whipped cream.

242
00:08:39,307 --> 00:08:41,818
It's rich, sweetheart,

243
00:08:41,818 --> 00:08:43,417
so small cups.

244
00:08:43,597 --> 00:08:46,129
A big glass of eggnog is like

245
00:08:46,129 --> 00:08:47,788
eating a whole pie.

246
00:08:47,968 --> 00:08:50,855
Grandma Pearl served it in little glass

247
00:08:50,855 --> 00:08:53,297
punch cups no bigger than an egg.

248
00:08:53,647 --> 00:08:56,158
And it's wonderful in other things,

249
00:08:56,158 --> 00:08:56,445
too.

250
00:08:56,625 --> 00:08:59,028
A splash in your morning coffee.

251
00:08:59,208 --> 00:09:01,545
Use it instead of milk for French

252
00:09:01,545 --> 00:09:03,457
toast on Christmas morning.

253
00:09:03,637 --> 00:09:05,378
Or in a bread pudding,

254
00:09:05,378 --> 00:09:06,644
or a pound cake.

255
00:09:06,824 --> 00:09:10,831
My granddaughter makes eggnog pancakes on Christmas

256
00:09:10,831 --> 00:09:14,052
morning, and the house smells like nutmeg

257
00:09:14,052 --> 00:09:14,916
until noon.

258
00:09:15,267 --> 00:09:18,336
Homemade eggnog keeps three days in the

259
00:09:18,336 --> 00:09:20,619
icebox, in a covered pitcher.

260
00:09:20,799 --> 00:09:23,222
Give it a good stir before serving,

261
00:09:23,222 --> 00:09:24,537
because it settles.

262
00:09:24,717 --> 00:09:26,566
It doesn't freeze well,

263
00:09:26,566 --> 00:09:29,942
honey, because it separates when it thaws.

264
00:09:30,122 --> 00:09:32,673
So make only what you'll drink in

265
00:09:32,673 --> 00:09:33,523
a few days.

266
00:09:33,703 --> 00:09:36,432
That's never a problem in my family.

267
00:09:36,612 --> 00:09:39,296
The pitcher is always empty by the

268
00:09:39,296 --> 00:09:40,164
second day.

269
00:09:40,515 --> 00:09:42,824
And if somebody can't have dairy,

270
00:09:42,824 --> 00:09:45,344
sweetheart, you can make it with oat

271
00:09:45,344 --> 00:09:47,374
milk or almond milk and a can

272
00:09:47,374 --> 00:09:49,963
of coconut cream instead of the heavy

273
00:09:49,963 --> 00:09:50,383
cream.

274
00:09:50,563 --> 00:09:52,447
It's not quite the same,

275
00:09:52,447 --> 00:09:55,037
but it's thick and sweet and full

276
00:09:55,037 --> 00:09:55,822
of nutmeg.

277
00:09:56,002 --> 00:09:58,609
My grandson's wife can't have milk,

278
00:09:58,609 --> 00:10:00,918
and I make her a little pitcher

279
00:10:00,918 --> 00:10:01,738
every year.

280
00:10:01,918 --> 00:10:04,066
She says it tastes like Christmas,

281
00:10:04,066 --> 00:10:05,772
and that's the whole point.

282
00:10:06,123 --> 00:10:07,562
So one more time.

283
00:10:07,742 --> 00:10:09,731
Whole milk and cream,

284
00:10:09,731 --> 00:10:10,772
never skim.

285
00:10:10,952 --> 00:10:12,241
Fresh nutmeg.

286
00:10:12,421 --> 00:10:15,475
Whisk the yolks and sugar until pale.

287
00:10:15,655 --> 00:10:18,093
Temper the eggs slowly with the hot

288
00:10:18,093 --> 00:10:18,441
milk.

289
00:10:18,621 --> 00:10:19,857
Cook it gently,

290
00:10:19,857 --> 00:10:21,752
stirring, to one sixty,

291
00:10:21,752 --> 00:10:22,905
and strain it.

292
00:10:23,085 --> 00:10:24,385
Chill it overnight.

293
00:10:24,565 --> 00:10:26,386
Spirits for the grown-ups,

294
00:10:26,386 --> 00:10:29,116
and a ribbon on the children's pitcher.

295
00:10:29,296 --> 00:10:31,729
That's Grandma Pearl's eggnog,

296
00:10:31,729 --> 00:10:34,405
thick enough to stand a spoon in.

297
00:10:34,755 --> 00:10:36,482
Tell me in the comments,

298
00:10:36,482 --> 00:10:37,274
sweetheart.

299
00:10:37,454 --> 00:10:38,853
Do you love eggnog,

300
00:10:38,853 --> 00:10:40,473
or can't you stand it?

301
00:10:40,653 --> 00:10:42,986
I know families are divided.

302
00:10:43,166 --> 00:10:46,182
The whole playlist of Grandma's recipes is

303
00:10:46,182 --> 00:10:48,120
right there on your screen,

304
00:10:48,120 --> 00:10:50,131
and I'll see you in the next

305
00:10:50,131 --> 00:10:50,562
video.

306
00:10:50,742 --> 00:10:52,390
Good night, honey.

307
00:10:52,570 --> 00:10:54,056
Merry Christmas.
-UKXkMq9Vf4:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:02,251
Sweetheart, when I was a girl,

2
00:00:02,251 --> 00:00:04,503
potato soup was what we ate on

3
00:00:04,503 --> 00:00:06,904
Thursday, the day before payday,

4
00:00:06,904 --> 00:00:09,456
when there was nothing left in the

5
00:00:09,456 --> 00:00:11,633
house but a sack of potatoes,

6
00:00:11,633 --> 00:00:13,734
an onion, and a little milk.

7
00:00:13,914 --> 00:00:16,067
And it was the best night of

8
00:00:16,067 --> 00:00:16,759
the week.

9
00:00:16,939 --> 00:00:18,737
My mother made it in a big

10
00:00:18,737 --> 00:00:20,813
dented pot, and we ate it with

11
00:00:20,813 --> 00:00:23,719
saltine crackers crumbled on top until the

12
00:00:23,719 --> 00:00:25,449
bowls were scraped clean.

13
00:00:25,799 --> 00:00:28,660
But people tell me their potato soup

14
00:00:28,660 --> 00:00:31,045
comes out like wallpaper glue,

15
00:00:31,045 --> 00:00:32,556
or thin and watery,

16
00:00:32,556 --> 00:00:35,179
or it tastes like boiled nothing.

17
00:00:35,359 --> 00:00:38,103
So tonight I'm giving you my mother's

18
00:00:38,103 --> 00:00:39,883
potato soup, every step,

19
00:00:39,883 --> 00:00:42,404
and the five mistakes that make it

20
00:00:42,404 --> 00:00:43,591
gluey and bland.

21
00:00:43,771 --> 00:00:45,005
And stay with me,

22
00:00:45,005 --> 00:00:47,329
because the last trick is how to

23
00:00:47,329 --> 00:00:49,944
make it thick and creamy without any

24
00:00:49,944 --> 00:00:50,888
flour at all.

25
00:00:51,238 --> 00:00:54,157
My father worked at the Westinghouse plant

26
00:00:54,157 --> 00:00:56,382
in Mansfield, and he got paid on

27
00:00:56,382 --> 00:00:56,868
Friday.

28
00:00:57,048 --> 00:01:00,331
By Thursday, my mother had stretched every

29
00:01:00,331 --> 00:01:02,598
dollar as far as it would go.

30
00:01:02,778 --> 00:01:05,251
So Thursday was potato soup.

31
00:01:05,431 --> 00:01:07,479
She said a good cook could feed

32
00:01:07,479 --> 00:01:09,526
a family of four on fifty cents

33
00:01:09,526 --> 00:01:11,178
and a little imagination.

34
00:01:11,358 --> 00:01:13,618
She had a lot of imagination,

35
00:01:13,618 --> 00:01:14,086
honey.

36
00:01:14,437 --> 00:01:15,480
When I grew up,

37
00:01:15,480 --> 00:01:18,262
I found out other families called potato

38
00:01:18,262 --> 00:01:19,723
soup poor man's soup,

39
00:01:19,723 --> 00:01:22,018
and they were a little ashamed of

40
00:01:22,018 --> 00:01:22,227
it.

41
00:01:22,407 --> 00:01:23,579
We never were.

42
00:01:23,759 --> 00:01:25,938
My father said it was the only

43
00:01:25,938 --> 00:01:28,043
soup that made him feel rich.

44
00:01:28,223 --> 00:01:29,890
And when I got married,

45
00:01:29,890 --> 00:01:32,427
the first thing my husband asked me

46
00:01:32,427 --> 00:01:35,108
to learn was my mother's potato soup.

47
00:01:35,288 --> 00:01:37,484
In a minute I'll tell you why

48
00:01:37,484 --> 00:01:40,362
hers was better than everybody else's.

49
00:01:40,712 --> 00:01:42,096
And today, honey,

50
00:01:42,096 --> 00:01:45,191
it's still one of the cheapest suppers

51
00:01:45,191 --> 00:01:45,924
there is.

52
00:01:46,104 --> 00:01:48,751
A pot that feeds six costs about

53
00:01:48,751 --> 00:01:52,143
eight dollars, even with bacon and cheese

54
00:01:52,143 --> 00:01:52,722
on top.

55
00:01:52,902 --> 00:01:55,096
It's ready in forty minutes.

56
00:01:55,276 --> 00:01:57,937
And it's the perfect supper for a

57
00:01:57,937 --> 00:02:00,275
cold, gray night in November,

58
00:02:00,275 --> 00:02:03,662
when everybody's tired and nobody wants to

59
00:02:03,662 --> 00:02:04,065
cook.

60
00:02:04,416 --> 00:02:06,330
Here's what you need,

61
00:02:06,330 --> 00:02:06,877
honey.

62
00:02:07,057 --> 00:02:09,120
Three pounds of potatoes,

63
00:02:09,120 --> 00:02:11,678
about six or seven medium ones.

64
00:02:11,858 --> 00:02:13,866
Four slices of bacon.

65
00:02:14,046 --> 00:02:15,764
One onion, chopped.

66
00:02:15,944 --> 00:02:17,644
Two ribs of celery,

67
00:02:17,644 --> 00:02:18,359
chopped.

68
00:02:18,539 --> 00:02:20,258
Two cloves of garlic.

69
00:02:20,438 --> 00:02:22,446
Four cups of chicken broth.

70
00:02:22,626 --> 00:02:24,603
One and a half cups of whole

71
00:02:24,603 --> 00:02:26,156
milk or half and half.

72
00:02:26,336 --> 00:02:28,518
Two tablespoons of butter.

73
00:02:28,698 --> 00:02:31,982
Salt, pepper, and a little fresh thyme

74
00:02:31,982 --> 00:02:33,191
or a bay leaf.

75
00:02:33,371 --> 00:02:34,833
And for the top,

76
00:02:34,833 --> 00:02:36,935
cheddar cheese, chives,

77
00:02:36,935 --> 00:02:38,305
and sour cream.

78
00:02:38,656 --> 00:02:41,144
And here's mistake number one,

79
00:02:41,144 --> 00:02:44,130
and it's the reason most potato soup

80
00:02:44,130 --> 00:02:45,540
tastes like glue.

81
00:02:45,720 --> 00:02:47,171
The wrong potato.

82
00:02:47,351 --> 00:02:50,961
Russet potatoes, the big brown baking kind,

83
00:02:50,961 --> 00:02:52,388
are very starchy,

84
00:02:52,388 --> 00:02:54,991
and they fall apart into paste.

85
00:02:55,171 --> 00:02:56,723
Yukon Gold potatoes,

86
00:02:56,723 --> 00:02:57,966
the yellow ones,

87
00:02:57,966 --> 00:03:01,071
are creamy and buttery and hold together

88
00:03:01,071 --> 00:03:01,614
better.

89
00:03:01,794 --> 00:03:04,600
My mother used whatever was cheapest,

90
00:03:04,600 --> 00:03:06,040
but when she could,

91
00:03:06,040 --> 00:03:07,936
she used the yellow ones.

92
00:03:08,286 --> 00:03:11,095
Or, honey, use half and half.

93
00:03:11,275 --> 00:03:13,841
Half Yukon Gold for the creamy body,

94
00:03:13,841 --> 00:03:14,981
and half russet,

95
00:03:14,981 --> 00:03:17,547
because they break down a little and

96
00:03:17,547 --> 00:03:19,472
thicken the soup naturally.

97
00:03:19,652 --> 00:03:21,544
That's what I do now.

98
00:03:21,724 --> 00:03:24,325
Peel them or leave the skins on,

99
00:03:24,325 --> 00:03:25,544
it's up to you.

100
00:03:25,724 --> 00:03:28,596
My mother always peeled them and gave

101
00:03:28,596 --> 00:03:29,915
the peels to Mrs.

102
00:03:30,095 --> 00:03:31,953
Kowalski's chickens.

103
00:03:32,303 --> 00:03:33,429
Step one.

104
00:03:33,609 --> 00:03:35,961
Chop the bacon and cook it slowly

105
00:03:35,961 --> 00:03:38,099
in a big heavy pot over medium

106
00:03:38,099 --> 00:03:39,739
heat, until it's crisp.

107
00:03:39,919 --> 00:03:41,818
Lift it out with a spoon and

108
00:03:41,818 --> 00:03:43,649
set it on a paper towel for

109
00:03:43,649 --> 00:03:44,191
the top.

110
00:03:44,371 --> 00:03:47,318
Leave about two tablespoons of the bacon

111
00:03:47,318 --> 00:03:48,423
fat in the pot.

112
00:03:48,603 --> 00:03:49,700
Add the butter,

113
00:03:49,700 --> 00:03:51,528
the onion and the celery,

114
00:03:51,528 --> 00:03:54,307
and cook them for about eight minutes,

115
00:03:54,307 --> 00:03:56,428
until they're soft and sweet.

116
00:03:56,608 --> 00:03:57,783
Then the garlic,

117
00:03:57,783 --> 00:03:58,884
for one minute.

118
00:03:59,234 --> 00:04:01,590
And here's mistake number two.

119
00:04:01,770 --> 00:04:03,266
Skipping that step,

120
00:04:03,266 --> 00:04:06,414
and boiling the onion with the potatoes.

121
00:04:06,594 --> 00:04:10,252
Raw boiled onion tastes sharp and flat.

122
00:04:10,432 --> 00:04:13,138
Onions cooked slowly in bacon fat and

123
00:04:13,138 --> 00:04:15,259
butter turn sweet and golden,

124
00:04:15,259 --> 00:04:17,600
and they give the whole soup its

125
00:04:17,600 --> 00:04:18,477
deep flavor.

126
00:04:18,657 --> 00:04:21,200
That's my mother's first secret.

127
00:04:21,380 --> 00:04:24,244
Every good soup starts in the fat,

128
00:04:24,244 --> 00:04:25,002
she said.

129
00:04:25,352 --> 00:04:26,362
Step two.

130
00:04:26,542 --> 00:04:28,767
Cut the potatoes into even chunks,

131
00:04:28,767 --> 00:04:30,861
about three quarters of an inch.

132
00:04:31,041 --> 00:04:34,094
Mistake number three is uneven pieces.

133
00:04:34,274 --> 00:04:36,617
The little ones turn to mush while

134
00:04:36,617 --> 00:04:38,546
the big ones are still hard.

135
00:04:38,726 --> 00:04:41,106
Even pieces cook evenly.

136
00:04:41,286 --> 00:04:42,851
Add them to the pot,

137
00:04:42,851 --> 00:04:44,024
with the broth,

138
00:04:44,024 --> 00:04:45,745
the thyme or bay leaf,

139
00:04:45,745 --> 00:04:47,544
and a teaspoon of salt.

140
00:04:47,724 --> 00:04:50,708
The broth should just cover the potatoes.

141
00:04:51,058 --> 00:04:52,753
If this is helping you,

142
00:04:52,753 --> 00:04:55,260
honey, tap the like button for me.

143
00:04:55,440 --> 00:04:58,099
It helps Grandma more than you know.

144
00:04:58,279 --> 00:04:59,694
Bring it to a boil,

145
00:04:59,694 --> 00:05:01,778
then turn it down and let it

146
00:05:01,778 --> 00:05:03,491
simmer, partly covered,

147
00:05:03,491 --> 00:05:06,171
for about fifteen to twenty minutes,

148
00:05:06,171 --> 00:05:08,851
until a fork slides through a potato

149
00:05:08,851 --> 00:05:09,819
chunk easily.

150
00:05:09,999 --> 00:05:11,405
Don't boil it hard,

151
00:05:11,405 --> 00:05:14,067
or the outside of the potatoes falls

152
00:05:14,067 --> 00:05:16,582
apart before the inside is cooked.

153
00:05:16,933 --> 00:05:19,556
So far, the right potatoes,

154
00:05:19,556 --> 00:05:22,666
onions cooked slow in bacon fat,

155
00:05:22,666 --> 00:05:25,872
even pieces, and a gentle simmer.

156
00:05:26,052 --> 00:05:28,012
Now the trick I promised you,

157
00:05:28,012 --> 00:05:30,175
how to make it thick without any

158
00:05:30,175 --> 00:05:30,580
flour.

159
00:05:30,760 --> 00:05:32,386
Take out the bay leaf.

160
00:05:32,566 --> 00:05:34,401
Then take a potato masher,

161
00:05:34,401 --> 00:05:36,447
and mash about a third of the

162
00:05:36,447 --> 00:05:38,706
potatoes right there in the pot,

163
00:05:38,706 --> 00:05:40,611
leaving the rest in chunks.

164
00:05:40,791 --> 00:05:44,223
The mashed potato thickens the soup naturally,

165
00:05:44,223 --> 00:05:46,759
and you still have pieces to bite.

166
00:05:47,109 --> 00:05:49,542
And here's mistake number four,

167
00:05:49,542 --> 00:05:52,368
the other reason soup turns to glue.

168
00:05:52,548 --> 00:05:55,134
Using a blender or a food processor

169
00:05:55,134 --> 00:05:56,391
on the whole pot.

170
00:05:56,571 --> 00:05:59,414
The fast blades break open the potato

171
00:05:59,414 --> 00:06:02,104
starch, and it turns into a sticky,

172
00:06:02,104 --> 00:06:03,026
gummy paste.

173
00:06:03,206 --> 00:06:05,215
If you want it smooth,

174
00:06:05,215 --> 00:06:06,858
use a hand masher,

175
00:06:06,858 --> 00:06:09,324
or blend only a cup or two,

176
00:06:09,324 --> 00:06:09,963
gently.

177
00:06:10,143 --> 00:06:12,485
My mother didn't own a blender,

178
00:06:12,485 --> 00:06:15,054
and her soup was never once gluey.

179
00:06:15,404 --> 00:06:16,634
Step three.

180
00:06:16,814 --> 00:06:18,654
Turn the heat down to low,

181
00:06:18,654 --> 00:06:20,636
and stir in the milk or half

182
00:06:20,636 --> 00:06:21,272
and half.

183
00:06:21,452 --> 00:06:23,403
And mistake number five.

184
00:06:23,583 --> 00:06:26,219
Boiling the soup after the milk goes

185
00:06:26,219 --> 00:06:26,439
in.

186
00:06:26,619 --> 00:06:29,472
Milk can curdle and separate when it

187
00:06:29,472 --> 00:06:32,563
boils, and you get little white flecks.

188
00:06:32,743 --> 00:06:33,944
Keep it on low,

189
00:06:33,944 --> 00:06:36,586
just until it's hot and steaming.

190
00:06:36,766 --> 00:06:37,964
Then taste it,

191
00:06:37,964 --> 00:06:40,017
and add salt and pepper.

192
00:06:40,197 --> 00:06:42,798
Potatoes need a lot of salt,

193
00:06:42,798 --> 00:06:43,355
honey.

194
00:06:43,535 --> 00:06:44,812
Taste it twice.

195
00:06:45,162 --> 00:06:47,741
And my mother had one more trick,

196
00:06:47,741 --> 00:06:50,398
honey, for a soup with real depth.

197
00:06:50,578 --> 00:06:52,770
A tiny splash of vinegar or a

198
00:06:52,770 --> 00:06:55,340
squeeze of lemon right at the end,

199
00:06:55,340 --> 00:06:57,834
just a teaspoon in the whole pot.

200
00:06:58,014 --> 00:06:59,428
You can't taste it,

201
00:06:59,428 --> 00:07:01,809
but it wakes up all the flavors,

202
00:07:01,809 --> 00:07:03,819
the way a little salt does.

203
00:07:03,999 --> 00:07:06,576
My father always said her soup tasted

204
00:07:06,576 --> 00:07:08,109
better than anybody's,

205
00:07:08,109 --> 00:07:10,617
and he never knew about the vinegar.

206
00:07:10,797 --> 00:07:13,045
She took that secret all the way

207
00:07:13,045 --> 00:07:14,802
to nineteen ninety-eight.

208
00:07:15,152 --> 00:07:17,411
Ladle it into big bowls,

209
00:07:17,411 --> 00:07:19,482
and now the best part.

210
00:07:19,662 --> 00:07:21,253
Pile the toppings on.

211
00:07:21,433 --> 00:07:24,178
A handful of shredded sharp cheddar,

212
00:07:24,178 --> 00:07:25,627
the crumbled bacon,

213
00:07:25,627 --> 00:07:27,305
a spoon of sour cream,

214
00:07:27,305 --> 00:07:30,279
and some chopped chives or green onion.

215
00:07:30,459 --> 00:07:33,049
It's like a loaded baked potato in

216
00:07:33,049 --> 00:07:33,583
a bowl.

217
00:07:33,763 --> 00:07:37,211
My grandchildren call it baked potato soup,

218
00:07:37,211 --> 00:07:39,697
and they put so much cheese on,

219
00:07:39,697 --> 00:07:41,541
you can't see the soup.

220
00:07:41,892 --> 00:07:43,567
And my mother's way,

221
00:07:43,567 --> 00:07:45,661
sweetheart, on Thursdays,

222
00:07:45,661 --> 00:07:48,509
when there was no bacon or cheese.

223
00:07:48,689 --> 00:07:51,673
A handful of saltine crackers crumbled on

224
00:07:51,673 --> 00:07:53,928
top, a pat of butter melting in

225
00:07:53,928 --> 00:07:56,184
the middle, and a good shake of

226
00:07:56,184 --> 00:07:57,130
black pepper.

227
00:07:57,310 --> 00:07:58,308
That's all.

228
00:07:58,488 --> 00:08:00,731
And honestly, some nights,

229
00:08:00,731 --> 00:08:03,492
that's still how I like it best.

230
00:08:03,672 --> 00:08:06,052
It tastes like Elm Street.

231
00:08:06,402 --> 00:08:08,862
You can make this soup a hundred

232
00:08:08,862 --> 00:08:09,246
ways.

233
00:08:09,426 --> 00:08:11,395
Add a cup of corn and some

234
00:08:11,395 --> 00:08:14,198
diced ham, and it's a potato chowder.

235
00:08:14,378 --> 00:08:16,888
Add broccoli florets for the last ten

236
00:08:16,888 --> 00:08:19,262
minutes, and stir in cheddar at the

237
00:08:19,262 --> 00:08:21,704
end for broccoli cheese potato soup.

238
00:08:21,884 --> 00:08:23,609
Or leave out the bacon,

239
00:08:23,609 --> 00:08:25,109
use vegetable broth,

240
00:08:25,109 --> 00:08:26,159
and add leeks,

241
00:08:26,159 --> 00:08:27,584
for a lighter soup.

242
00:08:27,764 --> 00:08:30,857
Linda makes it with smoked sausage on

243
00:08:30,857 --> 00:08:31,526
Sundays.

244
00:08:31,876 --> 00:08:33,747
And if it's too thick,

245
00:08:33,747 --> 00:08:36,299
add a splash of broth or milk.

246
00:08:36,479 --> 00:08:37,728
If it's too thin,

247
00:08:37,728 --> 00:08:39,565
mash a few more potatoes,

248
00:08:39,565 --> 00:08:41,917
or let it simmer uncovered a few

249
00:08:41,917 --> 00:08:42,505
minutes.

250
00:08:42,685 --> 00:08:46,575
Remember, potato soup always gets thicker as

251
00:08:46,575 --> 00:08:47,282
it sits.

252
00:08:47,462 --> 00:08:49,739
So make it a little thinner than

253
00:08:49,739 --> 00:08:51,375
you want it in the pot,

254
00:08:51,375 --> 00:08:53,297
and by the time it's in the

255
00:08:53,297 --> 00:08:55,218
bowls, it'll be just right.

256
00:08:55,568 --> 00:08:58,122
And serve it with something warm on

257
00:08:58,122 --> 00:08:59,654
the side, sweetheart.

258
00:08:59,834 --> 00:09:01,245
A pan of cornbread,

259
00:09:01,245 --> 00:09:02,582
or buttered toast,

260
00:09:02,582 --> 00:09:05,924
or grilled cheese sandwiches cut in triangles

261
00:09:05,924 --> 00:09:07,706
for the children to dip.

262
00:09:07,886 --> 00:09:11,239
My grandson calls grilled cheese and potato

263
00:09:11,239 --> 00:09:13,734
soup the best supper in America,

264
00:09:13,734 --> 00:09:15,839
and I can't argue with him.

265
00:09:16,019 --> 00:09:18,627
It costs about a dollar a person,

266
00:09:18,627 --> 00:09:21,394
and nobody leaves the table hungry.

267
00:09:21,744 --> 00:09:24,600
It keeps four days in the icebox.

268
00:09:24,780 --> 00:09:26,335
When you warm it up,

269
00:09:26,335 --> 00:09:27,890
it'll be very thick,

270
00:09:27,890 --> 00:09:30,144
so add a little milk or broth

271
00:09:30,144 --> 00:09:31,621
and heat it gently,

272
00:09:31,621 --> 00:09:33,487
stirring, never boiling.

273
00:09:33,667 --> 00:09:36,221
And here's something people don't know.

274
00:09:36,401 --> 00:09:38,995
Potato soup with milk in it doesn't

275
00:09:38,995 --> 00:09:39,884
freeze well.

276
00:09:40,064 --> 00:09:42,270
The potatoes turn grainy.

277
00:09:42,450 --> 00:09:44,128
If you want to freeze it,

278
00:09:44,128 --> 00:09:46,409
freeze it before you add the milk,

279
00:09:46,409 --> 00:09:48,422
and add the milk when you warm

280
00:09:48,422 --> 00:09:48,824
it up.

281
00:09:49,174 --> 00:09:50,660
So one more time.

282
00:09:50,840 --> 00:09:52,550
Yukon Gold potatoes,

283
00:09:52,550 --> 00:09:55,031
or half and half with russet.

284
00:09:55,211 --> 00:09:58,234
Onion and celery cooked slow in bacon

285
00:09:58,234 --> 00:09:59,460
fat and butter.

286
00:09:59,640 --> 00:10:01,033
Even pieces.

287
00:10:01,213 --> 00:10:02,734
A gentle simmer.

288
00:10:02,914 --> 00:10:05,354
Mash a third of the potatoes,

289
00:10:05,354 --> 00:10:07,036
by hand, no blender.

290
00:10:07,216 --> 00:10:08,411
Milk on low,

291
00:10:08,411 --> 00:10:09,805
never boiling.

292
00:10:09,985 --> 00:10:11,390
Plenty of salt.

293
00:10:11,570 --> 00:10:13,451
And pile on the toppings.

294
00:10:13,631 --> 00:10:16,638
That's my mother's Thursday potato soup,

295
00:10:16,638 --> 00:10:18,216
and it's never gluey.

296
00:10:18,567 --> 00:10:20,326
Tell me in the comments,

297
00:10:20,326 --> 00:10:21,133
sweetheart.

298
00:10:21,313 --> 00:10:23,525
What did your family eat the day

299
00:10:23,525 --> 00:10:24,494
before payday?

300
00:10:24,674 --> 00:10:26,596
I bet a lot of you had

301
00:10:26,596 --> 00:10:27,994
potato soup too.

302
00:10:28,174 --> 00:10:31,327
The whole playlist of Grandma's recipes is

303
00:10:31,327 --> 00:10:33,354
right there on your screen,

304
00:10:33,354 --> 00:10:35,456
and I'll see you in the next

305
00:10:35,456 --> 00:10:35,906
video.

306
00:10:36,086 --> 00:10:37,735
Good night, honey.
9R3jsGwKuSU:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:02,739
Sweetheart, if you grew up in Ohio,

2
00:00:02,739 --> 00:00:05,479
you know exactly what a buckeye is.

3
00:00:05,659 --> 00:00:08,293
A little ball of sweet peanut butter,

4
00:00:08,293 --> 00:00:09,717
dipped in chocolate,

5
00:00:09,717 --> 00:00:12,279
with a round circle of peanut butter

6
00:00:12,279 --> 00:00:13,702
left showing on top,

7
00:00:13,702 --> 00:00:15,909
so it looks just like the shiny

8
00:00:15,909 --> 00:00:18,187
brown nut from the buckeye tree.

9
00:00:18,367 --> 00:00:21,289
Every Christmas cookie tray in Ohio has

10
00:00:21,289 --> 00:00:21,664
them.

11
00:00:21,844 --> 00:00:23,234
If yours doesn't,

12
00:00:23,234 --> 00:00:25,768
somebody will ask what's wrong.

13
00:00:26,118 --> 00:00:28,520
But people tell me their buckeyes are

14
00:00:28,520 --> 00:00:30,599
too soft and slump into puddles,

15
00:00:30,599 --> 00:00:33,066
or the chocolate is thick and streaky,

16
00:00:33,066 --> 00:00:35,339
or they fall off the toothpick into

17
00:00:35,339 --> 00:00:36,508
the chocolate pot.

18
00:00:36,688 --> 00:00:39,417
So tonight I'm giving you my buckeyes,

19
00:00:39,417 --> 00:00:42,146
every step, and the five mistakes that

20
00:00:42,146 --> 00:00:43,295
make them messy.

21
00:00:43,475 --> 00:00:44,696
And stay with me,

22
00:00:44,696 --> 00:00:46,995
because the last trick is how to

23
00:00:46,995 --> 00:00:49,367
get rid of that toothpick hole on

24
00:00:49,367 --> 00:00:51,451
top, and it takes one second.

25
00:00:51,800 --> 00:00:54,376
Ohio is the Buckeye State,

26
00:00:54,376 --> 00:00:54,970
honey.

27
00:00:55,150 --> 00:00:57,907
The buckeye tree grows all over Ohio,

28
00:00:57,907 --> 00:01:00,216
and its nut is shiny dark brown

29
00:01:00,216 --> 00:01:02,377
with a light tan spot on top,

30
00:01:02,377 --> 00:01:03,718
like a deer's eye.

31
00:01:03,898 --> 00:01:06,185
That's where the name comes from.

32
00:01:06,365 --> 00:01:07,457
Buck eye.

33
00:01:07,637 --> 00:01:08,902
When I was a girl,

34
00:01:08,902 --> 00:01:11,151
we carried a real buckeye nut in

35
00:01:11,151 --> 00:01:12,908
our pocket for good luck.

36
00:01:13,088 --> 00:01:15,602
My father carried the same one for

37
00:01:15,602 --> 00:01:16,489
forty years.

38
00:01:16,669 --> 00:01:18,968
It's in my jewelry box now.

39
00:01:19,319 --> 00:01:20,956
The candy came later.

40
00:01:21,136 --> 00:01:23,270
The story goes that a woman in

41
00:01:23,270 --> 00:01:25,476
Ohio made the first ones in the

42
00:01:25,476 --> 00:01:28,606
nineteen sixties, and the recipe spread from

43
00:01:28,606 --> 00:01:31,879
church cookbook to church cookbook until every

44
00:01:31,879 --> 00:01:33,872
kitchen in the state had it.

45
00:01:34,052 --> 00:01:35,866
I first had them at a church

46
00:01:35,866 --> 00:01:38,521
Christmas bazaar in nineteen sixty-eight.

47
00:01:38,701 --> 00:01:39,912
I bought a dozen,

48
00:01:39,912 --> 00:01:41,620
ate them all in the car,

49
00:01:41,620 --> 00:01:44,112
and went back in for another dozen.

50
00:01:44,461 --> 00:01:46,790
And they're perfect for Christmas,

51
00:01:46,790 --> 00:01:49,872
sweetheart, because there's no baking at all.

52
00:01:50,052 --> 00:01:52,827
No oven, no cookie sheets,

53
00:01:52,827 --> 00:01:53,895
no timing.

54
00:01:54,075 --> 00:01:55,056
Just a bowl,

55
00:01:55,056 --> 00:01:57,918
your hands, and a pot of chocolate.

56
00:01:58,098 --> 00:02:00,048
Children love making them.

57
00:02:00,228 --> 00:02:02,168
In a minute I'll tell you the

58
00:02:02,168 --> 00:02:04,575
first mistake, and it's the one that

59
00:02:04,575 --> 00:02:06,381
makes them too soft to dip.

60
00:02:06,732 --> 00:02:08,328
Here's what you need,

61
00:02:08,328 --> 00:02:09,924
for about five dozen.

62
00:02:10,104 --> 00:02:12,304
One and a half cups of creamy

63
00:02:12,304 --> 00:02:13,367
peanut butter.

64
00:02:13,547 --> 00:02:15,367
Half a cup of butter,

65
00:02:15,367 --> 00:02:16,147
softened.

66
00:02:16,327 --> 00:02:18,313
One teaspoon of vanilla.

67
00:02:18,493 --> 00:02:20,757
A quarter teaspoon of salt.

68
00:02:20,937 --> 00:02:23,003
Four cups of powdered sugar.

69
00:02:23,183 --> 00:02:24,408
And for dipping,

70
00:02:24,408 --> 00:02:27,393
two cups of semi-sweet chocolate chips,

71
00:02:27,393 --> 00:02:30,072
or twelve ounces of good chocolate,

72
00:02:30,072 --> 00:02:32,675
and a tablespoon of coconut oil or

73
00:02:32,675 --> 00:02:34,282
vegetable shortening.

74
00:02:34,633 --> 00:02:36,769
And here's mistake number one.

75
00:02:36,949 --> 00:02:38,876
Natural peanut butter.

76
00:02:39,056 --> 00:02:41,117
The kind with the oil on top

77
00:02:41,117 --> 00:02:43,473
makes the filling oily and soft,

78
00:02:43,473 --> 00:02:45,093
and it never firms up.

79
00:02:45,273 --> 00:02:48,048
Use the regular creamy kind from the

80
00:02:48,048 --> 00:02:50,437
jar, the kind you don't have to

81
00:02:50,437 --> 00:02:50,823
stir.

82
00:02:51,003 --> 00:02:52,522
And soft butter,

83
00:02:52,522 --> 00:02:54,230
honey, not melted.

84
00:02:54,410 --> 00:02:57,166
Melted butter makes the filling greasy,

85
00:02:57,166 --> 00:02:59,285
and the balls slump as soon as

86
00:02:59,285 --> 00:03:00,204
they warm up.

87
00:03:00,554 --> 00:03:01,506
Step one.

88
00:03:01,686 --> 00:03:03,421
Beat the peanut butter,

89
00:03:03,421 --> 00:03:06,742
soft butter, vanilla and salt together until

90
00:03:06,742 --> 00:03:07,270
smooth.

91
00:03:07,450 --> 00:03:09,538
Then add the powdered sugar,

92
00:03:09,538 --> 00:03:10,731
a cup at a time,

93
00:03:10,731 --> 00:03:13,042
mixing on low so it doesn't fly

94
00:03:13,042 --> 00:03:14,683
all over your kitchen.

95
00:03:14,863 --> 00:03:16,813
The dough will be stiff,

96
00:03:16,813 --> 00:03:18,114
like play dough.

97
00:03:18,294 --> 00:03:21,289
Mistake number two is not enough sugar.

98
00:03:21,469 --> 00:03:23,312
If it's sticky and soft,

99
00:03:23,312 --> 00:03:25,846
the balls won't hold their shape.

100
00:03:26,026 --> 00:03:27,435
Add more sugar,

101
00:03:27,435 --> 00:03:29,126
a spoon at a time.

102
00:03:29,476 --> 00:03:30,915
Here's the test.

103
00:03:31,095 --> 00:03:33,754
Roll a little piece between your palms.

104
00:03:33,934 --> 00:03:36,654
If it rolls smooth and doesn't stick

105
00:03:36,654 --> 00:03:37,712
to your hands,

106
00:03:37,712 --> 00:03:38,543
it's right.

107
00:03:38,723 --> 00:03:39,898
If it sticks,

108
00:03:39,898 --> 00:03:42,067
add more powdered sugar.

109
00:03:42,247 --> 00:03:44,905
Every peanut butter is a little different.

110
00:03:45,085 --> 00:03:47,203
Some days I need four and a

111
00:03:47,203 --> 00:03:47,988
half cups.

112
00:03:48,168 --> 00:03:50,418
And don't be afraid to get in

113
00:03:50,418 --> 00:03:52,126
there with your hands,

114
00:03:52,126 --> 00:03:52,591
honey.

115
00:03:52,771 --> 00:03:55,453
It mixes better that way anyway.

116
00:03:55,803 --> 00:03:57,513
If this is helping you,

117
00:03:57,513 --> 00:04:00,041
honey, tap the like button for me.

118
00:04:00,221 --> 00:04:02,903
It helps Grandma more than you know.

119
00:04:03,083 --> 00:04:05,699
Now roll the dough into balls about

120
00:04:05,699 --> 00:04:06,894
one inch across,

121
00:04:06,894 --> 00:04:09,286
about the size of a real buckeye

122
00:04:09,286 --> 00:04:09,585
nut.

123
00:04:09,765 --> 00:04:11,802
Set them on a baking sheet lined

124
00:04:11,802 --> 00:04:13,584
with wax paper or parchment.

125
00:04:13,764 --> 00:04:16,057
Make them all the same size,

126
00:04:16,057 --> 00:04:18,513
so they look nice on the tray.

127
00:04:18,862 --> 00:04:21,178
Step two, and this is the one

128
00:04:21,178 --> 00:04:22,137
people skip.

129
00:04:22,317 --> 00:04:24,279
Mistake number three.

130
00:04:24,459 --> 00:04:26,723
Dipping warm, soft balls.

131
00:04:26,903 --> 00:04:28,940
They fall off the toothpick,

132
00:04:28,940 --> 00:04:30,905
melt in the warm chocolate,

133
00:04:30,905 --> 00:04:32,069
and make a mess.

134
00:04:32,249 --> 00:04:34,659
Put the whole tray in the freezer

135
00:04:34,659 --> 00:04:36,703
for at least thirty minutes,

136
00:04:36,703 --> 00:04:38,602
or the icebox for an hour,

137
00:04:38,602 --> 00:04:41,084
until the balls are firm and cold.

138
00:04:41,264 --> 00:04:44,266
Cold balls hold onto the toothpick and

139
00:04:44,266 --> 00:04:46,082
set the chocolate fast.

140
00:04:46,433 --> 00:04:48,685
And here's a trick from Mrs.

141
00:04:48,865 --> 00:04:50,180
Hartman at church,

142
00:04:50,180 --> 00:04:53,469
who made five hundred buckeyes every December

143
00:04:53,469 --> 00:04:54,565
for the bazaar.

144
00:04:54,745 --> 00:04:57,053
Stick the toothpick in each ball before

145
00:04:57,053 --> 00:04:58,414
they go in the freezer.

146
00:04:58,594 --> 00:05:01,396
Then they freeze solid around the toothpick,

147
00:05:01,396 --> 00:05:02,925
and they never slip off.

148
00:05:03,105 --> 00:05:03,987
Mrs.

149
00:05:04,167 --> 00:05:06,605
Hartman said that one trick saved her

150
00:05:06,605 --> 00:05:08,846
about two hundred buckeyes a year.

151
00:05:09,196 --> 00:05:11,274
Step three, the chocolate.

152
00:05:11,454 --> 00:05:14,564
Melt the chocolate chips with the coconut

153
00:05:14,564 --> 00:05:16,764
oil or shortening in a small,

154
00:05:16,764 --> 00:05:18,813
deep bowl in the microwave,

155
00:05:18,813 --> 00:05:20,709
thirty seconds at a time,

156
00:05:20,709 --> 00:05:22,151
stirring each time,

157
00:05:22,151 --> 00:05:23,516
until it's smooth.

158
00:05:23,696 --> 00:05:25,397
Or in a bowl over a pot

159
00:05:25,397 --> 00:05:27,319
of barely simmering water.

160
00:05:27,499 --> 00:05:30,320
Mistake number four is overheating it.

161
00:05:30,500 --> 00:05:32,260
Chocolate burns easily,

162
00:05:32,260 --> 00:05:34,709
and burnt chocolate turns thick,

163
00:05:34,709 --> 00:05:35,933
dull and grainy.

164
00:05:36,113 --> 00:05:37,671
Low and slow,

165
00:05:37,671 --> 00:05:38,749
and stir.

166
00:05:39,099 --> 00:05:41,898
The coconut oil or shortening is the

167
00:05:41,898 --> 00:05:43,376
secret to a smooth,

168
00:05:43,376 --> 00:05:44,776
shiny coat, honey.

169
00:05:44,956 --> 00:05:48,150
It thins the chocolate just a little,

170
00:05:48,150 --> 00:05:50,567
so it coats evenly and thin,

171
00:05:50,567 --> 00:05:51,862
not in a thick,

172
00:05:51,862 --> 00:05:53,071
lumpy blanket.

173
00:05:53,251 --> 00:05:54,406
And use a small,

174
00:05:54,406 --> 00:05:56,931
deep bowl, so the chocolate is deep

175
00:05:56,931 --> 00:05:58,301
enough to dip into.

176
00:05:58,481 --> 00:06:01,669
A wide, shallow bowl is how buckeyes

177
00:06:01,669 --> 00:06:03,706
end up with bald spots.

178
00:06:04,056 --> 00:06:06,205
And a word about the chocolate,

179
00:06:06,205 --> 00:06:06,621
honey.

180
00:06:06,801 --> 00:06:08,949
Chocolate chips work fine,

181
00:06:08,949 --> 00:06:12,583
and they're what most Ohio grandmothers use.

182
00:06:12,763 --> 00:06:14,730
But a good chocolate bar,

183
00:06:14,730 --> 00:06:18,034
chopped, melts smoother and tastes richer.

184
00:06:18,214 --> 00:06:20,353
Don't let even one drop of water

185
00:06:20,353 --> 00:06:22,893
get into the chocolate while it melts.

186
00:06:23,073 --> 00:06:25,739
A single drop makes it seize up,

187
00:06:25,739 --> 00:06:27,821
thick and lumpy like mud.

188
00:06:28,001 --> 00:06:29,783
Dry bowl, dry spoon,

189
00:06:29,783 --> 00:06:32,634
and keep the steam away from it.

190
00:06:32,983 --> 00:06:35,515
So far, regular peanut butter,

191
00:06:35,515 --> 00:06:38,047
enough sugar, same-size balls,

192
00:06:38,047 --> 00:06:40,494
frozen with the toothpick in,

193
00:06:40,494 --> 00:06:43,363
and chocolate melted low and slow.

194
00:06:43,543 --> 00:06:45,752
Now, take out a few balls at

195
00:06:45,752 --> 00:06:48,041
a time, and leave the rest in

196
00:06:48,041 --> 00:06:48,988
the freezer.

197
00:06:49,168 --> 00:06:50,470
Hold the toothpick,

198
00:06:50,470 --> 00:06:53,006
and dip each ball into the chocolate,

199
00:06:53,006 --> 00:06:55,405
about three quarters of the way up,

200
00:06:55,405 --> 00:06:58,078
leaving a round circle of peanut butter

201
00:06:58,078 --> 00:06:59,106
showing on top.

202
00:06:59,286 --> 00:07:01,190
That's the buckeye's eye.

203
00:07:01,540 --> 00:07:04,015
Let the extra chocolate drip off for

204
00:07:04,015 --> 00:07:04,977
a few seconds,

205
00:07:04,977 --> 00:07:06,834
and give it a little twirl.

206
00:07:07,014 --> 00:07:09,265
Then set it back on the wax

207
00:07:09,265 --> 00:07:09,765
paper.

208
00:07:09,945 --> 00:07:12,527
Mistake number five is dipping them all

209
00:07:12,527 --> 00:07:13,057
the way.

210
00:07:13,237 --> 00:07:16,153
Then it's just a chocolate peanut butter

211
00:07:16,153 --> 00:07:17,393
ball, sweetheart.

212
00:07:17,573 --> 00:07:20,534
It's delicious, but it's not a buckeye.

213
00:07:20,714 --> 00:07:24,406
In Ohio, that's practically against the law.

214
00:07:24,756 --> 00:07:26,756
And now the trick I promised,

215
00:07:26,756 --> 00:07:28,343
for the toothpick hole.

216
00:07:28,523 --> 00:07:30,726
After you set the buckeye down and

217
00:07:30,726 --> 00:07:32,217
pull out the toothpick,

218
00:07:32,217 --> 00:07:34,096
there's a little hole on top.

219
00:07:34,276 --> 00:07:36,747
Just touch it with your fingertip and

220
00:07:36,747 --> 00:07:39,419
gently smooth the peanut butter over it.

221
00:07:39,599 --> 00:07:41,967
One second, and it's gone.

222
00:07:42,147 --> 00:07:44,875
It looks like a real buckeye nut,

223
00:07:44,875 --> 00:07:46,281
perfectly smooth.

224
00:07:46,461 --> 00:07:47,424
Mrs.

225
00:07:47,604 --> 00:07:50,537
Hartman's always looked like they came from

226
00:07:50,537 --> 00:07:51,424
a candy shop.

227
00:07:51,774 --> 00:07:53,958
Put the finished tray back in the

228
00:07:53,958 --> 00:07:56,143
icebox for about fifteen minutes,

229
00:07:56,143 --> 00:07:58,658
until the chocolate is completely set.

230
00:07:58,838 --> 00:08:01,256
And if the chocolate in your bowl

231
00:08:01,256 --> 00:08:03,161
gets thick while you work,

232
00:08:03,161 --> 00:08:05,506
put it back in the microwave for

233
00:08:05,506 --> 00:08:06,385
ten seconds.

234
00:08:06,565 --> 00:08:08,196
If it gets too low,

235
00:08:08,196 --> 00:08:10,601
tip the bowl a little to one

236
00:08:10,601 --> 00:08:12,405
side, so it's deeper.

237
00:08:12,585 --> 00:08:14,129
Patience, honey.

238
00:08:14,309 --> 00:08:17,327
Five dozen buckeyes takes about an hour.

239
00:08:17,678 --> 00:08:20,336
Buckeyes keep two weeks in the icebox

240
00:08:20,336 --> 00:08:22,564
in a tin with wax paper between

241
00:08:22,564 --> 00:08:25,079
the layers, and three months in the

242
00:08:25,079 --> 00:08:25,654
freezer.

243
00:08:25,834 --> 00:08:28,778
Take them out about fifteen minutes before

244
00:08:28,778 --> 00:08:31,441
serving, so the peanut butter is soft.

245
00:08:31,621 --> 00:08:34,454
They make the best gift in Ohio.

246
00:08:34,634 --> 00:08:37,097
Put a dozen in little paper candy

247
00:08:37,097 --> 00:08:38,142
cups in a box,

248
00:08:38,142 --> 00:08:40,008
and tie it with a red and

249
00:08:40,008 --> 00:08:42,695
gray ribbon, if you're an Ohio State

250
00:08:42,695 --> 00:08:42,993
fan.

251
00:08:43,343 --> 00:08:45,902
And you can make them fancy,

252
00:08:45,902 --> 00:08:46,908
sweetheart.

253
00:08:47,088 --> 00:08:49,313
Add half a cup of crushed graham

254
00:08:49,313 --> 00:08:51,886
crackers or crispy rice cereal to the

255
00:08:51,886 --> 00:08:53,903
filling, for a little crunch.

256
00:08:54,083 --> 00:08:55,894
Or use dark chocolate.

257
00:08:56,074 --> 00:08:58,376
Or sprinkle a few flakes of sea

258
00:08:58,376 --> 00:09:01,124
salt on the chocolate before it sets.

259
00:09:01,304 --> 00:09:04,188
My granddaughter makes a chocolate chip cookie

260
00:09:04,188 --> 00:09:05,066
dough version.

261
00:09:05,246 --> 00:09:06,106
In my day,

262
00:09:06,106 --> 00:09:08,601
that would've been a scandal.

263
00:09:08,951 --> 00:09:11,715
And here's a shortcut for busy people.

264
00:09:11,895 --> 00:09:15,042
Press the whole peanut butter mixture into

265
00:09:15,042 --> 00:09:17,140
a buttered nine by nine pan,

266
00:09:17,140 --> 00:09:20,063
pour the melted chocolate over the top,

267
00:09:20,063 --> 00:09:22,611
chill it, and cut it into squares.

268
00:09:22,791 --> 00:09:24,973
They call them buckeye bars.

269
00:09:25,153 --> 00:09:27,255
They taste exactly the same,

270
00:09:27,255 --> 00:09:29,507
and they take fifteen minutes.

271
00:09:29,687 --> 00:09:30,674
Mrs.

272
00:09:30,854 --> 00:09:33,814
Hartman called them lazy buckeyes.

273
00:09:33,994 --> 00:09:35,515
But she ate three.

274
00:09:35,865 --> 00:09:37,352
So one more time.

275
00:09:37,532 --> 00:09:41,119
Regular creamy peanut butter and soft butter.

276
00:09:41,299 --> 00:09:44,231
Enough powdered sugar that the dough doesn't

277
00:09:44,231 --> 00:09:44,631
stick.

278
00:09:44,811 --> 00:09:47,180
Roll them the size of a buckeye.

279
00:09:47,360 --> 00:09:50,517
Toothpick in, and freeze them thirty minutes.

280
00:09:50,697 --> 00:09:53,678
Chocolate melted low and slow with a

281
00:09:53,678 --> 00:09:55,251
little coconut oil,

282
00:09:55,251 --> 00:09:56,162
in a small,

283
00:09:56,162 --> 00:09:56,990
deep bowl.

284
00:09:57,170 --> 00:09:59,811
Dip them three quarters of the way,

285
00:09:59,811 --> 00:10:01,849
and smooth the hole on top.

286
00:10:02,029 --> 00:10:04,548
That's a real Ohio buckeye.

287
00:10:04,899 --> 00:10:07,072
Tell me in the comments,

288
00:10:07,072 --> 00:10:08,068
sweetheart.

289
00:10:08,248 --> 00:10:09,718
Where are you from,

290
00:10:09,718 --> 00:10:13,275
and what's the Christmas candy everybody makes

291
00:10:13,275 --> 00:10:13,740
there?

292
00:10:13,920 --> 00:10:15,557
I'd love to know.

293
00:10:15,737 --> 00:10:18,890
The whole playlist of Grandma's recipes is

294
00:10:18,890 --> 00:10:20,916
right there on your screen,

295
00:10:20,916 --> 00:10:23,018
and I'll see you in the next

296
00:10:23,018 --> 00:10:23,469
video.

297
00:10:23,649 --> 00:10:25,239
Good night, honey.

298
00:10:25,419 --> 00:10:26,801
Merry Christmas.
